the spellblade's control over arcane arsenal has matured, allowing their manifested weapons to remain stable for far longer while requiring less mana to sustain. every arcane weapon now feels less like a temporary creation and more like a true extension of the spellblade's body, responding instantly to every movement and intention.

with greater experience comes greater refinement. the spellblade learns to weave intricate mana patterns throughout the weapon during its creation, strengthening its structure and allowing it to endure prolonged combat without losing cohesion. the chosen magical affinity burns brighter within the weapon, making every strike a seamless combination of martial skill and arcane power.

although still limited to manifesting a single weapon, experienced spellblades no longer fear being separated from their equipment. their weapon can be recreated whenever needed, ensuring they are always prepared for whatever battle lies ahead.

### effects

- spend **30 mp** and **1 action point** to manifest **one arcane weapon**.
- the arcane weapon lasts for **20 minutes**, or until dismissed.
- you may only maintain **one arcane weapon** at a time.
- choose **any weapon type** you are proficient with when the weapon is manifested.
- choose one of your **known magical affinities** when the weapon is created. the weapon retains this affinity until it disappears.
- the arcane weapon counts as a **magical weapon**.
- the weapon deals its **normal weapon damage**, plus an additional **2d6** damage matching its chosen magical affinity.
- arcane weapons created through this talent are considered exceptionally stable and cannot be destroyed by mundane means.
- if disarmed, the arcane weapon immediately dissipates.
- arcane weapons cannot be traded, sold, permanently stored, or wielded by another creature.
- this rank replaces the effects of **arcane arsenal — rank i**.

### lore

among the spellblade orders, rank ii is known as the **forgemaster's grip**, marking the stage where a spellblade no longer creates a weapon through effort alone. instead, the weapon forms naturally in response to its wielder's will, flowing from raw mana into solid form with remarkable speed and precision.

masters often challenge apprentices to dismiss and recreate their weapon repeatedly until the process becomes instinctive. they teach that hesitation in battle can be fatal, and that a true spellblade should never worry about losing their weapon, only about choosing the right one for the moment.

veteran spellblades often become recognised by their arcane arsenal alone. whether forged from radiant light, living flame, crackling lightning, or pure arcane mana, every weapon reflects the personality and discipline of its creator, making each manifestation as unique as the warrior who wields it.

> *"a forged blade is carried by its master. an arcane weapon is carried by its master's will."*

> — grand spellblade aetherion lux, first blade of the infinite well

## rank 3
### description

arcane arsenal reaches a new level of mastery as the spellblade learns that a weapon forged from mana is never fixed in form. instead of dismissing and recreating their arcane weapon, the spellblade can reshape it instantly into another weapon they have mastered, allowing them to adapt to the ever-changing flow of battle without interrupting their momentum.

veteran spellblades often transition seamlessly between weapons during combat. a longsword becomes a spear to engage a distant foe, a warhammer forms to crush heavy armour, or twin daggers become a greatsword in preparation for a decisive strike. to an outside observer, the weapon appears to dissolve into streams of mana before reforming almost instantly into its new shape.

this level of mastery marks the point where the arcane weapon truly becomes an extension of the spellblade's will. the weapon no longer dictates the style of combat—the spellblade simply creates the weapon that best suits the moment.

### effects

- spend **30 mp** and **1 action point** to manifest **one arcane weapon**.
- the arcane weapon lasts for **30 minutes**, or until dismissed.
- you may only maintain **one arcane weapon** at a time.
- choose **any weapon type** you are proficient with when the weapon is first manifested.
- choose one of your **known magical affinities** when the weapon is created. the weapon retains this affinity until dismissed.
- the arcane weapon counts as a **magical weapon**.
- the weapon deals its **normal weapon damage**, plus an additional **3d6** damage matching its chosen magical affinity.
- **once per turn**, you may spend **1 action point** to instantly reshape your arcane weapon into any other weapon you are proficient with without dismissing it. the weapon retains its chosen magical affinity.
- arcane weapons cannot be destroyed by mundane means.
- if disarmed, the arcane weapon immediately dissipates.
- arcane weapons cannot be traded, sold, permanently stored, or wielded by another creature.
- this rank replaces the effects of **arcane arsenal — rank ii**.

### lore

within the spellblade orders, rank iii is known as the **living arsenal**. masters teach that no single weapon is perfect for every battle, and a true spellblade should never be limited by the weapon they currently hold. instead, they learn to view every weapon as merely another shape their mana can assume.

watching a master of the living arsenal is a breathtaking display of martial artistry. weapons shift effortlessly between strikes, each transformation occurring so fluidly that many enemies fail to realise the change until it is too late. every form is deliberate, chosen to exploit an opening, counter an opponent's fighting style, or adapt to the changing battlefield.

to master the living arsenal is to abandon the idea of favourite weapons entirely. every weapon becomes your weapon, and every battle becomes an opportunity to demonstrate complete mastery over both steel and mana.

> *"the greatest weapon is not the sword in your hand—it is the one you choose to create next."*

> — grand spellblade aetherion lux, first blade of the infinite well

## rank 4
### description

the spellblade has achieved a level of mastery where a single arcane weapon is no longer sufficient. through exceptional control over their mana, they can now maintain multiple manifestations simultaneously, allowing them to wield paired weapons or combine offence and defence without sacrificing the stability of their creations.

rather than simply increasing the power of their arsenal, the spellblade expands its versatility. twin blades flow together in perfect harmony, a spear and shield appear as one seamless creation, or an axe and dagger allow the spellblade to adapt instantly to shifting battlefield conditions. every manifestation remains an extension of the spellblade's will, responding as naturally as their own limbs.

among the spellblade orders, rank iv represents complete confidence in one's martial abilities. masters no longer think about the weapon they require—they simply will it into existence, knowing their arcane arsenal will always provide the perfect tool for the task.

### effects

- spend **25 mp** and **1 action point** to manifest your **arcane arsenal**.
- your arcane arsenal lasts for **1 hour**, or until dismissed.
- your arcane weapons deal their **normal weapon damage**, plus an additional **3d6** damage matching their chosen magical affinity.
- choose one of your **known magical affinities** when your arcane arsenal is manifested. all manifested weapons share this affinity until dismissed.
- arcane weapons count as **magical weapons**.

when manifesting your arcane arsenal, choose one of the following:

- **one two-handed weapon.**
- **two one-handed weapons.**
- **one one-handed weapon and one arcane shield.**

additional benefits:

- you may reshape any manifested weapon into another weapon you are proficient with by spending **1 action point**.
- the chosen magical affinity remains unchanged when reshaping.
- arcane weapons cannot be destroyed by mundane means.
- if disarmed, only the affected arcane weapon dissipates. remaining manifested equipment is unaffected.
- arcane weapons cannot be traded, sold, permanently stored, or wielded by another creature.
- this rank replaces the effects of **arcane arsenal — rank iii**.

### lore

within the oldest spellblade orders, rank iv is known as the **master arsenal**. reaching this stage signifies that a spellblade no longer sees weapons as individual tools, but as parts of a complete fighting style. every weapon exists only as another expression of their mana, ready to be reshaped whenever the battle demands.

veterans often demonstrate this mastery by flowing effortlessly between weapon combinations without ever breaking their rhythm. a sword becomes twin daggers, twin daggers become a spear, and moments later a shield forms beside them as though it had always existed. to an observer, the transformations appear less like magic and more like the weapon itself is alive.

the greatest masters teach that adaptability is the true strength of arcane arsenal. victory belongs not to the warrior carrying the strongest weapon, but to the one capable of creating the perfect weapon for every challenge.

> *"an ordinary warrior masters a weapon. a spellblade masters every weapon before the battle has even begun."*

> — grand spellblade aetherion lux, first blade of the infinite well

## rank 5
### description

arcane arsenal reaches its ultimate expression, becoming the defining symbol of a true spellblade master. no longer bound by the limitations of conventional weapons, the spellblade effortlessly shapes their mana into any weapon they have mastered, seamlessly adapting to every challenge without interrupting the flow of battle. every manifestation is an extension of their body, mind, and soul, forged not from steel, but from absolute control over arcane energy.

at this level, the arcane arsenal no longer feels like a summoned weapon. it becomes a permanent companion while maintained, capable of shifting between countless forms without losing its magical affinity or structural integrity. whether wielding twin blades, a towering greataxe, a spear and shield, or a finely crafted bow, the spellblade is never without the perfect weapon for the moment.

among the oldest spellblade orders, rank v is known as the **infinite arsenal**. masters believe this is the moment where the spellblade transcends the idea of weapon mastery. they no longer wield weapons—they command them through will alone.

### effects

- spend **20 mp** and **1 action point** to manifest your **arcane arsenal**.
- your arcane arsenal remains until **dismissed**, or until you become **unconscious**.
- your arcane weapons deal their **normal weapon damage**, plus an additional **3d6** damage matching their chosen magical affinity.
- choose one of your **known magical affinities** when your arcane arsenal is manifested. all arcane weapons retain this affinity until dismissed.
- arcane weapons count as **legendary magical weapons**.

when manifesting your arcane arsenal, you may choose:

- one two-handed weapon.
- two one-handed weapons.
- one one-handed weapon and one arcane shield.

#### infinite arsenal

- once per turn, you may spend **1 action point** to instantly reshape any arcane weapon into another weapon you are proficient with.
- reshaping does not dismiss the weapon or change its chosen magical affinity.
- arcane weapons cannot be destroyed by mundane means.
- if disarmed, only the affected arcane weapon dissipates and may be immediately recreated on your next turn.
- arcane weapons cannot be traded, sold, permanently stored, or wielded by another creature.

#### weapon mastery

each manifested weapon gains an additional passive benefit based on its weapon type.

examples include:

- **sword** — +1 weapon attack rolls.
- **greatsword** — reroll one weapon damage die once per attack.
- **axe** — critical hits inflict **bleeding**.
- **warhammer** — successful hits force a **strength saving throw** or the target is **knocked prone**.
- **spear** — gain **+2 metres** weapon reach.
- **bow** — increased range and ignores **half cover**.
- **arcane shield** — gain **+1 armour** and advantage against being **disarmed**.

the gm may create additional mastery effects for other weapon types.

### lore

within the oldest spellblade orders, rank v is spoken of only in legend. those who achieve the infinite arsenal are said to possess perfect harmony between martial discipline and arcane mastery, creating weapons so flawless that they are often mistaken for relics forged by the gods themselves. every weapon reflects the spellblade's soul, carrying their chosen magical affinity in both form and function.

masters of the infinite arsenal have been witnessed changing weapons in the blink of an eye, effortlessly adapting to every opponent and every battlefield. enemies who prepare to face a swordsman suddenly find themselves duelling a spearman, while heavily armoured champions are met with crushing hammers moments later. to fight such a spellblade is to face every weapon ever mastered by their order.

the infinite arsenal is regarded as the pinnacle of weapon mastery. it teaches that true strength is never found within the weapon itself, but within the warrior capable of creating exactly what is needed at precisely the right moment.

> *"a king commands an army. a master spellblade commands every weapon that army has ever carried."*

> — grand spellblade aetherion lux, first blade of the infinite well

# Arcane Catalyst

## Overview
Arcane Catalyst is one of the most closely guarded techniques of the Spellblade Orders. Rather than drawing mana from within themselves alone, the Spellblade temporarily becomes a living conduit through which the surrounding arcane currents naturally flow. Every spell becomes easier to shape, every weapon strike carries greater magical force, and the connection between blade and mana reaches an extraordinary level of harmony.

As the Catalyst awakens, brilliant streams of arcane energy spiral around the Spellblade, continuously feeding their Arcane Weapon and reinforcing every technique they perform. The air shimmers with unstable magical energy as mana is drawn from the environment itself before being refined into perfectly controlled power.

Unlike Avatar of the Blade, Arcane Catalyst is not about overwhelming strength. It is about absolute efficiency, allowing the Spellblade to accomplish far more with every point of mana they expend.

## Rank 1
### Description

Arcane Catalyst is one of the most closely guarded techniques of the Spellblade Orders. Rather than drawing mana from within themselves alone, the Spellblade temporarily becomes a living conduit through which the surrounding arcane currents naturally flow. Every spell becomes easier to shape, every weapon strike carries greater magical force, and the connection between blade and mana reaches an extraordinary level of harmony.

As the Catalyst awakens, brilliant streams of arcane energy spiral around the Spellblade, continuously feeding their Arcane Weapon and reinforcing every technique they perform. The air shimmers with unstable magical energy as mana is drawn from the environment itself before being refined into perfectly controlled power.

Unlike Avatar of the Blade, Arcane Catalyst is not about overwhelming strength. It is about absolute efficiency, allowing the Spellblade to accomplish far more with every point of mana they expend.

### Effects

Spend **1 Action Point** and **100 MP** to activate **Arcane Catalyst**.

Arcane Catalyst lasts for **5 Turns**.

**1 Use per Long Rest.**

While Arcane Catalyst is active:

- All Spellblade Talent Mana Costs are reduced by **25%** (minimum 1 MP).
- Recover **25 MP** at the start of each of your turns.
- Gain **+2** to Spell Attack Rolls.
- Gain **+2** to Spellblade Save DC.
- Arcane Edge remains active without paying its upkeep cost.
- Arcane Arsenal gains **+1d6** magical damage.
- Arcane Cut deals an additional **1d10** damage.
- Spellbreaker gains **+2** to Spellbreaker Rolls.
- Arcane Dominion restores an additional **10 MP** to allies inside the Dominion.

When Arcane Catalyst ends:

- Gain **Mana Fatigue** until the end of your next turn.
- During Mana Fatigue, your Mana regeneration is reduced by **50%**.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Arcane Catalyst is known as the **Living Conduit**, representing complete mastery over the movement of mana itself. Rather than forcing mana to obey, the Spellblade learns to guide it naturally, allowing arcane energy to pass effortlessly through their body before being shaped into devastating techniques.

Only the greatest masters can maintain this delicate balance. Too little control causes the surrounding mana to disperse harmlessly, while too much force risks catastrophic feedback capable of injuring the Spellblade from within. Those who succeed become living nexuses of magical energy, their presence alone strengthening the flow of mana around them.

Legends speak of masters who fought for hours without exhausting their reserves, each spell flowing into the next with effortless precision. To witness Arcane Catalyst is to see mana itself willingly answer the call of a true Spellblade.

> *"Power is not found in how much mana you possess... but in how perfectly you allow it to flow."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 2
### Description

The Spellblade's understanding of Arcane Catalyst has matured, allowing them to refine the flow of mana with remarkable precision. Every spell, every technique, and every weapon enhancement is executed with minimal waste, enabling the Spellblade to sustain their most demanding abilities for extended periods without exhausting their reserves.

As Arcane Catalyst awakens, streams of magical energy continuously circulate around the Spellblade before flowing back into their body, creating a near-perfect cycle of mana. Their Arcane Weapon shines brighter, their spells become easier to control, and every technique feels lighter to perform. Veteran Spellblades describe the sensation as though the world itself is willingly lending them its mana.

While still requiring tremendous focus, Rank II transforms Arcane Catalyst from a powerful enhancement into a reliable source of sustained magical supremacy, allowing the Spellblade to dominate prolonged engagements where other mages would quickly exhaust themselves.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **90 MP** to activate **Arcane Catalyst**.
- Arcane Catalyst lasts for **6 Turns**.
- **2 Uses per Long Rest.**

While Arcane Catalyst is active:

- All Spellblade Talent Mana Costs are reduced by **35%** (minimum 1 MP).
- Recover **35 MP** at the start of each of your turns.
- Gain **+3** to Spell Attack Rolls.
- Gain **+3** to your Spellblade Save DC.
- Arcane Edge remains active without paying its Mana Cost.
- Arcane Arsenal gains an additional **+1d6** magical damage.
- Arcane Cut deals an additional **2d10** damage.
- Spellbreaker gains **+3** to Spellbreaker Rolls.
- Arcane Dominion restores an additional **15 MP** to allied creatures within its area.
- Mystic Recovery restores **25%** additional HP, SP or MP while Arcane Catalyst is active.

#### Mana Conduit

While Arcane Catalyst is active, whenever you successfully defeat a hostile creature or successfully counter a spell using **Spellbreaker**, immediately recover **15 MP**.

When Arcane Catalyst ends:

- Gain **Mana Fatigue** until the end of your next turn.
- During Mana Fatigue, Mana regeneration is reduced by **50%**.

### Lore

Among the Spellblade Orders, Rank II is known as the **Flowing Conduit**. Masters teach that true magical strength is not measured by the size of one's Mana Pool, but by the efficiency with which every fragment of mana is used. Those who achieve this state appear tireless, maintaining devastating techniques long after other warriors and mages have exhausted themselves.

Veterans often describe the Flowing Conduit as a living river of mana. Every spell cast, every weapon strike, and every technique naturally feeds into the next, creating an endless rhythm that few opponents can withstand. Watching a master fight is like witnessing a current that never stops flowing—relentless, graceful, and impossible to interrupt.

To master Rank II is to learn that the greatest source of power is not limitless mana, but the wisdom to never waste it.

> *"A single drop of mana, perfectly placed, outweighs an ocean cast without purpose."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 3
### Description

Arcane Catalyst has evolved beyond simple efficiency, transforming the Spellblade into a living nexus through which vast currents of mana naturally flow. Every spell cast, every technique performed, and every strike delivered becomes part of an unbroken cycle of arcane energy. Rather than consuming mana alone, the Spellblade continuously refines and recycles it, dramatically reducing waste while empowering every technique.

The Spellblade's chosen magical affinity radiates from their body in waves, surrounding them with an ever-changing aura of concentrated mana. Their Arcane Weapon hums with overwhelming magical power, and even experienced mages can feel the surrounding arcane currents bending toward the Catalyst's presence.

Masters of the Spellblade Orders describe Rank III as the point where a Spellblade no longer forces mana to obey. Instead, mana willingly gathers around them, recognising them as a perfect conduit through which it may safely flow.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **80 MP** to activate **Arcane Catalyst**.
- Arcane Catalyst lasts for **7 Turns**.
- **3 Uses per Long Rest.**

While Arcane Catalyst is active:

- All **Spellblade Talent Mana Costs** are reduced by **50%** (minimum 1 MP).
- Recover **45 MP** at the start of each of your turns.
- Gain **+4** to Spell Attack Rolls.
- Gain **+4** to your Spellblade Save DC.
- Arcane Edge remains active without paying its Mana Cost.
- Arcane Arsenal gains an additional **+2d6** magical damage.
- Arcane Cut deals an additional **2d10** damage.
- Spellbreaker gains **+4** to Spellbreaker Rolls.
- Arcane Dominion restores an additional **20 MP** to allied creatures within its area.
- Mystic Recovery restores **50%** additional HP, SP or MP while Arcane Catalyst is active.

#### Arcane Overflow

Whenever you successfully:

- Defeat a hostile creature,
- Successfully counter a spell using **Spellbreaker**, or
- Restore HP, MP or SP using **Mystic Recovery**,

Immediately recover **25 MP**.

This effect may trigger **once per turn**.

When Arcane Catalyst ends:

- Gain **Mana Fatigue** until the end of your next turn.
- During Mana Fatigue, your natural Mana regeneration is reduced by **50%**, and Spellblade Talents cost **25% more MP**.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank III is known as the **Living Nexus**. Few Spellblades ever achieve this level of mastery, for it requires absolute harmony between body, blade, and mana. Those who succeed become walking centres of magical energy, drawing mana from the world around them and refining it with extraordinary efficiency.

Legends speak of Living Nexus masters continuing to fight long after entire battalions of mages had exhausted their reserves. Every spell seemed to fuel the next, every technique flowed effortlessly into another, and every strike strengthened the Spellblade instead of weakening them. To fight alongside such a master was to witness mana itself choosing its champion.

The Living Nexus is revered as proof that true mastery lies not in possessing limitless power, but in ensuring that no fragment of power is ever wasted.

> *"Mana is never truly spent. The wise simply learn how to make it return."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

Arcane Catalyst has reached a level where the Spellblade no longer relies solely upon the mana within their own body. Instead, they become a living conduit capable of drawing upon the surrounding arcane currents, weaving environmental mana into every strike, spell, and technique. Their presence alone alters the magical landscape, strengthening allies while destabilising hostile magic.

The Spellblade's chosen magical affinity radiates in brilliant waves, surrounding them with an ever-shifting mantle of arcane energy. Every movement leaves shimmering trails of mana behind, and every Spellblade technique flows together without interruption. Even veteran mages can feel the surrounding mana responding instinctively to the Catalyst's presence.

Among the Spellblade Orders, Rank IV is known as the **Grand Catalyst**, a title reserved for those whose mastery allows them to command not only their own mana, but the mana of the battlefield itself.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **70 MP** to activate **Arcane Catalyst**.
- Arcane Catalyst lasts for **8 Turns**.
- **4 Uses per Long Rest.**

While Arcane Catalyst is active:

- All **Spellblade Talent Mana Costs** are reduced by **50%** (minimum 1 MP).
- Recover **60 MP** at the start of each of your turns.
- Gain **+5** to Spell Attack Rolls.
- Gain **+5** to your **Spellblade Save DC**.
- Arcane Edge remains active without paying its Mana Cost.
- Arcane Arsenal gains an additional **+2d6** magical damage.
- Arcane Cut deals an additional **3d10** damage.
- Spellbreaker gains **+5** to Spellbreaker Rolls.
- Arcane Dominion restores an additional **25 MP** to allied creatures within its area.
- Mystic Recovery restores **75%** additional HP, SP or MP while Arcane Catalyst is active.

#### Arcane Convergence

While standing within your **Arcane Dominion**, your first Spellblade Talent used each turn costs **0 MP**.

#### Arcane Overflow

Once per turn, whenever you:

- Defeat a hostile creature.
- Successfully counter a spell with **Spellbreaker**.
- Restore resources using **Mystic Recovery**.

Recover **35 MP** immediately.

#### Mana Mastery

During Arcane Catalyst, your Spellblade Talents cannot suffer **Mana Feedback**, **Spell Feedback**, or similar effects caused by insufficient mana or unstable mana flow.

When Arcane Catalyst ends:

- Gain **Mana Fatigue** until the end of your next turn.
- During Mana Fatigue:
  - Natural Mana regeneration is reduced by **50%**.
  - Spellblade Talents cost **25% more MP**.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank IV is known as the **Grand Catalyst**, a title earned by only a handful of masters throughout history. At this stage, the Spellblade ceases to be merely a wielder of mana and instead becomes one of its greatest conductors. The surrounding magical currents willingly flow towards them, reinforcing every spell and every swing of their weapon.

Ancient accounts describe Grand Catalysts walking through battlefields where allied mages found their spells strengthened simply by fighting nearby, while hostile spellcasters struggled to maintain even the simplest incantations beneath the overwhelming pressure of the Catalyst's presence.

The greatest masters teach that true magical supremacy is not achieved by possessing endless mana, but by ensuring that every fragment of mana serves a purpose.

> *"The greatest conduit is not the one that holds the most power... but the one through which no power is ever wasted."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Catalyst reaches its final evolution, transforming the Spellblade into the ultimate conduit of arcane power. Mana no longer feels like a finite resource but a living force flowing through every movement, every strike and every spell. The Spellblade no longer expends magic inefficiently—instead, they guide it with perfect precision, ensuring every fragment of mana fulfils its purpose before returning to the endless currents of the world.

As the Catalyst reaches its peak, the Spellblade's chosen affinity surrounds them in an overwhelming display of magical energy. Their Arcane Weapon pulses with incredible power, the air hums with condensed mana, and nearby spellcasters instinctively recognise that they stand in the presence of one who has mastered magic itself.

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank V is known as the **Infinite Catalyst**. It is regarded as the highest achievement of magical discipline, proving that limitless power is not created through endless mana, but through flawless control over every drop that is used.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **60 MP** to activate **Arcane Catalyst**.
- Arcane Catalyst lasts for **10 Turns**.
- **5 Uses per Long Rest.**

While Arcane Catalyst is active:

- All **Spellblade Talent Mana Costs** are reduced by **50%** (minimum **1 MP**).
- Recover **75 MP** at the start of each of your turns.
- Gain **+6** to Spell Attack Rolls.
- Gain **+6** to your **Spellblade Save DC**.
- Arcane Edge remains active without paying its Mana Cost.
- Arcane Arsenal gains an additional **+3d6** magical damage.
- Arcane Cut deals an additional **3d10** damage.
- Spellbreaker gains **+6** to Spellbreaker Rolls.
- Arcane Dominion restores an additional **30 MP** to allied creatures within its area.
- Mystic Recovery restores **100%** additional HP, SP or MP while Arcane Catalyst is active.

#### Infinite Catalyst

Once per turn, the **first Spellblade Talent** you activate costs **0 MP**.

If you are standing within your **Arcane Dominion**, the first **two Spellblade Talents** you activate each turn cost **0 MP**.

#### Arcane Overflow

Once per turn, whenever you:

- Defeat a hostile creature.
- Successfully counter a spell using **Spellbreaker**.
- Restore HP, SP or MP using **Mystic Recovery**.

Recover **50 MP**.

Excess Mana restored while Arcane Catalyst is active may temporarily exceed your normal Maximum MP by **20%**. This excess Mana disappears when Arcane Catalyst ends.

#### Mana Mastery

While Arcane Catalyst is active:

- You cannot suffer **Mana Feedback**, **Spell Feedback**, or **Mana Burn** caused by your own Spellblade Talents.
- Your Spellblade Talents cannot have their Mana Costs increased by enemy effects.
- Your Mana cannot be drained by magical effects unless they originate from **Artifact**, **Divine**, or **World Magic**.

When Arcane Catalyst ends:

- Gain **Mana Fatigue** until the end of your next turn.
- During Mana Fatigue:
  - Natural Mana regeneration is reduced by **50%**.
  - Spellblade Talents cost **25%** more MP.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, the Infinite Catalyst is considered the final lesson of magical mastery. It is said that those who reach this state cease to think about mana entirely. Every spell, every technique and every movement becomes instinctive, guided by an understanding so complete that the world's own arcane currents willingly answer their call.

Ancient chronicles describe Infinite Catalysts standing beside exhausted armies of mages, continuing to weave spell after spell while their reserves seemed impossible to deplete. Many believed they possessed limitless mana, yet the truth was far more remarkable—they simply wasted none.

The Infinite Catalyst is not remembered as the Spellblade with the greatest Mana Pool, but as the one who demonstrated that perfect control will always surpass limitless power.

> *"The fool seeks more mana. The master seeks to waste none."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

# arcane catalyst

## overview
arcane catalyst is one of the most closely guarded techniques of the spellblade orders. rather than drawing mana from within themselves alone, the spellblade temporarily becomes a living conduit through which the surrounding arcane currents naturally flow. every spell becomes easier to shape, every weapon strike carries greater magical force, and the connection between blade and mana reaches an extraordinary level of harmony.

as the catalyst awakens, brilliant streams of arcane energy spiral around the spellblade, continuously feeding their arcane weapon and reinforcing every technique they perform. the air shimmers with unstable magical energy as mana is drawn from the environment itself before being refined into perfectly controlled power.

unlike avatar of the blade, arcane catalyst is not about overwhelming strength. it is about absolute efficiency, allowing the spellblade to accomplish far more with every point of mana they expend.

### effects

### lore

within the spellblade orders, arcane catalyst is known as the **living conduit**, representing complete mastery over the movement of mana itself. rather than forcing mana to obey, the spellblade learns to guide it naturally, allowing arcane energy to pass effortlessly through their body before being shaped into devastating techniques.

only the greatest masters can maintain this delicate balance. too little control causes the surrounding mana to disperse harmlessly, while too much force risks catastrophic feedback capable of injuring the spellblade from within. those who succeed become living nexuses of magical energy, their presence alone strengthening the flow of mana around them.

legends speak of masters who fought for hours without exhausting their reserves, each spell flowing into the next with effortless precision. to witness arcane catalyst is to see mana itself willingly answer the call of a true spellblade.

> *"power is not found in how much mana you possess... but in how perfectly you allow it to flow."*

> — grand spellblade aetherion lux, first blade of the infinite well

as arcane catalyst awakens, streams of magical energy continuously circulate around the spellblade before flowing back into their body, creating a near-perfect cycle of mana. their arcane weapon shines brighter, their spells become easier to control, and every technique feels lighter to perform. veteran spellblades describe the sensation as though the world itself is willingly lending them its mana.

# Arcane Cut

## Overview
Arcane Cut is one of the most devastating techniques ever developed by the Spellblade Orders. Rather than empowering the blade itself, the Spellblade channels an immense quantity of mana along the weapon's edge before releasing it in a single overwhelming slash. The stored energy erupts from the blade as a massive crescent of arcane force, carving through the battlefield and striking everything caught within its path.

A Spellblade may unleash Arcane Cut as pure Arcane Mana or shape it into one of their mastered magical affinities. Pure Arcane Cuts are exceptionally stable and devastating against magical constructs, summoned creatures, and enchanted barriers, while elemental Arcane Cuts inherit the properties of their chosen element, allowing the attack to ignite, freeze, shock, or otherwise affect their targets.

Unlike Bladestorm, Arcane Cut is a technique of commitment rather than speed. It requires absolute concentration, physical strength, and precise mana control to release a single strike capable of deciding the outcome of an entire battle.

## Rank 1
### Description

Arcane Cut is one of the most devastating techniques ever developed by the Spellblade Orders. Rather than empowering the blade itself, the Spellblade channels an immense quantity of mana along the weapon's edge before releasing it in a single overwhelming slash. The stored energy erupts from the blade as a massive crescent of arcane force, carving through the battlefield and striking everything caught within its path.

A Spellblade may unleash Arcane Cut as pure Arcane Mana or shape it into one of their mastered magical affinities. Pure Arcane Cuts are exceptionally stable and devastating against magical constructs, summoned creatures, and enchanted barriers, while elemental Arcane Cuts inherit the properties of their chosen element, allowing the attack to ignite, freeze, shock, or otherwise affect their targets.

Unlike Bladestorm, Arcane Cut is a technique of commitment rather than speed. It requires absolute concentration, physical strength, and precise mana control to release a single strike capable of deciding the outcome of an entire battle.

### Effects

- Spend **2 Action Points**, **50 MP**, and **30 SP** to activate **Arcane Cut**.
- Arcane Cut may be used **once per Short Rest**.
- Choose either **Pure Arcane** or one of your known **magical affinities** before releasing the attack.
- Release a **15 metre long, 1 metre wide** wave of mana in a straight line.
- Every creature within the attack's path must make a **Wisdom Saving Throw** against your **Spellblade Save DC**.
- **Failure:** The target suffers your **normal weapon damage** plus an additional **3d10** damage of the chosen damage type.
- **Success:** The target takes **half of all damage**.

#### Arcane Charge

If you do not have **2 available Action Points** during your current turn, you may begin charging Arcane Cut.

- Spend **1 Action Point** to begin charging.
- Your weapon visibly gathers Arcane Mana or your chosen element.
- At the start of your next turn, spend **1 additional Action Point** to immediately release Arcane Cut.
- Mana and Stamina are only spent when the attack is released.

#### Interrupted Charge

If the charge is interrupted before release by being **Disarmed**, **Stunned**, **Unconscious**, your weapon being destroyed or willingly released, or any effect that prevents you from completing the technique:

- Arcane Cut immediately fails.
- The talent use is expended.
- The committed Action Point is lost.
- You lose **50%** of the Mana and Stamina cost as the unstable energy disperses harmlessly.

#### Weapon Conduit

Arcane Cut may only be performed while wielding a melee weapon. The weapon serves as the conduit that shapes and releases the arcane wave. Without it, the technique cannot be completed.

- **Pure Arcane Cuts** are exceptionally effective against magical barriers, magical constructs, summoned creatures, and other magically created objects.
- **Elemental Arcane Cuts** retain the secondary effects of their chosen element where applicable.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Arcane Cut is known as the **First Severance**, the technique that proves a Spellblade's reach extends far beyond the length of their blade. Masters teach that steel is merely the vessel—the true weapon is the mana released from its edge.

Each Spellblade develops a unique Arcane Cut reflecting their magical affinity. Some unleash silent crescents of shimmering mana capable of cleaving enchanted stone, while others release roaring infernos, crashing tides, razor winds, or crackling lightning that embody their elemental mastery. Regardless of its appearance, every Arcane Cut is intended to end the battle with a single perfect strike.

Veterans caution apprentices that the greatest danger is not the attack itself, but the moments spent charging it. An impatient Spellblade releases an incomplete strike. An overconfident one may never release it at all.

> *"Steel begins the cut. Mana carries it. Patience decides whether it reaches its destination."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 2
### Description

The Spellblade has refined Arcane Cut into a far more stable and destructive technique. Greater control over the flow of mana allows the arcane wave to travel farther while maintaining its shape, increasing both its reach and its ability to cleave through multiple opponents. What was once a powerful finishing attack becomes a reliable battlefield technique capable of changing the tide of combat.

As mastery improves, the Spellblade learns to compress mana with even greater precision before its release. Whether formed from pure arcane energy or one of the Spellblade's magical affinities, the resulting wave carries tremendous force as it races across the battlefield, leaving little opportunity for enemies to escape its path.

Despite this growing mastery, Arcane Cut remains a technique demanding patience and commitment. Masters continue to remind their students that every charge leaves them vulnerable, and only those who understand the perfect moment to strike will realise the technique's full potential.

- Release a **20 metre long, 1.5 metre wide** wave of mana in a straight line.
- Every creature within the attack's path must make a **Wisdom Saving Throw** against your **Spellblade Save DC**.
- **Failure:** The target suffers your **normal weapon damage** plus an additional **4d10** damage of the chosen damage type.
- **Success:** The target takes **half of all damage**.

Arcane Cut may only be performed while wielding a melee weapon. The weapon acts as the focus through which the arcane wave is shaped and released.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank II is known as the **Second Severance**, marking the stage where Arcane Cut evolves from a powerful technique into a dependable battlefield weapon. Spellblades no longer struggle to maintain the arcane wave as it leaves their blade, instead shaping it with enough precision to strike distant foes while preserving its destructive power.

Veterans often describe the technique as a lesson in restraint rather than aggression. Charging Arcane Cut teaches patience, awareness, and discipline, for a poorly timed release wastes both energy and opportunity. Those who master Rank II quickly earn a fearsome reputation, as enemies learn that allowing a Spellblade even a brief moment to prepare can have devastating consequences.

> *"Power gathers in silence. The wise recognise the danger before the blade is ever swung."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 3
### Description

Arcane Cut has evolved into a terrifying display of martial and arcane mastery. The Spellblade's command over mana has become so refined that every slash releases an immense wave of compressed energy capable of carving across the battlefield with incredible force. The expanding arc maintains its structure over far greater distances, making escape increasingly difficult for those caught within its path.

At this level, the Spellblade no longer relies solely upon raw power. Every Arcane Cut is carefully prepared, every movement deliberate, and every release perfectly timed. Whether formed from pure Arcane Mana or one of the Spellblade's elemental affinities, the attack becomes a devastating expression of discipline rather than uncontrolled destruction.

Veteran Spellblades teach that Rank III marks the point where Arcane Cut ceases to be simply an attack. It becomes a battlefield technique capable of forcing enemies to reposition, disrupting formations, and punishing those who underestimate the reach of a Spellblade.

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank III is known as the **Battlefield Severance**. It is the point where Arcane Cut becomes feared not for its power alone, but for its ability to reshape the battlefield itself. Entire shield walls have been broken apart by a single perfectly executed strike, forcing enemies to abandon carefully prepared formations.

Masters remind their students that Arcane Cut is never about overwhelming strength. It is about patience, precision, and choosing the exact moment when a single attack will achieve more than a hundred ordinary strikes. Those who master this lesson become warriors capable of ending battles before they truly begin.

To witness a Rank III Arcane Cut is to understand why the Spellblade Orders have long been respected by kings and feared by archmages alike.

> *"A sword may cut a warrior. A perfected Arcane Cut divides the battlefield itself."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

Arcane Cut has become a technique capable of carving through both armies and magic itself. The Spellblade's mastery over mana has reached the point where the arcane wave no longer loses cohesion as it tears across the battlefield. Every slash is compressed into an impossibly dense edge of magical force, capable of cleaving through physical obstacles and lesser magical defences before continuing towards its intended targets.

Whether released as pure Arcane Mana or shaped into one of the Spellblade's elemental affinities, Arcane Cut now carries tremendous destructive force. Entire battle lines have been broken by a single perfectly executed strike, while enemy spellcasters watch their magical barriers split apart beneath the weight of the attack.

Only the greatest Spellblades can safely wield Arcane Cut at this level. The amount of mana compressed into the blade is immense, and even the slightest lapse in concentration can cause the technique to collapse before it is released.

### Effects

- Spend **2 Action Points**, **35 MP**, and **25 SP** to activate **Arcane Cut**.
- Arcane Cut may be used **4 times per Short Rest**.
- Choose either **Pure Arcane** or one of your known **magical affinities** before releasing the attack.
- Release a **30 metre long, 2.5 metre wide** wave of mana in a straight line.
- Every creature within the attack's path must make a **Wisdom Saving Throw** against your **Spellblade Save DC**.
- **Failure:** The creature suffers your **normal weapon damage** plus an additional **6d10** damage matching the chosen damage type.
- **Success:** The creature takes **half of all damage**.

#### Arcane Charge

If you do not have **2 available Action Points** during your current turn, you may begin charging Arcane Cut.

- Spend **1 Action Point** to begin charging.
- Your weapon gathers Arcane Mana or your chosen magical affinity.
- At the start of your next turn, spend **1 additional Action Point** to release Arcane Cut.
- Mana and Stamina are only spent when the attack is successfully released.

#### Interrupted Charge

If the charge is interrupted by becoming **Disarmed**, **Stunned**, **Unconscious**, your weapon being destroyed or willingly released, or any effect preventing the technique from being completed:

- Arcane Cut immediately fails.
- One use of Arcane Cut is expended.
- The committed Action Point is lost.
- You lose **50%** of the Mana and Stamina cost as the unstable mana disperses harmlessly.

#### Weapon Conduit

Arcane Cut may only be performed while wielding a melee weapon. The weapon serves as the focus that shapes and releases the arcane wave.

- **Elemental Arcane Cuts** deal damage matching the chosen affinity and apply the secondary effects of that element where applicable.
- Arcane Cut ignores **Half Cover** and **Three-Quarters Cover**.

At this level, Arcane Cut is no longer feared solely for its destructive power, but for its ability to shatter carefully prepared defences. Shield walls, fortified positions, and lesser magical wards offer little protection against a perfectly executed strike.

Veteran masters teach that Rank IV demands absolute patience. The immense concentration of mana required to sustain the attack pushes both body and weapon to their limits, and many promising Spellblades have lost control by attempting to release the technique too early.

Those who master the Grand Severance are spoken of with equal parts admiration and caution, for every witness understands that a single swing of their blade can alter the course of an entire battle.

> *"When steel, mana and purpose become one, even the strongest walls forget they were ever meant to stand."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

# Arcane Dominion

## Overview
Arcane Dominion is one of the highest disciplines practiced by the Spellblade Orders, allowing the Spellblade to claim a portion of the battlefield as their own. By plunging their weapon into the ground or focusing its point before them, they release a surge of arcane energy that spreads across the surrounding area, creating a Dominion where the natural flow of mana bends to their will.

Within this territory, the Spellblade's mastery over both swordsmanship and magic reaches its peak. Mana answers their commands more readily, while hostile spellcasters find their own magic becoming unstable and increasingly difficult to control. Every movement, every spell, and every strike is influenced by the Dominion's overwhelming arcane pressure.

Although incredibly powerful, maintaining a Dominion demands immense concentration and a tremendous amount of mana. Masters teach that the ability should only be invoked when the outcome of a battle hangs in the balance.

Those who witness the technique often describe the air itself changing. Arcane runes shimmer across the ground, the atmosphere vibrates with restrained magical energy, and even seasoned spellcasters find their magic becoming sluggish beneath the Dominion's oppressive influence.

Veterans teach that a true Spellblade never seeks to control the entire battlefield. Instead, they create a single place where victory becomes inevitable.

> *"Do not chase the battle. Make the battle come to you."*

## Rank 2
### Description

The Spellblade's understanding of Arcane Dominion has deepened, allowing them to establish a larger and more stable zone of arcane influence. Rather than simply empowering themselves, the Spellblade begins manipulating the very flow of mana across the battlefield, creating an area where allies flourish and enemy spellcasters struggle to maintain control.

Experienced Spellblades no longer create their Dominion beneath their own feet. Instead, they project it onto the battlefield, placing it exactly where it will have the greatest tactical impact. Whether protecting allies, controlling an objective, or denying enemy mages access to stable mana, every Dominion becomes a carefully planned extension of the Spellblade's strategy.

Veterans often describe Arcane Dominion as an invisible fortress. While walls cannot be seen, every creature entering the area immediately feels the overwhelming presence of disciplined arcane energy pressing against them.

# arcane dominion

## overview
arcane dominion is one of the highest disciplines practiced by the spellblade orders, allowing the spellblade to claim a portion of the battlefield as their own. by plunging their weapon into the ground or focusing its point before them, they release a surge of arcane energy that spreads across the surrounding area, creating a dominion where the natural flow of mana bends to their will.

within this territory, the spellblade's mastery over both swordsmanship and magic reaches its peak. mana answers their commands more readily, while hostile spellcasters find their own magic becoming unstable and increasingly difficult to control. every movement, every spell, and every strike is influenced by the dominion's overwhelming arcane pressure.

although incredibly powerful, maintaining a dominion demands immense concentration and a tremendous amount of mana. masters teach that the ability should only be invoked when the outcome of a battle hangs in the balance.

# Arcane Echo

## Overview
A Spellblade's mastery extends beyond blades and spells. Through careful manipulation of arcane energy, they learn to leave behind fragments of their presence, creating convincing images that linger within the world.

These manifestations, known as Arcane Echoes, are not living beings, summoned creatures, or independent entities. They are reflections of the Spellblade's arcane signature given temporary form. To an observer, the Echo appears identical to its creator, standing motionless as though waiting for the perfect moment to act.

At Rank 1, the Echo lacks intelligence, movement, and substance. It cannot attack, speak, cast spells, or interact with the world. Its purpose is deception. Whether used to distract enemies, conceal the Spellblade's true position, or create uncertainty during an encounter, the Echo forces opponents to question what they are seeing.

Many Spellblades consider Arcane Echo one of the most valuable tactical abilities available to them. A well-placed illusion can create opportunities that brute force never could.

## Rank 1
### Description

A Spellblade's mastery extends beyond blades and spells. Through careful manipulation of arcane energy, they learn to leave behind fragments of their presence, creating convincing images that linger within the world.

These manifestations, known as Arcane Echoes, are not living beings, summoned creatures, or independent entities. They are reflections of the Spellblade's arcane signature given temporary form. To an observer, the Echo appears identical to its creator, standing motionless as though waiting for the perfect moment to act.

At Rank 1, the Echo lacks intelligence, movement, and substance. It cannot attack, speak, cast spells, or interact with the world. Its purpose is deception. Whether used to distract enemies, conceal the Spellblade's true position, or create uncertainty during an encounter, the Echo forces opponents to question what they are seeing.

Many Spellblades consider Arcane Echo one of the most valuable tactical abilities available to them. A well-placed illusion can create opportunities that brute force never could.

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to create an Arcane Echo.
- The Echo appears within **5 metres** of the Spellblade.
- The Echo remains for **1 minute** or until destroyed.
- Only **one Arcane Echo** may exist at a time.

#### Arcane Echo Properties

The Echo:

- Appears visually identical to the Spellblade.
- Occupies a physical space.
- Remains completely stationary.
- Cannot move.
- Cannot attack.
- Cannot cast abilities.
- Cannot speak.
- Cannot interact with objects.
- Does not provide flanking bonuses.
- Does not block movement.

#### Investigation

A creature that suspects the Echo is not real may use an:

- Investigation Check
- Arcana Check

The creature must bet a DC10

On a success:
- The creature identifies the Echo as an illusion.

On a failure:
- The creature believes the Echo is genuine.

#### Destruction

The Arcane Echo immediately disappears if:

- It is successfully struck by an attack.
- The Spellblade dismisses it.
- The duration expires.
- The Spellblade is reduced to 0 HP.

#### Restrictions

- Maximum of one Echo active at a time.
- The Echo cannot move.
- The Echo cannot perform actions.
- The Echo cannot activate abilities.
- The Echo provides no direct offensive benefits.
- The Echo is clearly magical when physically interacted with.

### Lore

Among the oldest Spellblade traditions, Arcane Echo was originally developed as a dueling technique. Practitioners sought methods of confusing opponents without relying on brute force or overwhelming magical power.

The first Echoes were crude and unstable, often flickering in and out of existence. Over generations, Spellblades refined the technique until their illusions became nearly indistinguishable from the real practitioner at a glance.

Many instructors teach that Arcane Echo embodies an important lesson: victory does not always belong to the strongest combatant. Sometimes it belongs to the one who controls what their opponent believes.

Veteran Spellblades often claim that the greatest strength of an Echo is not convincing an enemy that it is real. It is making them doubt whether anything they see can be trusted.

> "A sword threatens the body. Uncertainty threatens the mind."
>
> — Master Illarian Voss, Keeper of the Mirror Hall

## Rank 2
### Description

As the Spellblade's understanding of illusion and arcane projection improves, their Arcane Echo becomes more stable and convincing. The image no longer flickers as easily, allowing it to remain present for extended periods and over greater distances.

The Echo remains incapable of movement or independent action, but the quality of the illusion improves considerably. Fine details such as armour, clothing, weapons, and posture are replicated with greater accuracy, making it more difficult for observers to immediately identify the deception.

Experienced Spellblades often use Arcane Echo as a scouting aid, distraction, or means of controlling the battlefield. An enemy forced to question what they are seeing is already at a disadvantage.

While still a simple projection, the Echo begins to feel less like a magical construct and more like a genuine reflection of the Spellblade's presence.

### Effects

- Spend **25 MP** to create an Arcane Echo.
- The Echo appears within **10 metres** of the Spellblade.
- The Echo remains for **5 minutes** or until destroyed.
- Only **one Arcane Echo** may exist at a time.

#### Arcane Echo Properties

The Echo:

- Appears visually identical to the Spellblade.
- Occupies a physical space.
- Remains completely stationary.
- Cannot move.
- Cannot attack.
- Cannot cast abilities.
- Cannot speak.
- Cannot interact with objects.
- Does not provide flanking bonuses.
- Does not block movement.

#### Improved Illusion

The Arcane Echo now reproduces:

- Current equipment.
- Current weapon.
- Current armour.
- Current stance and posture.

Observers see the Echo exactly as the Spellblade appeared when the Echo was created.

#### Investigation

A creature that suspects the Echo is not real may use an:

- Investigation Check
- Arcana Check

The creature must beat a **DC 12**.

On a success:

- The creature identifies the Echo as an illusion.

On a failure:

- The creature believes the Echo is genuine.

#### Destruction

The Arcane Echo immediately disappears if:

- It is successfully struck by an attack.
- The Spellblade dismisses it.
- The duration expires.
- The Spellblade is reduced to 0 HP.

#### Restrictions

- Maximum of one Echo active at a time.
- The Echo cannot move.
- The Echo cannot perform actions.
- The Echo cannot activate abilities.
- The Echo provides no direct offensive benefits.
- The Echo is clearly magical when physically interacted with.

### Lore

Among Spellblade academies, Rank II is often referred to as the Stage of Refinement. At this point, the Echo becomes convincing enough that even experienced combatants may hesitate before dismissing it as a simple illusion.

The greatest strength of Arcane Echo has never been the illusion itself. It is the uncertainty it creates. A moment of hesitation can be worth more than any blade strike, and many Spellblades have secured victory through deception rather than force.

Records from the Mirror Hall tell of duelists who won entire tournaments without ever striking first, relying instead on confusion, misdirection, and flawless positioning. Their Echoes forced opponents to second-guess every decision they made.

A wise Spellblade understands that battles are fought in both the mind and the body. Arcane Echo targets the former long before the latter.

> "When your enemy doubts their own eyes, the battle is already half won."
>
> — Master Illarian Voss, Keeper of the Mirror Hall

## Rank 3
### Description

The Spellblade's Arcane Echo evolves beyond a simple stationary illusion. Through greater control over mana and projection, the Echo can now imitate basic movement, making it significantly more difficult to distinguish from the real Spellblade at a glance.

The movement is limited and lacks true intelligence. The Echo cannot make decisions, engage in combat, or interact with the world around it. Instead, it follows simple commands issued by its creator, moving in a deliberate and predictable manner.

For the first time, the Arcane Echo begins to create genuine uncertainty on the battlefield. Enemies can no longer rely on the Echo remaining where it was created, forcing them to spend precious moments determining which Spellblade is real.

Many veteran Spellblades consider this the point where Arcane Echo becomes a true battlefield deception technique rather than a simple distraction.

### Effects

- Spend **30 MP** to create an Arcane Echo.
- The Echo appears within **15 metres** of the Spellblade.
- The Echo remains for **10 minutes** or until destroyed.
- Only **one Arcane Echo** may exist at a time.

#### Arcane Echo Properties

The Echo:

- Appears visually identical to the Spellblade.
- Occupies a physical space.
- Can move up to **3 metres per turn**.
- Cannot attack.
- Cannot cast abilities.
- Cannot speak.
- Cannot interact with objects.
- Does not provide flanking bonuses.
- Does not block movement.

#### Controlled Movement

The Spellblade may direct the Echo to:

- Walk.
- Turn.
- Change facing.
- Follow simple movement paths.

The Echo cannot:

- Run.
- Jump.
- Climb.
- Use talents.
- Mimic combat actions.

#### Improved Illusion

The Arcane Echo now reproduces:

- Current equipment.
- Current weapon.
- Current armour.
- Current stance and posture.
- Basic walking movements.

Observers see the Echo exactly as the Spellblade appeared when the Echo was created.

#### Investigation

A creature that suspects the Echo is not real may use an:

- Investigation Check
- Arcana Check

The creature must beat a **DC 14**.

On a success:

- The creature identifies the Echo as an illusion.

On a failure:

- The creature believes the Echo is genuine.

#### Destruction

The Arcane Echo immediately disappears if:

- It is successfully struck by an attack.
- The Spellblade dismisses it.
- The duration expires.
- The Spellblade is reduced to 0 HP.

#### Restrictions

- Maximum of one Echo active at a time.
- The Echo cannot perform actions.
- The Echo cannot activate abilities.
- The Echo cannot attack.
- The Echo provides no direct offensive benefits.
- The Echo is clearly magical when physically interacted with.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade traditions, Rank III is known as the Stage of Motion. It represents the point where an Echo ceases to be a simple image and begins to imitate life itself.

Many apprentices are surprised to learn that movement is often more convincing than appearance. A perfectly crafted illusion that never moves quickly becomes suspicious, while even a simple projection can appear genuine when it behaves naturally.

Historical accounts tell of Spellblades using moving Echoes to lure enemies into traps, distract guards, and create confusion during battles. Entire skirmishes have been decided by opponents chasing a false target while the real Spellblade positioned themselves elsewhere.

Masters of Arcane Echo often remind their students that deception is not about creating a perfect lie. It is about creating enough doubt that the truth becomes difficult to see.

> "The eye sees what it expects to see. A moving shadow is often enough."
>
> — Master Illarian Voss, Keeper of the Mirror Hall

## Rank 4
### Description

The Spellblade's mastery of Arcane Echo reaches a level where a single illusion is no longer sufficient. Through refined control over their mana, they learn to divide their arcane signature between multiple projections, creating a web of uncertainty across the battlefield.

Each Echo remains a construct of mana rather than a true duplicate, yet the presence of multiple projections dramatically increases the difficulty of identifying the real Spellblade. Enemies can no longer focus on a single target, forcing them to question every movement and every decision.

The Echoes are still limited in their capabilities, unable to fight or cast spells, but their ability to move independently creates a powerful tool for deception, scouting, distraction, and battlefield manipulation.

Among veteran Spellblades, Rank IV is often considered the point where Arcane Echo becomes genuinely dangerous. Not because the Echoes can harm an opponent, but because they make mistakes far more likely.

### Effects

- Spend **35 MP** to create Arcane Echoes.
- Create up to **2 Arcane Echoes** within **20 metres** of the Spellblade.
- The Echoes remain for **15 minutes** or until destroyed.
- Both Echoes may exist simultaneously.

#### Arcane Echo Properties

Each Echo:

- Appears visually identical to the Spellblade.
- Occupies a physical space.
- Can move up to **5 metres per turn**.
- Cannot attack.
- Cannot cast abilities.
- Cannot speak.
- Cannot interact with objects.
- Does not provide flanking bonuses.
- Does not block movement.

#### Independent Movement

The Spellblade may direct each Echo individually.

Each Echo may:

- Walk.
- Turn.
- Change facing.
- Follow simple movement paths.
- Move in different directions from other Echoes.

The Echoes cannot:

- Run.
- Jump.
- Climb.
- Use talents.
- Mimic combat actions.

#### Advanced Illusion

The Echoes now reproduce:

- Current equipment.
- Current weapon.
- Current armour.
- Current stance and posture.
- Basic walking movements.
- Minor idle movements such as shifting weight, looking around, and adjusting stance.

#### Investigation

A creature that suspects an Echo is not real may use an:

- Investigation Check
- Arcana Check

The creature must beat a **DC 16**.

On a success:

- The creature identifies the Echo as an illusion.

On a failure:

- The creature believes the Echo is genuine.

A creature must investigate each Echo separately.

#### Destruction

An Arcane Echo immediately disappears if:

- It is successfully struck by an attack.
- The Spellblade dismisses it.
- The duration expires.
- The Spellblade is reduced to 0 HP.

#### Restrictions

- Maximum of two Echoes active at a time.
- Echoes cannot perform actions.
- Echoes cannot activate abilities.
- Echoes cannot attack.
- Echoes provide no direct offensive benefits.
- Echoes are clearly magical when physically interacted with.

### Lore

Rank IV is often referred to as the Stage of Multiplicity within the Mirror Hall traditions. The Spellblade learns that confusion does not come from creating a perfect illusion—it comes from creating too many possibilities.

Military records contain numerous accounts of enemy formations wasting valuable time and resources attempting to identify the true Spellblade among multiple projections. Some commanders even ordered volleys of arrows directed at every visible target, only to discover they had spent precious resources attacking illusions.

Masters of Arcane Echo often teach that deception is strongest when certainty becomes impossible. When an opponent can no longer trust their own eyes, every decision becomes slower, every action becomes hesitant, and every mistake becomes more likely.

To a skilled Spellblade, uncertainty is a weapon as sharp as any blade.

> "One illusion creates doubt. Two create confusion. Beyond that, the enemy defeats themselves."
>
> — Master Illarian Voss, Keeper of the Mirror Hall

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Echo reaches its ultimate form, allowing the Spellblade to create projections so convincing that even experienced warriors struggle to distinguish illusion from reality. The Echoes no longer merely stand or move—they imitate the behaviour of their creator with startling accuracy.

Through exceptional control over mana, the Spellblade can command their Echoes to mimic simple combat actions, gestures, and movements. Though still incapable of causing harm, these projections create uncertainty on a scale that few opponents are prepared to face.

Enemies attempting to identify the real Spellblade must now contend with multiple moving targets, each behaving as though it could be genuine. Every hesitation creates an opportunity, and every mistake can shift the outcome of a battle.

Among the ancient Spellblade Orders, Rank V is known as the Stage of Mirrors. It is said that a master of Arcane Echo never enters a battle alone, for every reflection of their presence becomes another threat their enemies must account for.

### Effects

- Spend **40 MP** to create Arcane Echoes.
- Create up to **3 Arcane Echoes** within **25 metres** of the Spellblade.
- The Echoes remain for **30 minutes** or until destroyed.
- All three Echoes may exist simultaneously.

#### Arcane Echo Properties

Each Echo:

- Appears visually identical to the Spellblade.
- Occupies a physical space.
- Can move up to **6 metres per turn**.
- Cannot deal damage.
- Cannot cast abilities.
- Cannot interact with objects.
- Does not provide flanking bonuses.
- Does not block movement.

#### Advanced Mimicry

The Echoes may perform:

- Walking.
- Running.
- Turning.
- Drawing or sheathing weapons.
- Combat stances.
- Practice swings.
- Defensive postures.
- Pointing and gesturing.

The Echoes cannot:

- Deal damage.
- Cast spells.
- Activate talents.
- Speak.
- Physically interact with creatures or objects.

#### Masterful Illusion

The Echoes now reproduce:

- Current equipment.
- Current weapon.
- Current armour.
- Current stance and posture.
- Movement patterns.
- Combat motions.
- Basic behavioural mannerisms.

To casual observation, the Echoes are nearly indistinguishable from the real Spellblade.

#### Investigation

A creature that suspects an Echo is not real may use an:

- Investigation Check
- Arcana Check

The creature must beat a **DC 18**.

On a success:

- The creature identifies the Echo as an illusion.

On a failure:

- The creature believes the Echo is genuine.

A creature must investigate each Echo separately.

#### Destruction

An Arcane Echo immediately disappears if:

- It is successfully struck by an attack.
- The Spellblade dismisses it.
- The duration expires.
- The Spellblade is reduced to 0 HP.

#### Restrictions

- Maximum of three Echoes active at a time.
- Echoes cannot deal damage.
- Echoes cannot activate abilities.
- Echoes cannot cast spells.
- Echoes provide no direct offensive benefits.
- Echoes are clearly magical when physically interacted with.

### Lore

The greatest masters of Arcane Echo are remembered throughout Asteria as impossible opponents to track. Witnesses often described battles where multiple Spellblades appeared to be fighting at once, each moving with such confidence that identifying the real combatant became nearly impossible.

Legends tell of duelists who defeated stronger opponents through deception alone, exhausting their enemies as they chased illusions while the true Spellblade waited for the perfect opportunity to strike. Whether these stories are exaggerated or entirely truthful remains a matter of debate.

Within the Mirror Hall, Rank V is regarded as the pinnacle of illusionary combat. Students who achieve this level are taught that the purpose of Arcane Echo is not to create falsehoods, but to create uncertainty. When certainty disappears, mistakes follow.

A master Spellblade understands that a blade can wound the body, but doubt can unravel an entire battle.

> "The enemy sees four Spellblades. The wise enemy asks which one is real. The fool attacks the first one they see."
>
> — Master Illarian Voss, Keeper of the Mirror Hallv

historical accounts tell of spellblades using moving echoes to lure enemies into traps, distract guards, and create confusion during battles. entire skirmishes have been decided by opponents chasing a false target while the real spellblade positioned themselves elsewhere.

masters of arcane echo often remind their students that deception is not about creating a perfect lie. it is about creating enough doubt that the truth becomes difficult to see.

> "the eye sees what it expects to see. a moving shadow is often enough."
>
> — master illarian voss, keeper of the mirror hall

## rank 4
### description

the spellblade's mastery of arcane echo reaches a level where a single illusion is no longer sufficient. through refined control over their mana, they learn to divide their arcane signature between multiple projections, creating a web of uncertainty across the battlefield.

each echo remains a construct of mana rather than a true duplicate, yet the presence of multiple projections dramatically increases the difficulty of identifying the real spellblade. enemies can no longer focus on a single target, forcing them to question every movement and every decision.

the echoes are still limited in their capabilities, unable to fight or cast spells, but their ability to move independently creates a powerful tool for deception, scouting, distraction, and battlefield manipulation.

among veteran spellblades, rank iv is often considered the point where arcane echo becomes genuinely dangerous. not because the echoes can harm an opponent, but because they make mistakes far more likely.

### effects

- spend **35 mp** to create arcane echoes.
- create up to **2 arcane echoes** within **20 metres** of the spellblade.
- the echoes remain for **15 minutes** or until destroyed.
- both echoes may exist simultaneously.

#### arcane echo properties

each echo:

- appears visually identical to the spellblade.
- occupies a physical space.
- can move up to **5 metres per turn**.
- cannot attack.
- cannot cast abilities.
- cannot speak.
- cannot interact with objects.
- does not provide flanking bonuses.
- does not block movement.

#### independent movement

the spellblade may direct each echo individually.

each echo may:

- walk.
- turn.
- change facing.
- follow simple movement paths.
- move in different directions from other echoes.

the echoes cannot:

- run.
- jump.
- climb.
- use talents.
- mimic combat actions.

#### advanced illusion

the echoes now reproduce:

- current equipment.
- current weapon.
- current armour.
- current stance and posture.
- basic walking movements.
- minor idle movements such as shifting weight, looking around, and adjusting stance.

#### investigation

a creature that suspects an echo is not real may use an:

- investigation check
- arcana check

the creature must beat a **dc 16**.

on a success:

- the creature identifies the echo as an illusion.

on a failure:

- the creature believes the echo is genuine.

a creature must investigate each echo separately.

#### destruction

an arcane echo immediately disappears if:

- it is successfully struck by an attack.
- the spellblade dismisses it.
- the duration expires.
- the spellblade is reduced to 0 hp.

#### restrictions

- maximum of two echoes active at a time.
- echoes cannot perform actions.
- echoes cannot activate abilities.
- echoes cannot attack.
- echoes provide no direct offensive benefits.
- echoes are clearly magical when physically interacted with.

### lore

rank iv is often referred to as the stage of multiplicity within the mirror hall traditions. the spellblade learns that confusion does not come from creating a perfect illusion—it comes from creating too many possibilities.

military records contain numerous accounts of enemy formations wasting valuable time and resources attempting to identify the true spellblade among multiple projections. some commanders even ordered volleys of arrows directed at every visible target, only to discover they had spent precious resources attacking illusions.

masters of arcane echo often teach that deception is strongest when certainty becomes impossible. when an opponent can no longer trust their own eyes, every decision becomes slower, every action becomes hesitant, and every mistake becomes more likely.

to a skilled spellblade, uncertainty is a weapon as sharp as any blade.

> "one illusion creates doubt. two create confusion. beyond that, the enemy defeats themselves."
>
> — master illarian voss, keeper of the mirror hall

## rank 5
### description

arcane echo reaches its ultimate form, allowing the spellblade to create projections so convincing that even experienced warriors struggle to distinguish illusion from reality. the echoes no longer merely stand or move—they imitate the behaviour of their creator with startling accuracy.

through exceptional control over mana, the spellblade can command their echoes to mimic simple combat actions, gestures, and movements. though still incapable of causing harm, these projections create uncertainty on a scale that few opponents are prepared to face.

enemies attempting to identify the real spellblade must now contend with multiple moving targets, each behaving as though it could be genuine. every hesitation creates an opportunity, and every mistake can shift the outcome of a battle.

among the ancient spellblade orders, rank v is known as the stage of mirrors. it is said that a master of arcane echo never enters a battle alone, for every reflection of their presence becomes another threat their enemies must account for.

### effects

- spend **40 mp** to create arcane echoes.
- create up to **3 arcane echoes** within **25 metres** of the spellblade.
- the echoes remain for **30 minutes** or until destroyed.
- all three echoes may exist simultaneously.

#### arcane echo properties

- occupies a physical space.

#### advanced mimicry

- walking.
- running.
- turning.

- combat stances.
- practice swings.
- defensive postures.
- pointing and gesturing.

the echoes cannot:

### lore

the greatest masters of arcane echo are remembered throughout asteria as impossible opponents to track. witnesses often described battles where multiple spellblades appeared to be fighting at once, each moving with such confidence that identifying the real combatant became nearly impossible.

legends tell of duelists who defeated stronger opponents through deception alone, exhausting their enemies as they chased illusions while the true spellblade waited for the perfect opportunity to strike. whether these stories are exaggerated or entirely truthful remains a matter of debate.

within the mirror hall, rank v is regarded as the pinnacle of illusionary combat. students who achieve this level are taught that the purpose of arcane echo is not to create falsehoods, but to create uncertainty. when certainty disappears, mistakes follow.

a master spellblade understands that a blade can wound the body, but doubt can unravel an entire battle.

> "the enemy sees four spellblades. the wise enemy asks which one is real. the fool attacks the first one they see."
>
> — master illarian voss, keeper of the mirror hallv
