# Arcane Edge

## Overview
The defining trait of every Spellblade is the ability to merge martial skill with arcane power. Rather than casting magic separately from combat, they learn to channel mana directly through their weapon, temporarily transforming it into a conduit of raw magical energy.

When Arcane Edge is activated, mana flows from the Spellblade's core into the weapon, causing its edge to shimmer with arcane light. Every strike delivered while the enchantment is active carries a pulse of magical force, allowing the Spellblade to inflict wounds that ordinary steel alone could never achieve.

At Rank I, maintaining this enchantment is physically and mentally demanding, limiting how long the weapon can remain empowered. Even so, mastering this technique marks the first true step towards becoming a Spellblade, teaching that the greatest weapon is one where steel and mana strike together as one.

## Rank 1
### Description

The defining trait of every Spellblade is the ability to merge martial skill with arcane power. Rather than casting magic separately from combat, they learn to channel mana directly through their weapon, temporarily transforming it into a conduit of raw magical energy.

When Arcane Edge is activated, mana flows from the Spellblade's core into the weapon, causing its edge to shimmer with arcane light. Every strike delivered while the enchantment is active carries a pulse of magical force, allowing the Spellblade to inflict wounds that ordinary steel alone could never achieve.

At Rank I, maintaining this enchantment is physically and mentally demanding, limiting how long the weapon can remain empowered. Even so, mastering this technique marks the first true step towards becoming a Spellblade, teaching that the greatest weapon is one where steel and mana strike together as one.

### Effects

- Spend **15 MP** to activate **Arcane Edge**.
- Arcane Edge remains active for **2 Turns**.
- While active, your melee weapon deals an additional **1d4 Arcane Damage** on each successful hit.
- The weapon emits a visible arcane glow while Arcane Edge is active.
- Requires a melee weapon to activate. This talent does not affect ranged weapons.
- Arcane Edge ends immediately if you are no longer wielding the infused weapon.
- Arcane Edge cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

Arcane Edge is one of the oldest techniques preserved within the Spellblade Orders. Before learning advanced combat magic, every apprentice is taught that a weapon should become an extension of their mana, not merely a piece of sharpened steel.

The earliest practitioners discovered that even a simple infusion of mana dramatically increased the lethality of a weapon without requiring complex enchantments. Although temporary, this technique proved invaluable in battle, allowing Spellblades to adapt instantly to changing situations without relying upon permanently enchanted arms.

To this day, many masters consider Arcane Edge the moment an apprentice truly earns the title of Spellblade, for it is the first time they successfully unite steel and sorcery into a single weapon.

> *"A blade without mana is only steel. A blade with mana carries the will of its master."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 2
### Description

As the Spellblade's control over mana improves, so too does their ability to sustain an arcane enchantment upon their weapon. Rather than releasing short bursts of unstable energy, the Spellblade learns to maintain a steadier flow of mana, strengthening both the duration and potency of Arcane Edge.

The weapon's aura burns brighter and the magical energy coursing through its edge becomes more refined. Each successful strike releases a greater surge of arcane power, allowing the Spellblade to carve through both physical armour and magical defences with increasing efficiency.

Rank II represents the first significant refinement of Arcane Edge. The enchantment lasts longer, strikes harder, and requires greater discipline to maintain. Veteran Spellblades often encourage apprentices to master this rank before pursuing more advanced offensive techniques, as a stable Arcane Edge forms the foundation of nearly every magical weapon art practiced within the Order.

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to activate **Arcane Edge**.
- Arcane Edge remains active for **3 Turns**.
- While active, your melee weapon deals an additional **1d6 Arcane Damage** on each successful hit.
- The weapon emits a visible arcane glow while Arcane Edge is active.
- Requires a melee weapon to activate. This talent does not affect ranged weapons.
- Arcane Edge ends immediately if you are no longer wielding the infused weapon.
- Arcane Edge cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

Spellblade historians often refer to Rank II as the stage where mana and steel begin to trust one another. The unstable surges experienced by novices become controlled currents, allowing the weapon to channel greater power without risking the integrity of the blade.

Many ancient duelling schools considered mastery of this rank a rite of passage. Only once a Spellblade could reliably maintain Arcane Edge throughout an entire duel were they permitted to study the more advanced techniques of their Order.

Although stronger enchantments await those who continue their training, Rank II is where Arcane Edge first begins to resemble the legendary weapon enchantment that made the Spellblade Orders famous across Asteria.

> *"Power without control burns the blade. Control allows the blade to burn the world."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 3
### Description

With greater experience, the Spellblade no longer struggles to contain the immense flow of mana coursing through their weapon. Arcane Edge becomes a stable combat enchantment, allowing the Spellblade to maintain overwhelming magical pressure throughout prolonged engagements.

When activated, the weapon radiates a vibrant arcane aura as streams of mana race across its surface. Every strike lands with both physical force and concentrated magical energy, making each blow increasingly difficult to defend against. The weapon itself feels lighter in the Spellblade's hands, as if recognising the mana flowing through it and responding as a natural extension of its wielder.

Rank III is often regarded as the point where Arcane Edge becomes a signature combat technique rather than a simple enhancement. Spellblades capable of maintaining this level of enchantment are recognised as experienced warriors whose mastery of blade and mana has become second nature.

### Effects

- Spend **25 MP** to activate **Arcane Edge**.
- Arcane Edge remains active for **3 Turns**.
- While active, your melee weapon deals an additional **1d8 Arcane Damage** on each successful hit.
- The weapon emits a visible arcane glow while Arcane Edge is active.
- Requires a melee weapon to activate. This talent does not affect ranged weapons.
- Arcane Edge ends immediately if you are no longer wielding the infused weapon.
- Arcane Edge cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

Among the Spellblade Orders, Rank III is known as the **Awakened Edge**. It is the stage where apprentices cease relying on conscious effort to maintain the enchantment, allowing mana to flow naturally between themselves and their weapon.

Many renowned Spellblades have described this experience as hearing the blade "sing" for the first time. Whether this is merely poetic tradition or evidence of a deeper bond between mana and steel remains a topic of debate among arcane scholars.

Regardless of the explanation, every master agrees on one truth: once a Spellblade reaches this stage, their weapon is no longer simply carried into battle—it becomes an extension of their own soul.

> *"When your blade begins to answer your mana without hesitation, you no longer wield a weapon—you wield yourself."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

The Spellblade has mastered the art of maintaining an Arcane Edge through even the fiercest battles. Mana now flows effortlessly from their core into their weapon, creating a stable enchantment that burns with immense arcane power. The weapon hums with energy, its edge glowing brightly as each strike releases concentrated bursts of magic.

Unlike earlier ranks, maintaining the enchantment no longer demands complete focus. The Spellblade has learned to weave mana into every movement, allowing them to fight naturally while their weapon remains empowered. Every swing reinforces the harmony between blade and magic, making the Spellblade an increasingly dangerous opponent in prolonged combat.

Rank IV is regarded as the hallmark of veteran Spellblades. The enchantment is no longer an experimental technique but a reliable extension of their combat style, capable of carrying them through the most demanding encounters. Few warriors can withstand a sustained assault from a Spellblade whose Arcane Edge has reached this level of refinement.

### Effects

- Spend **30 MP** to activate **Arcane Edge**.
- Arcane Edge remains active for **4 Turns**.
- While active, your melee weapon deals an additional **1d10 Arcane Damage** on each successful hit.
- The weapon emits a visible arcane glow while Arcane Edge is active.
- Requires a melee weapon to activate. This talent does not affect ranged weapons.
- Arcane Edge ends immediately if you are no longer wielding the infused weapon.
- Arcane Edge cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank IV is known as the **Veteran's Edge**. Reaching this stage signifies years of disciplined training and countless battles fought with blade and mana working as one.

Many master smiths claim they can recognise a veteran Spellblade simply by examining their weapon. Though Arcane Edge leaves no permanent enchantment behind, repeated infusions gradually leave faint traces of mana within the steel, a testament to the countless times it has served as a conduit for arcane power.

To fellow Spellblades, the sight of a brilliantly glowing blade is both inspiring and intimidating. It is a reminder that true mastery is not measured by the strength of a single strike, but by the ability to maintain perfect harmony between steel and sorcery throughout an entire battle.

> *"A true Spellblade does not borrow power from magic. They teach their blade to breathe it."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Edge reaches its ultimate form, becoming the signature technique of a true Spellblade Master. The flow of mana between wielder and weapon is now effortless, allowing the Spellblade to maintain an enchantment of extraordinary potency without interrupting the rhythm of combat. Every strike becomes a perfect union of martial precision and arcane might.

When activated, the weapon blazes with brilliant arcane light, its edge surrounded by streams of concentrated mana that shimmer with every movement. The enchantment resonates through the blade, releasing devastating bursts of magical energy with every successful strike. To those who witness it, the weapon appears less like forged steel and more like a living extension of the Spellblade's soul.

Few warriors ever achieve this level of mastery. Rank V is reserved for those who have devoted years to perfecting the harmony between magic and swordsmanship. Every swing demonstrates absolute control, proving that the greatest strength of a Spellblade is not their magic or their blade alone, but the flawless balance between the two.

### Effects

- Spend **35 MP** to activate **Arcane Edge**.
- Arcane Edge remains active for **8 Turns**.
- While active, your melee weapon deals an additional **1d12 Arcane Damage** on each successful hit.
- The weapon emits a visible arcane glow while Arcane Edge is active.
- Requires a melee weapon to activate. This talent does not affect ranged weapons.
- Arcane Edge ends immediately if you are no longer wielding the infused weapon.
- Arcane Edge cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

The ancient Spellblade Orders refer to this technique as the **Master's Edge**, the highest expression of their martial philosophy. It is said that the greatest Spellblades no longer distinguish between themselves, their mana, and their weapon. All three become one, moving with perfect unity in battle.

Legends tell of masters whose Arcane Edge shone so brightly that it illuminated entire battlefields, their enchanted blades carving through monsters, enchanted armour, and even powerful magical barriers. Whether these tales have grown through centuries of retelling is unknown, but they remain a source of inspiration for every aspiring Spellblade.

To achieve Rank V is to embody everything the Spellblade path represents. It is the culmination of countless hours of discipline, sacrifice, and unwavering dedication to mastering both steel and sorcery. Few will ever wield an Arcane Edge of this calibre, and fewer still will be remembered for doing so.

> *"When steel and mana can no longer be told apart, you have reached the edge where legends are born."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

many master smiths claim they can recognise a veteran spellblade simply by examining their weapon. though arcane edge leaves no permanent enchantment behind, repeated infusions gradually leave faint traces of mana within the steel, a testament to the countless times it has served as a conduit for arcane power.

to fellow spellblades, the sight of a brilliantly glowing blade is both inspiring and intimidating. it is a reminder that true mastery is not measured by the strength of a single strike, but by the ability to maintain perfect harmony between steel and sorcery throughout an entire battle.

> *"a true spellblade does not borrow power from magic. they teach their blade to breathe it."*
>
> — grand spellblade aetherion lux, first blade of the infinite well

## rank 5
### description

arcane edge reaches its ultimate form, becoming the signature technique of a true spellblade master. the flow of mana between wielder and weapon is now effortless, allowing the spellblade to maintain an enchantment of extraordinary potency without interrupting the rhythm of combat. every strike becomes a perfect union of martial precision and arcane might.

when activated, the weapon blazes with brilliant arcane light, its edge surrounded by streams of concentrated mana that shimmer with every movement. the enchantment resonates through the blade, releasing devastating bursts of magical energy with every successful strike. to those who witness it, the weapon appears less like forged steel and more like a living extension of the spellblade's soul.

few warriors ever achieve this level of mastery. rank v is reserved for those who have devoted years to perfecting the harmony between magic and swordsmanship. every swing demonstrates absolute control, proving that the greatest strength of a spellblade is not their magic or their blade alone, but the flawless balance between the two.

### effects

- spend **35 mp** to activate **arcane edge**.
- arcane edge remains active for **8 turns**.
- while active, your melee weapon deals an additional **1d12 arcane damage** on each successful hit.
- the weapon emits a visible arcane glow while arcane edge is active.
- requires a melee weapon to activate. this talent does not affect ranged weapons.
- arcane edge ends immediately if you are no longer wielding the infused weapon.
- arcane edge cannot be activated again while already active.

### lore

the ancient spellblade orders refer to this technique as the **master's edge**, the highest expression of their martial philosophy. it is said that the greatest spellblades no longer distinguish between themselves, their mana, and their weapon. all three become one, moving with perfect unity in battle.

legends tell of masters whose arcane edge shone so brightly that it illuminated entire battlefields, their enchanted blades carving through monsters, enchanted armour, and even powerful magical barriers. whether these tales have grown through centuries of retelling is unknown, but they remain a source of inspiration for every aspiring spellblade.

to achieve rank v is to embody everything the spellblade path represents. it is the culmination of countless hours of discipline, sacrifice, and unwavering dedication to mastering both steel and sorcery. few will ever wield an arcane edge of this calibre, and fewer still will be remembered for doing so.

> *"when steel and mana can no longer be told apart, you have reached the edge where legends are born."*
>
> — grand spellblade aetherion lux, first blade of the infinite well

# Arcane Guard

## Overview
Spellblades understand that not every threat can be avoided through speed alone. Against hostile magic, they learn to shape mana into a protective barrier that surrounds their body, disrupting incoming spells before they can fully take hold.

Unlike Arcane Reflex, which relies upon agility and precise movement, Arcane Guard stands firm against magical assault. The Spellblade condenses raw mana into a shimmering defensive aura that absorbs and weakens hostile arcane energies, allowing them to endure attacks that would overwhelm lesser warriors.

At Rank I, the barrier is temporary and can only withstand modest magical punishment. Even so, it provides invaluable protection against enemy spellcasters, allowing the Spellblade to remain in the fight while closing the distance to their greatest threat.

## Rank 1
### Description

Spellblades understand that not every threat can be avoided through speed alone. Against hostile magic, they learn to shape mana into a protective barrier that surrounds their body, disrupting incoming spells before they can fully take hold.

Unlike Arcane Reflex, which relies upon agility and precise movement, Arcane Guard stands firm against magical assault. The Spellblade condenses raw mana into a shimmering defensive aura that absorbs and weakens hostile arcane energies, allowing them to endure attacks that would overwhelm lesser warriors.

At Rank I, the barrier is temporary and can only withstand modest magical punishment. Even so, it provides invaluable protection against enemy spellcasters, allowing the Spellblade to remain in the fight while closing the distance to their greatest threat.

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to activate **Arcane Guard**.
- Arcane Guard remains active for **3 Turns**.
- While active, gain **+2 on all Saving Throws against spells and magical abilities.**
- Reduce all magical damage you receive by **1d4**.
- Arcane Guard only protects the Spellblade.
- Arcane Guard cannot be activated again while already active.
- This talent does not reduce damage from non-magical attacks.

### Lore

Arcane Guard was developed after early Spellblades discovered that their greatest weakness was enemy spellcasters. While heavily armoured warriors could withstand blades and arrows, concentrated magical attacks often proved devastating before a Spellblade could close the distance.

Rather than abandoning their offensive style, the founders created a technique that allowed mana to defend as effectively as it could destroy. By weaving a protective current around their bodies, they learned to endure magical assaults long enough to bring the battle back into melee range.

Today, Arcane Guard is considered an essential technique within every Spellblade Order. Apprentices are taught that a master Spellblade should fear neither steel nor sorcery, for both can be answered with disciplined control over mana.

> *"Steel may break against armour, but magic breaks against a disciplined mind."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 2
### Description

As a Spellblade's understanding of defensive magic deepens, Arcane Guard evolves from a simple protective barrier into a resilient mantle of arcane energy. The flow of mana surrounding the Spellblade becomes steadier and more efficient, allowing it to intercept a greater amount of hostile magic without disrupting the warrior's rhythm in combat.

The barrier pulses in harmony with the Spellblade's mana core, weakening incoming spells before they fully manifest. Fire burns colder, lightning loses its bite, and curses struggle to take hold as the guard disperses part of the magical force before it reaches its target.

Rank II marks the beginning of true magical resilience. Veteran Spellblades rely on Arcane Guard to push through barrages of hostile magic, trusting their barrier to carry them safely into melee where their enemies are at their weakest.

### Effects

- Spend **25 MP** to activate **Arcane Guard**.
- Arcane Guard remains active for **4 Turns**.
- While active, gain **+3 on all Saving Throws against magical effects.**
- Reduce all magical damage you receive by **1d6**.
- Arcane Guard only protects the Spellblade.
- Arcane Guard cannot be activated again while already active.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Guard — Rank I**.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank II is often called the **Warden's Mantle**. At this stage, apprentices stop fearing enemy spellcasters and begin treating hostile magic as another obstacle to overcome rather than an impossible threat.

Masters teach that Arcane Guard should never be relied upon to make a Spellblade invincible. Instead, it exists to buy precious moments—enough time to survive a devastating spell, close the distance, and bring the battle back to the edge of a blade.

Many famous Spellblades earned their reputations not by avoiding powerful magic, but by walking calmly through it. Their unwavering confidence inspired allies and unsettled enemy mages who watched their greatest spells lose much of their power against the shimmering barrier.

> *"Magic is only frightening until you learn to stand within the storm."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 3
### Description

Arcane Guard has become an instinctive defense, allowing the Spellblade to withstand powerful magical assaults without breaking their offensive momentum. The protective aura surrounding their body strengthens into a dense layer of mana that instinctively intercepts hostile magical energy before it reaches its target.

Rather than simply absorbing spells, the barrier disrupts and weakens the arcane structure holding them together. Flames lose their intensity, bolts of lightning fracture upon impact, and curses struggle to bind themselves to the Spellblade's soul. Although the barrier cannot completely negate powerful magic, it significantly reduces its effectiveness.

Rank III represents a turning point in a Spellblade's training. Having mastered both martial combat and magical resilience, they are capable of advancing directly into enemy spellcasters, trusting Arcane Guard to shield them while they close the distance.

### Effects

- Spend **30 MP** to activate **Arcane Guard**.
- Arcane Guard remains active for **5 Turns**.
- While active, gain **+4 on all Saving Throws against magical effects.**
- Reduce all magical damage you receive by **1d8**.
- Arcane Guard only protects the Spellblade.
- Arcane Guard cannot be activated again while already active.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Guard — Rank II**.

### Lore

Spellblade Masters refer to Rank III as the **Arcane Bastion**, a milestone where the barrier begins to function as naturally as breathing. The Spellblade no longer consciously maintains the ward; instead, their mana instinctively responds whenever hostile magic threatens them.

Throughout Asteria's history, many legendary Spellblades have survived encounters with powerful archmages through Arcane Guard alone. Rather than attempting to overpower devastating spells, they relied upon discipline, patience, and unwavering control of their own mana until they stood within striking distance.

Among the Orders, reaching Rank III is considered proof that a Spellblade has learned one of their greatest lessons: magic is not only a weapon to command, but a force that can be resisted through mastery and resolve.

> *"The strongest shield is not forged from steel, but from the unwavering will to endure."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

Arcane Guard has become a masterpiece of defensive spellcraft, allowing the Spellblade to stand firm against even the most destructive magical assaults. The protective barrier no longer simply absorbs hostile mana—it actively disrupts and disperses incoming magical energy before it can fully manifest.

When activated, shimmering currents of arcane energy envelop the Spellblade, constantly shifting to intercept hostile spells. Every wave of magical force that collides with the barrier is weakened as the guard redirects unstable mana harmlessly into the surrounding air. Veteran Spellblades often walk directly through magical bombardments, trusting their Arcane Guard to protect them while they close the distance to their prey.

Rank IV is regarded as the hallmark of an elite Spellblade. Those who achieve this level are feared by enemy mages, for they can withstand magical punishment that would overwhelm most warriors and continue advancing without hesitation.

### Effects

- Spend **35 MP** to activate **Arcane Guard**.
- Arcane Guard remains active for **6 Turns**.
- While active, gain **+5 on all Saving Throws against magical effects**.
- Reduce all magical damage you receive by **1d10**.
- Arcane Guard only protects the Spellblade.
- Arcane Guard cannot be activated again while already active.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Guard — Rank III**.

### Lore

Within the great Spellblade Orders, Rank IV is known as the **Magebreaker Ward**. It represents the point where enemy spellcasters begin to view the Spellblade not as a warrior to defeat, but as an unstoppable force that refuses to yield before arcane power.

Ancient battle records describe elite Spellblades advancing through storms of fire, lightning, and shadow while their shimmering wards steadily unravelled each spell before it could inflict its full devastation. Their resilience became legendary, inspiring allies while sowing doubt among even the most accomplished mages.

Masters teach that Arcane Guard is not about becoming immune to magic. It is about possessing the courage and discipline to continue advancing when every instinct tells others to retreat.

> *"The greatest victory over magic is not to destroy it, but to walk through it without fear."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Guard reaches its ultimate form, surrounding the Spellblade in an almost impenetrable mantle of arcane energy. The barrier no longer merely resists hostile magic—it instinctively unravels and disperses magical attacks before they can reach their full potential. To enemy spellcasters, striking a master Spellblade feels like casting into a storm that tears their spells apart.

The barrier pulses in perfect harmony with the Spellblade's mana core, reinforcing itself with every passing moment. Even the most devastating magical assaults lose much of their strength as the guard absorbs, redirects, and dissipates hostile arcane energy. While no defence is absolute, Arcane Guard allows the Spellblade to endure magical punishment that few mortals could survive.

Only the greatest Spellblades achieve this level of mastery. They are renowned as Magebreakers, warriors who charge fearlessly into the heart of magical battlefields, trusting their discipline and mana to shield them from destruction.

### Effects

- Spend **40 MP** to activate **Arcane Guard**.
- Arcane Guard remains active for **8 Turns**.
- While active, gain **+6 on all Saving Throws against magical effects**.
- Reduce all magical damage you receive by **1d12**.
- The first magical effect each round that would inflict a negative status effect on you is made with **Disadvantage** (or the caster suffers a penalty, depending on the effect's rules).
- Arcane Guard only protects the Spellblade.
- Arcane Guard cannot be activated again while already active.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Guard — Rank IV**.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank V is known as the **Aegis of the Arcane**, a title reserved for masters whose command of defensive mana borders on legendary. They have learned that true protection is not created through overwhelming power, but through absolute control over the flow of magic itself.

Stories tell of Spellblades who walked unharmed through storms of fire, shattered curses with sheer force of will, and stood against archmages without yielding a single step. Whether these tales have grown through centuries of retelling is unknown, but they remain the ideal every apprentice strives to achieve.

To become a master of Arcane Guard is to embody one of the Spellblade's greatest philosophies: magic is neither feared nor worshipped—it is understood, mastered, and ultimately turned aside by unwavering discipline.

> *"The greatest shield is not forged from steel or stone. It is forged from a will that refuses to yield before magic."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Prerequisites
None

## Scaling
See individual rank details.

## Synergy
Information coming soon.

## GM Notes
GM-only information coming soon.

stories tell of spellblades who walked unharmed through storms of fire, shattered curses with sheer force of will, and stood against archmages without yielding a single step. whether these tales have grown through centuries of retelling is unknown, but they remain the ideal every apprentice strives to achieve.

to become a master of arcane guard is to embody one of the spellblade's greatest philosophies: magic is neither feared nor worshipped—it is understood, mastered, and ultimately turned aside by unwavering discipline.

> *"the greatest shield is not forged from steel or stone. it is forged from a will that refuses to yield before magic."*

> — grand spellblade aetherion lux, first blade of the infinite well

# Arcane Phase

## Overview
Arcane Phase is one of the most dangerous techniques taught within the Spellblade Orders, allowing the practitioner to partially convert their physical body into raw arcane energy. For a brief moment, the Spellblade exists between the physical and magical planes, enabling them to move through obstacles that would otherwise halt their advance.

While phased, the Spellblade's body becomes intangible to most physical matter. Stone walls, iron bars, enemy warriors, and difficult terrain become little more than passing obstacles. However, this transformation comes at a great risk. By becoming living mana, the Spellblade becomes significantly more vulnerable to hostile magic, as spells can interact directly with their unstable arcane form.

Masters repeatedly warn their apprentices that Arcane Phase is a technique of precision, not recklessness. Countless Spellblades have suffered horrific injuries by allowing the technique to expire while still inside solid matter. Those who master Arcane Phase always know exactly where they intend to return before they ever step beyond the physical world.

## Rank 1
### Description

Arcane Phase is one of the most dangerous techniques taught within the Spellblade Orders, allowing the practitioner to partially convert their physical body into raw arcane energy. For a brief moment, the Spellblade exists between the physical and magical planes, enabling them to move through obstacles that would otherwise halt their advance.

While phased, the Spellblade's body becomes intangible to most physical matter. Stone walls, iron bars, enemy warriors, and difficult terrain become little more than passing obstacles. However, this transformation comes at a great risk. By becoming living mana, the Spellblade becomes significantly more vulnerable to hostile magic, as spells can interact directly with their unstable arcane form.

Masters repeatedly warn their apprentices that Arcane Phase is a technique of precision, not recklessness. Countless Spellblades have suffered horrific injuries by allowing the technique to expire while still inside solid matter. Those who master Arcane Phase always know exactly where they intend to return before they ever step beyond the physical world.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **40 MP** to activate **Arcane Phase**.
- Arcane Phase lasts for **1 Turn**.
- **1 Use per Short Rest.**
- While Arcane Phase is active:
  - Ignore difficult terrain.
  - Move through creatures.
  - Move through thin, non-magical solid objects such as doors, gates, bars and walls.
  - You are immune to Opportunity Attacks.
  - You cannot interact with or manipulate physical objects while phased unless the GM determines otherwise.

#### Arcane Vulnerability

While Arcane Phase is active:

- You have **Disadvantage on Saving Throws against magical effects.**
- You take **25% additional magical damage** (rounded up).

#### ⚠ Phase Instability

Arcane Phase **must not** end while any part of your body occupies a creature or solid object.

If this occurs:

- You are immediately expelled to the nearest unoccupied space.
- You are **Knocked Prone**.
- You suffer **6d6 Arcane Damage**.
- You gain **Arcane Fatigue** until the end of your next turn.

### Lore

Among the Spellblade Orders, Arcane Phase is considered both a marvel and a warning. It represents the ultimate trust between a Spellblade and their mana, requiring absolute confidence that one's body can safely return to the physical world. Those who hesitate often discover too late that the arcane currents show little mercy to careless practitioners.

Veteran masters insist that Arcane Phase should never be viewed as an escape. It is a calculated commitment, demanding complete awareness of one's surroundings before taking even a single step beyond reality. Every apprentice is taught the same lesson before learning the technique: always know where you intend to reappear.

Legends speak of master Spellblades walking unharmed through castle walls, collapsing caverns, and enemy battle lines. Yet those same stories always end with a reminder that even the greatest masters respected the dangers of the technique, for the arcane realm rewards discipline and punishes arrogance in equal measure.

> *"The world will gladly let you pass through it... but it may not welcome you back if you choose your path poorly."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 2
### Description

The Spellblade's control over Arcane Phase has improved, allowing them to maintain their incorporeal form for longer without destabilising their mana. What was once a brief step between worlds becomes a sustained state, enabling the Spellblade to navigate dangerous terrain and bypass physical obstacles with greater confidence.

Although the technique has become more stable, it remains one of the most hazardous abilities within the Spellblade arsenal. While partially transformed into arcane energy, the Spellblade becomes increasingly susceptible to hostile magic. Enemy spellcasters quickly learn to exploit this vulnerability, making careful timing and battlefield awareness essential.

Experienced Spellblades are taught that Arcane Phase should never be used recklessly. A poorly planned phase can leave them trapped between solid objects or exposed to devastating magical attacks. Every use demands discipline, patience, and absolute awareness of one's surroundings.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **35 MP** to activate **Arcane Phase**.
- Arcane Phase lasts for **2 Turns**.
- **2 Uses per Short Rest.**
- While Arcane Phase is active:
  - Ignore difficult terrain.
  - Move through creatures.
  - Move through non-magical doors, gates, walls, bars and other solid objects up to **1 metre thick**.
  - You are immune to Opportunity Attacks.
  - You cannot interact with or manipulate physical objects while phased unless the GM determines otherwise.

#### Arcane Vulnerability

While Arcane Phase is active:

- You have **Disadvantage on Saving Throws against magical effects.**
- You take **25% additional magical damage** (rounded up).

#### ⚠ Phase Instability

Arcane Phase **must not** end while any part of your body occupies a creature or solid object.

If this occurs:

- You are immediately expelled to the nearest unoccupied space.
- You are **Knocked Prone**.
- You suffer **6d6 Arcane Damage**.
- You gain **Arcane Fatigue** until the end of your next turn.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank II is known as the **Ghost Step**, marking the point where the practitioner begins to trust the flow of mana rather than fear it. Remaining phased for several moments requires exceptional concentration, as even the slightest lapse can cause the arcane currents to become unstable.

Veteran instructors often send apprentices through abandoned ruins and ancient fortresses to teach them a simple lesson: always know where you intend to emerge. Many overconfident students have found themselves painfully expelled from stone walls after losing track of time, a mistake that every Spellblade remembers only once.

Those who master Rank II learn that Arcane Phase is not simply a means of movement. It is a lesson in restraint, precision, and respect for the unpredictable nature of arcane energy.

> *"The greatest danger is not stepping beyond the world—it is forgetting that the world still expects you to return."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 3
### Description

The Spellblade has reached a level of mastery where Arcane Phase is no longer a desperate gamble, but a calculated manipulation of the boundary between the physical and arcane realms. Maintaining an incorporeal form has become second nature, allowing the Spellblade to traverse obstacles and hostile battlefields with remarkable precision.

While phased, the Spellblade exists only partially within the physical world. Weapons, creatures, and solid terrain struggle to impede their movement, making them exceptionally difficult to pin down. However, this freedom comes at a significant cost. Their body, now composed largely of unstable arcane energy, becomes increasingly vulnerable to hostile spells and magical effects capable of disrupting their fragile form.

Spellblade Masters teach that Rank III is where overconfidence claims the lives of many practitioners. The longer one remains phased, the easier it is to forget the dangers of the physical world waiting to reclaim them. Every experienced Spellblade knows that the greatest threat is not entering the arcane state—it is returning from it safely.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **30 MP** to activate **Arcane Phase**.
- Arcane Phase lasts for **3 Turns**.
- **3 Uses per Short Rest.**
- While Arcane Phase is active:
  - Ignore difficult terrain.
  - Move through creatures.
  - Move through most non-magical structures and natural obstacles, including walls, floors, ceilings, doors, gates, and large rock formations up to **2 metres thick**.
  - You are immune to Opportunity Attacks.
  - You cannot interact with or manipulate physical objects while phased unless the GM determines otherwise.

#### Arcane Vulnerability

While Arcane Phase is active:

- You have **Disadvantage on Saving Throws against magical effects.**
- You take **25% additional magical damage** (rounded up).

#### ⚠ Phase Instability

Arcane Phase **must not** end while any part of your body occupies a creature or solid object.

If this occurs:

- You are immediately expelled to the nearest unoccupied space.
- You are **Knocked Prone**.
- You suffer **8d6 Arcane Damage**.
- You gain **Arcane Fatigue** until the end of your next turn.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank III is known as the **Veil Walker**, a title earned by those capable of walking confidently between the material world and the arcane currents that surround it. At this stage, Arcane Phase ceases to be viewed as a simple movement technique and becomes an expression of complete trust in one's mastery over mana.

Veterans often recount stories of Spellblades slipping effortlessly through fortress walls, collapsing caverns, and enemy shield lines before reappearing exactly where they intended. Yet every tale is accompanied by another, warning of those who misjudged a wall's thickness, underestimated the duration of the technique, or ignored the presence of enemy mages. The arcane realm is unforgiving to those who become complacent.

Masters remind every student that Arcane Phase does not make them invincible. It merely changes the dangers they face. Wisdom lies in knowing not only when to phase, but when to return.

> *"Any fool can step beyond the world. Only a master knows exactly where to step back into it."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

The Spellblade has become a true master of Arcane Phase, effortlessly shifting between the physical world and the arcane plane. Their body now exists only loosely within reality, allowing them to bypass obstacles that even powerful magic was designed to stop. Walls, fortifications, and many magical barriers become little more than temporary inconveniences to a practitioner of this calibre.

Yet with such mastery comes even greater danger. While their connection to the physical world weakens, their arcane form becomes increasingly exposed to hostile magical forces. Enemy spellcasters can exploit this vulnerability, making every use of Arcane Phase a calculated risk rather than a guaranteed escape.

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank IV is considered the threshold of true mastery. It is said that a master no longer asks whether a path exists—they simply decide to walk through it. Even so, the oldest instructors continually warn that arrogance has claimed more lives than any blade ever has.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **25 MP** to activate **Arcane Phase**.
- Arcane Phase lasts for **4 Turns**.
- **4 Uses per Short Rest.**
- While Arcane Phase is active:
  - Ignore difficult terrain.
  - Move through creatures.
  - Move through most non-magical structures regardless of thickness, provided your movement is sufficient to completely pass through them.
  - You may pass through **lesser magical barriers**, magical walls, force effects, and magically sealed doorways at the GM's discretion.
  - You are immune to Opportunity Attacks.
  - You cannot interact with or manipulate physical objects while phased unless the GM determines otherwise.

#### Arcane Vulnerability

While Arcane Phase is active:

- You have **Disadvantage on Saving Throws against magical effects.**
- You take **25% additional magical damage** (rounded up).

#### ⚠ Phase Instability

Arcane Phase **must not** end while any part of your body occupies a creature or solid object.

If this occurs:

- You are immediately expelled to the nearest unoccupied space.
- You are **Knocked Prone**.
- You suffer **10d6 Arcane Damage**.
- You gain **Arcane Fatigue** until the end of your next turn.

### Lore

Within the ancient Spellblade Orders, Rank IV is known as the **Veil Master**. Very few practitioners ever reach this stage, for it demands absolute trust in one's mastery over both body and mana. Those who succeed no longer view walls or barriers as obstacles, but as temporary boundaries between one step and the next.

Stories tell of Veil Masters infiltrating heavily fortified castles without opening a single gate, escaping collapsing temples by walking through solid stone, and pursuing enemies through magically sealed chambers thought to be impenetrable. Such feats have earned them equal measures of admiration and fear throughout Asteria.

Even so, every master shares the same warning with their apprentices: the arcane plane is unforgiving. A moment of carelessness, a lapse in concentration, or a misjudged path can turn Arcane Phase from a miraculous technique into a fatal mistake.

> *"Stone yields to patience. Magic yields to understanding. Pride yields to neither."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Phase reaches its ultimate form, allowing the Spellblade to exist almost entirely as living arcane energy. Through absolute mastery of their mana core, they freely shift between the material world and the Arcane Plane, slipping through obstacles that would stop even the greatest warriors. To onlookers, the Spellblade appears to fade from reality itself, moving effortlessly through walls, fortifications, creatures, and magical barriers before reforming exactly where they intend.

Despite this mastery, Arcane Phase remains one of the most dangerous techniques ever created. While the Spellblade is incredibly difficult for physical forces to hinder, they become exceptionally vulnerable to hostile magic. Every spell threatens to destabilise their arcane form, and the greatest enemy of a master Spellblade is often overconfidence.

The oldest masters teach that Arcane Phase is not an escape from reality—it is a temporary surrender to it. The world will always reclaim those who linger too long beyond its grasp.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **20 MP** to activate **Arcane Phase**.
- Arcane Phase lasts for **5 Turns**.
- **5 Uses per Short Rest.**
- While Arcane Phase is active:
  - Ignore difficult terrain.
  - Move freely through creatures.
  - Move through all non-magical structures regardless of thickness, provided your movement is sufficient to completely pass through them.
  - Move through nearly all magical barriers, force effects, magical walls, and magically sealed structures.
  - **Artifact-grade wards, Divine Magic, and World Magic cannot be phased through unless the GM rules otherwise.**
  - You are immune to Opportunity Attacks.
  - You cannot interact with or manipulate physical objects while phased unless the GM determines otherwise.

#### Arcane Vulnerability

While Arcane Phase is active:

- You have **Disadvantage on Saving Throws against magical effects.**
- You take **25% additional magical damage** (rounded up).

#### ⚠ Phase Instability

Arcane Phase **must never** end while any part of your body occupies a creature or solid object.

If this occurs:

- You are immediately expelled to the nearest unoccupied space.
- You are **Knocked Prone**.
- You suffer **12d6 Arcane Damage**.
- You gain **Arcane Fatigue** until the end of your next turn.
- The GM may apply additional consequences if you attempted to phase through an object or barrier beyond your current mastery.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank V is known as the **Phantom Ascendant**, a title granted only to those who have mastered the impossible. These legendary warriors no longer perceive walls, fortifications, or magical prisons as barriers. Instead, they see them as temporary imperfections within the fabric of reality, capable of being crossed through perfect harmony with the arcane.

Legends tell of Phantom Ascendants walking unhindered through impregnable citadels, escaping collapsing mountains, and crossing battlefields untouched by volleys of arrows. Yet every tale carries the same warning. Those who forget that they remain bound by the laws of reality inevitably discover that the Arcane Plane shows no mercy to the careless.

To master Arcane Phase is to accept that immense power always demands equal responsibility. A true Spellblade knows that the greatest danger is never the wall before them, but the decision of where they choose to return.

> *"Reality is not your enemy. It is your destination. Never forget to return to it."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

None

within the ancient spellblade orders, rank iv is known as the **veil master**. very few practitioners ever reach this stage, for it demands absolute trust in one's mastery over both body and mana. those who succeed no longer view walls or barriers as obstacles, but as temporary boundaries between one step and the next.

stories tell of veil masters infiltrating heavily fortified castles without opening a single gate, escaping collapsing temples by walking through solid stone, and pursuing enemies through magically sealed chambers thought to be impenetrable. such feats have earned them equal measures of admiration and fear throughout asteria.

even so, every master shares the same warning with their apprentices: the arcane plane is unforgiving. a moment of carelessness, a lapse in concentration, or a misjudged path can turn arcane phase from a miraculous technique into a fatal mistake.

> *"stone yields to patience. magic yields to understanding. pride yields to neither."*

> — grand spellblade aetherion lux, first blade of the infinite well

## rank 5
### description

arcane phase reaches its ultimate form, allowing the spellblade to exist almost entirely as living arcane energy. through absolute mastery of their mana core, they freely shift between the material world and the arcane plane, slipping through obstacles that would stop even the greatest warriors. to onlookers, the spellblade appears to fade from reality itself, moving effortlessly through walls, fortifications, creatures, and magical barriers before reforming exactly where they intend.

despite this mastery, arcane phase remains one of the most dangerous techniques ever created. while the spellblade is incredibly difficult for physical forces to hinder, they become exceptionally vulnerable to hostile magic. every spell threatens to destabilise their arcane form, and the greatest enemy of a master spellblade is often overconfidence.

the oldest masters teach that arcane phase is not an escape from reality—it is a temporary surrender to it. the world will always reclaim those who linger too long beyond its grasp.

### effects

- spend **1 action point** and **20 mp** to activate **arcane phase**.
- arcane phase lasts for **5 turns**.
- **5 uses per short rest.**
- while arcane phase is active:
  - ignore difficult terrain.
  - move freely through creatures.
  - move through all non-magical structures regardless of thickness, provided your movement is sufficient to completely pass through them.
  - move through nearly all magical barriers, force effects, magical walls, and magically sealed structures.
  - **artifact-grade wards, divine magic, and world magic cannot be phased through unless the gm rules otherwise.**
  - you are immune to opportunity attacks.
  - you cannot interact with or manipulate physical objects while phased unless the gm determines otherwise.

#### arcane vulnerability

while arcane phase is active:

- you have **disadvantage on saving throws against magical effects.**
- you take **25% additional magical damage** (rounded up).

#### ⚠ phase instability

arcane phase **must never** end while any part of your body occupies a creature or solid object.

if this occurs:

- you are immediately expelled to the nearest unoccupied space.
- you are **knocked prone**.
- you suffer **12d6 arcane damage**.
- you gain **arcane fatigue** until the end of your next turn.
- the gm may apply additional consequences if you attempted to phase through an object or barrier beyond your current mastery.

### lore

within the oldest spellblade orders, rank v is known as the **phantom ascendant**, a title granted only to those who have mastered the impossible. these legendary warriors no longer perceive walls, fortifications, or magical prisons as barriers. instead, they see them as temporary imperfections within the fabric of reality, capable of being crossed through perfect harmony with the arcane.

legends tell of phantom ascendants walking unhindered through impregnable citadels, escaping collapsing mountains, and crossing battlefields untouched by volleys of arrows. yet every tale carries the same warning. those who forget that they remain bound by the laws of reality inevitably discover that the arcane plane shows no mercy to the careless.

to master arcane phase is to accept that immense power always demands equal responsibility. a true spellblade knows that the greatest danger is never the wall before them, but the decision of where they choose to return.

> *"reality is not your enemy. it is your destination. never forget to return to it."*

> — grand spellblade aetherion lux, first blade of the infinite well

# Arcane Pursuit

## Overview
Spellblades are taught that fleeing enemies create openings. Arcane Pursuit was developed to punish opponents who attempt to retreat, reposition, or escape the reach of a blade.

By locking onto the motion of a moving target, the Spellblade floods their body with mana and surges after them with explosive speed. Unlike Arcane Rush, which allows free repositioning, Arcane Pursuit is focused entirely on chasing movement. It does not carry the Spellblade wherever they wish to go; it carries them toward a target that has already begun to move.

At Rank I, Arcane Pursuit allows the Spellblade to close distance against enemies who attempt to flee or reposition. It is a reactive hunting technique, rewarding awareness and timing rather than simple speed.

## Rank 1
### Description

Spellblades are taught that fleeing enemies create openings. Arcane Pursuit was developed to punish opponents who attempt to retreat, reposition, or escape the reach of a blade.

By locking onto the motion of a moving target, the Spellblade floods their body with mana and surges after them with explosive speed. Unlike Arcane Rush, which allows free repositioning, Arcane Pursuit is focused entirely on chasing movement. It does not carry the Spellblade wherever they wish to go; it carries them toward a target that has already begun to move.

At Rank I, Arcane Pursuit allows the Spellblade to close distance against enemies who attempt to flee or reposition. It is a reactive hunting technique, rewarding awareness and timing rather than simple speed.

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to activate **Arcane Pursuit**.
- Choose one hostile creature within **10 metres** that has moved this turn.
- Instantly move to the nearest valid unoccupied space adjacent to that creature.
- This movement ignores difficult terrain.
- This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- After arriving, you may make **one melee weapon attack** against the chosen target.
- If no valid adjacent space exists, Arcane Pursuit fails.
- If Arcane Pursuit fails, you still spend **10 MP**.
- Arcane Pursuit cannot target creatures that have not moved this turn.

### Lore

Arcane Pursuit was created by Spellblades who refused to let enemies control the distance of battle. Archers, mages, and skirmishers often relied on movement to stay beyond the reach of melee warriors, but Spellblades answered with a technique designed to hunt motion itself.

The earliest masters described Arcane Pursuit as listening to the disturbance left behind by movement. Once a target shifted position, the Spellblade could follow that motion through mana, crossing the distance before the enemy fully escaped.

Among the Orders, apprentices are taught that Arcane Pursuit is not a charge. It is a response. The enemy moves first, and the Spellblade answers.

> *"Run if you wish. Every step only tells me where to follow."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 2
### Description

As a Spellblade's mastery grows, Arcane Pursuit becomes faster, more precise, and capable of following enemies over greater distances. Rather than simply reacting to movement, the Spellblade begins to anticipate it, reading the flow of mana left in an opponent's wake before they have fully completed their reposition.

The burst of speed is almost instantaneous. To spectators, the Spellblade appears to vanish in a flash of arcane light before materialising beside their quarry, denying even the most agile foes the opportunity to escape.

At Rank II, Arcane Pursuit extends its reach and improves its efficiency, allowing the Spellblade to relentlessly pressure enemies who rely on movement to survive. Those who believe a few extra metres will save them quickly discover that distance means little to a determined Spellblade.

### Effects

- Spend **25 MP** to activate **Arcane Pursuit**.
- Choose one hostile creature within **15 metres** that has moved this turn.
- Instantly move to the nearest valid unoccupied space adjacent to that creature.
- This movement ignores difficult terrain.
- This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- After arriving, you may make **one melee weapon attack** against the chosen target.
- If no valid adjacent space exists, Arcane Pursuit fails.
- If Arcane Pursuit fails, you still spend **12 MP** (rounded down).
- Arcane Pursuit cannot target creatures that have not moved this turn.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Pursuit — Rank I**.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank II is known as the **Hunter's Step**. Apprentices begin to realise that Arcane Pursuit is not powered by speed alone, but by recognising the arcane disturbance created when a creature moves across the battlefield.

Veteran Spellblades often describe the sensation as chasing an echo rather than a body. Every movement leaves behind a fleeting trail of mana that an experienced practitioner can instinctively follow, allowing them to intercept enemies before they can capitalise on their new position.

Many skirmishers and battle mages have learned to fear this technique. The moment they choose to retreat, they also choose to invite the Spellblade into striking distance.

> *"Every step your enemy takes leaves a trail. Learn to follow it, and no one truly escapes."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 3
### Description

Arcane Pursuit has evolved into one of the Spellblade's most feared battlefield techniques. By reading the flow of mana left behind by moving creatures, the Spellblade can instantly close even greater distances, denying opponents the opportunity to disengage safely.

The pursuit is no longer simply a burst of speed. It becomes an act of prediction, allowing the Spellblade to intercept fleeing enemies before they can establish a new position. To an observer, the Spellblade appears to disappear into a streak of arcane light, emerging beside their target with flawless precision.

At Rank III, Arcane Pursuit allows experienced Spellblades to relentlessly pressure mobile opponents, forcing enemies to think twice before attempting to reposition during combat.

### Effects

- Spend **30 MP** to activate **Arcane Pursuit**.
- Choose one hostile creature within **20 metres** that has moved this turn.
- Instantly move to the nearest valid unoccupied space adjacent to that creature.
- This movement ignores difficult terrain and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- Immediately after arriving, you may make **one melee weapon attack** against the chosen target.
- If no valid adjacent space exists, Arcane Pursuit fails.
- If Arcane Pursuit fails, you still spend **15 MP**.
- Arcane Pursuit cannot target creatures that have not moved this turn.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Pursuit — Rank II**.

### Lore

Spellblade masters refer to Rank III as the **Relentless Pursuit**, the stage where distance begins to lose its meaning. Practitioners no longer chase an enemy's footsteps; they instinctively follow the lingering currents of mana disturbed by movement itself.

Throughout Asteria's history, countless generals have underestimated this technique, believing a tactical withdrawal would create breathing room against a Spellblade. Instead, they found the arcane warrior already standing beside them before their formation could recover.

Among the Orders, students are reminded that Arcane Pursuit is not about moving faster than an opponent. It is about ensuring that movement itself becomes a liability.

> *"The moment your enemy chooses to flee is the moment they have already been caught."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

The Spellblade has refined Arcane Pursuit into a technique that borders on supernatural. Rather than merely chasing a moving opponent, they instinctively predict where their quarry will be, allowing them to intercept even the swiftest combatants before they can gain an advantage.

At this level, Arcane Pursuit becomes a terrifying display of battlefield dominance. Every attempted retreat, tactical reposition, or desperate escape risks placing the Spellblade directly beside their target. Those who rely upon mobility quickly discover that every movement creates another opportunity for pursuit.

Veteran Spellblades often describe Rank IV as the point where the hunter no longer follows their prey—they simply arrive where the prey intends to be.

### Effects

- Spend **35 MP** to activate **Arcane Pursuit**.
- Choose one hostile creature within **25 metres** that has moved this turn.
- Instantly move to the nearest valid unoccupied space adjacent to that creature.
- This movement ignores difficult terrain and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- Immediately after arriving, you may make **one melee weapon attack** against the chosen target.
- If the attack hits, the target's **Movement Speed is reduced by 50% until the end of its next turn.**
- If no valid adjacent space exists, Arcane Pursuit fails.
- If Arcane Pursuit fails, you still spend **17 MP** (half the Mana Cost, rounded down).
- Arcane Pursuit cannot target creatures that have not moved this turn.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Pursuit — Rank III**.

### Lore

Rank IV is known within the Spellblade Orders as the **Hunter's Mark**, not because it brands an enemy with magic, but because few creatures escape once a master Spellblade has chosen to pursue them.

Military records speak of elite Spellblades who specialised in hunting enemy commanders, scouts, and battle mages. Attempts to retreat often proved futile, as the Spellblade would appear beside their target before orders could even be given.

Masters teach that Arcane Pursuit is more than a technique—it is a promise. Once a Spellblade commits to the chase, the battle is no longer fought on the enemy's terms.

> *"Movement creates opportunity. For my enemy, it is the opportunity to be caught."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Pursuit reaches its ultimate form, allowing the Spellblade to hunt even the fastest opponents across the battlefield. Through complete mastery of mana and movement, they no longer react to where an enemy has been—they instinctively intercept where they are attempting to go.

To witnesses, the technique appears impossible. A fleeing opponent takes only a few steps before the Spellblade vanishes in a surge of arcane energy, materialising beside them with blade already in motion. Distance offers no safety, and movement itself becomes a dangerous gamble.

Only the greatest Spellblades ever master Arcane Pursuit to this degree. Those who do become relentless hunters, capable of punishing any enemy who believes they can escape the reach of steel and sorcery.

### Effects

- Spend **40 MP** to activate **Arcane Pursuit**.
- Choose one hostile creature within **30 metres** that has moved this turn.
- Instantly move to the nearest valid unoccupied space adjacent to that creature.
- This movement ignores difficult terrain and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- Immediately after arriving, you may make **one melee weapon attack** against the chosen target.
- If the attack hits, the target's **Movement Speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn**.
- If no valid adjacent space exists, Arcane Pursuit fails.
- If Arcane Pursuit fails, you still spend **20 MP**.
- Arcane Pursuit cannot target creatures that have not moved this turn.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Pursuit — Rank IV**.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank V is known as the **Unbroken Chase**. It represents the pinnacle of pursuit magic, where distance, obstacles, and momentum cease to matter. The Spellblade no longer follows an enemy—they simply deny them the ability to escape.

Stories of the Unbroken Chase are common throughout Asteria. Assassins who vanished into crowded streets, battle mages who blinked across fortifications, and monsters that outran entire companies have all fallen to Spellblades who mastered this technique. Their prey quickly learned that every attempt to flee only hastened the inevitable.

To a master of Arcane Pursuit, movement is not an obstacle to overcome—it is an invitation to strike.

> *"You may outrun a soldier. You may outpace a knight. But once a Spellblade begins the chase, your journey ends where my blade begins."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

# Arcane Reflex

## Overview
A Spellblade survives not by enduring every strike, but by avoiding the ones that matter.

Through training and repeated exposure to combat, the Spellblade learns to channel mana through their nervous system, briefly accelerating their reactions beyond normal limits. This surge of arcane energy allows them to read danger more quickly and adjust their position in the instant before an attack lands.

To outside observers, the movement appears insignificant—a slight shift of the shoulder, a subtle turn of the body, or a single step placed at precisely the right moment. Yet those tiny adjustments often mean the difference between a devastating blow and a harmless miss.

At Rank 1, Arcane Reflex represents the beginning of this discipline. The Spellblade learns to instinctively call upon mana when threatened, increasing their ability to evade incoming attacks.

## Rank 1
### Description

A Spellblade survives not by enduring every strike, but by avoiding the ones that matter.

Through training and repeated exposure to combat, the Spellblade learns to channel mana through their nervous system, briefly accelerating their reactions beyond normal limits. This surge of arcane energy allows them to read danger more quickly and adjust their position in the instant before an attack lands.

To outside observers, the movement appears insignificant—a slight shift of the shoulder, a subtle turn of the body, or a single step placed at precisely the right moment. Yet those tiny adjustments often mean the difference between a devastating blow and a harmless miss.

At Rank 1, Arcane Reflex represents the beginning of this discipline. The Spellblade learns to instinctively call upon mana when threatened, increasing their ability to evade incoming attacks.

### Effects

When you are targeted by an attack, you may activate Arcane Reflex as a Reaction.

- Spend **12 MP**.
- Gain **+1 AC** against the triggering attack.
- This bonus applies only to the attack that triggered the reaction.
- Does not protect against environmental hazards.
- Cannot be used while unable to react.
- Does not affect saving throws.

#### Timing

- Must be declared before the attack roll is resolved.
- May only be used once per turn.
- Uses an action from you next round.

### Lore

The earliest Spellblade instructors taught that survival begins with awareness. Before a warrior can master advanced techniques, they must first learn to recognise danger and respond to it without hesitation.

Arcane Reflex was developed as a means of enhancing this instinct through mana. Rather than creating barriers or relying on heavy armour, the Spellblade learns to trust their reactions and use magic to sharpen them.

Many apprentices underestimate the value of such a simple technique. Veteran Spellblades rarely make the same mistake. They understand that surviving a battle is often more important than winning a single exchange.

Among the older duelling schools, students are often told that every great Spellblade has one thing in common: they lived long enough to become one.

> "Victory belongs to those who survive long enough to claim it."
>
> — Blademaster Kaelis Vorn, Instructor of the Azure Path

## Rank 2
### Description

As the Spellblade's mastery of Arcane Reflex grows, they learn that avoidance is not always possible. Even the fastest reaction cannot prevent every strike from finding its mark.

Rather than relying solely on evasion, the Spellblade learns to reinforce their body with mana at the moment of impact. Arcane energy instinctively flows to vulnerable areas, lessening the force of incoming blows and reducing the harm suffered when an attack cannot be completely avoided.

This technique requires precise timing. Too early and mana is wasted. Too late and the attack lands with full force. Through constant training, the Spellblade develops the instinct to react at exactly the right moment.

At Rank 2, Arcane Reflex evolves from simple avoidance into a layered defensive technique. The Spellblade becomes harder to hit and more resilient when they are struck.

### Effects

When you are targeted by an attack, you may activate Arcane Reflex as a Reaction.

- Spend **15 MP**.
- Gain **+2 AC** against the triggering attack.
- This bonus applies only to the attack that triggered the reaction.
- Does not protect against environmental hazards.
- Cannot be used while unable to react.
- Does not affect saving throws.

#### Timing

- Must be declared before the attack roll is resolved.
- May only be used once per turn.
- Uses an action from you next round.

### Lore

Among veteran Spellblades, Rank 2 is often called the Lesson of Reality. It teaches a simple truth: perfection is impossible.

No matter how skilled a warrior becomes, there will always be attacks that cannot be completely avoided. The difference between a novice and a master is not whether they are hit, but how they respond when they are.

The arcane reinforcement techniques used by Spellblades were originally developed during the Age of Fractured Crowns, when battlefield mages sought ways to survive against heavily armoured opponents. Rather than matching strength with strength, they learned to redirect and disperse force through carefully controlled mana flows.

Modern Spellblades continue this tradition. Every successful use of Arcane Reflex strengthens the connection between instinct and magic, allowing them to survive situations that would cripple lesser combatants.

> "The greatest warriors are not those who never fall. They are those who learn how to fall without breaking."
>
> — High Spellblade Arkanis Thorne, Warden of the Azure Depths

## Rank 3
### Description

A seasoned Spellblade understands that combat is a balance between avoidance and endurance. While Arcane Reflex allows them to evade many attacks, experience teaches that not every strike can be escaped completely.

As their control over mana improves, the Spellblade learns to instinctively direct arcane energy to vulnerable areas of the body at the moment of impact. This reinforcement does not stop an attack, but it can lessen the force behind it and prevent potentially devastating injuries.

The process occurs almost subconsciously. The moment danger is recognised, mana surges through the body, sharpening reflexes while simultaneously preparing for the possibility of failure. If the attack misses, the Spellblade avoids harm entirely. If it lands, the mana absorbs part of the impact.

At Rank 3, Arcane Reflex becomes a complete defensive technique, providing both improved evasion and limited protection when avoidance alone is not enough.

### Effects

When you are targeted by an attack, you may activate Arcane Reflex as a Reaction.

- Spend **18 MP**.
- Gain **+3 AC** against the triggering attack.
- This bonus applies only to the attack that triggered the reaction.
- Does not protect against environmental hazards.
- Cannot be used while unable to react.
- Does not affect saving throws.

#### Timing

- Must be declared before the attack roll is resolved.
- May only be used once per turn.
- Uses your Reaction for the round.

### Lore

Among the ancient Spellblade Orders, Rank 3 is known as the Stage of Resilience. It marks the point where a practitioner learns that survival is not determined solely by avoiding danger, but by enduring it when necessary.

The earliest forms of Arcane Mitigation were developed during prolonged border wars where Spellblades often found themselves outnumbered and unable to evade every attack. By learning to reinforce their bodies with mana at the moment of impact, they dramatically improved their chances of surviving extended engagements.

Veteran instructors often describe this stage as a shift in mindset. Students stop viewing defense as a single action and begin understanding it as a layered system. First avoid the attack. If that fails, lessen the damage. If that fails, remain standing.

Many Spellblades consider Rank 3 the moment Arcane Reflex becomes truly reliable, transforming it from a useful trick into a cornerstone of battlefield survival.

> "The perfect defense is not avoiding every blow. It is surviving the ones you cannot."
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aethon Vale, Master of the Sapphire Hall

## Rank 4
### Description

Arcane Reflex evolves beyond simple defense and becomes a tool of battlefield control. The Spellblade no longer focuses solely on avoiding danger or enduring a strike—they learn to use every attack against them as an opportunity to reposition and reclaim the advantage.

Through years of combat experience, the Spellblade's reactions become intertwined with their mana flow. The moment an attack is launched, their body instinctively prepares not only to evade or mitigate the strike, but also to move into a more favorable position.

To observers, the movement appears unnatural. An attack is thrown, a flash of mana erupts around the Spellblade, and suddenly they are somewhere else entirely. What seemed like a successful attack becomes an opening for the Spellblade to exploit.

At Rank 4, Arcane Reflex transforms from a purely defensive talent into a tactical one. Surviving is no longer the goal—controlling the battlefield is.

### Effects

When you are targeted by an attack, you may activate Arcane Reflex as a Reaction.

- Spend **21 MP**.
- Gain **+4 AC** against the triggering attack.
- This bonus applies only to the triggering attack.
- Does not protect against environmental hazards.
- Cannot be used while unable to react.
- Does not affect saving throws.

#### Timing

- Must be declared before the attack roll is resolved.
- May only be used once per turn.
- Uses your Reaction for the round.

#### Arcane Mitigation

If the triggering attack still hits:

- Reduce the damage taken by **1d4**. Can not reduce damage to 0.

### Lore

Among veteran Spellblades, Rank 4 is known as the Stage of Control. At this point, practitioners stop reacting to the battlefield and begin shaping it.

The technique was refined during the Wars of the Shattered Frontier, where Spellblades frequently fought against numerically superior forces. Rather than remaining locked in place against overwhelming odds, they learned to transform enemy attacks into opportunities for movement.

Masters of Arcane Reflex often appear impossible to pin down. Every attack seems to place them exactly where they wish to be, turning an enemy's aggression into a tool for their own positioning.

Many young Spellblades believe Arcane Reflex exists to avoid damage. Experienced masters know the truth: avoiding damage is merely the beginning. The real purpose is deciding where the battle happens.

> "A master does not avoid danger. They decide where danger is allowed to exist."
>
> — High Spellblade Arkanis Thorne, Warden of the Azure Depths

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Reflex reaches its pinnacle, transforming the Spellblade's defensive instincts into a seamless blend of awareness, protection, and opportunity. At this stage, reacting to danger is no longer a conscious decision—it is an extension of the Spellblade's very nature.

The moment an attack is launched, mana surges through the body, enhancing perception, reinforcing vulnerable areas, and preparing a path of escape before the threat has fully materialised. Every motion becomes precise, efficient, and deliberate.

What separates masters from apprentices is not merely their ability to survive an attack, but their ability to turn that survival into an advantage. A failed strike against a master Spellblade often becomes the first step toward an enemy's defeat.

At Rank 5, Arcane Reflex no longer exists solely to prevent harm. It allows the Spellblade to seize control of the battle's momentum and create openings where none previously existed.

### Effects

When you are targeted by an attack, you may activate Arcane Reflex as a Reaction.

- Spend **24 MP**.
- Gain **+4 AC** against the triggering attack.
- This bonus applies only to the triggering attack.
- Does not protect against environmental hazards.
- Cannot be used while unable to react.
- Does not affect saving throws.

#### Timing

- Must be declared before the attack roll is resolved.
- May only be used once per turn.
- Uses your Reaction for the round.

#### Arcane Mitigation

If the triggering attack still hits:

- Reduce the damage taken by **1d6**.

#### Arcane Reposition

After the triggering attack resolves, whether it hits or misses:

- Instantly move up to **3 metres** to an unoccupied space you can see.
- This movement does **not** provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- You may move through enemy spaces but cannot end your movement inside one.
- You cannot move through solid walls, magical barriers, or impassable terrain.

#### Tactical Uses

Arcane Reposition may be used to:

- Break enemy engagement.
- Move behind cover.
- Reposition for your next attack.
- Escape hazardous terrain.
- Create distance from dangerous opponents.

### Lore

The oldest Spellblade records describe Rank 5 as the Stage of Anticipation. Practitioners no longer react to attacks in the traditional sense. Instead, they appear to move before danger fully manifests, as though they instinctively understand the shape of the battle moments before it unfolds.

Stories of legendary Spellblades often speak of warriors who seemed untouchable in combat. Opponents would launch strike after strike, only to find their target already gone, standing elsewhere with blade in hand and a counterattack prepared.

Scholars debate whether this level of Arcane Reflex is simply the result of extraordinary training or whether prolonged exposure to mana grants fleeting glimpses of future possibilities. Most Spellblades dismiss such theories, claiming that experience and discipline are sufficient explanations.

Whatever the truth, masters of Arcane Reflex are feared throughout Asteria. Every missed attack places them in a stronger position than before, turning an enemy's aggression into the very tool that leads to their downfall.

> "The novice reacts to danger. The master has already moved."
>
> — Grandmaster Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Prerequisites
None

## Scaling
