# Channel Divinity

## Overview
Your devotion has opened a permanent spiritual connection between yourself and your chosen patron. Divine power now flows through that bond, allowing your patron’s influence to shape your abilities, miracles and sacred presence.

Channel Divinity does not grant a universal effect of its own. Instead, it unlocks the Rank I Channel Divinity effects recorded on your patron’s page. These effects represent the unique blessings, restrictions and divine influence granted by the being you serve.

Some patrons may strengthen healing, protection or restoration, while others influence death, warfare, knowledge, nature or fate. Whatever form the connection takes, its power is determined entirely by the patron rather than by the Cleric talent itself.

## Rank 1
### Description

Your devotion has opened a permanent spiritual connection between yourself and your chosen patron. Divine power now flows through that bond, allowing your patron’s influence to shape your abilities, miracles and sacred presence.

Channel Divinity does not grant a universal effect of its own. Instead, it unlocks the Rank I Channel Divinity effects recorded on your patron’s page. These effects represent the unique blessings, restrictions and divine influence granted by the being you serve.

Some patrons may strengthen healing, protection or restoration, while others influence death, warfare, knowledge, nature or fate. Whatever form the connection takes, its power is determined entirely by the patron rather than by the Cleric talent itself.

### Effects

- Channel Divinity is a **passive talent** and requires no action or resource cost.
- Upon unlocking this talent, you gain access to the **Rank I Channel Divinity effects** listed on your chosen patron’s page.
- Channel Divinity has no universal mechanical effects of its own.
- All bonuses, penalties, triggers, restrictions and special abilities granted by Channel Divinity are determined entirely by the chosen patron.
- Patron effects granted through Channel Divinity remain active whenever their listed conditions are met.
- Channel Divinity effects may interact with Cleric talents, spells, Blessing Aura or other divine abilities when stated on the patron’s page.
- You cannot benefit from Channel Divinity effects belonging to more than one patron at the same time.
- Changing patrons removes the previous patron’s Channel Divinity effects and replaces them with those of the new patron once the change is accepted by the GM.
- Channel Divinity is considered a **Divine Patron connection** rather than a spell or activated ability.

### Lore

To the faithful, Channel Divinity marks the moment devotion becomes communion. The Cleric no longer reaches toward the divine through prayer alone; their patron has answered by forming a lasting bond through which sacred influence may pass.

This connection differs greatly between religions. Some Clerics feel their patron as warmth beneath the skin, a whisper behind every prayer or a presence that watches through their eyes. Others bear visible signs such as shifting runes, sacred markings, spectral light or changes in their voice when invoking divine authority.

The bond is not ownership, nor does it allow the Cleric to command their patron. It is an agreement of faith and purpose. The patron grants power, but also expects the Cleric to uphold the ideals through which that power was given.

> *“Prayer asks the divine to listen. Channeling begins when the divine answers.”*
>
> — The First Covenant of the Ordained

## Rank 2
### Description

Your spiritual bond with your patron deepens, allowing a greater portion of their divine essence to flow through you. The connection becomes steadier and more responsive, enabling your patron to bestow additional blessings upon those they deem worthy.

As your faith matures, your patron entrusts you with greater responsibilities and reveals more of their divine nature. Every miracle you perform, every blessing you grant and every prayer you answer becomes a reflection of their will. While all Clerics share the same path toward Channel Divinity, the power they ultimately wield remains unique to the deity they serve.

At this stage, your patron's influence extends beyond a single blessing, granting new manifestations that reinforce their domains and strengthen your identity as one of their chosen servants.

### Effects

- Channel Divinity remains a **passive talent**.
- You gain access to the **Rank II Channel Divinity effects** listed on your chosen patron's page.
- You retain all effects gained from **Channel Divinity – Rank I**.
- Channel Divinity has no universal mechanical effects of its own.
- All effects, triggers, bonuses, penalties and restrictions are determined entirely by your chosen patron.
- Patron effects may interact with your **Blessing Aura**, Cleric talents, spells and other divine abilities when specified on the patron's page.
- You cannot benefit from Channel Divinity effects belonging to more than one patron at the same time.
- If your patron changes, all previous Channel Divinity effects are lost and replaced with those granted by your new patron, subject to the GM's approval.
- Channel Divinity is considered a permanent **Divine Patron Connection**.

### Lore

Those who achieve this level of communion are recognised as trusted servants of their deity. The bond between patron and Cleric has grown beyond simple faith, becoming a lasting spiritual covenant that shapes the Cleric's every action. Many temples regard this stage as the beginning of true divine service, where miracles are no longer isolated gifts but natural expressions of the patron's presence.

Experienced Clerics often describe this connection differently. Some hear their patron's guidance as quiet whispers, while others experience vivid dreams, visions or fleeting sensations that direct their path. Regardless of how the bond manifests, all agree that the relationship becomes increasingly personal as their devotion strengthens.

The faithful believe that every act performed through Channel Divinity carries a fragment of the patron's own purpose. It is this shared purpose that separates an ordinary priest from a true Cleric, for their power is no longer borrowed—it is willingly entrusted to them.

> *"Faith opens the door. Trust invites the divine to remain."*
>
> — Archbishop Elion, Keeper of the Sacred Covenant

## Rank 3
### Description

Your soul has become a trusted vessel for your patron's divine essence. The bond between deity and Cleric is no longer one of simple devotion, but one of enduring partnership. Through this connection, your patron entrusts you with greater manifestations of their divine will, allowing their influence to shape your miracles, blessings and sacred authority.

As your understanding of your patron's teachings deepens, so too does the strength of your Channel Divinity. Every prayer carries greater purpose, every blessing reflects more of your deity's nature, and every miracle serves as a reminder that the gods continue to guide the world through their faithful servants.

While every Cleric advances through the same stages of spiritual growth, the path each follows remains unique. No two patrons grant identical gifts, ensuring that every expression of Channel Divinity reflects the ideals, domains and personality of the deity who bestowed it.

### Effects

- Channel Divinity remains a **passive talent**.
- You gain access to the **Rank III Channel Divinity effects** listed on your chosen patron's page.
- You retain all benefits gained from **Channel Divinity – Ranks I and II**.
- Channel Divinity has no universal mechanical effects of its own.
- All effects, triggers, bonuses, penalties and restrictions are determined entirely by your chosen patron.
- Patron effects may interact with your **Blessing Aura**, Cleric talents, spells and other divine abilities whenever specified on the patron's page.
- You cannot benefit from Channel Divinity effects granted by more than one patron at a time.
- If your patron changes, all previous Channel Divinity effects are lost and replaced by those granted by your new patron, subject to the GM's approval.
- Channel Divinity is considered a permanent **Divine Patron Connection**.

### Lore

To reach this level of communion is considered a rare honour among the clergy of Asteria. Senior priests often recognise these individuals not by the miracles they perform, but by the quiet confidence and unwavering faith that surrounds them. Their patron's presence has become a constant companion, guiding their actions and strengthening their resolve in times of doubt.

Ancient texts describe this stage as the beginning of true divine stewardship. The Cleric no longer simply receives blessings—they become an instrument through which their patron's purpose is fulfilled. Each act of compassion, judgement or sacrifice echoes the teachings of the deity they serve, reinforcing the sacred covenant between mortal and divine.

Many faiths believe that only those who remain steadfast in both belief and action are entrusted with such responsibility. To betray a patron's ideals is to risk weakening the very bond that grants these sacred gifts.

> *"Power is not the reward of faith. It is the responsibility entrusted to those who never abandon it."*
>
> — Saint Veridan, Keeper of the Divine Covenant

## Rank 4
### Description

Your connection to your patron has become unshakable, allowing an even greater measure of divine power to flow through your soul. The bond between deity and servant is no longer simply recognised by the faithful—it is undeniable. Your presence alone reflects your patron's authority, and every miracle you perform carries the unmistakable signature of the divine being you serve.

As your spiritual journey continues, your patron entrusts you with deeper mysteries and greater responsibilities. The blessings they bestow become more profound, while their expectations of your faith and devotion grow equally demanding. Every decision you make reflects upon your patron, strengthening the sacred covenant that binds you together.

To those who witness your miracles, it becomes clear that your power is not your own. You are an extension of your patron's will, carrying their influence wherever your journey leads and serving as a living testament to the strength of your faith.

### Effects

- Channel Divinity remains a **passive talent**.
- You gain access to the **Rank IV Channel Divinity effects** listed on your chosen patron's page.
- You retain all benefits gained from **Channel Divinity – Ranks I, II and III**.
- Channel Divinity has no universal mechanical effects of its own.
- All effects, triggers, bonuses, penalties and restrictions are determined entirely by your chosen patron.
- Patron effects may interact with your **Blessing Aura**, Cleric talents, spells and other divine abilities whenever specified on the patron's page.
- You cannot benefit from Channel Divinity effects granted by more than one patron at a time.
- If your patron changes, all previous Channel Divinity effects are removed and replaced with those granted by your new patron, subject to the GM's approval.
- Channel Divinity is considered a permanent **Divine Patron Connection**.

### Lore

Within the grand temples of Asteria, Clerics who attain this level of communion are often regarded as among their patron's greatest mortal representatives. Their unwavering devotion has forged a bond so strong that many believe the deity actively watches over them, guiding their words and deeds in subtle but meaningful ways.

The scriptures of many faiths describe these individuals as "Living Vessels," not because they contain the full power of a god, but because they have proven worthy of carrying a greater fragment of divine purpose than most mortals could endure. Their lives become inseparable from the teachings of their patron, inspiring followers and reminding the world that the gods continue to shape history through those who remain faithful.

Such responsibility is never taken lightly. The stronger the bond becomes, the greater the expectation that the Cleric will uphold the ideals of their patron, for every miracle reflects not only upon the servant, but upon the deity who granted it.

> *"The faithful seek the gods through prayer. The gods answer through those they trust."*
>
> — High Hierophant Lucian, Voice of the Celestial Synod
```

## Rank 5
### Description

Your communion with your patron has reached its highest mortal expression. The divine bond that began as an act of faith has become an unbreakable covenant, allowing your patron's influence to flow through you with unparalleled clarity. You no longer simply receive divine gifts—you have become one of your deity's most trusted representatives within the mortal world.

Every blessing you bestow, every miracle you witness and every sacred rite you perform carries the unmistakable mark of your patron. Their teachings have become inseparable from your own actions, and your unwavering devotion has earned you access to the greatest manifestations of their divine power.

Although every Cleric reaches this pinnacle through the same path of faith, no two Channel Divinities are ever alike. Each patron grants different gifts, responsibilities and expectations, ensuring that every master Cleric reflects the unique ideals and purpose of the deity they faithfully serve.

### Effects

- Channel Divinity remains a **passive talent**.
- You gain access to the **Rank V Channel Divinity effects** listed on your chosen patron's page.
- You retain all benefits gained from **Channel Divinity – Ranks I–IV**.
- Channel Divinity has no universal mechanical effects of its own.
- All effects, bonuses, penalties, triggers and restrictions are determined entirely by your chosen patron.
- Patron effects may interact with your **Blessing Aura**, Cleric talents, spells, miracles and other divine abilities whenever specified on the patron's page.
- You cannot benefit from Channel Divinity effects granted by more than one patron at a time.
- If your patron changes, all previous Channel Divinity effects are lost and replaced by those of your new patron, subject to the GM's approval.
- Channel Divinity is considered a permanent **Divine Patron Connection**.

### Lore

The highest-ranking Clerics are remembered throughout history not because of the miracles they performed, but because of the unwavering bond they shared with their patron. Their presence alone is said to inspire faith, command reverence and remind those around them that the gods remain active within the world of Asteria.

Many sacred texts describe these individuals as the "Chosen Hands" of their deity. While they never possess a god's true power, they are entrusted with carrying their patron's will further than any ordinary servant could. Their lives become examples for future generations, shaping religions, guiding kingdoms and preserving the teachings of their faith long after their mortal journey has ended.

To achieve this level of communion is both an honour and a burden. The patron's greatest gifts are reserved for those whose devotion has never faltered, for divine power without unwavering faith is a trust that can never truly be earned.

> *"The gods do not seek perfect servants. They seek faithful hearts through which their will may endure."*
>
> — Saint Elyndor, First Voice of the Divine Covenant
```

# Chlorokinesis

## Overview
You awaken your first true connection to the living plants around you. By weaving Mana into nearby vegetation and directing it through physical effort, you can command roots, vines, branches, shrubs, and grasses to move at your will.

Unlike conjuration magic, Chlorokinesis cannot create plant life from nothing. Instead, it manipulates vegetation that already exists within the environment, making the battlefield itself an extension of your abilities. Even the smallest patch of roots or overgrown vines can become a useful tool in the hands of a skilled Druid.

Though your control is still limited, you quickly learn that nature rarely needs overwhelming force. A single root can halt a charging enemy, a bent branch can shelter an ally, and a moving vine can uncover what was once hidden.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

You awaken your first true connection to the living plants around you. By weaving Mana into nearby vegetation and directing it through physical effort, you can command roots, vines, branches, shrubs, and grasses to move at your will.

Unlike conjuration magic, Chlorokinesis cannot create plant life from nothing. Instead, it manipulates vegetation that already exists within the environment, making the battlefield itself an extension of your abilities. Even the smallest patch of roots or overgrown vines can become a useful tool in the hands of a skilled Druid.

Though your control is still limited, you quickly learn that nature rarely needs overwhelming force. A single root can halt a charging enemy, a bent branch can shelter an ally, and a moving vine can uncover what was once hidden.

---

### Effects

When casting **Chlorokinesis**, choose **one** of the following techniques:

#### 🌱 Root Snare

Command nearby roots or vines to hinder a creature's movement.

- Target one creature within range.
- The target must make a **D20 Agility Saving Throw** against your **Spell Save DC**.
- **Failure:** The target's movement speed is reduced by **50%** until the end of its next turn.
- **Success:** The target's movement speed is reduced by **25%** until the end of its next turn.

#### 🌿 Living Cover

Manipulate nearby branches, shrubs, or vines to provide protection.

Choose one:

- Grant one creature **Half Cover** until the start of your next turn.
- Create a **2-metre** patch of **Difficult Terrain** until the start of your next turn.

#### 🍃 Verdant Utility

Use nearby vegetation to assist outside of combat.

Examples include:

- Moving vines into climbing ropes.
- Clearing overgrown pathways.
- Revealing hidden tracks or objects.
- Pulling a light object within range.
- Moving foliage to improve visibility.

- Gain **+10** to one **Nature**, **Survival**, or **Tracking** **D100 Skill Check** related to the action.

---

### Lore

Among the Druidic Circles, Chlorokinesis is considered the first lesson in working alongside nature rather than commanding it. Young Druids are taught that every plant possesses its own purpose, and their role is simply to guide that purpose instead of forcing it.

Many apprentices spend months practising with a single vine before they are trusted to manipulate larger plants. The exercise is less about power and more about patience, teaching that even the smallest movement can change the outcome of a journey or battle.

To an outsider, the forest may appear still. To a Druid, every leaf, root, and branch is waiting for a gentle request.

---

> *"Do not ask how strong a tree is. Ask how willing it is to help."*  
> — **Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your bond with the natural world deepens, allowing your influence over plants to become stronger, faster, and more deliberate. The vegetation around you no longer reacts with hesitation—it answers your call with growing confidence.

Roots spread farther beneath the earth, vines tighten with greater strength, and branches bend more naturally to your commands. What once required careful concentration now feels instinctive, allowing you to adapt the battlefield in moments.

Experienced Druids understand that victory is not always won through overwhelming force. Restricting a foe's movement, shielding an ally from danger, or opening a safe path through dense wilderness can prove just as decisive as any spell. Chlorokinesis teaches that nature rewards those who think ahead, shaping the environment to favour patience, preparation, and harmony.

---

### Effects

When casting **Chlorokinesis**, choose **one** of the following techniques:

#### 🌱 Root Snare

Command roots and vines to bind a creature's legs.

- Target one creature within range.
- The target must make a **D20 Agility Saving Throw** against your **Spell Save DC**.
- **Failure:** The target becomes **Snared** until the end of its next turn.
  - A Snared creature's movement becomes **0 metres**.
- **Success:** The target's movement speed is reduced by **50%** until the end of its next turn.

#### 🌿 Living Cover

Command nearby vegetation to grow into a stronger defensive position.

Choose one:

- Grant one creature **Half Cover** until the start of your next turn.
- Create a **3-metre** area of **Difficult Terrain** that lasts for **2 rounds**.
- Block a narrow passage with dense vines or branches, requiring a creature to spend **2 metres of movement for every metre travelled** through the obstacle.

#### 🍃 Verdant Utility

Manipulate surrounding plant life to assist exploration and survival.

Examples include:

- Growing stronger vine ladders.
- Retrieving objects from difficult locations.
- Revealing concealed paths.
- Stabilising loose terrain.
- Clearing dense undergrowth.
- Pulling or pushing unattended objects using vines.

- Gain **+15** to one **Nature**, **Survival**, or **Tracking** **D100 Skill Check** related to the chosen action.

---

### Lore

As Druids continue to refine Chlorokinesis, they discover that plants possess remarkable resilience and adaptability. Every root searches endlessly for water, every vine seeks something to climb, and every branch instinctively reaches toward the light.

Rather than forcing these instincts, experienced practitioners simply encourage them. This philosophy lies at the heart of Druidic teaching: nature is strongest when allowed to follow its own course.

Those who master this lesson begin to view every forest, meadow, and overgrown ruin not as scenery, but as a living companion ready to answer their call.

---

> *"Power is not making the forest obey. Power is asking so gently that it chooses to."*  
> — **Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 3
### Description

Your mastery of Chlorokinesis allows you to command multiple plants with confidence, transforming the natural world into a powerful extension of your will. What once required careful focus now flows instinctively, as roots burst from the earth, vines lash outward, and branches bend to answer your call.

The battlefield itself begins to change around you. Dense undergrowth becomes a hindrance to your enemies, towering trees become living shields, and tangled vines become relentless restraints. Every forest, meadow, and overgrown ruin offers new opportunities to shape the course of battle.

Veteran Druids know that nature does not seek to destroy—it seeks to endure. By redirecting that enduring strength, they can halt advancing foes, protect companions, and manipulate the terrain without disturbing the balance they have sworn to preserve.

---

### Effects

When casting **Chlorokinesis**, choose **one** of the following techniques:

#### 🌱 Entangling Roots

Command a network of roots and vines to erupt beneath your enemies.

- Choose a **3-metre radius** within range.
- All creatures in the area must make a **D20 Agility Saving Throw** against your **Spell Save DC**.
- **Failure:** The creature becomes **Restrained** until the end of its next turn.
- **Success:** The creature's movement speed is reduced by **50%** until the end of its next turn.
- The affected area becomes **Difficult Terrain** for **3 rounds**.

#### 🌿 Living Barrier

Weave branches, vines, and shrubs into a durable natural wall.

Choose one:

- Create a **4-metre-wide**, **2-metre-high** living barrier that grants **Three-Quarters Cover**.
- Create a **4-metre** area of **Difficult Terrain** that lasts for **3 rounds**.
- Seal a doorway, pathway, or narrow passage with dense vegetation. The obstruction can be cleared with a successful **Strength Check** against your **Spell Save DC**.

#### 🍃 Verdant Utility

Manipulate large amounts of vegetation to aid exploration or survival.

Examples include:

- Creating stable vine bridges.
- Revealing concealed trails or entrances.
- Moving fallen trees or heavy branches.
- Constructing temporary platforms.
- Clearing dense vegetation for safe travel.
- Retrieving distant objects using living vines.

- Gain **+20** to one **Nature**, **Survival**, or **Tracking** **D100 Skill Check** related to the chosen action.

---

### Lore

By the third stage of Chlorokinesis, a Druid no longer sees individual plants—they see an interconnected living system. Every root communicates through the earth, every vine searches for support, and every tree contributes to the harmony of the forest.

Experienced Druids become conductors of this silent symphony, encouraging countless plants to work together toward a single purpose. Their power does not come from domination, but from understanding how every part of nature supports another.

It is said that when an Archdruid enters an ancient forest, the woodland recognises them long before they speak. Leaves rustle without wind, branches bow gently aside, and roots shift beneath their feet—not from magic alone, but from mutual respect between guardian and grove.

---

> *"One vine may catch a traveller. A thousand vines may change the course of a battle."*  
> — **Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 4
### Description

Your communion with the natural world has reached a level where entire groves answer your call without hesitation. Roots surge through the earth with tremendous force, towering hedges rise within moments, and ancient branches twist into formidable barriers. Every living plant within your reach becomes a willing extension of your intent.

At this stage, Chlorokinesis is no longer simply about controlling individual plants—it is about shaping the battlefield itself. Dense vegetation slows advancing enemies, towering walls protect your allies, and the wilderness bends to create paths where none existed before.

Master Druids understand that nature is neither cruel nor merciful. It simply adapts. By embracing this lesson, you learn to guide the forest's endless resilience, turning even the smallest patch of greenery into a decisive advantage.

---

### Effects

When casting **Chlorokinesis**, choose **one** of the following techniques:

#### 🌱 Verdant Grasp

Command an immense network of roots and vines to erupt across the battlefield.

- Choose a **5-metre radius** within range.
- All creatures in the area must make a **D20 Agility Saving Throw** against your **Spell Save DC**.
- **Failure:** The creature becomes **Restrained** for **2 rounds**.
- **Success:** The creature's movement speed is reduced by **50%** for **2 rounds**.
- The affected area becomes **Difficult Terrain** for **4 rounds**.

#### 🌿 Living Bastion

Shape surrounding vegetation into a powerful defensive structure.

Choose one:

- Create a living wall up to **6 metres wide** and **3 metres high** that grants **Full Cover**.
- Create a **6-metre** area of **Difficult Terrain** for **4 rounds**.
- Seal a doorway, bridge, tunnel, or narrow passage with dense vegetation. Creatures must succeed on a **Strength Check** against your **Spell Save DC** to force their way through.

#### 🍃 Verdant Dominion

Command large sections of natural vegetation to assist exploration and survival.

Examples include:

- Creating broad vine bridges capable of supporting a party.
- Opening safe routes through dense forests.
- Stabilising collapsing embankments or hillsides.
- Raising natural platforms for climbing.
- Revealing hidden ruins or forgotten pathways.
- Manipulating large trees, shrubs, and vines to reshape the surrounding environment.

- Gain **+25** to one **Nature**, **Survival**, or **Tracking** **D100 Skill Check** related to the chosen action.

---

### Lore

Among the oldest Druidic Circles, this level of mastery is known as **The Forest's Embrace**. It marks the point where a Druid ceases to feel like an individual standing within nature and instead becomes part of its living rhythm.

Veteran Druids often describe hearing the quiet whispers of roots beneath the soil and sensing the slow heartbeat of ancient trees. To them, every forest is a community of countless lives working together, each willing to lend its strength when called upon with respect.

Few sights inspire greater caution than a master of Chlorokinesis standing calmly within an ancient woodland. For while the Druid may appear alone, the forest itself has already risen to stand beside them.

---

> *"The forest does not march to war. It simply reminds trespassers that they were never alone."*  
> — **Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 5
### Description

You have achieved true mastery over Chlorokinesis, becoming a living conduit through which the natural world expresses its will. The distinction between your command and the forest's response has all but disappeared. With little more than a thought, roots erupt from the earth, towering hedgerows rise into defensive fortifications, and ancient trees bend their branches to shield those under your protection.

Where novice Druids manipulate individual plants, you orchestrate entire ecosystems. Every vine, shrub, flower, and towering tree within your reach contributes to a unified purpose. The battlefield itself becomes alive, restricting your enemies while providing sanctuary for your allies.

To those who witness this mastery, it appears as though the forest itself has awakened. Yet experienced Druids know the truth—they are not rulers of nature, but trusted guardians who have earned its unwavering cooperation through years of respect and understanding.

---

### Effects

When casting **Chlorokinesis**, choose **one** of the following techniques:

#### 🌱 Forest's Embrace

Command an immense network of roots, vines, and vegetation to seize the battlefield.

- Choose an **8-metre radius** within range.
- All creatures in the area must make a **D20 Agility Saving Throw** against your **Spell Save DC**.
- **Failure:** The creature becomes **Restrained** for **2 rounds**.
- **Success:** The creature's movement speed is reduced by **50%** for **3 rounds**.
- The affected area becomes **Difficult Terrain** for **5 rounds**.
- A creature restrained by this ability may use its action to repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

#### 🌿 Verdant Fortress

Shape the surrounding vegetation into a formidable natural stronghold.

Choose one:

- Create a living structure up to **8 metres wide** and **4 metres high** that grants **Full Cover**.
- Create an **8-metre** area of **Difficult Terrain** lasting **5 rounds**.
- Seal a large doorway, bridge, canyon pass, or similar opening with dense vegetation. Creatures must succeed on a **Strength Check** against your **Spell Save DC** to force a passage.

#### 🍃 Nature's Dominion

Exercise complete control over nearby vegetation to overcome environmental challenges.

Examples include:

- Constructing large vine bridges capable of supporting groups and mounts.
- Clearing extensive overgrowth to reveal roads or ruins.
- Raising natural platforms and stairways through trees or cliffs.
- Moving fallen trees and dense vegetation to reshape the landscape.
- Concealing campsites or entrances beneath living foliage.
- Guiding large sections of vegetation to create safe travel routes.

- Gain **+30** to one **Nature**, **Survival**, or **Tracking** **D100 Skill Check** related to the chosen action.

---

### Lore

Only a handful of Druids within each generation reach this level of communion with the living world. They are no longer recognised merely as practitioners of Chlorokinesis, but as true Wardens of the Wild—individuals whose presence alone calms forests and stirs ancient groves into quiet life.

Legends tell of these masters halting invading armies without drawing blood, raising forests to block advancing forces, and restoring devastated lands simply by guiding nature back into balance. Such feats are remembered not because they display overwhelming power, but because they embody perfect harmony between mortal and wilderness.

The oldest circles teach that this is not the end of a Druid's journey, but the beginning of a deeper responsibility. Once the forest answers your every call, it also begins to trust you with its future.

---

> *"Mastery is not the moment the forest obeys you. It is the moment the forest believes your voice is its own."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

many apprentices spend months practising with a single vine before they are trusted to manipulate larger plants. the exercise is less about power and more about patience, teaching that even the smallest movement can change the outcome of a journey or battle.

to an outsider, the forest may appear still. to a druid, every leaf, root, and branch is waiting for a gentle request.

---

> *"do not ask how strong a tree is. ask how willing it is to help."*  
> — **archdruid rowan thornbark, warden of the emerald wilds**

## rank 2
### description

your bond with the natural world deepens, allowing your influence over plants to become stronger, faster, and more deliberate. the vegetation around you no longer reacts with hesitation—it answers your call with growing confidence.

roots spread farther beneath the earth, vines tighten with greater strength, and branches bend more naturally to your commands. what once required careful concentration now feels instinctive, allowing you to adapt the battlefield in moments.

experienced druids understand that victory is not always won through overwhelming force. restricting a foe's movement, shielding an ally from danger, or opening a safe path through dense wilderness can prove just as decisive as any spell. chlorokinesis teaches that nature rewards those who think ahead, shaping the environment to favour patience, preparation, and harmony.

---

### effects

when casting **chlorokinesis**, choose **one** of the following techniques:

#### 🌱 root snare

command roots and vines to bind a creature's legs.

- target one creature within range.
- the target must make a **d20 agility saving throw** against your **spell save dc**.
- **failure:** the target becomes **snared** until the end of its next turn.
  - a snared creature's movement becomes **0 metres**.
- **success:** the target's movement speed is reduced by **50%** until the end of its next turn.

#### 🌿 living cover

command nearby vegetation to grow into a stronger defensive position.

choose one:

- grant one creature **half cover** until the start of your next turn.
- create a **3-metre** area of **difficult terrain** that lasts for **2 rounds**.
- block a narrow passage with dense vines or branches, requiring a creature to spend **2 metres of movement for every metre travelled** through the obstacle.

#### 🍃 verdant utility

manipulate surrounding plant life to assist exploration and survival.

examples include:

- growing stronger vine ladders.
- retrieving objects from difficult locations.
- revealing concealed paths.
- stabilising loose terrain.
- clearing dense undergrowth.
- pulling or pushing unattended objects using vines.

- gain **+15** to one **nature**, **survival**, or **tracking** **d100 skill check** related to the chosen action.

---

### lore

as druids continue to refine chlorokinesis, they discover that plants possess remarkable resilience and adaptability. every root searches endlessly for water, every vine seeks something to climb, and every branch instinctively reaches toward the light.

rather than forcing these instincts, experienced practitioners simply encourage them. this philosophy lies at the heart of druidic teaching: nature is strongest when allowed to follow its own course.

those who master this lesson begin to view every forest, meadow, and overgrown ruin not as scenery, but as a living companion ready to answer their call.

---

> *"power is not making the forest obey. power is asking so gently that it chooses to."*  
> — **archdruid rowan thornbark, warden of the emerald wilds**

## rank 3
### description

your mastery of chlorokinesis allows you to command multiple plants with confidence, transforming the natural world into a powerful extension of your will. what once required careful focus now flows instinctively, as roots burst from the earth, vines lash outward, and branches bend to answer your call.

the battlefield itself begins to change around you. dense undergrowth becomes a hindrance to your enemies, towering trees become living shields, and tangled vines become relentless restraints. every forest, meadow, and overgrown ruin offers new opportunities to shape the course of battle.

veteran druids know that nature does not seek to destroy—it seeks to endure. by redirecting that enduring strength, they can halt advancing foes, protect companions, and manipulate the terrain without disturbing the balance they have sworn to preserve.

---

### effects

when casting **chlorokinesis**, choose **one** of the following techniques:

#### 🌱 entangling roots

command a network of roots and vines to erupt beneath your enemies.

- choose a **3-metre radius** within range.
- all creatures in the area must make a **d20 agility saving throw** against your **spell save dc**.
- **failure:** the creature becomes **restrained** until the end of its next turn.
- **success:** the creature's movement speed is reduced by **50%** until the end of its next turn.
- the affected area becomes **difficult terrain** for **3 rounds**.

#### 🌿 living barrier

weave branches, vines, and shrubs into a durable natural wall.

choose one:

- create a **4-metre-wide**, **2-metre-high** living barrier that grants **three-quarters cover**.
- create a **4-metre** area of **difficult terrain** that lasts for **3 rounds**.
- seal a doorway, pathway, or narrow passage with dense vegetation. the obstruction can be cleared with a successful **strength check** against your **spell save dc**.

#### 🍃 verdant utility

manipulate large amounts of vegetation to aid exploration or survival.

examples include:

- creating stable vine bridges.
- revealing concealed trails or entrances.
- moving fallen trees or heavy branches.
- constructing temporary platforms.
- clearing dense vegetation for safe travel.
- retrieving distant objects using living vines.

- gain **+20** to one **nature**, **survival**, or **tracking** **d100 skill check** related to the chosen action.

---

### lore

by the third stage of chlorokinesis, a druid no longer sees individual plants—they see an interconnected living system. every root communicates through the earth, every vine searches for support, and every tree contributes to the harmony of the forest.

experienced druids become conductors of this silent symphony, encouraging countless plants to work together toward a single purpose. their power does not come from domination, but from understanding how every part of nature supports another.

it is said that when an archdruid enters an ancient forest, the woodland recognises them long before they speak. leaves rustle without wind, branches bow gently aside, and roots shift beneath their feet—not from magic alone, but from mutual respect between guardian and grove.

---

> *"one vine may catch a traveller. a thousand vines may change the course of a battle."*  
> — **archdruid rowan thornbark, warden of the emerald wilds**

## rank 4
### description

your communion with the natural world has reached a level where entire groves answer your call without hesitation. roots surge through the earth with tremendous force, towering hedges rise within moments, and ancient branches twist into formidable barriers. every living plant within your reach becomes a willing extension of your intent.

at this stage, chlorokinesis is no longer simply about controlling individual plants—it is about shaping the battlefield itself. dense vegetation slows advancing enemies, towering walls protect your allies, and the wilderness bends to create paths where none existed before.

master druids understand that nature is neither cruel nor merciful. it simply adapts. by embracing this lesson, you learn to guide the forest's endless resilience, turning even the smallest patch of greenery into a decisive advantage.

---

### effects

when casting **chlorokinesis**, choose **one** of the following techniques:

#### 🌱 verdant grasp

command an immense network of roots and vines to erupt across the battlefield.

- choose a **5-metre radius** within range.
- all creatures in the area must make a **d20 agility saving throw** against your **spell save dc**.
- **failure:** the creature becomes **restrained** for **2 rounds**.
- **success:** the creature's movement speed is reduced by **50%** for **2 rounds**.
- the affected area becomes **difficult terrain** for **4 rounds**.

#### 🌿 living bastion

shape surrounding vegetation into a powerful defensive structure.

choose one:

- create a living wall up to **6 metres wide** and **3 metres high** that grants **full cover**.
- create a **6-metre** area of **difficult terrain** for **4 rounds**.
- seal a doorway, bridge, tunnel, or narrow passage with dense vegetation. creatures must succeed on a **strength check** against your **spell save dc** to force their way through.

#### 🍃 verdant dominion

command large sections of natural vegetation to assist exploration and survival.

examples include:

- creating broad vine bridges capable of supporting a party.
- opening safe routes through dense forests.
- stabilising collapsing embankments or hillsides.
- raising natural platforms for climbing.
- revealing hidden ruins or forgotten pathways.
- manipulating large trees, shrubs, and vines to reshape the surrounding environment.

- gain **+25** to one **nature**, **survival**, or **tracking** **d100 skill check** related to the chosen action.

---

### lore

among the oldest druidic circles, this level of mastery is known as **the forest's embrace**. it marks the point where a druid ceases to feel like an individual standing within nature and instead becomes part of its living rhythm.

veteran druids often describe hearing the quiet whispers of roots beneath the soil and sensing the slow heartbeat of ancient trees. to them, every forest is a community of countless lives working together, each willing to lend its strength when called upon with respect.

few sights inspire greater caution than a master of chlorokinesis standing calmly within an ancient woodland. for while the druid may appear alone, the forest itself has already risen to stand beside them.

---

> *"the forest does not march to war. it simply reminds trespassers that they were never alone."*  
> — **archdruid rowan thornbark, warden of the emerald wilds**

## rank 5
### description

you have achieved true mastery over chlorokinesis, becoming a living conduit through which the natural world expresses its will. the distinction between your command and the forest's response has all but disappeared. with little more than a thought, roots erupt from the earth, towering hedgerows rise into defensive fortifications, and ancient trees bend their branches to shield those under your protection.

where novice druids manipulate individual plants, you orchestrate entire ecosystems. every vine, shrub, flower, and towering tree within your reach contributes to a unified purpose. the battlefield itself becomes alive, restricting your enemies while providing sanctuary for your allies.

to those who witness this mastery, it appears as though the forest itself has awakened. yet experienced druids know the truth—they are not rulers of nature, but trusted guardians who have earned its unwavering cooperation through years of respect and understanding.

---

### effects

when casting **chlorokinesis**, choose **one** of the following techniques:

#### 🌱 forest's embrace

command an immense network of roots, vines, and vegetation to seize the battlefield.

- choose an **8-metre radius** within range.
- all creatures in the area must make a **d20 agility saving throw** against your **spell save dc**.
- **failure:** the creature becomes **restrained** for **2 rounds**.
- **success:** the creature's movement speed is reduced by **50%** for **3 rounds**.
- the affected area becomes **difficult terrain** for **5 rounds**.
- a creature restrained by this ability may use its action to repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

#### 🌿 verdant fortress

shape the surrounding vegetation into a formidable natural stronghold.

choose one:

- create a living structure up to **8 metres wide** and **4 metres high** that grants **full cover**.
- create an **8-metre** area of **difficult terrain** lasting **5 rounds**.
- seal a large doorway, bridge, canyon pass, or similar opening with dense vegetation. creatures must succeed on a **strength check** against your **spell save dc** to force a passage.

#### 🍃 nature's dominion

exercise complete control over nearby vegetation to overcome environmental challenges.

examples include:

- constructing large vine bridges capable of supporting groups and mounts.
- clearing extensive overgrowth to reveal roads or ruins.
- raising natural platforms and stairways through trees or cliffs.
- moving fallen trees and dense vegetation to reshape the landscape.
- concealing campsites or entrances beneath living foliage.
- guiding large sections of vegetation to create safe travel routes.

- gain **+30** to one **nature**, **survival**, or **tracking** **d100 skill check** related to the chosen action.

---

### lore

only a handful of druids within each generation reach this level of communion with the living world. they are no longer recognised merely as practitioners of chlorokinesis, but as true wardens of the wild—individuals whose presence alone calms forests and stirs ancient groves into quiet life.

legends tell of these masters halting invading armies without drawing blood, raising forests to block advancing forces, and restoring devastated lands simply by guiding nature back into balance. such feats are remembered not because they display overwhelming power, but because they embody perfect harmony between mortal and wilderness.

the oldest circles teach that this is not the end of a druid's journey, but the beginning of a deeper responsibility. once the forest answers your every call, it also begins to trust you with its future.

---

> *"mastery is not the moment the forest obeys you. it is the moment the forest believes your voice is its own."*  
> — **grand archdruid rowan thornbark, first warden of the emerald wilds**

# Commune with Nature

## Overview
You still your thoughts and attune yourself to the rhythm of the natural world, allowing the land to share its knowledge. Every tree, stream, mountain, and blade of grass carries traces of the life that has passed through it, and by opening your spirit you begin to understand these silent echoes.

Commune with Nature does not grant perfect vision or reveal every secret. Instead, it provides instinctive awareness of your surroundings, helping you understand the health of the land, recognise natural features, and sense the presence of nearby wildlife. The stronger and more vibrant the environment, the clearer these impressions become.

To a Druid, nature is not simply a place—it is a living companion with countless stories to tell. This talent marks the first step in learning to listen.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

You still your thoughts and attune yourself to the rhythm of the natural world, allowing the land to share its knowledge. Every tree, stream, mountain, and blade of grass carries traces of the life that has passed through it, and by opening your spirit you begin to understand these silent echoes.

Commune with Nature does not grant perfect vision or reveal every secret. Instead, it provides instinctive awareness of your surroundings, helping you understand the health of the land, recognise natural features, and sense the presence of nearby wildlife. The stronger and more vibrant the environment, the clearer these impressions become.

To a Druid, nature is not simply a place—it is a living companion with countless stories to tell. This talent marks the first step in learning to listen.

---

### Effects

- Spend **10 MP** to enter a state of communion with the surrounding natural environment.
- Commune with Nature lasts for **10 minutes**.
- While active, you become aware of the natural environment within a **50-metre radius**.
- You may determine:
  - Whether the land is **healthy**, **damaged**, or **corrupted**.
  - The location of significant natural features, such as rivers, caves, cliffs, ancient trees, clearings, or dense vegetation.
  - The presence of nearby natural water sources.
- You become aware of the **general presence** of nearby beasts and naturally occurring creatures, but not their exact location, number, or species.
- Gain **+2** to **Nature**, **Survival**, and **Tracking** **D20 Skill Checks** while Commune with Nature is active.
- You can identify whether an area has recently been affected by natural events, including storms, floods, fires, landslides, or earthquakes.
- This talent cannot detect humanoids, constructs, undead, or creatures completely severed from the natural world.
- Areas protected by powerful anti-divination or anti-nature magic may prevent or distort the information received.

---

### Lore

Among the oldest Druidic teachings, it is said that the world is constantly speaking. The rustling of leaves, the movement of rivers, and the shifting of roots beneath the earth form an ancient language that predates kingdoms, dragons, and even the first mortal races.

Most travellers hear only the wind. Druids hear warnings carried through birdsong, the passing of great beasts within the soil, and the quiet sorrow of forests scarred by corruption. These impressions are subtle, but those who learn to trust them rarely lose their way.

Every great Archdruid began with a single lesson: before you can ask nature for its strength, you must first learn to listen.

---

> *"The world has whispered since the dawn of time. Wisdom belongs to those who choose to listen."*  
> — **Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your connection to the natural world strengthens, allowing the voices of the land to become clearer and more detailed. What once felt like vague instincts now forms a coherent understanding of the environment around you. The forest no longer merely tells you that life is present—it begins to reveal how that life exists within its ecosystem.

As your communion deepens, you become increasingly aware of the relationships between the creatures, plants, and terrain around you. Disturbed habitats, unnatural changes, and damaged ecosystems become immediately apparent, while the flow of nature itself guides your senses toward areas of significance.

Experienced Druids often rely upon this gift before making camp, exploring unknown wilderness, or tracking dangerous beasts. By trusting the wisdom of the land rather than their own eyes alone, they rarely find themselves surprised by the natural world.

---

### Effects

- Spend **15 MP** to enter a state of communion with the surrounding natural environment.
- Commune with Nature lasts for **15 minutes**.
- While active, you become aware of the natural environment within a **75-metre radius**.
- You may determine:
  - Whether the land is **healthy**, **damaged**, **corrupted**, or **recovering**.
  - The location of significant natural features, including rivers, lakes, caves, cliffs, ancient trees, dense forests, and clearings.
  - The presence of nearby natural water sources and whether the water is safe or polluted.
- You become aware of the **approximate size** of nearby groups of natural creatures (solitary, small group, herd, or large gathering), though not their exact location or species.
- Gain **+4** to **Nature**, **Survival**, and **Tracking** **D20 Skill Checks** while Commune with Nature is active.
- You can determine whether an area has been recently disturbed by:
  - Natural disasters.
  - Large beasts.
  - Extensive logging or deforestation.
  - Wildfires.
  - Unnatural environmental damage.
- You can sense the general direction of the strongest concentration of natural life within range.
- This talent cannot detect humanoids, constructs, undead, or creatures completely severed from the natural world.
- Areas protected by powerful anti-divination or anti-nature magic may prevent or distort the information received.

---

### Lore

To most people, a forest is simply a collection of trees. To a seasoned Druid, it is a living community whose countless voices weave together into a single harmonious chorus. Every creature leaves an imprint upon its surroundings, every river remembers those who drink from it, and every ancient tree silently watches over generations of life.

With experience comes clarity. Druids who reach this level of communion begin to recognise patterns invisible to others—the migration of wildlife, the scars left by ancient disasters, and the subtle imbalance caused by corruption or reckless civilisation.

Among many circles, this stage is known as the **Listening Grove**, where apprentices first realise that nature does not merely answer questions—it freely shares its wisdom with those patient enough to hear it.

---

> *"The land remembers every footprint. Listen carefully, and it will tell you who walked before you."*  
> — **Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 3
### Description

Your communion with the natural world has matured into a profound spiritual bond. The land no longer offers only glimpses of its condition—it willingly shares the stories unfolding within it. Every forest, mountain, river, and valley speaks through countless subtle impressions, allowing you to perceive the balance of life with remarkable clarity.

As your understanding grows, you begin to recognise the relationships between every living thing. Predator and prey, healthy groves and dying woodlands, thriving rivers and polluted streams all become part of a greater picture. By reading these natural currents, you can often anticipate danger long before it becomes visible.

Many Druids regard this level of mastery as the point where one truly becomes a guardian of the wild. Rather than merely surviving within nature, you begin to understand its needs, its struggles, and the delicate balance that sustains all life.

---

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to enter a state of communion with the surrounding natural environment.
- Commune with Nature lasts for **20 minutes**.
- While active, you become aware of the natural environment within a **100-metre radius**.
- You may determine:
  - Whether the land is **healthy**, **damaged**, **recovering**, **corrupted**, or **unnaturally altered**.
  - The location of significant natural landmarks, including rivers, lakes, caves, cliffs, ancient trees, dense forests, ruins reclaimed by nature, and natural shelters.
  - The condition of nearby water sources, including whether they are clean, polluted, poisoned, or magically tainted.
- You become aware of the **approximate location**, **size**, and **general type** of nearby natural creatures, such as beasts, birds, reptiles, insects, or aquatic life.
- Gain **+6** to **Nature**, **Survival**, and **Tracking** **D20 Skill Checks** while Commune with Nature is active.
- You can determine whether an area has recently been disturbed by:
  - Large predators.
  - Natural disasters.
  - Extensive deforestation.
  - Wildfires.
  - Corruption.
  - Powerful magical events that have affected the natural environment.
- You instinctively sense the direction of the healthiest natural area and the most environmentally damaged area within range.
- This talent cannot detect humanoids, constructs, undead, or creatures completely severed from the natural world.
- Areas protected by powerful anti-divination or anti-nature magic may prevent or distort the information received.

---

### Lore

At this stage, the distinction between the Druid and the wilderness begins to fade. The world no longer feels like a place to be explored, but a living network of countless voices working together to preserve balance.

Ancient circles teach that every stream remembers those who drank from it, every tree recalls the seasons it has endured, and every mountain silently witnesses the passage of ages. A skilled Druid learns to interpret these memories, allowing the land itself to become both guide and teacher.

Those who possess this level of communion are often entrusted with protecting sacred groves, restoring blighted forests, and advising entire communities that live alongside nature. Their greatest strength lies not in commanding the wilderness, but in understanding what it asks of them.

---

> *"When you stop searching for nature's wisdom, you will discover it has been walking beside you all along."*  
> — **Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 4
### Description

Your bond with the natural world has become so refined that the land willingly reveals far more than its surface. The forests, rivers, mountains, and plains share not only their current state, but the lingering echoes of what has shaped them. You perceive the invisible connections between life, terrain, and magic as though they were threads woven into a single tapestry.

Nature now warns you of disturbances before they become visible. Corruption stains the land like a spreading sickness, powerful magical events leave lasting scars upon the environment, and unnatural creatures stand apart from the world's natural rhythm. To you, these disruptions feel as obvious as a broken branch beneath your feet.

Only the oldest Druids are entrusted with this level of communion, for they no longer simply observe nature—they serve as its eyes, ears, and protectors.

---

- Spend **25 MP** to enter a state of communion with the surrounding natural environment.
- Commune with Nature lasts for **25 minutes**.
- While active, you become aware of the natural environment within a **150-metre radius**.

---

Among the ancient circles, this mastery is known as **The Whispering Wilds**. It is said that a Druid who reaches this stage no longer searches for nature's wisdom—the wilderness seeks them out instead.

The oldest forests remember forgotten kingdoms, rivers recall the countless lives they have sustained, and mountains bear silent witness to the passing of ages. Through deep communion, these memories become fleeting impressions that guide a Druid toward truth without ever revealing every answer.

Many Wardens of the Wild serve as protectors of sacred lands because few others can recognise the first signs of corruption before they spread. To them, every imbalance is a plea for restoration, and every healthy grove is proof that harmony can endure.

# commune with nature

## overview
you still your thoughts and attune yourself to the rhythm of the natural world, allowing the land to share its knowledge. every tree, stream, mountain, and blade of grass carries traces of the life that has passed through it, and by opening your spirit you begin to understand these silent echoes.

commune with nature does not grant perfect vision or reveal every secret. instead, it provides instinctive awareness of your surroundings, helping you understand the health of the land, recognise natural features, and sense the presence of nearby wildlife. the stronger and more vibrant the environment, the clearer these impressions become.

to a druid, nature is not simply a place—it is a living companion with countless stories to tell. this talent marks the first step in learning to listen.

---

### effects

every great archdruid began with a single lesson: before you can ask nature for its strength, you must first learn to listen.

# Crimson Ritual

## Overview
The **Crimson Ritual** is one of the oldest ceremonies preserved by the Bloodhunter Orders, performed before every hunt worthy of remembrance. Rather than strengthening the Bloodhunter directly, the ritual empowers the tools that will carry out the hunt. Through ancient Sangramantic runes carved into the earth with their own blood, the Bloodhunter creates a **Blood Circle**—a sacred ritual site where weapons are infused with the essence of sacrifice.

As blood fills the engraved sigils, the circle awakens with a slow, rhythmic pulse, echoing the heartbeat of its creator. Weapons laid within the circle gradually absorb this crimson energy, binding a fragment of the Bloodhunter's life force into their steel, wood, or stone. Every empowered weapon becomes an extension of the Bloodhunter's resolve, carrying the promise that blood has already been offered before the battle has begun.

Bloodhunter Orders teach that monsters are defeated long before the first strike is made. Preparation, discipline, and sacrifice are the true foundations of every successful hunt. A Bloodhunter who neglects the Crimson Ritual is seen as reckless, while one who performs it honours both the traditions of their Order and every hunter who shed their blood before them.

Though simple compared to the legendary rituals performed by Bloodhunter Masters, every Crimson Ritual is a solemn oath: *the Bloodhunter will always be the first to bleed.*

## Rank 1

### Description

The **Crimson Ritual** is one of the oldest ceremonies preserved by the Bloodhunter Orders, performed before every hunt worthy of remembrance. Rather than strengthening the Bloodhunter directly, the ritual empowers the tools that will carry out the hunt. Through ancient Sangramantic runes carved into the earth with their own blood, the Bloodhunter creates a **Blood Circle**—a sacred ritual site where weapons are infused with the essence of sacrifice.

As blood fills the engraved sigils, the circle awakens with a slow, rhythmic pulse, echoing the heartbeat of its creator. Weapons laid within the circle gradually absorb this crimson energy, binding a fragment of the Bloodhunter's life force into their steel, wood, or stone. Every empowered weapon becomes an extension of the Bloodhunter's resolve, carrying the promise that blood has already been offered before the battle has begun.

Bloodhunter Orders teach that monsters are defeated long before the first strike is made. Preparation, discipline, and sacrifice are the true foundations of every successful hunt. A Bloodhunter who neglects the Crimson Ritual is seen as reckless, while one who performs it honours both the traditions of their Order and every hunter who shed their blood before them.

Though simple compared to the legendary rituals performed by Bloodhunter Masters, every Crimson Ritual is a solemn oath: *the Bloodhunter will always be the first to bleed.*

### Effects

- Performing the ritual requires **5 minutes** outside of combat.
- Spend **50 MP**, sacrifice **20 HP**, and gain **15 Blood Points (BP)**.
- Create a **Blood Circle** with a **2 metre radius** centred on yourself.
- The Blood Circle remains active for **5 minutes**.
- Up to **3 weapons or items** may be placed inside the Blood Circle at one time.
- A weapon or item must remain within the Blood Circle for **1 minute** to become **Bloodbound**.
- Bloodbound weapons retain their enchantment for **1 hour**, provided they are not used in combat.
- Once a Bloodbound weapon is used in combat, the enchantment lasts for the **first 4 successful attacks** made with that weapon before fading.
- Bloodbound weapons gain the following benefits:
  - Count as **Magical Weapons**.
  - Deal an additional **+3 Blood Damage** on each successful attack.
- If a Bloodbound ranged weapon is used, any ammunition fired from it while the enchantment remains active also gains the Bloodbound effect.
- A Bloodbound weapon or item may only benefit from one **Crimson Ritual** at a time.
- Only **one Blood Circle** may exist at any time.
- This talent synergises with **Blood Rite**, **Blood Control**, and other Bloodhunter talents.

### Lore

Every Bloodhunter Order maintains at least one ancient Blood Circle carved into the stone beneath its sanctuary floor. These circles have been stained by generations of hunters, each adding their own blood to an unbroken tradition stretching back centuries. Apprentices are taught their first Crimson Ritual within these sacred halls, learning that sacrifice is not an act of desperation, but one of purpose.

Many Bloodhunters perform the ritual in complete silence, laying each weapon carefully within the circle before whispering the names of those they have lost. By the time the ceremony is complete, the weapons are no longer ordinary tools—they have become symbols of the Bloodhunter's oath to stand between innocent lives and the horrors that threaten them.

The Blood Circle is never a place of celebration. It is a place where resolve is forged, where fear is accepted, and where the first sacrifice of every hunt is willingly made by the hunter themselves.

> *"Every hunt begins with blood. I simply choose that the first blood spilled will be my own."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

### Description

As a Bloodhunter's mastery of Sangramancy grows, so too does the potency of the Crimson Ritual. The Blood Circle expands, its runes becoming more intricate as greater quantities of blood and mana are woven into the ancient sigils. What was once a simple blessing of weapons evolves into a refined ceremony capable of preparing an entire hunting party for the dangers ahead.

The Blood Circle no longer merely empowers steel—it binds each weapon to the Bloodhunter's will. Every blade, bow, shield, or tool placed within the circle absorbs a fragment of the hunter's life essence, becoming Bloodbound through sacrifice rather than enchantment. The ritual leaves faint crimson veins beneath the surface of each item, visible only to those sensitive to magical energy.

Among the Orders, Rank II is often called **The Hunter's Preparation**, as experienced Bloodhunters rarely venture into dangerous territory without first gathering their companions around the Blood Circle. It serves as a reminder that victory is earned through discipline and preparation long before the first monster is encountered.

Although more powerful than before, the ritual still demands a price. Every weapon blessed carries a fragment of the Bloodhunter's own vitality, ensuring that every successful strike is paid for with blood willingly given.

### Effects

- Performing the ritual requires **5 minutes** outside of combat.
- Spend **60 MP**, sacrifice **25 HP**, and gain **20 Blood Points (BP)**.
- Create a **Blood Circle** with a **3 metre radius** centred on yourself.
- The Blood Circle remains active for **10 minutes**.
- Up to **4 weapons or items** may be placed inside the Blood Circle at one time.
- A weapon or item must remain within the Blood Circle for **1 minute** to become **Bloodbound**.
- Bloodbound weapons retain their enchantment for **2 hours**, provided they are not used in combat.
- Once a Bloodbound weapon is used in combat, the enchantment lasts for the **first 6 successful attacks** made with that weapon before fading.
- Bloodbound weapons gain the following benefits:
  - Count as **Magical Weapons**.
  - Deal an additional **+5 Blood Damage** on each successful attack.
- If a Bloodbound ranged weapon is used, any ammunition fired from it while the enchantment remains active also gains the Bloodbound effect.
- A Bloodbound weapon or item may only benefit from one **Crimson Ritual** at a time.
- Only **one Blood Circle** may exist at any time.
- This talent synergises with **Blood Rite**, **Blood Control**, and other Bloodhunter talents.

### Lore

Within every Bloodhunter Order, reaching the Second Rank of Crimson Ritual marks the first time an apprentice is trusted to prepare the weapons of others. This is considered a great honour, for the Bloodhunter is no longer sacrificing blood solely for themselves, but for every companion who will stand beside them.

Many veteran hunters claim they can identify a skilled Bloodhunter simply by examining the weapons they prepare. A perfectly performed Crimson Ritual leaves behind barely visible crimson markings beneath the surface of the weapon, evidence that the Sangramantic energy has been bound cleanly into the material without wasting a single drop of blood.

Some Bloodhunters perform this ritual before every expedition, regardless of the danger ahead. Others reserve it only for hunts worthy of legend. Regardless of tradition, every Order agrees on one truth—the Blood Circle is not merely a ritual of power, but a promise that the Bloodhunter's blood will always be the first offered in defence of their allies.

> *"Steel cuts flesh. Blood gives steel purpose."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor
