# Hunter's Arsenal

## Overview
A seasoned Ranger understands that every hunt eventually becomes unpredictable. A carefully aimed shot may suddenly become a desperate struggle at arm's length, forcing the hunter to adapt without hesitation. Rather than specialising in a single weapon, Rangers train relentlessly with the tools they carry, ensuring they remain deadly whether their quarry is hundreds of metres away or standing directly before them.

Hunter's Arsenal represents the beginning of this mastery. The Ranger develops the confidence and discipline to fight effectively at any distance, refusing to let close-quarters combat become a weakness. Every weapon carried serves a purpose, and every encounter becomes another opportunity to prove that a true hunter is never caught unprepared.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

A seasoned Ranger understands that every hunt eventually becomes unpredictable. A carefully aimed shot may suddenly become a desperate struggle at arm's length, forcing the hunter to adapt without hesitation. Rather than specialising in a single weapon, Rangers train relentlessly with the tools they carry, ensuring they remain deadly whether their quarry is hundreds of metres away or standing directly before them.

Hunter's Arsenal represents the beginning of this mastery. The Ranger develops the confidence and discipline to fight effectively at any distance, refusing to let close-quarters combat become a weakness. Every weapon carried serves a purpose, and every encounter becomes another opportunity to prove that a true hunter is never caught unprepared.

---

### Effects

- You **no longer suffer Disadvantage** when making **ranged weapon attacks** against creatures within your melee range.
- Gain a **+2 bonus to attack rolls** when wielding the following hunting weapons:
  - Daggers.
  - Hatchets and Hand Axes.
  - Short Swords.
  - Spears.
  - Other hunting weapons approved by the GM.
- While wielding a ranged weapon, creatures making **Opportunity Attacks** against you suffer a **-2 penalty to their attack roll**.

---

### Lore

Within the Ranger Lodges, apprentices quickly discover that the wilderness rarely allows the perfect engagement. A wounded beast may charge unexpectedly, an ambush may force combat into narrow passages, or an enemy may close the distance before another arrow can be loosed. Those who survive learn to trust every weapon at their side.

Veteran Rangers move confidently between melee and ranged combat without hesitation, understanding that versatility is one of a hunter's greatest strengths. To them, victory does not belong to the weapon—it belongs to the one who knows exactly when to use it.

---

> *"The prey decides the distance. The hunter decides how the fight ends."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's weapon mastery continues to evolve until changing between bow and blade becomes effortless. Every movement has been refined through countless hunts, allowing the Ranger to adapt instantly as enemies close the distance or attempt to retreat. Rather than interrupting the flow of combat, each weapon naturally complements the next.

At this stage, the Ranger no longer thinks about switching weapons—it simply happens. A bow is lowered as a blade is drawn, a spear is cast aside as an axe is gripped, and every transition maintains the relentless momentum of the hunt. Regardless of range, the Ranger always has the right weapon ready.

---

### Effects

- You **no longer suffer Disadvantage** when making **ranged weapon attacks** against creatures within your melee range.
- Gain a **+3 bonus to attack rolls** when wielding the following hunting weapons:
  - Daggers.
  - Hatchets and Hand Axes.
  - Short Swords.
  - Spears.
  - Other hunting weapons approved by the GM.
- While wielding a ranged weapon, creatures making **Opportunity Attacks** against you suffer a **-3 penalty to their attack roll**.
- **Once per turn**, you may **draw, sheathe, or swap between a ranged weapon and a hunting weapon** without spending an **Action** or **Action Point**.

---

### Lore

Experienced Rangers know that hesitation is often the difference between a successful hunt and becoming the hunted. Within the Ranger Lodges, apprentices spend years practising weapon transitions until every movement becomes instinctive. The goal is not speed alone, but seamless adaptation to an ever-changing battlefield.

Veteran hunters often appear to carry only a single weapon until the moment combat changes. In one fluid motion, a bow gives way to a blade, or a spear is replaced by an axe, all without breaking stride. To those watching, it seems effortless. To the Ranger, it is simply another lesson learned from the wilderness.

---

> *"The greatest weapon is the one already in your hand when the moment demands it."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The Ranger has mastered the seamless transition between ranged and melee combat. Every weapon is an extension of the same fighting style, allowing them to respond instinctively as the battlefield shifts around them. Whether striking with a blade before creating distance or firing an arrow at point-blank range, the Ranger wastes neither movement nor opportunity.

Experienced Rangers understand that versatility is their greatest weapon. They no longer think in terms of melee or ranged combat; instead, they simply choose the right tool for the next moment of the hunt. Their fluidity allows them to pressure enemies relentlessly, denying them the chance to exploit distance as a weakness.

---

### Effects

- You **no longer suffer Disadvantage** when making **ranged weapon attacks** against creatures within your melee range.
- Gain a **+4 bonus to attack rolls** when wielding the following hunting weapons:
  - Daggers.
  - Hatchets and Hand Axes.
  - Short Swords.
  - Spears.
  - Other hunting weapons approved by the GM.
- While wielding a ranged weapon, creatures making **Opportunity Attacks** against you suffer a **-4 penalty** to their attack rolls.
- **Once per turn**, you may **draw, sheathe, or swap** between a ranged weapon and a hunting weapon without spending an **Action** or **Action Point**.
- **After making a melee attack with a hunting weapon, you may move up to 2 metres without provoking an Opportunity Attack from the creature you attacked.**

---

### Lore

Only veteran Rangers reach the point where weapon changes become almost impossible to perceive. Their movements are smooth and uninterrupted, flowing naturally from bow to blade and back again as though every weapon were crafted as part of the same whole.

Within the Ranger Lodges, this level of mastery is considered a defining trait of a true hunter. Apprentices often spend years attempting to imitate these fluid transitions, only to realise that such precision comes not from speed alone, but from absolute confidence in every weapon they carry.

---

> *"Distance is an illusion. A true hunter is always fighting where they are strongest."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger has become a master of adaptive combat, effortlessly transitioning between ranged and melee engagements without sacrificing speed or precision. Every weapon carried serves a purpose, and every movement is calculated to keep the Ranger one step ahead of their opponent. Whether striking from afar or fighting face-to-face, the Ranger maintains complete control over the flow of battle.

At this level, the distinction between ranged and melee combat begins to disappear. The Ranger instinctively knows when to create distance, when to close the gap, and how to seamlessly combine both fighting styles into a relentless assault that keeps enemies constantly reacting.

---

### Effects

- You **no longer suffer Disadvantage** when making **ranged weapon attacks** against creatures within your melee range.
- Gain a **+5 bonus to attack rolls** when wielding the following hunting weapons:
  - Daggers.
  - Hatchets and Hand Axes.
  - Short Swords.
  - Spears.
  - Other hunting weapons approved by the GM.
- While wielding a ranged weapon, creatures making **Opportunity Attacks** against you suffer a **-5 penalty** to their attack rolls.
- **Once per turn**, you may **draw, sheathe, or swap** between a ranged weapon and a hunting weapon without spending an **Action** or **Action Point**.
- **After hitting a creature with a hunting weapon**, you may immediately make **one ranged weapon attack** against the same target, provided your ranged weapon is loaded or ready. This attack is made as part of the same Action and may occur only **once per turn**.
- **After making the ranged attack**, you may move **up to 3 metres** without provoking an Opportunity Attack from that creature.

---

### Lore

Among the Ranger Lodges, mastery of Hunter's Arsenal is considered the point where a hunter truly becomes unpredictable. Enemies expecting a drawn-out melee suddenly find themselves struck by an arrow at point-blank range, while those attempting to keep their distance are quickly met with flashing steel.

Veteran Rangers often describe combat as a flowing current rather than a series of isolated attacks. Every movement leads naturally into the next, allowing them to dictate the pace of battle while forcing their quarry to constantly adapt. Those fortunate enough to witness this level of mastery often struggle to identify where one attack ended and the next began.

---

> *"The greatest hunters never choose between bow and blade. They let the hunt decide."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has achieved complete mastery over every weapon carried into the hunt. To them, bows, blades, spears, and axes are no longer separate disciplines but parts of a single, fluid fighting style. Every movement is deliberate, every transition seamless, allowing the Ranger to adapt instantly to changing threats without ever losing momentum.

Whether an enemy charges into melee or attempts to flee beyond bowshot, the Ranger is always prepared. Their combat style becomes impossible to predict as they flow effortlessly between close-quarters combat and ranged precision. Few opponents survive long enough to exploit a weakness, for the Ranger no longer has one.

Within the Ranger Lodges, only the greatest Huntmasters are said to possess such mastery. They are regarded as warriors capable of defeating their prey regardless of the battlefield, the terrain, or the distance separating hunter and quarry.

---

### Effects

- You **no longer suffer Disadvantage** when making **ranged weapon attacks** against creatures within your melee range.
- Gain a **+6 bonus to attack rolls** when wielding the following hunting weapons:
  - Daggers.
  - Hatchets and Hand Axes.
  - Short Swords.
  - Spears.
  - Other hunting weapons approved by the GM.
- While wielding a ranged weapon, creatures making **Opportunity Attacks** against you suffer a **-6 penalty** to their attack rolls.
- **Once per turn**, you may **draw, sheathe, or swap** between a ranged weapon and a hunting weapon without spending an **Action** or **Action Point**.
- **Once per turn**, after successfully hitting with a **melee attack**, you may immediately make **one ranged weapon attack** against the same creature, provided your ranged weapon is loaded or otherwise ready.
- **Once per turn**, after successfully hitting with a **ranged weapon attack**, you may immediately make **one melee attack** against the same creature if it is within your melee reach.
- After resolving either combination, you may immediately move **up to 3 metres** without provoking an **Opportunity Attack** from that creature.

---

### Lore

The fifth rank of Hunter's Arsenal is considered the pinnacle of martial versatility within the Ranger Lodges. Those who achieve it no longer think in terms of melee or ranged combat. Every weapon becomes part of the same rhythm, each strike naturally flowing into the next as though the hunt itself guides their movements.

Stories tell of legendary Huntmasters who felled charging beasts with an arrow before finishing them with a blade in the same heartbeat, or who cut down a foe in melee before drawing their bow to strike another across the battlefield. Whether embellished or not, these tales all share one truth: a master Ranger is never limited by the weapon in their hands.

---

> *"The weapon does not make the hunter. The hunter makes every weapon worthy of the hunt."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Huntmaster of the Emerald Lodge**

None

GM-only information coming soon.

# Hunter's Bane

## Overview
Every Bloodhunter eventually discovers that there is one creature they cannot ignore.

Whether born from vengeance, duty, fear, or obsession, every hunter develops a relentless fixation upon a particular kind of prey. Some dedicate their lives to destroying the undead that slaughtered their family. Others swear to eradicate fiends that plague the mortal realm, while others pursue dragons, aberrations, or monsters that ordinary people dare not face.

This lifelong dedication is known as a **Hunter's Bane**.

Through years of study, relentless pursuit, and countless Blood Communions, the Bloodhunter learns every weakness, behaviour, hunting pattern, and instinct of their chosen prey. Their Blood Codex steadily grows with observations gathered from every encounter, making them one of the most dangerous adversaries that creature type will ever face.

Yet obsession comes at a terrible price.

The blood of a Hunter's Bane resonates more violently than any other. Every drop carries stronger emotions, stronger memories, and stronger hatred. Sangramancy eagerly feeds upon these emotions, granting the Bloodhunter greater focus while simultaneously accelerating the accumulation of Blood Points. Against their sworn prey, the Bloodhunter walks far closer to Bloodlust than they ever would against any other creature.

## Rank 1
### Description

Every Bloodhunter eventually discovers that there is one creature they cannot ignore.

Whether born from vengeance, duty, fear, or obsession, every hunter develops a relentless fixation upon a particular kind of prey. Some dedicate their lives to destroying the undead that slaughtered their family. Others swear to eradicate fiends that plague the mortal realm, while others pursue dragons, aberrations, or monsters that ordinary people dare not face.

This lifelong dedication is known as a **Hunter's Bane**.

Through years of study, relentless pursuit, and countless Blood Communions, the Bloodhunter learns every weakness, behaviour, hunting pattern, and instinct of their chosen prey. Their Blood Codex steadily grows with observations gathered from every encounter, making them one of the most dangerous adversaries that creature type will ever face.

Yet obsession comes at a terrible price.

The blood of a Hunter's Bane resonates more violently than any other. Every drop carries stronger emotions, stronger memories, and stronger hatred. Sangramancy eagerly feeds upon these emotions, granting the Bloodhunter greater focus while simultaneously accelerating the accumulation of Blood Points. Against their sworn prey, the Bloodhunter walks far closer to Bloodlust than they ever would against any other creature.

### Effects

- Choose **one creature type** from the following list. This choice is **permanent**:
  - Aberration
  - Beast
  - Celestial
  - Construct
  - Dragon
  - Elemental
  - Fey
  - Fiend
  - Giant
  - Humanoid
  - Monstrosity
  - Ooze
  - Plant
  - Undead
- This creature type becomes your **Hunter's Bane**.
- Gain **+2 to Survival checks** made to track creatures of your Hunter's Bane.
- Gain **+2 to Monster Knowledge checks** regarding creatures of your Hunter's Bane.
- Blood Communion performed on your Hunter's Bane requires only **30 seconds** instead of **1 minute**.
- The first successful Blood Communion performed on your Hunter's Bane immediately records that species within your **Blood Codex** if it has not already been documented.
- If a creature is both your **Hunter's Bane** and your **Marked Prey**, gain:
  - **+1 to Attack Rolls**.
  - **+1 to Damage Rolls**.
- **Whenever you gain Blood Points (BP) from an ability, talent, Blood Communion, Blood Rite, Blood Curse, or any other Sangramancy effect while interacting with your Hunter's Bane, the Blood Points gained are doubled.**
- This doubling is mandatory and cannot be ignored unless another ability specifically states otherwise.

### Lore

Every Bloodhunter carries a story that begins with a single monster.

For some, it is the vampire that slaughtered their village. For others, the demon that corrupted their homeland or the ancient dragon that reduced an entire kingdom to ash. These encounters leave scars deeper than flesh, shaping the hunter's purpose for the rest of their life.

The ritual of declaring a Hunter's Bane is among the oldest traditions of every Bloodhunter Order. Before their peers, the hunter speaks the name of the creatures they will dedicate their life to destroying before sealing the oath with their own blood. From that day onward, every hunt deepens their understanding, but also their obsession.

The elders teach that hatred is the sharpest weapon a Bloodhunter possesses—and the most dangerous. Sangramancy amplifies every emotion carried within blood, and no blood burns hotter than that of a sworn enemy. Many Bloodhunters who succumb to Bloodlust do so not while facing impossible odds, but while standing before the very creature they swore they would one day destroy.

> *"Beware the hunter who knows your blood... but fear the one who has sworn an oath upon it."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 2
# 

### Description

A Bloodhunter's obsession grows stronger with every successful hunt. What once began as hatred evolves into unparalleled understanding, allowing the hunter to anticipate the instincts, habits, and behaviour of their chosen prey with frightening accuracy. Every battle, every Blood Communion, and every page added to the Blood Codex strengthens the bond between hunter and quarry.

At this stage, the Bloodhunter no longer studies their Hunter's Bane simply to destroy it—they begin to think like it. They recognise territorial patterns, preferred methods of attack, weaknesses hidden beneath instinctive behaviour, and the subtle signs that reveal when a creature is preparing to flee, ambush, or strike.

This deeper understanding comes at an equally dangerous cost. The emotions carried within the blood of their sworn prey resonate far more violently than before. Every encounter awakens powerful feelings of determination, vengeance, and obsession, causing Sangramancy to react with greater intensity. The Bloodhunter becomes increasingly efficient at hunting their chosen enemy, but every victory brings them closer to surrendering themselves to Bloodlust.

Among the Orders, veterans often warn that a Bloodhunter should never allow their Hunter's Bane to become their only purpose. Those who do frequently forget why they became hunters in the first place, until the hunt itself becomes all that remains.

### Effects

- Your Hunter's Bane remains the creature type chosen at Rank I.
- Gain **+3 to Survival checks** made to track creatures of your Hunter's Bane.
- Gain **+3 to Monster Knowledge checks** regarding creatures of your Hunter's Bane.
- Blood Communion performed on your Hunter's Bane now requires only **15 seconds**.
- Blood Communion performed on your Hunter's Bane reveals:
  - The creature's approximate health.
  - Signs of disease, corruption, curses, or magical influence.
  - Whether the creature has recently fought or consumed another creature.
- If a creature is both your **Hunter's Bane** and your **Marked Prey**, gain:
  - **+2 to Attack Rolls**.
  - **+2 to Damage Rolls**.
- Whenever you gain Blood Points (BP) from an ability, talent, Blood Rite, Blood Communion, Blood Curse, or any other Sangramancy effect while interacting with your Hunter's Bane, the Blood Points gained are **doubled**.
- Once your Hunter's Bane has been permanently recorded within your Blood Codex, you immediately recognise blood belonging to that creature type without needing to perform Blood Communion again.

### Lore

Only seasoned Bloodhunters reach the point where instinct begins to rival experience. The Blood Codex grows beyond a simple record of hunts and becomes a detailed study of a single enemy, documenting generations of knowledge gathered by countless hunters before them.

Many Bloodhunter Orders pass these records from master to apprentice, ensuring that no lesson earned in blood is ever forgotten. Over decades, the Bloodhunter develops an uncanny familiarity with their Hunter's Bane, recognising patterns invisible to everyone else and predicting behaviour with remarkable precision.

Yet obsession is never without consequence. Sangramancy rewards dedication with power, but it also magnifies every emotion tied to that dedication. The Bloodhunter must constantly ask themselves whether they are still hunting their prey—or whether their prey has begun hunting them from within.

> *"Know your enemy so completely that they believe escape is possible... right until the moment they realise you were always one step behind them."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 3
### Description

By the Third Rank, your Hunter's Bane has become more than a sworn enemy—it has become your life's work. Years of study, countless Blood Communions, and relentless pursuit have transformed your Blood Codex into a comprehensive record of your chosen prey. Every hunt refines your understanding, allowing you to predict behaviour before it happens and recognise weaknesses invisible to ordinary hunters.

Your Blood Scent reacts instinctively whenever your Hunter's Bane is near. Even the faintest trace of fresh blood can reveal the creature's passing, while your Sangramancy resonates more violently than ever before. Every encounter awakens powerful emotions that sharpen your focus while simultaneously drawing you ever closer to Bloodlust.

Experienced Bloodhunters often describe this stage as becoming one with the hunt. They no longer simply pursue their prey—they begin to anticipate its every decision. Every failed ambush, every attempted escape, and every desperate last stand becomes another lesson added to the Blood Codex.

Yet this mastery carries a terrible burden. The stronger your obsession becomes, the more Sangramancy responds to it. Every drop of blood belonging to your Hunter's Bane burns like fire within your soul, granting incredible strength while threatening to consume your reason. Few Bloodhunters can maintain such discipline for long, and many legendary hunters have ultimately fallen to the very obsession that once made them great.

### Effects

- Your Hunter's Bane remains the creature type chosen at Rank I.
- Gain **+4 to Survival checks** made to track creatures of your Hunter's Bane.
- Gain **+4 to Monster Knowledge checks** regarding creatures of your Hunter's Bane.
- Blood Communion performed on your Hunter's Bane requires only **1 Action**.
- If a creature is both your **Hunter's Bane** and your **Marked Prey**, gain:
  - **+3 to Attack Rolls**.
  - **+3 to Damage Rolls**.
- Gain **Advantage** on checks made to identify, investigate, or recall information about your Hunter's Bane.
- Blood Communion now reveals:
  - Approximate remaining vitality.
  - Active magical effects.
  - Curses, diseases, corruption, mutations, and bloodline abnormalities.
  - Whether the creature has previously been encountered by you.
- Whenever you gain Blood Points (BP) from an ability, talent, Blood Rite, Blood Communion, Blood Curse, or any other Sangramancy effect while interacting with your Hunter's Bane, the Blood Points gained are **doubled**.
- Once recorded within your Blood Codex, you immediately recognise fresh blood belonging to your Hunter's Bane by scent alone.

### Lore

The Third Rank is known among the Bloodhunter Orders as the **Hunter's Awakening**. By this stage, a Bloodhunter has accumulated enough knowledge that hunting their chosen prey becomes almost instinctive. Stories tell of masters recognising a single drop of blood upon stone, immediately identifying not only the creature that shed it but also the direction it travelled and the wounds it carried.

The Blood Codex grows ever larger with every successful hunt. Some Bloodhunters dedicate entire libraries to documenting the habits of a single creature type, ensuring that future generations never begin their hunt without centuries of accumulated knowledge guiding them.

But obsession is a dangerous companion. The Orders teach that every Bloodhunter eventually reaches a point where they must choose whether they control the hunt—or whether the hunt has begun to control them. Those who fail that choice often become legends... remembered as warnings rather than heroes.

> *"The day you understand your prey better than it understands itself is the day the hunt truly begins."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 4
# 

### Description

Your Hunter's Bane is no longer simply a sworn enemy—it has become an obsession that defines your existence. Years of relentless pursuit have transformed your Blood Codex into an unrivalled archive of knowledge, containing every weakness, instinct, hunting pattern, and behaviour your chosen prey has ever revealed. Every encounter reinforces what you know, making each hunt more efficient than the last.

At this level, your Sangramancy instinctively reacts whenever your Hunter's Bane is near. The scent of their blood immediately sharpens your focus, while your Blood Signature and Blood Codex work together to predict their movements before they are made. Few creatures can deceive a Bloodhunter who has dedicated their life to understanding them.

The Bloodhunter Orders teach that this is the point where hunters stop reacting to monsters and instead begin controlling the hunt itself. Every trap, every pursuit, and every confrontation unfolds according to the Bloodhunter's expectations, forcing even the most intelligent prey into a losing battle.

Yet obsession has now become inseparable from power. Every encounter with your Hunter's Bane causes your Blood Points to surge violently, feeding Sangramancy with emotions that grow stronger with every victory. Many Bloodhunters who reach this level begin to fear not their enemies, but the calm certainty they feel whenever the hunt begins.

### Effects

- Your Hunter's Bane remains the creature type chosen at Rank I.
- Gain **+5 to Survival checks** made to track creatures of your Hunter's Bane.
- Gain **+5 to Monster Knowledge checks** regarding creatures of your Hunter's Bane.
- Blood Communion performed on your Hunter's Bane is completed as a **Bonus Action**.
- If a creature is both your **Hunter's Bane** and your **Marked Prey**, gain:
  - **+4 to Attack Rolls**.
  - **+4 to Damage Rolls**.
- Gain **Advantage** on Initiative rolls whenever your Hunter's Bane is present.
- You cannot be surprised by your Hunter's Bane while it is within the range of your Blood Scent.
- Blood Communion additionally reveals:
  - The creature's approximate remaining Health.
  - Active magical enchantments or curses.
  - Recent injuries and their severity.
  - Whether the creature has consumed, transformed into, or been influenced by another creature.
- Whenever you gain Blood Points (BP) from an ability, talent, Blood Rite, Blood Communion, Blood Curse, or any other Sangramancy effect while interacting with your Hunter's Bane, the Blood Points gained are **doubled**.
- Once recorded within your Blood Codex, blood belonging to your Hunter's Bane is instantly recognised by scent, regardless of age, provided some trace of its essence remains.

### Lore

Within the Bloodhunter Orders, Rank IV is known as the **Master Hunter's Oath**. Hunters who reach this level have devoted so much of their lives to a single enemy that they often understand their prey better than the creatures understand themselves. Every victory becomes another lesson, and every lesson strengthens both the Bloodhunter and the obsession driving them forward.

Many legendary Bloodhunters have ended ancient bloodlines through nothing more than patience. They waited, observed, studied, and struck only when every possible outcome had already been calculated. To such hunters, the battle itself is merely the final chapter of a hunt won long before blades are ever drawn.

The elders warn, however, that the line between mastery and obsession has all but disappeared. The Bloodhunter's hatred has become an inexhaustible source of strength, but Sangramancy eagerly feeds upon that hatred. One careless moment is all that separates a legendary hunter from becoming another victim of Bloodlust.

> *"The greatest hunters do not chase monsters. They become the fate those monsters can never escape."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 5
### Description

You have become the embodiment of the hunt.

Your Hunter's Bane is no longer merely a creature type you specialise in—it has become the purpose around which your Sangramancy has evolved. Every Blood Communion, every Blood Signature committed to your Blood Codex, and every battle fought against your sworn prey has reshaped both your body and mind into the ultimate predator.

The Blood Codex has become a living archive of generations of knowledge, allowing you to understand your Hunter's Bane with frightening clarity. Their instincts, behaviours, strengths, and weaknesses are no longer mysteries. You read them as easily as others read a book, often predicting their actions moments before they occur.

Yet no Bloodhunter reaches this level without sacrifice.

The blood of your Hunter's Bane resonates with overwhelming intensity. Every drop fuels your Sangramancy, causing your Blood Points to surge faster than ever before. To lesser Bloodhunters this would guarantee Bloodlust, but masters willingly walk that razor's edge, accepting the growing burden because no one else can stand against the horrors they were born to destroy.

Among the Orders, those who achieve this rank are known as **Apex Hunters**. Legends claim entire monsters species have altered their migration routes after learning one of these hunters has entered their territory.

### Effects

- Your Hunter's Bane remains the creature type chosen at Rank I.
- Gain **+6 to Survival checks** made to track creatures of your Hunter's Bane.
- Gain **+6 to Monster Knowledge checks** regarding creatures of your Hunter's Bane.
- Blood Communion performed on your Hunter's Bane is **instantaneous** and requires no additional action beyond interacting with the blood.
- If a creature is both your **Hunter's Bane** and your **Marked Prey**, gain:
  - **+5 to Attack Rolls**.
  - **+5 to Damage Rolls**.
- Gain **Advantage** on Initiative rolls whenever your Hunter's Bane is present.
- Your Hunter's Bane cannot gain Advantage against you through being hidden, invisible, or disguised while within the range of your Blood Scent.
- Your Blood Codex immediately identifies any blood belonging to your Hunter's Bane, regardless of its age, provided a trace of its essence remains.
- Blood Communion reveals everything known through previous ranks, as well as:
  - The creature's approximate age.
  - Its bloodline or lineage.
  - Magical mutations or inherited traits.
  - Signs of previous Bloodhunter encounters.
- **Whenever you gain Blood Points (BP) from an ability, talent, Blood Rite, Blood Communion, Blood Curse, or any other Sangramancy effect while interacting with your Hunter's Bane, the Blood Points gained are doubled.**
- This effect is mandatory and cannot be prevented unless another ability specifically overrides it.

### Lore

Very few Bloodhunters survive long enough to become an Apex Hunter. Those who do are spoken of with equal measures of admiration and fear, for they have devoted an entire lifetime to understanding a single enemy so completely that the hunt itself has become instinct.

Entire Bloodhunter Orders preserve the journals of Apex Hunters within their Blood Codices. These writings contain centuries of accumulated knowledge, allowing future generations to continue the hunt where others left off. It is said that no Bloodhunter truly dies while their Blood Codex remains, for every lesson learned in blood continues to guide those who follow.

The greatest irony of the Apex Hunter is that they stand closer to Bloodlust than any other Bloodhunter. Every encounter with their sworn prey floods their soul with overwhelming emotion, pushing them to the brink of losing themselves. Yet they willingly embrace that burden, believing there is no greater sacrifice than becoming the very weapon needed to destroy the monsters that threaten the world.

> *"Every hunter dreams of slaying the monster. Only an Apex Hunter understands that the greatest victory is surviving the monster within."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

the third rank is known among the bloodhunter orders as the **hunter's awakening**. by this stage, a bloodhunter has accumulated enough knowledge that hunting their chosen prey becomes almost instinctive. stories tell of masters recognising a single drop of blood upon stone, immediately identifying not only the creature that shed it but also the direction it travelled and the wounds it carried.

the blood codex grows ever larger with every successful hunt. some bloodhunters dedicate entire libraries to documenting the habits of a single creature type, ensuring that future generations never begin their hunt without centuries of accumulated knowledge guiding them.

but obsession is a dangerous companion. the orders teach that every bloodhunter eventually reaches a point where they must choose whether they control the hunt—or whether the hunt has begun to control them. those who fail that choice often become legends... remembered as warnings rather than heroes.

> *"the day you understand your prey better than it understands itself is the day the hunt truly begins."*  
> — grand bloodhunter serik vaelor

## rank 4
# 

### description

your hunter's bane is no longer simply a sworn enemy—it has become an obsession that defines your existence. years of relentless pursuit have transformed your blood codex into an unrivalled archive of knowledge, containing every weakness, instinct, hunting pattern, and behaviour your chosen prey has ever revealed. every encounter reinforces what you know, making each hunt more efficient than the last.

at this level, your sangramancy instinctively reacts whenever your hunter's bane is near. the scent of their blood immediately sharpens your focus, while your blood signature and blood codex work together to predict their movements before they are made. few creatures can deceive a bloodhunter who has dedicated their life to understanding them.

the bloodhunter orders teach that this is the point where hunters stop reacting to monsters and instead begin controlling the hunt itself. every trap, every pursuit, and every confrontation unfolds according to the bloodhunter's expectations, forcing even the most intelligent prey into a losing battle.

yet obsession has now become inseparable from power. every encounter with your hunter's bane causes your blood points to surge violently, feeding sangramancy with emotions that grow stronger with every victory. many bloodhunters who reach this level begin to fear not their enemies, but the calm certainty they feel whenever the hunt begins.

### effects

- your hunter's bane remains the creature type chosen at rank i.
- gain **+5 to survival checks** made to track creatures of your hunter's bane.
- gain **+5 to monster knowledge checks** regarding creatures of your hunter's bane.
- blood communion performed on your hunter's bane is completed as a **bonus action**.
- if a creature is both your **hunter's bane** and your **marked prey**, gain:
  - **+4 to attack rolls**.
  - **+4 to damage rolls**.
- gain **advantage** on initiative rolls whenever your hunter's bane is present.
- you cannot be surprised by your hunter's bane while it is within the range of your blood scent.
- blood communion additionally reveals:
  - the creature's approximate remaining health.
  - active magical enchantments or curses.
  - recent injuries and their severity.
  - whether the creature has consumed, transformed into, or been influenced by another creature.
- whenever you gain blood points (bp) from an ability, talent, blood rite, blood communion, blood curse, or any other sangramancy effect while interacting with your hunter's bane, the blood points gained are **doubled**.
- once recorded within your blood codex, blood belonging to your hunter's bane is instantly recognised by scent, regardless of age, provided some trace of its essence remains.

### lore

within the bloodhunter orders, rank iv is known as the **master hunter's oath**. hunters who reach this level have devoted so much of their lives to a single enemy that they often understand their prey better than the creatures understand themselves. every victory becomes another lesson, and every lesson strengthens both the bloodhunter and the obsession driving them forward.

many legendary bloodhunters have ended ancient bloodlines through nothing more than patience. they waited, observed, studied, and struck only when every possible outcome had already been calculated. to such hunters, the battle itself is merely the final chapter of a hunt won long before blades are ever drawn.

the elders warn, however, that the line between mastery and obsession has all but disappeared. the bloodhunter's hatred has become an inexhaustible source of strength, but sangramancy eagerly feeds upon that hatred. one careless moment is all that separates a legendary hunter from becoming another victim of bloodlust.

> *"the greatest hunters do not chase monsters. they become the fate those monsters can never escape."*  
> — grand bloodhunter serik vaelor

## rank 5
### description

you have become the embodiment of the hunt.

your hunter's bane is no longer merely a creature type you specialise in—it has become the purpose around which your sangramancy has evolved. every blood communion, every blood signature committed to your blood codex, and every battle fought against your sworn prey has reshaped both your body and mind into the ultimate predator.

the blood codex has become a living archive of generations of knowledge, allowing you to understand your hunter's bane with frightening clarity. their instincts, behaviours, strengths, and weaknesses are no longer mysteries. you read them as easily as others read a book, often predicting their actions moments before they occur.

yet no bloodhunter reaches this level without sacrifice.

the blood of your hunter's bane resonates with overwhelming intensity. every drop fuels your sangramancy, causing your blood points to surge faster than ever before. to lesser bloodhunters this would guarantee bloodlust, but masters willingly walk that razor's edge, accepting the growing burden because no one else can stand against the horrors they were born to destroy.

among the orders, those who achieve this rank are known as **apex hunters**. legends claim entire monsters species have altered their migration routes after learning one of these hunters has entered their territory.

### effects

- your hunter's bane remains the creature type chosen at rank i.
- gain **+6 to survival checks** made to track creatures of your hunter's bane.
- gain **+6 to monster knowledge checks** regarding creatures of your hunter's bane.
- blood communion performed on your hunter's bane is **instantaneous** and requires no additional action beyond interacting with the blood.
- if a creature is both your **hunter's bane** and your **marked prey**, gain:
  - **+5 to attack rolls**.
  - **+5 to damage rolls**.
- gain **advantage** on initiative rolls whenever your hunter's bane is present.
- your hunter's bane cannot gain advantage against you through being hidden, invisible, or disguised while within the range of your blood scent.
- your blood codex immediately identifies any blood belonging to your hunter's bane, regardless of its age, provided a trace of its essence remains.
- blood communion reveals everything known through previous ranks, as well as:
  - the creature's approximate age.
  - its bloodline or lineage.
  - magical mutations or inherited traits.
  - signs of previous bloodhunter encounters.
- **whenever you gain blood points (bp) from an ability, talent, blood rite, blood communion, blood curse, or any other sangramancy effect while interacting with your hunter's bane, the blood points gained are doubled.**
- this effect is mandatory and cannot be prevented unless another ability specifically overrides it.

### lore

very few bloodhunters survive long enough to become an apex hunter. those who do are spoken of with equal measures of admiration and fear, for they have devoted an entire lifetime to understanding a single enemy so completely that the hunt itself has become instinct.

entire bloodhunter orders preserve the journals of apex hunters within their blood codices. these writings contain centuries of accumulated knowledge, allowing future generations to continue the hunt where others left off. it is said that no bloodhunter truly dies while their blood codex remains, for every lesson learned in blood continues to guide those who follow.

the greatest irony of the apex hunter is that they stand closer to bloodlust than any other bloodhunter. every encounter with their sworn prey floods their soul with overwhelming emotion, pushing them to the brink of losing themselves. yet they willingly embrace that burden, believing there is no greater sacrifice than becoming the very weapon needed to destroy the monsters that threaten the world.

> *"every hunter dreams of slaying the monster. only an apex hunter understands that the greatest victory is surviving the monster within."*  
> — grand bloodhunter serik vaelor

# Hunter's Mark

## Overview
A skilled Ranger does not simply attack their quarry—they study it, understand it, and exploit every weakness it reveals. By focusing a small amount of mana upon a chosen creature, the Ranger forms a mystical bond that heightens their awareness of the target's movements and vulnerabilities.

Hunter's Mark represents the Ranger's transition from hunter to battlefield specialist. Rather than increasing accuracy, the mark allows the Ranger to strike with greater force whenever they successfully land a hit. Every arrow, thrown weapon, or ranged attack becomes more punishing as the Ranger learns exactly where to wound their quarry.

At this rank, the benefits of Hunter's Mark are known only to the Ranger. As mastery grows, they will learn to communicate these weaknesses to nearby allies, allowing an entire hunting party to bring down even the mightiest prey.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

A skilled Ranger does not simply attack their quarry—they study it, understand it, and exploit every weakness it reveals. By focusing a small amount of mana upon a chosen creature, the Ranger forms a mystical bond that heightens their awareness of the target's movements and vulnerabilities.

Hunter's Mark represents the Ranger's transition from hunter to battlefield specialist. Rather than increasing accuracy, the mark allows the Ranger to strike with greater force whenever they successfully land a hit. Every arrow, thrown weapon, or ranged attack becomes more punishing as the Ranger learns exactly where to wound their quarry.

At this rank, the benefits of Hunter's Mark are known only to the Ranger. As mastery grows, they will learn to communicate these weaknesses to nearby allies, allowing an entire hunting party to bring down even the mightiest prey.

---

### Effects

#### Mark Quarry

- Spend **20 MP** to mark one creature within **30 metres** that you can see.
- The mark lasts for **1 minute**.
- Only **one creature** may be marked at a time.
- Marking a new creature immediately ends the previous mark.

#### Hunter's Instinct

While your Quarry is marked:

- Your successful attacks against the marked target deal **+1d4 bonus damage**.
- This bonus applies to:
  - Ranged weapon attacks.
  - Melee weapon attacks.
  - Ranger talents that deal direct damage.
- The bonus damage is applied **once per successful attack**.

#### Limitations

- Allies gain no benefit from Hunter's Mark at this rank.
- The mark immediately ends if the target dies.
- The mark does not reveal the target's location if it leaves your line of sight.
- Hunter's Mark does not stack with another Ranger's Hunter's Mark on the same target. If multiple Rangers mark the same creature, each Ranger only gains the benefit of their own mark.

---

### Lore

The oldest Ranger Lodges teach that every creature has a weakness waiting to be uncovered. Through instinct, experience, and a small infusion of mana, a Ranger learns to focus entirely upon a single quarry, studying its movements until every successful strike lands with greater precision and force.

Many believe Hunter's Mark is a spell of tracking, but experienced Rangers know this is only part of its purpose. The true strength of the technique lies in the unwavering focus it demands. Once the quarry has been chosen, every thought, every movement, and every attack is dedicated to bringing the hunt to its conclusion.

---

> *"Choose your quarry wisely. Every hunt begins with a decision, but only the greatest Rangers see it through to the end."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's connection to their marked quarry deepens, allowing them to exploit weaknesses with increasing efficiency. Rather than simply identifying vulnerable areas, the Ranger instinctively predicts how their prey will move and where the next opening will appear. Every successful strike becomes more punishing as the hunt progresses.

As the mark strengthens, maintaining focus requires less conscious effort. The Ranger's attention remains fixed upon the quarry even amidst the chaos of battle, ensuring every attack is delivered with purpose. While the mark still benefits only the Ranger, it lays the foundation for the cooperative hunting techniques taught to veteran Rangers.

Experienced hunters often say that once a creature has been marked, every wound it suffers becomes easier to inflict than the last.

---

### Effects

#### Mark Quarry

- Spend **30 MP** to mark one creature within **40 metres** that you can see.
- The mark lasts for **2 minutes**.
- Only **one creature** may be marked at a time.
- Marking another creature immediately ends the previous mark.

#### Hunter's Instinct

While your Quarry is marked:

- Your successful attacks against the marked target deal **+1d6 bonus damage**.
- This bonus applies to:
  - Ranged weapon attacks.
  - Melee weapon attacks.
  - Ranger talents that deal direct damage.
- The bonus damage is applied **once per successful attack**.

#### Limitations

- Allies gain no benefit from Hunter's Mark at this rank.
- The mark immediately ends if the target dies.
- The mark does not reveal the target's location if it leaves your line of sight.
- Hunter's Mark does not stack with another Ranger's Hunter's Mark on the same target. If multiple Rangers mark the same creature, each Ranger only gains the benefit of their own mark.

---

### Lore

By the second rank, Hunter's Mark has become more than a simple hunting technique—it is a symbol of unwavering determination. Rangers learn to lock their attention onto a single quarry, studying every movement until striking vulnerable areas becomes second nature.

Within the Ranger Lodges, apprentices are reminded that discipline is just as important as skill. A distracted hunter misses opportunities, while a focused Ranger turns every opening into a decisive blow. Those who master Hunter's Mark are respected not for the number of creatures they defeat, but for the precision with which they bring every hunt to its conclusion.

---

> *"A marked quarry has already made its first mistake—it allowed a Ranger to choose it."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
# Description

The Ranger's mastery of Hunter's Mark evolves beyond personal gain, becoming a powerful tool for coordinated hunting. By carefully studying the marked quarry, the Ranger identifies weaknesses, damaged armour, and predictable movements, allowing not only themselves but also their companions to strike with greater effectiveness.

Through shouted commands, hand signals, or simple battlefield awareness, the Ranger instinctively guides nearby allies towards vulnerable areas. Every successful attack against the marked quarry contributes to wearing it down, turning even the most formidable foe into prey.

Within the Ranger Lodges, reaching the third rank is seen as the point where a hunter becomes a leader. The Ranger no longer hunts alone—they direct the entire pack.

---

### Effects

#### Mark Quarry

- Spend **40 MP** to mark one creature within **50 metres** that you can see.
- The mark lasts for **5 minutes**.
- Only **one creature** may be marked at a time.
- Marking another creature immediately ends the previous mark.

#### Hunter's Instinct

While your Quarry is marked:

**The Ranger gains:**

- **+1d8 bonus damage** on all successful attacks against the marked target.

**Allied creatures gain:**

- **+1d4 bonus damage** on successful attacks against the marked target.

This bonus applies to:

- Ranged weapon attacks.
- Melee weapon attacks.
- Talents and abilities that deal direct damage.
- Offensive spells that successfully hit the marked target.

The bonus damage is applied **once per successful attack**.

#### Limitations

- Allies must be aware of the marked target to gain the bonus.
- Hunter's Mark does not reveal the target's location if it leaves line of sight.
- The mark immediately ends if the target dies.
- Only one Hunter's Mark may affect a creature at a time. If multiple Rangers mark the same target, only the highest-ranked Hunter's Mark applies.

---

### Lore

By the third rank, Hunter's Mark becomes one of the defining techniques of an experienced Ranger. Their ability to recognise and communicate weaknesses transforms them from a solitary hunter into the leader of a coordinated hunt. Veteran adventuring parties quickly learn to trust a Ranger's judgement, knowing that every command is based upon careful observation rather than guesswork.

Stories tell of Ranger companies bringing down dragons, giants, and Elder Beasts by relentlessly exploiting a single weakness identified by their leader. These victories were not won through overwhelming strength, but through patience, precision, and cooperation—principles that define every true Ranger.

---

> *"One hunter may wound the beast. A guided pack will bring it down."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger's Hunter's Mark has become a symbol of battlefield leadership. With only a moment's observation, they identify weaknesses that would otherwise remain unnoticed, directing their allies to strike precisely where the quarry is most vulnerable. Every command, gesture, and call is deliberate, allowing the hunting party to work together with deadly efficiency.

The Ranger's connection to the marked quarry grows stronger as the hunt progresses. Every wound reveals another opportunity, and every successful attack builds momentum for the entire group. Few creatures can withstand a coordinated assault led by a master Ranger.

Veteran Rangers often say that by this stage, the quarry is defeated long before the final blow is delivered—it simply has not realised it yet.

---

### Effects

#### Mark Quarry

- Spend **50 MP** to mark one creature within **60 metres** that you can see.
- The mark lasts for **10 minutes**.
- Only **one creature** may be marked at a time.
- Marking another creature immediately ends the previous mark.

#### Hunter's Instinct

While your Quarry is marked:

**The Ranger gains:**

- **+1d10 bonus damage** on all successful attacks against the marked target.

**Allied creatures gain:**

- **+1d6 bonus damage** on successful attacks against the marked target.

This bonus applies to:

- Ranged weapon attacks.
- Melee weapon attacks.
- Talents and abilities that deal direct damage.
- Offensive spells that successfully hit the marked target.

The bonus damage is applied **once per successful attack**.

#### Pack Leader

While the Quarry remains marked:

- Allies always know which creature is marked.
- The Ranger may reapply Hunter's Mark to the same target without paying an additional Mana Cost if the mark expires naturally during its duration.

#### Limitations

- Hunter's Mark does not reveal the target's location if it leaves line of sight.
- The mark immediately ends if the target dies.
- Only one Hunter's Mark may affect a creature at a time. If multiple Rangers mark the same target, only the highest-ranked Hunter's Mark applies.
- Bonus damage from Hunter's Mark does not stack with another Hunter's Mark.

---

### Lore

Only accomplished Rangers achieve the fourth rank of Hunter's Mark. By this point, they have learned that hunting is rarely an individual pursuit. The greatest victories come from guiding companions toward the same objective, ensuring every strike contributes to bringing the quarry down.

Entire Ranger companies have built their tactics around Hunters capable of maintaining these advanced marks. Their commands carry absolute confidence, allowing warriors, mages, and scouts alike to focus their attacks with remarkable precision. To fight beside such a Ranger is to feel as though every weakness has already been uncovered before the battle has truly begun.

---

> *"The mark is not a promise that the quarry will fall. It is a promise that every hunter now knows where to strike."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has mastered Hunter's Mark, becoming the unquestioned leader of the hunt. A single marked quarry becomes the sole focus of the battlefield, with every ally instinctively recognising where to strike and every attack driving the prey closer to its inevitable end. What began as a personal hunting technique has evolved into one of the most feared battlefield tactics employed by the Ranger Lodges.

A master Ranger no longer simply identifies weaknesses—they orchestrate the downfall of their quarry. Through observation, experience, and unwavering focus, they direct every member of the hunting party towards the target's greatest vulnerabilities. Against such coordination, even legendary beasts struggle to withstand the relentless assault.

Throughout Asteria, stories tell of Dragons, Elder Beasts, and Demon Lords falling beneath the combined might of a hunting party guided by a single master Ranger. Their greatest weapon was never their bow, but their ability to unite every strike into one perfect hunt.

---

### Effects

#### Mark Quarry

- Spend **60 MP** to mark one creature within **80 metres** that you can see.
- The mark lasts for **30 minutes**.
- Only **one creature** may be marked at a time.
- Marking another creature immediately ends the previous mark.

#### Master Hunter

While your Quarry is marked:

**The Ranger gains:**

- **+1d12 bonus damage** on all successful attacks against the marked target.

**Allied creatures gain:**

- **+1d8 bonus damage** on successful attacks against the marked target.

This bonus applies to:

- Ranged weapon attacks.
- Melee weapon attacks.
- Talents and abilities that deal direct damage.
- Offensive spells that successfully damage the marked target.

The bonus damage is applied **once per successful attack**.

#### Hunt Leader

While Hunter's Mark is active:

- Allies always know which creature is marked.
- The Ranger may reapply Hunter's Mark to the same target without paying an additional Mana Cost if the mark expires naturally.
- If the marked target is reduced to **0 HP**, the Ranger may immediately transfer Hunter's Mark to another creature within range **without spending an action**, paying only the Mana Cost.

#### Limitations

- Hunter's Mark does not reveal the target's location if it leaves line of sight.
- Only one Hunter's Mark may affect a creature at a time.
- If multiple Rangers mark the same creature, only the highest-ranked Hunter's Mark applies.
- Bonus damage from Hunter's Mark does not stack with another Hunter's Mark.

---

### Lore

To achieve the fifth rank of Hunter's Mark is to become one of the legendary Huntmasters of Asteria. These Rangers are revered throughout the Lodges for their uncanny ability to coordinate entire hunting parties against seemingly unstoppable foes. Every order they give is calculated, every marked target carefully chosen, and every strike brings the quarry closer to its inevitable demise.

Many of history's greatest hunts have been led by Rangers who possessed this mastery. Their companions often spoke of battles that felt effortless, as though every weakness had already been discovered before the fighting had even begun. Whether facing towering Behemoths, ancient Dragons, or horrors from beyond the veil, a Huntmaster ensured that no attack was wasted.

To the Ranger Lodges, Hunter's Mark is more than a talent—it is the symbol of absolute trust between hunter and hunting party, where many act with the precision of one.

---

> *"One arrow begins the hunt. One mark ensures every arrow thereafter finds its purpose."*  
> — **Grand Huntmaster Elyas Thornwood, First Keeper of the Hunter's Mark**

None

the bonus damage is applied **once per successful attack**.

#### limitations

- allies must be aware of the marked target to gain the bonus.
- hunter's mark does not reveal the target's location if it leaves line of sight.
- the mark immediately ends if the target dies.
- only one hunter's mark may affect a creature at a time. if multiple rangers mark the same target, only the highest-ranked hunter's mark applies.

---

### lore

by the third rank, hunter's mark becomes one of the defining techniques of an experienced ranger. their ability to recognise and communicate weaknesses transforms them from a solitary hunter into the leader of a coordinated hunt. veteran adventuring parties quickly learn to trust a ranger's judgement, knowing that every command is based upon careful observation rather than guesswork.

stories tell of ranger companies bringing down dragons, giants, and elder beasts by relentlessly exploiting a single weakness identified by their leader. these victories were not won through overwhelming strength, but through patience, precision, and cooperation—principles that define every true ranger.

---

> *"one hunter may wound the beast. a guided pack will bring it down."*  
> — **grand ranger elyas thornwood**

## rank 4
### description

the ranger's hunter's mark has become a symbol of battlefield leadership. with only a moment's observation, they identify weaknesses that would otherwise remain unnoticed, directing their allies to strike precisely where the quarry is most vulnerable. every command, gesture, and call is deliberate, allowing the hunting party to work together with deadly efficiency.

the ranger's connection to the marked quarry grows stronger as the hunt progresses. every wound reveals another opportunity, and every successful attack builds momentum for the entire group. few creatures can withstand a coordinated assault led by a master ranger.

veteran rangers often say that by this stage, the quarry is defeated long before the final blow is delivered—it simply has not realised it yet.

---

#### mark quarry

- spend **50 mp** to mark one creature within **60 metres** that you can see.
- the mark lasts for **10 minutes**.
- only **one creature** may be marked at a time.
- marking another creature immediately ends the previous mark.

#### hunter's instinct

while your quarry is marked:

**the ranger gains:**

- **+1d10 bonus damage** on all successful attacks against the marked target.

**allied creatures gain:**

- **+1d6 bonus damage** on successful attacks against the marked target.

this bonus applies to:

- ranged weapon attacks.
- melee weapon attacks.
- talents and abilities that deal direct damage.
- offensive spells that successfully hit the marked target.

the bonus damage is applied **once per successful attack**.

#### pack leader

while the quarry remains marked:

- allies always know which creature is marked.
- the ranger may reapply hunter's mark to the same target without paying an additional mana cost if the mark expires naturally during its duration.

#### limitations

- hunter's mark does not reveal the target's location if it leaves line of sight.
- the mark immediately ends if the target dies.
- only one hunter's mark may affect a creature at a time. if multiple rangers mark the same target, only the highest-ranked hunter's mark applies.
- bonus damage from hunter's mark does not stack with another hunter's mark.

---

### lore

only accomplished rangers achieve the fourth rank of hunter's mark. by this point, they have learned that hunting is rarely an individual pursuit. the greatest victories come from guiding companions toward the same objective, ensuring every strike contributes to bringing the quarry down.

entire ranger companies have built their tactics around hunters capable of maintaining these advanced marks. their commands carry absolute confidence, allowing warriors, mages, and scouts alike to focus their attacks with remarkable precision. to fight beside such a ranger is to feel as though every weakness has already been uncovered before the battle has truly begun.

---

> *"the mark is not a promise that the quarry will fall. it is a promise that every hunter now knows where to strike."*  
> — **grand ranger elyas thornwood**

## rank 5
### description

the ranger has mastered hunter's mark, becoming the unquestioned leader of the hunt. a single marked quarry becomes the sole focus of the battlefield, with every ally instinctively recognising where to strike and every attack driving the prey closer to its inevitable end. what began as a personal hunting technique has evolved into one of the most feared battlefield tactics employed by the ranger lodges.

a master ranger no longer simply identifies weaknesses—they orchestrate the downfall of their quarry. through observation, experience, and unwavering focus, they direct every member of the hunting party towards the target's greatest vulnerabilities. against such coordination, even legendary beasts struggle to withstand the relentless assault.

throughout asteria, stories tell of dragons, elder beasts, and demon lords falling beneath the combined might of a hunting party guided by a single master ranger. their greatest weapon was never their bow, but their ability to unite every strike into one perfect hunt.

# Hunting Shots

## Overview
The greatest Rangers are not defined by the weapons they carry, but by the techniques they master. Hunting Shots represent years of specialised training, allowing a Ranger to perform extraordinary feats of marksmanship beyond a standard attack.

Upon learning this talent, the Ranger unlocks their first Hunting Shot and first Trick Shot. Hunting Shots are specialised combat techniques designed to control or weaken enemies, while Trick Shots demonstrate exceptional skill, allowing impossible angles and creative solutions both in and out of combat.

As the Ranger grows stronger, additional ranks unlock new shots rather than replacing old ones, creating an ever-expanding arsenal of precision techniques.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

The greatest Rangers are not defined by the weapons they carry, but by the techniques they master. Hunting Shots represent years of specialised training, allowing a Ranger to perform extraordinary feats of marksmanship beyond a standard attack.

Upon learning this talent, the Ranger unlocks their first Hunting Shot and first Trick Shot. Hunting Shots are specialised combat techniques designed to control or weaken enemies, while Trick Shots demonstrate exceptional skill, allowing impossible angles and creative solutions both in and out of combat.

As the Ranger grows stronger, additional ranks unlock new shots rather than replacing old ones, creating an ever-expanding arsenal of precision techniques.

---

### Effects

#### Hunting Shot — Stunning Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 15 SP

After making a successful ranged weapon attack, you may declare it as a **Stunning Shot**.

- The target must succeed on a **Constitution Saving Throw**.
- On a failure, the target becomes **Staggered** until the end of its next turn.
- While Staggered, the target cannot take Reactions and has Disadvantage on its next attack roll.
- On a successful save, the target suffers normal weapon damage with no additional effect.

#### Trick Shot — Curve Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 10 SP

The Ranger applies exceptional spin and trajectory to a projectile.

- Fire around corners, trees, pillars, or similar obstacles.
- Ignore partial line-of-sight restrictions where a curved trajectory is physically possible.
- Reduce penalties for difficult or unconventional ranged attacks, at the GM's discretion.
- This shot cannot pass through solid objects or total cover.

#### General Rules

- Only one Hunting Shot or Trick Shot may be applied to a single attack unless another ability states otherwise.
- Hunting Shots may only be used with ranged weapons.
- Additional Hunting Shots and Trick Shots are unlocked by increasing this talent's rank.

---

### Lore

Every Ranger Lodge teaches that an arrow is only as effective as the mind guiding it. While ordinary archers rely upon accuracy alone, Rangers develop specialised techniques that allow each shot to serve a unique purpose. Whether disabling prey, striking impossible angles, or controlling the battlefield, every technique reflects countless hours of disciplined practice.

Veteran Rangers often recognise one another not by the bows they carry, but by the techniques they employ. Many legendary Hunting Shots have been passed from mentor to apprentice for centuries, with each generation refining and expanding the art of precision marksmanship.

---

> *"Any archer can loose an arrow. A Ranger chooses exactly what that arrow will accomplish."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

As the Ranger's mastery grows, so too does their arsenal of specialised techniques. Every hunt presents new challenges, and experienced Rangers learn that a single type of shot cannot solve every problem. Through relentless practice, they develop new methods capable of overcoming heavily armoured prey and striking enemies from angles they believe to be impossible.

At this rank, the Ranger unlocks two new techniques: **Drill Shot**, a devastating armour-piercing attack designed to punch through resilient defences, and **Ricochet Shot**, a trick shot that uses hard surfaces to strike targets from unexpected directions. These techniques reward creativity, positioning, and battlefield awareness.

A skilled Ranger is never limited by a straight line. They learn to make every obstacle another tool in their hunt.

---

### Effects

#### Hunting Shot — Drill Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 20 SP

The Ranger fires a specialised armour-piercing projectile designed to bore through armour, scales, and hardened hides.

- Make a ranged weapon attack as normal.
- On a successful hit, the attack **ignores Half Cover**.
- The attack ignores **2 points of Armour Rating or Natural Armour** (or an equivalent value determined by the GM).
- Drill Shot may only affect the initial target and cannot strike additional creatures.

#### Trick Shot — Ricochet Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 15 SP

The Ranger deliberately bounces a projectile off a hard surface before striking the intended target.

- The projectile may ricochet off one solid surface before hitting its target.
- The shot may ignore obstacles that would normally block a direct line of fire, provided a reasonable ricochet path exists.
- Reduce penalties for indirect shots at the GM's discretion.
- Ricochet Shot cannot pass through solid objects or total cover.

#### General Rules

- The Ranger retains access to **Stunning Shot** and **Curve Shot**.
- Only one Hunting Shot or one Trick Shot may be applied to a single attack unless another ability states otherwise.
- Hunting Shots may only be used with ranged weapons.
- Additional Hunting Shots and Trick Shots are unlocked by increasing this talent's rank.

---

### Lore

Among Ranger Lodges, the second rank of Hunting Shots marks the point where an apprentice begins to think beyond conventional marksmanship. Rather than simply aiming at a target, they learn to manipulate both the projectile and the environment, turning armour into a weakness and obstacles into opportunities.

Many famous Rangers earned their reputations through shots that others believed impossible. Tales speak of arrows skipping from stone walls, bolts punching through thick scales, and hunters striking prey that never even realised they had been exposed. Such techniques are only possible through unwavering discipline and countless hours of practice.

---

> *"When the path is blocked, do not change your target—change the path."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The Ranger has progressed beyond mastering individual techniques and now learns to manipulate both the battlefield and the enemy's movements. Every shot is carefully chosen to restrict, outmanoeuvre, or overwhelm their quarry before the decisive strike is delivered.

At this rank, the Ranger unlocks **Pinning Shot**, a technique designed to hinder an opponent's movement, and **Split Shot**, a remarkable feat of precision that allows a single attack to threaten multiple targets. These techniques showcase the Ranger's growing mastery over both control and precision.

Veteran Rangers know that victory is often determined long before the final arrow is loosed. By controlling where an enemy can move and how they react, the hunt becomes all but inevitable.

---

### Effects

#### Hunting Shot — Pinning Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 25 SP

The Ranger fires a carefully placed shot intended to restrict the target's movement rather than inflict maximum injury.

- Make a ranged weapon attack as normal.
- On a successful hit, the target must succeed on a **Strength Saving Throw** or become **Pinned** until the end of its next turn.
- While Pinned:
  - The target's movement speed is reduced to **0**.
  - The target cannot Dash.
- Flying creatures that fail the saving throw immediately descend safely to the ground if able, or have their flying speed reduced to 0 until the effect ends (GM discretion).
- Creatures that are significantly larger than the projectile may gain Advantage on the saving throw.

#### Trick Shot — Split Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 20 SP

The Ranger performs an extraordinary feat of marksmanship, releasing two projectiles almost simultaneously.

- Make one attack roll against two creatures within **3 metres** of each other.
- Compare the same attack roll against each target's Armour Class.
- Roll damage separately for each creature that is successfully hit.
- Ammunition for both shots is still consumed.

#### General Rules

- The Ranger retains access to **Stunning Shot**, **Curve Shot**, **Drill Shot**, and **Ricochet Shot**.
- Only one Hunting Shot or one Trick Shot may be applied to a single attack unless another ability states otherwise.
- Hunting Shots may only be used with ranged weapons.
- Additional Hunting Shots and Trick Shots are unlocked by increasing this talent's rank.

---

### Lore

By the third rank, a Ranger's techniques become recognised throughout the Lodges as the mark of a seasoned hunter. They no longer rely solely on accuracy but instead shape the flow of battle itself, deciding where prey may run and when it must stand its ground.

Stories speak of master Rangers pinning charging beasts to ancient trees before turning a single fluid movement into two perfectly placed arrows that felled separate enemies. Such feats are impossible without years of disciplined practice, unwavering focus, and complete trust in one's own skill.

---

> *"A true hunter does not simply strike their prey—they decide where it may stand, where it may run, and when the hunt shall end."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

Master Rangers understand that a well-placed arrow can control the battlefield just as effectively as it can wound an enemy. By the fourth rank, they have developed techniques capable of overwhelming even the largest foes, using raw impact and exceptional skill to dictate the flow of combat.

At this rank, the Ranger unlocks **Impact Shot**, a devastating attack that uses tremendous force to drive enemies backwards or knock them from their feet, and **Arcing Shot**, a specialised technique that allows projectiles to travel in a high trajectory, striking enemies hiding behind walls, fortifications, or other obstacles.

These techniques demonstrate that a master Ranger is not limited by distance, cover, or terrain. Every obstacle becomes another opportunity to land the perfect shot.

---

### Effects

#### Hunting Shot — Impact Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 30 SP

The Ranger delivers a powerful shot designed to overwhelm the target through sheer force.

- Make a ranged weapon attack as normal.
- On a successful hit, the target must succeed on a **Strength Saving Throw**.
- On a failed save:
  - The target is pushed **3 metres** directly away from the Ranger.
  - If the target cannot be pushed because it collides with a solid object, it is instead **knocked Prone**.
- On a successful save, the target suffers normal weapon damage but is not pushed or knocked prone.
- **Large** creatures have **Advantage** on the saving throw.
- **Huge** and larger creatures cannot be pushed but may still be knocked **Prone** at the GM's discretion.

#### Trick Shot — Arcing Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 20 SP

The Ranger launches a projectile in a high, controlled arc to strike targets beyond conventional lines of fire.

- Ignore obstacles that block a direct shot provided a clear aerial trajectory exists.
- You may target creatures behind low walls, battlements, trenches, or similar cover.
- The target does not benefit from **Half Cover** provided the arc successfully bypasses it.
- The GM determines whether sufficient overhead clearance exists for the shot.

#### General Rules

- The Ranger retains access to all previously unlocked Hunting Shots and Trick Shots.
- Only one Hunting Shot or one Trick Shot may be applied to a single attack unless another ability states otherwise.
- Hunting Shots may only be used with ranged weapons.
- Additional Hunting Shots and Trick Shots are unlocked by increasing this talent's rank.

---

### Lore

Among the Ranger Lodges, the fourth rank of Hunting Shots is considered the mark of a battlefield master. These Rangers no longer think only about defeating a single opponent—they shape the entire battlefield, forcing enemies into vulnerable positions while striking those who believed themselves safely protected.

Many military commanders have sought the aid of master Rangers during sieges and large-scale battles. Their ability to strike defenders behind walls, scatter charging enemies, and manipulate the flow of combat has turned the tide of countless conflicts throughout Asteria.

---

> *"A wall is only protection until a Ranger learns to shoot over it. Strength is only an advantage until a Ranger learns to throw you backwards."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has reached the pinnacle of ranged weapon mastery. Every arrow, bolt, bullet, or thrown projectile becomes an extension of their will, capable of travelling extraordinary distances and striking with impossible precision. No battlefield is too large, no target too distant, and no obstacle too daunting for a true master of Hunting Shots.

At this rank, the Ranger unlocks **Horizon Shot**, a legendary technique that dramatically extends the effective range of their ranged weapon, allowing them to engage enemies long before those enemies can retaliate. Alongside it, the Ranger also masters **Impossible Shot**, a technique reserved for only the greatest marksmen, capable of accomplishing feats that most would consider beyond belief.

Among the Ranger Lodges, only a handful of hunters throughout history have ever demonstrated these techniques in battle. Their shots are remembered for generations, becoming stories told around campfires as examples of what true dedication can achieve.

---

### Effects

#### Hunting Shot — Horizon Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 35 SP

The Ranger unleashes a perfectly calculated shot designed to travel far beyond the normal limits of their weapon.

- Increase the weapon's **maximum range by 50%** for this attack.
- Ignore penalties associated with attacking at **long range**.
- The attack ignores **Half Cover**.
- Horizon Shot may be used with any ranged weapon.

#### Trick Shot — Impossible Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 25 SP

The Ranger performs a feat of marksmanship bordering on legend.

Choose one of the following when making the attack:

- Thread a projectile through an exceptionally narrow opening.
- Strike a tiny unattended object.
- Cut a rope, chain, or similar object.
- Trigger a distant mechanism.
- Perform another extraordinary ranged feat, subject to GM approval.

The GM may reduce or remove penalties for exceptionally difficult shots when Impossible Shot is used.

#### General Rules

- The Ranger retains access to every previously unlocked Hunting Shot and Trick Shot.
- Only one Hunting Shot or one Trick Shot may be applied to a single attack unless another ability states otherwise.
- Hunting Shots may only be used with ranged weapons.
- Impossible Shot cannot bypass magical barriers or ignore total cover.

---

### Lore

The fifth rank of Hunting Shots is spoken of with near-mythical reverence throughout the Ranger Lodges. Tales tell of Rangers striking enemy commanders from across entire valleys, severing bridge supports with a single arrow, or saving companions by cutting ropes and triggering mechanisms at precisely the right moment.

These feats are not considered luck or magic—they are the culmination of decades of unwavering discipline, flawless technique, and an intimate understanding of both weapon and environment. To witness a master Ranger employ Horizon Shot or Impossible Shot is to witness the very peak of mortal marksmanship.

---

> *"Distance is an obstacle only to those who doubt their aim."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, Master Marksman of the Emerald Lodge**

None
