### Lore

The first lesson taught to every Bloodhunter apprentice is simple: never divide your attention between multiple hunts. A distracted hunter is a dead hunter. Mark of the Quarry embodies this philosophy, teaching absolute focus upon a single foe until the hunt reaches its conclusion.

Veteran Bloodhunters often describe the mark as a quiet whisper carried through the blood. It is not a voice, nor a vision, but an instinct that constantly reminds the hunter where their purpose lies. Every heartbeat strengthens the connection until hunter and quarry become inseparably bound.

Many Bloodhunters have fallen to Bloodlust after allowing the thrill of a successful hunt to consume them. For this reason, the elders teach that the mark is more than a hunting technique—it is a test of discipline. The Bloodhunter must learn to end the hunt without allowing the hunt to consume them.

> *"A hunter without a quarry is merely a warrior. A Bloodhunter chooses one life... and does not stop until its final heartbeat."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 2
### Description

As a Bloodhunter's mastery of Sangramancy grows, so too does the strength of the bond forged between hunter and quarry. The Mark of the Quarry no longer serves merely as a declaration of intent—it becomes a supernatural tether that strengthens every instinct the Bloodhunter possesses. The marked creature's blood resonates with the hunter's own, making it increasingly difficult for the quarry to escape the inevitable conclusion of the hunt.

The Bloodhunter begins to anticipate the movements of their quarry with frightening accuracy. Every subtle shift in posture, every desperate attempt to flee, and every hesitation in combat seems almost instinctive to read. To outsiders, this appears to be incredible skill, but experienced Bloodhunters know the truth—it is the blood itself revealing the path of the hunt.

The connection between hunter and quarry also strengthens the Bloodhunter's Sangramancy. Techniques such as Blood Scent, Blood Rush, Veinlock, and Hunter's Bane become increasingly effective when directed towards the marked creature, rewarding the Bloodhunter for maintaining focus on a single target.

The Bloodhunter Orders teach that this unwavering focus is both a strength and a danger. Obsession is never far from purpose, and every successful hunt feeds the emotions that slowly build towards Bloodlust.

### Effects

- As a **Bonus Action**, mark one creature within **25 metres** as your **Marked Quarry**.
- Spend **20 MP**, sacrifice **8 HP**, and gain **10 Blood Points (BP)**.
- You may only have **one Marked Quarry** at a time.
- The mark remains until:
  - The target dies.
  - You mark another creature.
  - You complete a **Long Rest**.
- Gain **+2 to Attack Rolls** against your **Marked Quarry**.
- Gain **+3 Damage** against your **Marked Quarry**.
- Your **Blood Scent** automatically recognises the blood of your Marked Quarry while the mark remains active.
- Any Bloodhunter talent that references your **Marked Quarry** may target this creature.
- You always know the **general direction** of your Marked Quarry while it remains on the same plane of existence.
- When your Marked Quarry is reduced to **0 HP**, immediately gain **15 Blood Points (BP)**.

### Lore

Within the Bloodhunter Orders, the Second Rank is known as the point where the hunter truly begins to understand the meaning of pursuit. The mark is no longer simply placed upon a creature—it becomes a bond written into blood itself. No matter how desperately the quarry runs, the Bloodhunter feels the faint pull of the connection guiding them onward.

Veteran Bloodhunters describe the sensation as hearing a distant heartbeat that never truly fades. It is subtle, almost impossible for others to comprehend, yet unmistakable to the hunter who forged the bond. Every step taken by the quarry strengthens the Bloodhunter's resolve to see the hunt through to its inevitable end.

The elders often remind apprentices that Mark of the Quarry is not permission to become obsessed. A hunter who cannot let go after the hunt is finished has already begun walking the path towards Bloodlust. The mark exists to focus the hunt—not to consume the hunter.

> *"The quarry may lose sight of me... but it can never escape the blood that binds us together."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 3
### Description

By the Third Rank, the Mark of the Quarry has become an inseparable extension of the Bloodhunter's Sangramancy. The moment the ritual is completed, a fragment of the Bloodhunter's lifeblood intertwines with that of their chosen prey, creating a bond that neither distance nor deception can easily sever. To the Bloodhunter, the hunt has already begun—the only question remaining is how long the quarry can survive.

The Bloodhunter's instincts sharpen dramatically while confronting their Marked Quarry. Every movement, every hesitation, and every drop of blood spilled reinforces the supernatural connection between hunter and prey. The Bloodhunter no longer reacts to the battle; they anticipate it, predicting the quarry's actions through the rhythm of its blood.

This deeper bond also strengthens every Sangramancy technique the Bloodhunter possesses. Blood Rush drives them relentlessly towards the quarry, Veinlock seizes their blood with greater precision, Blood Scent recognises even the faintest trace of their lifeblood, and Hunter's Bane pushes the Bloodhunter ever closer to perfection against their chosen foe.

Yet such focus carries a terrible danger. The stronger the bond becomes, the greater the exhilaration when the hunt is finally complete. Every successful kill floods the Bloodhunter with powerful emotions, feeding Bloodlust and reminding them that obsession is never far removed from purpose.

The elders teach that the Crimson Bond is one of Sangramancy's greatest gifts—and one of its greatest temptations. A Bloodhunter who allows the bond to become obsession may eventually forget why they hunt at all. The greatest masters remember that the mark exists to protect the innocent, never to satisfy the darkness within.

> *"The mark does not tell me where you are. It reminds me that the hunt is not finished."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

### Description

Legends tell of Bloodhunters pursuing their quarry across continents, through ancient ruins, and into the darkest corners of the world. Distance becomes meaningless when blood itself remembers the bond that was forged. Even after weeks of pursuit, the Bloodhunter can still sense the faint pull guiding them toward the creature they swore to destroy.

The elders teach that this rank represents the greatest test of discipline before true mastery. The Bloodhunter must never allow the hunt to define who they are. They are protectors first, hunters second. Those who forget this truth eventually discover that Bloodlust no longer cares who has been marked—it only cares that blood continues to flow.

> *"Once I write your name in blood, the world itself becomes your prison."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 5
### Description

The Fifth Rank of Mark of the Quarry is the pinnacle of the Bloodhunter's hunting discipline. Through absolute mastery of Sangramancy, the Bloodhunter no longer merely marks a creature—they forge an unbreakable covenant written in blood itself. The moment the ritual is complete, the quarry becomes the sole focus of the hunt, bound to the Bloodhunter until one of them falls.

At this level, the Bloodhunter's instincts transcend ordinary perception. Masters teach that reaching this rank is not about learning to hunt monsters—it is about proving that the monster within will never become the one choosing the quarry.

### Effects

- As a **Bonus Action**, mark one creature within **40 metres** as your **Marked Quarry**.
- Spend **50 MP**, sacrifice **20 HP**, and gain **25 Blood Points (BP)**.
- You may only have **one Marked Quarry** at a time.
- The mark remains until:
  - The target dies.
  - You mark another creature.
  - You complete a **Long Rest**.
- Gain **+5 to Attack Rolls** against your **Marked Quarry**.
- Gain **+6 Damage** against your **Marked Quarry**.
- You always know the **direction and approximate distance** of your Marked Quarry while it remains on the same plane of existence.
- Your **Blood Scent** automatically recognises your Marked Quarry regardless of how old the blood trail is.

- All Bloodhunter talents that reference your **Marked Quarry** gain their maximum benefits against this creature.
- When your **Marked Quarry** is reduced to **0 HP**, immediately gain **30 Blood Points (BP)**.

### Lore

Among the Bloodhunter Orders, the Fifth Rank is known as **The Crimson Verdict**. Very few hunters ever achieve this level of mastery, for it demands complete understanding of both Sangramancy and the discipline required to wield it. Those who do are spoken of in hushed voices, for once they have chosen their quarry, the hunt is considered all but inevitable.

Ancient records tell of Bloodhunters pursuing dragons across mountain ranges, vampires through forgotten kingdoms, and eldritch horrors into realms untouched by mortal hands. Distance, deception, and time become meaningless when blood itself remembers the oath that has been sworn.

The elders teach one final lesson before granting this knowledge. The Mark of the Quarry is not permission to kill—it is a promise to finish what must be done. A Bloodhunter who marks out of hatred, vengeance, or obsession has already begun surrendering to Bloodlust. The greatest hunters are remembered not because they never failed, but because they always remained masters of their own blood.

> *"The mark is not your sentence. It is my promise that this hunt will have an end."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

# mark of the quarry

## overview
every bloodhunter understands that a hunt truly begins the moment prey is chosen. through sangramancy, the bloodhunter offers a small portion of their own blood, weaving it into the life force of a single creature. this crimson bond is known as the **mark of the quarry**—a supernatural connection that allows the hunter to relentlessly pursue their chosen prey.

unlike ordinary tracking magic, the mark is not placed upon the creature's body alone. it binds to the creature's blood itself. as long as the creature lives, the bloodhunter can instinctively feel the connection, making every strike more precise and every movement more deliberate. to the bloodhunter, there is no longer a battlefield filled with enemies—only the quarry.

the mark also serves as the foundation of every advanced sangramancy technique. blood scent becomes easier to follow, veinlock grips tighter, and the bloodhunter's predatory instincts sharpen whenever confronting their chosen target. every lesson taught within the bloodhunter orders begins with the same principle: one hunter, one quarry.

the ritual is not without cost. every mark requires a willing blood sacrifice and stirs the emotions carried within the bloodhunter's soul. the hunt becomes deeply personal, and the satisfaction of finally bringing down the marked creature only fuels the growing danger of bloodlust.

ancient records tell of bloodhunters pursuing dragons across mountain ranges, vampires through forgotten kingdoms, and eldritch horrors into realms untouched by mortal hands. distance, deception, and time become meaningless when blood itself remembers the oath that has been sworn.

the elders teach one final lesson before granting this knowledge. the mark of the quarry is not permission to kill—it is a promise to finish what must be done. a bloodhunter who marks out of hatred, vengeance, or obsession has already begun surrendering to bloodlust. the greatest hunters are remembered not because they never failed, but because they always remained masters of their own blood.

> *"the mark is not your sentence. it is my promise that this hunt will have an end."*  
> — grand bloodhunter serik vaelor

# Multi Shot

## Overview
Master Rangers learn that one arrow is not always enough. Through exceptional speed, coordination, and years of disciplined training, the Ranger can nock and release multiple arrows in rapid succession, engaging several enemies before they have time to react.

Unlike Hunting Shots, which focus on specialised techniques, Multi Shot is about overwhelming battlefield presence. The Ranger rapidly transitions between targets, placing accurate shots where they are needed most. Every arrow is individually aimed, ensuring precision is never sacrificed for speed.

While exhausting to perform, Multi Shot allows the Ranger to control groups of enemies without losing the deadly accuracy that defines their craft.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

Master Rangers learn that one arrow is not always enough. Through exceptional speed, coordination, and years of disciplined training, the Ranger can nock and release multiple arrows in rapid succession, engaging several enemies before they have time to react.

Unlike Hunting Shots, which focus on specialised techniques, Multi Shot is about overwhelming battlefield presence. The Ranger rapidly transitions between targets, placing accurate shots where they are needed most. Every arrow is individually aimed, ensuring precision is never sacrificed for speed.

While exhausting to perform, Multi Shot allows the Ranger to control groups of enemies without losing the deadly accuracy that defines their craft.

---

### Effects

#### Multi Shot

**Cost:** 30 SP

As an Action, make **two separate ranged weapon attacks**.

- Each attack may target the **same creature** or **two different creatures** within your weapon's range.
- Roll each attack and damage separately.
- Each attack consumes **one piece of ammunition**.
- Hunting Shots and Trick Shots may only be applied to **one** of the attacks unless another ability states otherwise.

#### Limitations

- Multi Shot may only be used with **bows, crossbows, firearms, or other ranged weapons** capable of making individual attacks.
- You cannot combine Multi Shot with another ability that grants additional attacks unless specifically stated.
- You must have sufficient ammunition for every attack made.

---

### Lore

The first Rangers to master Multi Shot were said to have defended entire mountain passes against overwhelming odds, loosing arrows so quickly that witnesses believed several hunters were fighting side by side. Though these stories have undoubtedly grown with time, every Ranger Lodge teaches that speed without discipline is meaningless.

Apprentices spend years strengthening their draw, refining their posture, and practising seamless transitions between targets before they are entrusted with this technique. A true master never fires wildly. Every arrow is released with purpose, whether protecting companions or bringing multiple foes low before they can close the distance.

---

> *"One arrow wins a duel. Many well-placed arrows win the battle."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's speed and coordination continue to improve, allowing them to engage multiple threats with astonishing efficiency. Years of training have taught the Ranger how to transition seamlessly between targets, loosing arrows with fluid precision while maintaining complete control over every shot.

Rather than relying on reckless speed, the Ranger carefully selects each target before releasing a rapid volley. Every arrow is deliberately placed, allowing the Ranger to protect allies, suppress advancing enemies, or concentrate fire where it is needed most.

Among the Ranger Lodges, mastery of the second rank marks the point where a Ranger is no longer considered a skilled archer, but a battlefield marksman capable of controlling the flow of combat through overwhelming precision.

---

### Effects

#### Multi Shot

**Cost:** 40 SP

As an Action, make **three separate ranged weapon attacks**.

- Each attack may target the **same creature** or **different creatures** within your weapon's range.
- Roll each attack and damage separately.
- Each attack consumes **one piece of ammunition**.
- You may freely choose the order in which the attacks are resolved.
- Hunting Shots or Trick Shots may only be applied to **one** of the attacks unless another ability specifically states otherwise.

#### Limitations

- Multi Shot may only be used with bows, crossbows, firearms, or other ranged weapons capable of making individual attacks.
- You cannot combine Multi Shot with abilities that grant additional attacks unless specifically stated.
- You must have sufficient ammunition for every attack made.

---

### Lore

Veteran Rangers often describe Multi Shot as a dance rather than a technique. Every movement flows naturally into the next, allowing the Ranger to draw, nock, and release arrows with such efficiency that onlookers struggle to follow the motion. To the untrained eye, it appears as though several archers are firing simultaneously.

Within the Ranger Lodges, apprentices spend years developing the strength, stamina, and coordination required to master this technique. Instructors teach that speed alone is meaningless—true mastery comes from ensuring every arrow still finds its intended mark.

---

> *"The greatest Rangers are never hurried. They are simply faster than everyone else can comprehend."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The Ranger has mastered the art of engaging entire groups of enemies without sacrificing precision. Through countless hours of practice, drawing, nocking, and releasing arrows becomes a seamless motion, allowing them to strike multiple targets before their opponents can react.

At this level, the Ranger's awareness of the battlefield is exceptional. They instinctively prioritise dangerous opponents, exploit openings, and shift their focus between enemies with effortless speed. Every arrow is released with purpose, ensuring that no shot is wasted, whether protecting allies or thinning advancing ranks.

Among the Ranger Lodges, Rangers capable of this level of marksmanship are often assigned to defend settlements and lead hunting parties, where controlling multiple threats can mean the difference between victory and defeat.

---

### Effects

#### Multi Shot

**Cost:** 50 SP

As an Action, make **four separate ranged weapon attacks**.

- Each attack may target the **same creature** or **different creatures** within your weapon's range.
- Roll each attack and damage separately.
- Each attack consumes **one piece of ammunition**.
- You may freely choose the order in which the attacks are resolved.
- Hunting Shots or Trick Shots may only be applied to **one** of the attacks unless another ability specifically states otherwise.

#### Limitations

- Multi Shot may only be used with bows, crossbows, firearms, or other ranged weapons capable of making individual attacks.
- You cannot combine Multi Shot with abilities that grant additional attacks unless specifically stated.
- You must have sufficient ammunition for every attack made.

---

### Lore

To witness a Ranger perform the third rank of Multi Shot is to watch years of relentless discipline brought to life. Arrows leave the bow with astonishing speed, each one guided by instinct and experience rather than conscious thought. Enemies often mistake the attack for the work of several archers until they realise every shot came from the same Ranger.

The Ranger Lodges consider this level of mastery to be one of the defining traits of a veteran hunter. Many legendary battles have been won by a single Ranger who stood their ground against overwhelming numbers, calmly releasing arrow after arrow until the battlefield fell silent once more.

---

> *"One target demands accuracy. Four targets demand mastery."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger's speed has reached a level few can comprehend. Every movement flows into the next with flawless precision, allowing them to loose a devastating volley that can dominate an entire battlefield. Rather than focusing on individual duels, the Ranger effortlessly shifts between multiple threats, delivering accurate fire wherever it is needed most.

At this stage, Multi Shot is no longer simply a demonstration of exceptional archery—it becomes battlefield control through overwhelming precision. The Ranger can suppress advancing enemies, eliminate vulnerable targets, or focus an incredible number of attacks against a single powerful foe.

Only the most accomplished Rangers within the Lodges are entrusted with teaching this technique. It represents years of physical conditioning, unwavering discipline, and countless hours spent perfecting every draw and release until they become instinct.

---

### Effects

#### Multi Shot

**Cost:** 60 SP

As an Action, make **five separate ranged weapon attacks**.

- Each attack may target the **same creature** or **different creatures** within your weapon's range.
- Roll each attack and damage separately.
- Each attack consumes **one piece of ammunition**.
- You may freely choose the order in which the attacks are resolved.
- You may apply **one Hunting Shot or one Trick Shot** to any **one** of these attacks unless another ability specifically states otherwise.

#### Limitations

- Multi Shot may only be used with **bows, crossbows, firearms, or other ranged weapons** capable of making individual attacks.
- Multi Shot cannot be combined with abilities that grant additional attacks unless specifically stated.
- You must have sufficient ammunition for every attack made.

---

### Lore

Master Rangers who wield the fourth rank of Multi Shot are feared across battlefields throughout Asteria. Witnesses often describe their attacks as a storm of arrows, each one striking with deliberate purpose rather than reckless speed. Every shot is carefully placed, demonstrating complete awareness of both allies and enemies alike.

Military commanders frequently seek these Rangers when defending fortifications or escorting important caravans. A single master marksman capable of engaging five threats within moments can often halt an assault before it reaches friendly lines. Their calm precision under pressure has become the standard by which all Ranger marksmen are judged.

---

> *"Five arrows. Five choices. Five opportunities to change the course of a battle."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has reached the pinnacle of ranged combat, capable of unleashing an extraordinary barrage of precision attacks in the blink of an eye. Years of relentless practice have refined every movement until drawing, nocking, and releasing become one seamless action. To onlookers, the volley appears less like individual shots and more like a relentless storm of perfectly aimed projectiles.

Unlike ordinary archers who rely on speed alone, a master of Multi Shot sacrifices none of their accuracy. Every arrow is deliberately placed, allowing the Ranger to engage entire groups of enemies, overwhelm powerful foes with concentrated fire, or adapt instantly to the changing flow of battle.

Only the greatest Huntmasters of Asteria are capable of performing this technique. Tales tell of legendary Rangers defending entire passes alone, their arrows falling so rapidly and accurately that enemies believed they were facing an entire company of archers rather than a single hunter.

---

### Effects

#### Multi Shot

**Cost:** 70 SP

As an Action, make **six separate ranged weapon attacks**.

- Each attack may target the **same creature** or **different creatures** within your weapon's range.
- Roll each attack and damage separately.
- Each attack consumes **one piece of ammunition**.
- Resolve the attacks in any order you choose.
- You may apply **one Hunting Shot or one Trick Shot** to **one** of these attacks unless another ability specifically states otherwise.

#### Limitations

- Multi Shot may only be used with **bows, crossbows, firearms, or other ranged weapons** capable of making individual attacks.
- Multi Shot cannot be combined with abilities that grant additional attacks unless specifically stated.
- You must have sufficient ammunition for every attack made.

---

### Lore

The fifth rank of Multi Shot represents one of the greatest achievements a Ranger can attain. Within the Lodges, only a select few ever master the technique, earning recognition as living legends whose skill borders on the impossible. Their arrows fly with such speed and precision that even experienced warriors struggle to follow their movements.

Stories of these Rangers have spread throughout Asteria for centuries. Some speak of Huntmasters holding narrow mountain passes against entire warbands, while others tell of impossible hunts where six beasts fell before the first had even reached the ground. Whether these tales have grown with time matters little—the legends endure because they are rooted in the extraordinary discipline and mastery of those who dedicated their lives to perfecting the bow.

---

> *"Six arrows leave the string, yet each finds its own destiny. That is not speed—it is mastery."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Huntmaster of the Emerald Lodge**

# Mystic Recovery

## Overview
Mystic Recovery teaches the Spellblade that health, stamina, and mana are not separate energies, but different expressions of the same life force. Through careful control of their mana core, a Spellblade can sacrifice one resource to restore another, allowing them to adapt to the ever-changing demands of battle.

At Rank I, the conversion process is crude and highly inefficient. Much of the energy is lost during the transmutation, requiring the Spellblade to sacrifice far more than they recover. Even so, experienced warriors understand that surviving a battle often depends upon having the right resource available at the right moment, regardless of the cost.

In addition to active transmutation, the Spellblade's growing understanding of their own life force naturally accelerates their recovery while resting, allowing their body and mana to replenish more efficiently between encounters.

## Rank 1
### Description

Mystic Recovery teaches the Spellblade that health, stamina, and mana are not separate energies, but different expressions of the same life force. Through careful control of their mana core, a Spellblade can sacrifice one resource to restore another, allowing them to adapt to the ever-changing demands of battle.

At Rank I, the conversion process is crude and highly inefficient. Much of the energy is lost during the transmutation, requiring the Spellblade to sacrifice far more than they recover. Even so, experienced warriors understand that surviving a battle often depends upon having the right resource available at the right moment, regardless of the cost.

In addition to active transmutation, the Spellblade's growing understanding of their own life force naturally accelerates their recovery while resting, allowing their body and mana to replenish more efficiently between encounters.

### Effects

#### Active

- Spend **1 Action Point** to activate **Mystic Recovery**.
- Instantly perform **one** of the following conversions using a **3:1 ratio**:
  - Spend **3 HP** to restore **1 MP**.
  - Spend **3 MP** to restore **1 SP**.
  - Spend **3 SP** to restore **1 HP**.
- Mystic Recovery may only be used **once per turn**.
- Restored resources cannot exceed their maximum values.
- This talent cannot reduce your HP below **1**.

#### Passive

- Increase your natural **Health, Mana, and Stamina regeneration by 10%** while resting outside of combat.

### Lore

Among the Spellblade Orders, Mystic Recovery is considered one of the first lessons in mastering the body's internal energies. Apprentices are taught that mana, stamina, and life are connected by a single current, and that with sufficient discipline, one form of energy can be transformed into another.

The process is imperfect at first, often leaving the practitioner drained after each conversion. However, every successful transmutation strengthens their understanding of this delicate balance, laying the foundation for far greater mastery in the years to come.

Veteran Spellblades often remind their students that Mystic Recovery is not a technique of abundance, but one of sacrifice. Victory belongs to those willing to give up what they have in order to preserve what they need most.

> *"Strength is not measured by what you possess, but by what you are willing to sacrifice to keep fighting."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 2
### Description

The Spellblade's understanding of internal energy has grown considerably, allowing them to perform resource transmutation with far greater efficiency. By strengthening the connection between their mana core, physical endurance, and life force, they reduce the amount of energy lost during each conversion.

While the process still requires sacrifice, experienced Spellblades learn to redirect energy with greater precision, making Mystic Recovery a dependable technique during prolonged battles. Whether restoring precious mana to continue casting, recovering stamina to maintain relentless attacks, or converting excess stamina into life, the Spellblade gains greater control over their own survival.

As their mastery improves, the Spellblade's body also becomes more efficient at recovering naturally. Even while resting, their internal energies continue to rebalance themselves, allowing them to recover faster than ordinary warriors or mages.

### Effects

#### Active

- Spend **1 Action Point** to activate **Mystic Recovery**.
- Instantly perform **one** of the following conversions using a **2:1 ratio**:
  - Spend **2 HP** to restore **1 MP**.
  - Spend **2 MP** to restore **1 SP**.
  - Spend **2 SP** to restore **1 HP**.
- Mystic Recovery may only be used **once per turn**.
- Restored resources cannot exceed their maximum values.
- This talent cannot reduce your HP below **1**.

#### Passive

- Increase your natural **Health, Mana, and Stamina regeneration by 20%** while resting outside of combat.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank II is known as the **Balanced Exchange**. Apprentices have moved beyond crude transmutation, learning instead to guide energy with careful precision rather than brute force. Every successful conversion strengthens the connection between body, mind, and soul.

Masters teach that Mystic Recovery is not merely a survival technique—it is an exercise in discipline. A Spellblade who understands when to sacrifice one resource for another can remain effective long after others have exhausted their strength.

Many veteran Spellblades credit this technique with saving their lives during long campaigns, where careful management of their own life force often proved more valuable than any potion or enchanted relic.

> *"Energy is never truly lost. The wise simply learn how to guide it where it is needed most."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 3
### Description

The Spellblade has mastered the balance between body, mind, and mana, achieving perfect harmony over the three fundamental energies that sustain all life. No longer wasting energy during transmutation, they can redirect their internal reserves with flawless precision, allowing them to adapt instantly to the demands of battle.

At Rank III, Mystic Recovery reaches perfect efficiency. Every resource sacrificed is converted without loss, enabling the Spellblade to replenish exactly what they require in the heat of combat. Whether restoring mana to unleash another spell, replenishing stamina to continue an assault, or converting stamina into vital health, every exchange becomes a calculated decision rather than a desperate gamble.

This mastery also strengthens the Spellblade's natural recovery. Their body instinctively restores itself during periods of rest, allowing them to return to battle sooner than most warriors or spellcasters.

### Effects

#### Active

- Spend **1 Action Point** to activate **Mystic Recovery**.
- Instantly perform **one** of the following conversions using a **1:1 ratio**:
  - Spend **1 HP** to restore **1 MP**.
  - Spend **1 MP** to restore **1 SP**.
  - Spend **1 SP** to restore **1 HP**.
- Mystic Recovery may only be used **once per turn**.
- Restored resources cannot exceed their maximum values.
- This talent cannot reduce your HP below **1**.

#### Passive

- Increase your natural **Health, Mana, and Stamina regeneration by 30%** while resting outside of combat.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank III is known as the **Perfect Exchange**. It is the stage where apprentices become true masters of internal transmutation, no longer sacrificing excess energy during the conversion process. Every movement of mana, every breath, and every heartbeat become part of a perfectly balanced cycle.

Veteran instructors often describe Mystic Recovery as the art of understanding that no energy is ever truly created or destroyed. A disciplined Spellblade merely guides it to where it is needed most, maintaining harmony between body and soul even amidst the chaos of battle.

Those who achieve this level of mastery are respected throughout the Orders, for they have proven that true strength lies not in possessing endless power, but in using every fragment of it with perfect efficiency.

> *"The moment nothing is wasted, every breath becomes a source of strength."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

The Spellblade's mastery over internal transmutation has surpassed perfect balance, allowing them to amplify the energy released during each conversion. Through absolute control of their mana core, they have learned to minimise waste and harness ambient arcane energy, producing greater returns than the energy originally sacrificed.

At Rank IV, Mystic Recovery no longer serves merely as a means of survival—it becomes a powerful tool for maintaining momentum throughout extended battles. A skilled Spellblade can rapidly adapt to changing circumstances, converting the resource they possess into the one they require most with remarkable efficiency.

The constant refinement of this technique also strengthens the Spellblade's natural vitality. Their body, mind, and mana recover in harmony during rest, ensuring they return to battle sooner and in far better condition than most warriors or mages.

### Effects

#### Active

- Spend **1 Action Point** to activate **Mystic Recovery**.
- Instantly perform **one** of the following conversions using a **1:2 ratio**:
  - Spend **1 HP** to restore **2 MP**.
  - Spend **1 MP** to restore **2 SP**.
  - Spend **1 SP** to restore **2 HP**.
- Mystic Recovery may only be used **once per turn**.
- Restored resources cannot exceed their maximum values.
- This talent cannot reduce your HP below **1**.

#### Passive

- Increase your natural **Health, Mana, and Stamina regeneration by 40%** while resting outside of combat.

### Lore

Among the greatest Spellblade Orders, Rank IV is known as the **Abundant Exchange**. At this stage, the practitioner has moved beyond simply conserving energy—they have learned to draw upon the natural arcane currents surrounding all living things, allowing each conversion to yield greater results than would otherwise be possible.

Masters caution that this is not the creation of energy from nothing. Instead, it is the result of flawless efficiency, discipline, and an intimate understanding of the world's arcane flow. To outsiders it appears miraculous, but to a Spellblade it is simply another expression of balance.

Veterans often say that a master of Mystic Recovery no longer fears exhaustion, for they have learned to transform every remaining reserve into exactly what the battle demands.

> *"The world is filled with untapped strength. Master yourself first, and the currents of mana will do the rest."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 5
### Description

Mystic Recovery reaches its ultimate expression as the Spellblade becomes a true master of internal transmutation. Their body, mind, and mana core exist in complete harmony, allowing energy to flow effortlessly between health, stamina, and mana with extraordinary efficiency. Every conversion is no longer a desperate sacrifice, but a deliberate manipulation of the life force that binds all things.

At Rank V, the Spellblade is capable of amplifying every exchange through flawless control of ambient mana. By drawing upon the natural arcane currents surrounding them, they recover far more than they expend, making Mystic Recovery one of the defining techniques of the Order. Even in the longest battles, a master Spellblade can adapt to changing circumstances, ensuring the resource they need is always within reach.

Combined with their exceptional natural regeneration, the Spellblade becomes remarkably self-sufficient. Though never immortal, they possess an endurance that few warriors or spellcasters can hope to match.

### Effects

#### Active

- Spend **1 Action Point** to activate **Mystic Recovery**.
- Instantly perform **one** of the following conversions using a **1:3 ratio**:
  - Spend **1 HP** to restore **3 MP**.
  - Spend **1 MP** to restore **3 SP**.
  - Spend **1 SP** to restore **3 HP**.
- Mystic Recovery may only be used **once per turn**.
- Restored resources cannot exceed their maximum values.
- This talent cannot reduce your HP below **1**.

#### Passive

- Increase your natural **Health, Mana, and Stamina regeneration by 50%** while resting outside of combat.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank V is known as the **Perfect Cycle**, representing absolute mastery over the three pillars of life: body, spirit, and mana. Those who achieve this level no longer think of health, stamina, and mana as separate resources. To them, they are simply different forms of the same energy, endlessly flowing and changing with purpose.

Legends tell of masters who fought for days without collapsing, continually redirecting their strength to meet the demands of battle. While others exhausted themselves through reckless expenditure, these Spellblades maintained an elegant balance, always possessing exactly what they needed when they needed it most.

To master Mystic Recovery is to embody one of the oldest teachings of the Spellblade: true power is not measured by how much energy you possess, but by how perfectly you can command its flow.

> *"The river never fears running dry, for it understands that every current returns. Become the current, and your strength shall never truly leave you."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

in addition to active transmutation, the spellblade's growing understanding of their own life force naturally accelerates their recovery while resting, allowing their body and mana to replenish more efficiently between encounters.

# Nature's Wrath

## Overview
The natural world rewards those who fight in harmony with it. Every spell you weave through the earth, every vine you command, and every blossom you nurture awakens a fragment of the forest's primal power.

This energy manifests as **Wrath Points**, representing the growing determination of the wild to preserve its balance. Rather than exploding uncontrollably, you may channel this energy to strengthen your spells at the moment they are cast.

Experienced Druids know that true strength lies not in overwhelming force, but in knowing when to release the power nature has entrusted to them.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

The natural world rewards those who fight in harmony with it. Every spell you weave through the earth, every vine you command, and every blossom you nurture awakens a fragment of the forest's primal power.

This energy manifests as **Wrath Points**, representing the growing determination of the wild to preserve its balance. Rather than exploding uncontrollably, you may channel this energy to strengthen your spells at the moment they are cast.

Experienced Druids know that true strength lies not in overwhelming force, but in knowing when to release the power nature has entrusted to them.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you successfully cast a **Life** or **Earth** spell, gain **1 Wrath Point**.
- You may have a maximum of **10 Wrath Points**.
- Wrath Points **resets every short rest**.
- You may only spend Wrath Points while casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell.
- Only **one Wrath Technique** may be applied to a spell.

#### Wrath Techniques

When casting a qualifying spell, you may choose **one** of the following:

**Deep Roots** *(2 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's range by **5 metres**.

**Primal Focus** *(3 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's **Spell Save DC by +1**.

**Verdant Surge** *(4 Wrath Points)*
- Add an additional **+1D4** damage or healing spells.

---

### Lore

The oldest Druids teach that nature is neither cruel nor kind—it simply seeks balance. Every spell cast in defence of that balance leaves behind a trace of primal energy, gathering quietly within those who respect the wild.

Unlike raw mana, this energy cannot be forced into existence. It must be earned through action, patience, and harmony with the natural world. Those who rush to spend it too quickly find only fleeting strength, while those who learn restraint discover that even the smallest seed can one day become an ancient forest.

To master Nature's Wrath is not to command the anger of the wild, but to become its trusted steward.

---

> *"The forest gives you its strength one leaf at a time. Wisdom is knowing which leaf to spend."*  
> — **Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your understanding of Nature's Wrath deepens, allowing you to shape the wild's energy with greater precision. The primal essence gathered through your spells no longer seeks only to empower your magic—it begins to respond to your intentions.

As your bond with the natural world strengthens, you learn to conserve the forest's fury until the perfect moment. Every Wrath Point becomes another root in the growing strength of your magic, ready to be woven into your next spell.

Experienced Druids rarely spend their Wrath carelessly. Instead, they allow it to build naturally, choosing the enhancement that best suits the situation before them.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you successfully cast a **Life** or **Earth** spell, gain **1 Wrath Point**.
- You may have a maximum of **10 Wrath Points**.
- Wrath Points are removed at the end of combat.
- You may only spend Wrath Points while casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell.
- Only **one Wrath Technique** may be applied to a spell.

#### Wrath Techniques

**Deep Roots** *(2 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's range by **5 metres**.

**Primal Focus** *(3 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's **Spell Save DC by +1**.

**Verdant Surge** *(4 Wrath Points)*
- Add an additional **+1D4** damage or healing spells.

**Enduring Growth** *(5 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's duration by **1 Round**.

---

### Lore

As Druids mature, they come to realise that the forest's power is not measured by how quickly it grows, but by how wisely it is used.

The oldest wardens compare Wrath to the changing seasons. It gathers slowly, almost unnoticed, before revealing its full strength when the moment is right. Those who master this balance learn to shape the battlefield without wasting the gifts the natural world has entrusted to them.

Within the Circle of the Emerald Wilds, young Druids are taught that every Wrath Point represents the trust of the forest. Spending it recklessly is seen as no different than cutting down an ancient tree for firewood.

---

> *"Power borrowed from the wild should never be wasted. The forest remembers every gift it gives."*  
> — **Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 3
### Description

The bond between you and the natural world has grown beyond simple harmony. The Wrath you gather is no longer merely energy waiting to be spent—it has become an extension of your will, flowing through your magic with remarkable control.

Experienced Druids learn that nature is at its strongest when it can endure. Rather than always seeking to strike harder, they learn to preserve life, strengthen their allies, and ensure that every spell leaves a lasting impact upon the battlefield.

Every Wrath Point spent is another expression of the forest's trust, allowing your magic to flourish in exactly the way the moment demands.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you successfully cast a **Life** or **Earth** spell, gain **1 Wrath Point**.
- You may have a maximum of **10 Wrath Points**.
- Wrath Points are removed at the end of combat.
- You may only spend Wrath Points while casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell.
- Only **one Wrath Technique** may be applied to a spell.

#### Wrath Techniques

**Deep Roots** *(2 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's range by **10 metres**.

**Primal Focus** *(3 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's **Spell Save DC by +1**.

**Verdant Surge** *(4 Wrath Points)*
- Add an additional **+1D4** damage or healing spells.

**Enduring Growth** *(5 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's duration by **1 Rounds**.

**Nature's Resilience** *(6 Wrath Points)*
- When casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell on yourself or an ally, grant **Temporary 5 Hit points** to target.
- Temporary HP gained this way lasts until the end of combat or until depleted.

---

### Lore

The oldest wardens believed that true mastery over Nature's Wrath was not measured by how much destruction a Druid could unleash, but by how wisely they chose to wield the gifts of the wild.

Every root that breaks stone also supports the forest above it. Every towering tree survives because its roots protect it long before danger arrives. Druids who reach this level of mastery begin to understand that nature's greatest strength has always been its resilience.

Among the Emerald Circles, this lesson marks the transition from apprentice to guardian. From this point onward, a Druid no longer fights for the forest alone—they fight as one of its protectors.

---

> *"The strongest roots are never seen. Yet without them, no forest could ever stand."*  
> — **High Warden Elowen Briarroot, Circle of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 4
### Description

Your mastery over Nature's Wrath has become instinctive. The primal energy gathered through your magic flows effortlessly, allowing you to weave the forest's power into every spell with remarkable precision.

The natural world no longer simply lends you its strength—it trusts your judgement. Every Wrath Point represents the growing will of the wild, waiting to be shaped into exactly the form the moment demands.

Veteran Druids rarely exhaust their Wrath through reckless displays of power. Instead, they reserve it for the decisive moment, empowering the spell that will protect their allies, reshape the battlefield, or bring an end to the conflict.

To the oldest Druidic Circles, this level of mastery marks the beginning of becoming a true Warden of Nature.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you successfully cast a **Life** or **Earth** spell, gain **1 Wrath Point**.
- You may have a maximum of **15 Wrath Points**.
- Wrath Points are removed at the end of combat.
- You may only spend Wrath Points while casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell.
- Only **one Wrath Technique** may be applied to a spell.

#### Wrath Techniques

**Deep Roots** *(2 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's range by **15 metres**.

**Primal Focus** *(3 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's **Spell Save DC by +2**.

**Verdant Surge** *(4 Wrath Points)*
- Add an additional **+1D6** damage or healing spells.

**Enduring Growth** *(5 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's duration by **2 Rounds**.

**Nature's Resilience** *(6 Wrath Points)*
- When casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell on yourself or an ally, grant **Temporary 5 Hit points** to target.
- Temporary HP gained this way lasts until the end of combat or until depleted.

**Primal Awakening** *(8 Wrath Points)*
Choose one when casting a qualifying spell:
- The spell **ignores Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover**.
- One **Plant-based Summon** you control may immediately move up to its Speed and make **one Basic Attack** as a free action.

---

### Lore

The oldest guardians believed the forest rewards wisdom above all else. It does not ask its protectors to unleash power at every opportunity, but to recognise the single moment when that power will matter most.

Druids who reach this stage are often entrusted with defending sacred groves, ancient Worldroots, and places where the balance of nature is most fragile. Their command of Nature's Wrath is no longer driven by instinct alone, but by centuries of teachings passed from one generation of wardens to the next.

To witness such a Druid in battle is to watch the wild itself respond with perfect timing. Every spell, every vine, and every bloom seems to arrive exactly when it is needed.

---

> *"The forest does not waste a single leaf. Neither should a Druid waste a single fragment of its strength."*  
> — **Grand Warden Sylvara Thornheart, Keeper of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 5
### Description

You have mastered the primal energies of the natural world, becoming a true Warden of the Wild. Every spell you cast leaves an imprint upon the land, and every Wrath Point you gather represents the trust the forest has placed in you.

No longer content with minor blessings, the natural world now allows you to channel its full might through a single spell. This ultimate technique, known simply as **Nature's Wrath**, is not an attack of rage but a perfect expression of harmony between Druid and nature.

The oldest Archdruids teach that Nature's Wrath should never be used lightly. It is a gift earned through patience, wisdom, and respect for the balance of life. When unleashed, the battlefield itself seems to answer your call, amplifying your magic beyond its normal limits.

Few Druids ever reach this level of mastery, and those who do are remembered as legends among the circles of Asteria.

---
### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- Whenever you successfully cast a **Life** or **Earth** spell, gain **1 Wrath Point**.
- You may have a maximum of **15 Wrath Points**.
- Wrath Points are removed at the end of combat.
- You may only spend Wrath Points while casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell.
- Only **one Wrath Technique** may be applied to a spell.

#### Wrath Techniques

**Deep Roots** *(2 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's range by **15 metres**.

**Primal Focus** *(3 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's **Spell Save DC by +3**.

**Verdant Surge** *(4 Wrath Points)*
- Add an additional **+1D6** damage or healing spells.

**Enduring Growth** *(5 Wrath Points)*
- Increase the spell's duration by **3 Rounds**.

**Nature's Resilience** *(6 Wrath Points)*
- When casting a **Life** or **Earth** spell on yourself or an ally, grant **Temporary 10 Hit points** to target.
- Temporary HP gained this way lasts until the end of combat or until depleted.

**Primal Awakening** *(8 Wrath Points)*
Choose one when casting a qualifying spell:
- The spell **ignores Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover**.
- One **Plant-based Summon** you control may immediately move up to its Speed and make **one Basic Attack** as a free action.

**Nature's Precision** (10 Wrath Points)
Choose one when casting a qualifying spell:
- **Support Spell:** Make rolls with **Advantage** when targeting an allies (such as healing, restoration, or beneficial effects).
**OR**
- **Offensive Spell:** Creatures affected by the spell make their **D20 Saving Throw with Disadvantage**.

---

### Lore

The oldest Druidic Circles believe that Nature's Wrath is not born from anger, but from perfect balance. It is the moment when every root, stone, flower, and tree willingly lends its strength to a single purpose.

Legends tell of Archdruids who ended battles without drawing blood, simply by commanding the forest to reclaim the land beneath invading armies. Others speak of healers whose Life magic became so overwhelming that entire companies rose to their feet beneath a single blossom.

To wield Nature's Wrath is to carry the trust of the wild itself. Such power is never demanded—it is given only to those who have spent a lifetime protecting the balance they now command.

---

> *"The wild does not ask whether you are worthy of its strength. It watches your actions until the answer becomes obvious."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Voice of the Emerald Wilds**

as your bond with the natural world strengthens, you learn to conserve the forest's fury until the perfect moment. every wrath point becomes another root in the growing strength of your magic, ready to be woven into your next spell.

experienced druids rarely spend their wrath carelessly. instead, they allow it to build naturally, choosing the enhancement that best suits the situation before them.

---

### effects

- this is a **passive talent**.
- whenever you successfully cast a **life** or **earth** spell, gain **1 wrath point**.
- you may have a maximum of **10 wrath points**.
- wrath points are removed at the end of combat.
- you may only spend wrath points while casting a **life** or **earth** spell.
- only **one wrath technique** may be applied to a spell.

#### wrath techniques

**deep roots** *(2 wrath points)*
- increase the spell's range by **5 metres**.

**primal focus** *(3 wrath points)*
- increase the spell's **spell save dc by +1**.

**verdant surge** *(4 wrath points)*
- add an additional **+1d4** damage or healing spells.

**enduring growth** *(5 wrath points)*
- increase the spell's duration by **1 round**.

---

### lore

as druids mature, they come to realise that the forest's power is not measured by how quickly it grows, but by how wisely it is used.

the oldest wardens compare wrath to the changing seasons. it gathers slowly, almost unnoticed, before revealing its full strength when the moment is right. those who master this balance learn to shape the battlefield without wasting the gifts the natural world has entrusted to them.

within the circle of the emerald wilds, young druids are taught that every wrath point represents the trust of the forest. spending it recklessly is seen as no different than cutting down an ancient tree for firewood.

---

> *"power borrowed from the wild should never be wasted. the forest remembers every gift it gives."*  
> — **archdruid rowan thornbark, warden of the emerald wilds**

## rank 3
### description

the bond between you and the natural world has grown beyond simple harmony. the wrath you gather is no longer merely energy waiting to be spent—it has become an extension of your will, flowing through your magic with remarkable control.

experienced druids learn that nature is at its strongest when it can endure. rather than always seeking to strike harder, they learn to preserve life, strengthen their allies, and ensure that every spell leaves a lasting impact upon the battlefield.

every wrath point spent is another expression of the forest's trust, allowing your magic to flourish in exactly the way the moment demands.

---

### effects

- this is a **passive talent**.
- whenever you successfully cast a **life** or **earth** spell, gain **1 wrath point**.
- you may have a maximum of **10 wrath points**.
- wrath points are removed at the end of combat.
- you may only spend wrath points while casting a **life** or **earth** spell.
- only **one wrath technique** may be applied to a spell.

#### wrath techniques

**deep roots** *(2 wrath points)*
- increase the spell's range by **10 metres**.

**primal focus** *(3 wrath points)*
- increase the spell's **spell save dc by +1**.

**verdant surge** *(4 wrath points)*
- add an additional **+1d4** damage or healing spells.

**enduring growth** *(5 wrath points)*
- increase the spell's duration by **1 rounds**.

**nature's resilience** *(6 wrath points)*
- when casting a **life** or **earth** spell on yourself or an ally, grant **temporary 5 hit points** to target.
- temporary hp gained this way lasts until the end of combat or until depleted.

---

### lore

the oldest wardens believed that true mastery over nature's wrath was not measured by how much destruction a druid could unleash, but by how wisely they chose to wield the gifts of the wild.

every root that breaks stone also supports the forest above it. every towering tree survives because its roots protect it long before danger arrives. druids who reach this level of mastery begin to understand that nature's greatest strength has always been its resilience.

among the emerald circles, this lesson marks the transition from apprentice to guardian. from this point onward, a druid no longer fights for the forest alone—they fight as one of its protectors.

---

> *"the strongest roots are never seen. yet without them, no forest could ever stand."*  
> — **high warden elowen briarroot, circle of the emerald wilds**

## rank 4
### description

your mastery over nature's wrath has become instinctive. the primal energy gathered through your magic flows effortlessly, allowing you to weave the forest's power into every spell with remarkable precision.

the natural world no longer simply lends you its strength—it trusts your judgement. every wrath point represents the growing will of the wild, waiting to be shaped into exactly the form the moment demands.

veteran druids rarely exhaust their wrath through reckless displays of power. instead, they reserve it for the decisive moment, empowering the spell that will protect their allies, reshape the battlefield, or bring an end to the conflict.

to the oldest druidic circles, this level of mastery marks the beginning of becoming a true warden of nature.

---

### effects

- this is a **passive talent**.
- whenever you successfully cast a **life** or **earth** spell, gain **1 wrath point**.
- you may have a maximum of **15 wrath points**.
- wrath points are removed at the end of combat.
- you may only spend wrath points while casting a **life** or **earth** spell.
- only **one wrath technique** may be applied to a spell.

#### wrath techniques

**deep roots** *(2 wrath points)*
- increase the spell's range by **15 metres**.

**primal focus** *(3 wrath points)*
- increase the spell's **spell save dc by +2**.

**verdant surge** *(4 wrath points)*
- add an additional **+1d6** damage or healing spells.

**enduring growth** *(5 wrath points)*
- increase the spell's duration by **2 rounds**.

**nature's resilience** *(6 wrath points)*
- when casting a **life** or **earth** spell on yourself or an ally, grant **temporary 5 hit points** to target.
- temporary hp gained this way lasts until the end of combat or until depleted.

**primal awakening** *(8 wrath points)*
choose one when casting a qualifying spell:
- the spell **ignores half cover and three-quarters cover**.
- one **plant-based summon** you control may immediately move up to its speed and make **one basic attack** as a free action.

---

### lore

the oldest guardians believed the forest rewards wisdom above all else. it does not ask its protectors to unleash power at every opportunity, but to recognise the single moment when that power will matter most.

druids who reach this stage are often entrusted with defending sacred groves, ancient worldroots, and places where the balance of nature is most fragile. their command of nature's wrath is no longer driven by instinct alone, but by centuries of teachings passed from one generation of wardens to the next.

to witness such a druid in battle is to watch the wild itself respond with perfect timing. every spell, every vine, and every bloom seems to arrive exactly when it is needed.

---

> *"the forest does not waste a single leaf. neither should a druid waste a single fragment of its strength."*  
> — **grand warden sylvara thornheart, keeper of the emerald wilds**

## rank 5
### description

you have mastered the primal energies of the natural world, becoming a true warden of the wild. every spell you cast leaves an imprint upon the land, and every wrath point you gather represents the trust the forest has placed in you.

no longer content with minor blessings, the natural world now allows you to channel its full might through a single spell. this ultimate technique, known simply as **nature's wrath**, is not an attack of rage but a perfect expression of harmony between druid and nature.

the oldest archdruids teach that nature's wrath should never be used lightly. it is a gift earned through patience, wisdom, and respect for the balance of life. when unleashed, the battlefield itself seems to answer your call, amplifying your magic beyond its normal limits.

few druids ever reach this level of mastery, and those who do are remembered as legends among the circles of asteria.

---
### effects

- this is a **passive talent**.
- whenever you successfully cast a **life** or **earth** spell, gain **1 wrath point**.
- you may have a maximum of **15 wrath points**.
- wrath points are removed at the end of combat.
- you may only spend wrath points while casting a **life** or **earth** spell.
- only **one wrath technique** may be applied to a spell.

#### wrath techniques

**deep roots** *(2 wrath points)*
- increase the spell's range by **15 metres**.

**primal focus** *(3 wrath points)*
- increase the spell's **spell save dc by +3**.

**verdant surge** *(4 wrath points)*
- add an additional **+1d6** damage or healing spells.

**enduring growth** *(5 wrath points)*
- increase the spell's duration by **3 rounds**.

**nature's resilience** *(6 wrath points)*
- when casting a **life** or **earth** spell on yourself or an ally, grant **temporary 10 hit points** to target.
- temporary hp gained this way lasts until the end of combat or until depleted.

**primal awakening** *(8 wrath points)*
choose one when casting a qualifying spell:
- the spell **ignores half cover and three-quarters cover**.
- one **plant-based summon** you control may immediately move up to its speed and make **one basic attack** as a free action.

**nature's precision** (10 wrath points)
choose one when casting a qualifying spell:
- **support spell:** make rolls with **advantage** when targeting an allies (such as healing, restoration, or beneficial effects).
**or**
- **offensive spell:** creatures affected by the spell make their **d20 saving throw with disadvantage**.

---

### lore

the oldest druidic circles believe that nature's wrath is not born from anger, but from perfect balance. it is the moment when every root, stone, flower, and tree willingly lends its strength to a single purpose.

legends tell of archdruids who ended battles without drawing blood, simply by commanding the forest to reclaim the land beneath invading armies. others speak of healers whose life magic became so overwhelming that entire companies rose to their feet beneath a single blossom.

to wield nature's wrath is to carry the trust of the wild itself. such power is never demanded—it is given only to those who have spent a lifetime protecting the balance they now command.

---

> *"the wild does not ask whether you are worthy of its strength. it watches your actions until the answer becomes obvious."*  
> — **grand archdruid rowan thornbark, voice of the emerald wilds**

# Paladin's Challenge

## Overview
A Paladin is more than a warrior clad in heavy armour—they are the shield that stands between the innocent and those who would bring them harm. Through unwavering conviction and absolute faith, a Paladin can issue a sacred challenge that demands the attention of friend and foe alike.

When you invoke **Paladin's Challenge**, you openly declare yourself as the greatest threat upon the battlefield. Your voice carries the authority of your oath, compelling enemies to acknowledge your presence and confront you before those who cannot defend themselves. It is not an enchantment that dominates the mind, but a divine proclamation that weighs heavily upon the conscience and instincts of those who hear it.

Experienced Paladins understand that protection is not achieved by simply enduring punishment—it begins by ensuring the enemy's focus remains where it belongs. Every successful challenge allows your allies the opportunity to reposition, recover, or strike while you hold the front line against overwhelming odds.

## Rank 1
### Description

A Paladin is more than a warrior clad in heavy armour—they are the shield that stands between the innocent and those who would bring them harm. Through unwavering conviction and absolute faith, a Paladin can issue a sacred challenge that demands the attention of friend and foe alike.

When you invoke **Paladin's Challenge**, you openly declare yourself as the greatest threat upon the battlefield. Your voice carries the authority of your oath, compelling enemies to acknowledge your presence and confront you before those who cannot defend themselves. It is not an enchantment that dominates the mind, but a divine proclamation that weighs heavily upon the conscience and instincts of those who hear it.

Experienced Paladins understand that protection is not achieved by simply enduring punishment—it begins by ensuring the enemy's focus remains where it belongs. Every successful challenge allows your allies the opportunity to reposition, recover, or strike while you hold the front line against overwhelming odds.

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to issue a **Divine Challenge**.
- Choose one creature within **15 metres** that can see or hear you.
- The target must make a **Wisdom Saving Throw**.
- **Saving Throw DC = 10 + your Charisma Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.**
- On a failed save, the target becomes **Challenged** for **2 Rounds**.
- A **Challenged** creature treats you as its primary combat target whenever it is reasonable to do so.
- A **Challenged** creature suffers **−2 to Attack Rolls** made against creatures other than you.
- The challenge immediately ends if you are reduced to **0 HP**.
- A creature may ignore the challenge if you become unreachable or another ability forces it to target a different creature.
- Bosses, Legendary creatures, and creatures of a significantly higher Threat Tier may gain Advantage on their Saving Throw at the GM's discretion.
- Your chosen patron's **Divine Authority** may grant additional bonuses against creatures that oppose its divine domain. See your patron's **Divine Authority** page for details.

### Lore

Among the knightly orders of Asteria, the Divine Challenge is considered a sacred promise rather than a battle cry. By speaking these words, a Paladin willingly places themselves between danger and those under their protection, accepting whatever consequences follow.

Veterans often teach that courage is not measured by the number of enemies defeated, but by the willingness to stand before impossible odds without yielding. To answer a Paladin's challenge is to confront not only the warrior before you, but the unwavering conviction of the divine power that guides them.

> *"If your hatred seeks the innocent, then let it first break itself against my shield."*  
> **— Sir Garrick Dawnshield, High Protector of the Argent Bastion**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your conviction grows stronger, carrying your challenge beyond a single foe. Through steadfast faith and commanding presence, you draw the attention of multiple enemies, placing yourself at the centre of the battle and giving your allies the opportunity to act without constant pressure.

A seasoned Paladin understands that protecting others is not achieved through brute strength alone. It requires absolute confidence, an unbreakable will, and the courage to become the enemy's greatest obstacle. Those who answer your challenge find it increasingly difficult to ignore the warrior who stands before them, shield raised and oath unbroken.

Every successful challenge reinforces your role as the defender of your companions, allowing you to dictate the flow of combat through unwavering resolve rather than fear or domination.

### Effects

- Spend **30 MP** to issue a **Divine Challenge**.
- Choose up to **2 creatures** within **15 metres** that can see or hear you.
- Each target must make a **Wisdom Saving Throw**.
- **Saving Throw DC = 10 + your Charisma Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.**
- On a failed save, the target becomes **Challenged** for **2 Rounds**.
- A **Challenged** creature treats you as its primary combat target whenever it is reasonable to do so.
- A **Challenged** creature suffers **−4 to Attack Rolls** made against creatures other than you.
- The challenge immediately ends for a creature if you are reduced to **0 HP**.
- A creature may ignore the challenge if you become unreachable or another ability forces it to attack a different target.
- Bosses, Legendary creatures, and creatures of a significantly higher Threat Tier may gain Advantage on their Saving Throw at the GM's discretion.
- Apply any additional bonuses granted by your patron's **Divine Authority**, if applicable.

### Lore

As Paladins gain experience, their presence alone becomes enough to command the attention of those around them. Their voice carries the weight of countless vows upheld and countless battles survived, causing even disciplined warriors to hesitate before looking past them.

Among the great knightly orders, mastering the challenge of multiple foes is considered a defining milestone. It marks the moment a Paladin ceases to be merely a protector of individuals and becomes the steadfast guardian of the battlefield itself.

> *"A shield protects one life. A true Paladin protects everyone standing behind it."*  
> **— Dame Elowyn, Captain of the Silver Wardens**

## Rank 3
### Description

Your divine authority has become impossible to ignore. Your challenge now echoes across the battlefield, drawing the attention of multiple enemies and forcing them to confront the living embodiment of your oath. Those who attempt to disregard your presence find their resolve shaken as the weight of your conviction bears down upon them.

Veteran Paladins understand that a challenge is more than a declaration of courage—it is a promise. You vow to stand between danger and those under your protection, and your enemies instinctively recognise that promise. While they may resist your authority, every moment spent ignoring you becomes increasingly difficult, allowing your allies to fight under the shelter of your unwavering resolve.

### Effects

- Spend **40 MP** to issue a **Divine Challenge**.
- Choose up to **3 creatures** within **20 metres** that can see or hear you.
- Each target must make a **Wisdom Saving Throw**.
- **Saving Throw DC = 10 + your Charisma Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.**
- On a failed save, the target becomes **Challenged** for **3 Rounds**.
- A **Challenged** creature treats you as its primary combat target whenever it is reasonable to do so.
- A **Challenged** creature suffers **−6 to Attack Rolls** made against creatures other than you.
- If a **Challenged** creature willingly attacks another target while you are a valid target, it suffers **Radiant damage equal to your Charisma Modifier** immediately after resolving its attack.
- The challenge immediately ends for a creature if you are reduced to **0 HP**.
- A creature may ignore the challenge if you become unreachable or another effect forces it to attack a different target.
- Bosses, Legendary creatures and creatures of a significantly higher Threat Tier may gain Advantage on their Saving Throw at the GM's discretion.
- Apply any additional bonuses granted by your patron's **Divine Authority**, if applicable.

### Lore

The greatest defenders are remembered not for the enemies they slew, but for the lives they preserved. A seasoned Paladin's challenge is no longer merely heard—it is felt. Those who witness it often describe an overwhelming certainty that the warrior before them cannot simply be ignored.

Many scriptures describe this as the moment a Paladin truly becomes a guardian. Their presence alone changes the course of battle, compelling allies to stand taller while forcing their enemies to confront the consequences of misplaced aggression.

> *"Ignore my warning if you must. The light will remember your choice."*  
> **— High Justicar Alaric, Keeper of the Sacred Bastion**

## Rank 4
### Description

Your divine presence has become impossible to ignore. Rather than issuing a challenge to individual foes, your conviction radiates across the battlefield, demanding the attention of every enemy that dares approach.

To stand before a veteran Paladin is to face the living embodiment of their oath. Every strike against an ally becomes a conscious rejection of your divine authority, while every step toward you is met with unwavering resolve. Even disciplined warriors find themselves instinctively drawn toward the greatest threat—the steadfast protector standing before them.

Your challenge no longer protects a single companion. It establishes a defensive bastion wherever you stand, allowing your allies to fight beneath the shelter of your conviction.

### Effects

- Spend **50 MP** to issue a **Divine Challenge**.
- All hostile creatures within a **10 metre radius** that can see or hear you must make a **Wisdom Saving Throw**.
- **Saving Throw DC = 10 + your Charisma Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.**
- On a failed save, a creature becomes **Challenged** for **3 Rounds**.
- Challenged creatures treat you as their primary combat target whenever it is reasonable to do so.
- Challenged creatures suffer **−6 to Attack Rolls** made against creatures other than you.
- If a Challenged creature willingly attacks another target while you are a valid target, it suffers **Radiant Damage equal to twice your Charisma Modifier** after its attack resolves.
- Challenged creatures cannot willingly move further away from you unless forced by another effect or they succeed on a new Wisdom Saving Throw at the end of their turn.
- The challenge immediately ends for a creature if you are reduced to **0 HP**.
- Bosses, Legendary creatures and creatures of a significantly higher Threat Tier may gain Advantage on their Saving Throw at the GM's discretion.
- Apply any additional bonuses granted by your patron's **Divine Authority**, if applicable.

### Lore

There comes a point where a Paladin no longer needs to seek the attention of evil—evil instinctively recognises them. Veterans of countless campaigns speak of battlefields falling strangely silent as a single knight steps forward, shield raised, daring every foe to pass.

Those who have witnessed such champions often describe the experience as standing before an immovable fortress. Their conviction is so absolute that even the most bloodthirsty monsters find their instincts drawn toward the greatest obstacle before them, unable to ignore the guardian who refuses to yield.

> *"Stand behind me and fear nothing. Stand before me and fear everything."*  
> **— Grandmaster Roland Ashbourne, First Shield of the Dawn**

## Rank 5
### Description

Your challenge has become a divine command that echoes across the battlefield. The strength of your conviction radiates from your very presence, compelling enemies to acknowledge you as the greatest obstacle between them and their quarry.

Those who stand beside you fight beneath the protection of an unbreakable oath, while those who oppose you feel the crushing weight of divine judgement. Though creatures still possess the freedom to resist your challenge, few can ignore the unwavering authority carried by a legendary Paladin.

Masters of this technique are remembered as living bulwarks. Entire battle lines have broken against their shields, not because they were impossible to defeat, but because no enemy could simply walk past them without paying a terrible price.

### Effects

- Spend **60 MP** to issue a **Divine Challenge**.
- All hostile creatures within a **15 metre radius** that can see or hear you must make a **Wisdom Saving Throw**.
- **Saving Throw DC = 10 + your Charisma Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.**
- On a failed save, creatures become **Challenged** for **4 Rounds**.
- Challenged creatures treat you as their primary combat target whenever it is reasonable to do so.
- Challenged creatures suffer **−6 to Attack Rolls** made against creatures other than you.
- If a Challenged creature willingly attacks another target while you remain a valid target, it immediately suffers **Radiant Damage equal to twice your Charisma Modifier** after resolving its attack.
- Challenged creatures provoke an **Opportunity Attack** from you if they willingly move away from you while within your reach.
- A Challenged creature may only attempt a new Wisdom Saving Throw at the end of its turn if you become unreachable or another effect prevents it from engaging you.
- The challenge immediately ends if you are reduced to **0 HP**.
- Bosses, Legendary creatures and creatures of a significantly higher Threat Tier may gain Advantage on their initial Saving Throw at the GM's discretion.
- Apply any bonuses granted by your patron's **Divine Authority**, if applicable.

### Lore

Among the greatest champions of Asteria, a Paladin's Challenge is spoken of with reverence. It is said that when such a Paladin plants their feet upon the battlefield and issues their sacred declaration, even the bravest warriors instinctively turn their attention toward them.

The challenge is not born from arrogance, but from sacrifice. Every word is a promise that no ally shall face the darkness alone while the Paladin still stands. Those who witness such resolve often discover that true courage is not measured by the enemies one defeats, but by the burdens one willingly bears for others.

> *"Come then. Let every blade, every spell and every ounce of your hatred fall upon me. My oath was forged to carry it."*  
> **— Saint Garrick, First Shield of the Radiant Host**

None
