# Spellblade

## Overview
# Spellblade Overview

The Spellblade is a master of both steel and sorcery, seamlessly blending martial discipline with arcane power to create a combat style unlike any other. Rather than separating swordsmanship and spellcasting, Spellblades weave the two together, empowering every strike with mana while using their weapon as the conduit through which their magic flows. Their greatest strength lies in adaptability, allowing them to transition effortlessly between close-quarters combat, ranged magical techniques, battlefield control, and defensive counterplay.

Throughout their journey, Spellblades learn to enhance their weapons, pursue fleeing enemies with supernatural speed, counter hostile spells, manipulate the battlefield through Arcane Dominion, and unleash devastating techniques such as Arcane Cut. As their mastery grows, they forge their own Arcane Arsenal, creating weapons directly from mana and reshaping them to suit any challenge. At the pinnacle of their training, legendary transformations such as Avatar of the Blade and Arcane Catalyst allow them to transcend mortal limits, becoming the ultimate expression of martial and magical harmony.

A Spellblade excels in versatility, capable of fulfilling the roles of warrior, mage, skirmisher, duelist, or battlefield commander depending on the situation. Success with the class rewards careful planning, resource management, and tactical decision-making. Every battle becomes a test of choosing the right weapon, the right spell, and the perfect moment to unleash overwhelming arcane power. Few can rival a true Spellblade, for they do not merely wield magic and steel—they become the perfect union of both.

# Spellbreaker

## Overview
Spellbreaker is one of the most revered techniques practiced by the Spellblade Orders, allowing a warrior to challenge hostile magic with nothing more than steel, mana, and unwavering resolve. Rather than avoiding incoming spells, the Spellblade steps forward, channeling arcane energy through their weapon to sever the spell before it can reach its intended target.

Executing the technique demands exceptional timing and concentration. The Spellblade must accurately read the flow of mana within an incoming spell and strike at precisely the right moment. A perfectly timed cut causes the spell's magical structure to collapse, dispersing its energy harmlessly into the air. However, hesitation or poor judgement can leave the Spellblade fully exposed to the attack, while a catastrophic mistake may cause the unstable mana to erupt against its would-be defender.

At Rank I, only the simplest travelling spells can be intercepted, making Spellbreaker a difficult but immensely rewarding technique for those willing to master its risks.

## Rank 1
### Description

Spellbreaker is one of the most revered techniques practiced by the Spellblade Orders, allowing a warrior to challenge hostile magic with nothing more than steel, mana, and unwavering resolve. Rather than avoiding incoming spells, the Spellblade steps forward, channeling arcane energy through their weapon to sever the spell before it can reach its intended target.

Executing the technique demands exceptional timing and concentration. The Spellblade must accurately read the flow of mana within an incoming spell and strike at precisely the right moment. A perfectly timed cut causes the spell's magical structure to collapse, dispersing its energy harmlessly into the air. However, hesitation or poor judgement can leave the Spellblade fully exposed to the attack, while a catastrophic mistake may cause the unstable mana to erupt against its would-be defender.

At Rank I, only the simplest travelling spells can be intercepted, making Spellbreaker a difficult but immensely rewarding technique for those willing to master its risks.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **20 MP** to activate **Spellbreaker**.
- You may only target **hostile travelling magical effects** that pass within your weapon's reach (such as bolts, lances, spears, beams, or magical projectiles).
- Make a **Weapon Attack Roll** against the Spellbreak DC.

#### Spellbreak DC

| Spell Rank | DC |
|------------|---:|
| Cantrip | 14 |
| Weak | 16 |
| Minor | 18 |

#### Results

- **Success:** The spell is severed and immediately dissipates, causing no effect.
- **Failure:** The spell continues normally and resolves against its target.
- **Natural 1 – Arcane Rebound:** The spell continues normally. You suffer an additional **1d8 Arcane Damage**, lose **10 MP**, and suffer any secondary elemental effects the spell would normally inflict, if applicable.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Spellbreaker is regarded as the first true test of mastery. Apprentices spend countless hours studying the structure of magic, learning that every spell possesses a fragile core where its mana is held together. Finding that weakness in the heartbeat before impact is what separates a Spellblade from an ordinary warrior.

Many never master the technique. Some hesitate, allowing the spell to pass unhindered, while others strike too soon or too late and suffer the violent backlash of unstable mana. Those who succeed, however, become legends—warriors capable of standing before a charging fireball or lightning spear with complete confidence, trusting only in the edge of their blade.

> *"A Spellblade does not fear magic. They simply teach it where to break."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

Having mastered the fundamentals of Spellbreaker, the Spellblade learns to read the flow of increasingly complex magic. The intricate weave of hostile spells becomes clearer to the trained eye, allowing the Spellblade to identify weaknesses within their structure and strike with greater confidence.

The technique remains dangerous, but experience has refined the Spellblade's judgement. Their weapon moves with unwavering precision, intercepting hostile magic at the precise moment before its arcane structure stabilises. Every successful Spellbreak is a testament to discipline, timing, and an intimate understanding of the forces that shape magic itself.

At Rank II, the Spellblade is capable of challenging **Greater Spells**, proving that even advanced magic can be overcome through skill rather than overwhelming power.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **25 MP** to activate **Spellbreaker**.
- You may only target **hostile travelling magical effects** that pass within your weapon's reach (such as bolts, lances, spears, beams, or magical projectiles).

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank II is known as the **Mage's Challenge**, for it marks the point where a Spellblade begins confronting the more devastating spells wielded by experienced mages. What once seemed impossible gradually becomes achievable as instinct and experience replace hesitation.

Veteran instructors remind their students that Spellbreaker is not an act of brute strength. It is a demonstration of absolute precision. The blade does not overpower the spell—it finds the single weakness holding the magic together and exploits it before the spell reaches its target.

Many accomplished Spellblades earn their reputation through this technique alone, becoming warriors whose mere presence forces enemy spellcasters to think twice before unleashing their strongest attacks.

> *"Every spell has a flaw. Your task is not to create it, but to find it before the spell finds you."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

- **Success:** The spell is severed and immediately dissipates, causing no effect.
- **Failure:** The spell continues normally and resolves against its target.
- **Natural 1 – Arcane Rebound:** The spell continues normally. You suffer an additional **1d12 Arcane Damage**, lose **20 MP**, and suffer any secondary elemental effects the spell would normally inflict, if applicable.

### Lore

Among the Spellblade Orders, Rank III is known as the **Spell Hunter's Edge**. It marks the point where a Spellblade ceases to merely defend against magic and begins actively challenging the greatest spellcasters on equal footing.

Masters teach that every spell, no matter how complex, is built upon a foundation of carefully woven mana. A single perfectly placed strike is capable of unravelling that foundation, causing even formidable magic to collapse before reaching its target.

Legends tell of veteran Spellblades standing before volleys of enchanted projectiles, calmly cutting each one from the air before advancing through the fading arcane mist. Such feats are only possible through absolute discipline, flawless timing, and an unbreakable resolve.

> *"Power alone does not break a spell. Precision reveals the flaw, and courage strikes it."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

The Spellblade has ascended into the ranks of the greatest mage hunters, capable of severing immensely powerful spells that would overwhelm most warriors. Years of relentless training have sharpened their understanding of arcane structure, allowing them to identify even the smallest instability within advanced magic.

To an observer, the technique appears effortless. The Spellblade calmly watches an incoming spell, waiting until the final heartbeat before impact before delivering a single precise strike. Rather than overpowering the spell through brute force, they cut through the delicate threads holding its mana together, causing the entire construct to collapse into harmless fragments.

At Rank IV, the Spellblade can challenge both **Enhanced** and **Superior Spells**, an achievement that places them among the elite of the Spellblade Orders. Enemy mages quickly learn that even their strongest attacks are no longer guaranteed to reach their target.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **35 MP** to activate **Spellbreaker**.
- You may only target **hostile travelling magical effects** that pass within your weapon's reach (such as bolts, lances, spears, beams, or magical projectiles).
- Make a **Weapon Attack Roll** against the Spellbreak DC.

|------------|---:|
| Cantrip | 8 |
| Weak | 10 |
| Minor | 12 |
| Greater | 16 |
| Strengthened | 20 |
| Enhanced | 24 |
| Superior | 26 |

- **Success:** The spell is severed and immediately dissipates, causing no effect.
- **Failure:** The spell continues normally and resolves against its target.
- **Natural 1 – Arcane Rebound:** The spell continues normally. You suffer an additional **2d8 Arcane Damage**, lose **25 MP**, and suffer any secondary elemental effects the spell would normally inflict, if applicable.

### Lore

Within the ancient Spellblade Orders, Rank IV is known as the **Mage's Bane**, a title bestowed upon warriors whose mastery allows them to stand before even the most accomplished spellcasters without fear. Their reputation is earned not through magical talent alone, but through their ability to deny magic itself.

Stories tell of Spellblades who marched through storms of arcane destruction, their blades flashing as spell after spell shattered into drifting motes of fading mana. To their allies, they appeared untouchable. To enemy mages, they became a nightmare that turned their greatest strength into uncertainty.

Masters teach that Spellbreaker is ultimately an act of understanding rather than destruction. Every spell possesses a weakness, and only those with absolute discipline can recognise it before the opportunity vanishes.

> *"A master does not ask whether a spell can be broken. They simply decide where to cut."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 5
### Description

Spellbreaker reaches its ultimate form, allowing the Spellblade to challenge some of the most devastating magic known throughout Asteria. Years of unwavering discipline have taught the Spellblade that every spell, no matter how complex, is built upon a delicate framework of mana. At Rank V, they possess the knowledge and precision to find that weakness in an instant and shatter it with a single, perfectly timed strike.

The technique is no longer driven by instinct alone—it has become an art. The Spellblade calmly studies the approaching spell, waiting until the final moment before cutting through its arcane core. To those who witness it, the impossible becomes reality as torrents of magical energy are split apart and dissolved into harmless fragments before they ever reach their target.

Only the greatest Spellblades are capable of wielding Spellbreaker at this level. Their mastery inspires allies and strikes fear into enemy spellcasters, who know that even their strongest spells may be reduced to nothing by the edge of a single enchanted blade.

### Effects

- Spend **1 Action Point** and **40 MP** to activate **Spellbreaker**.
- You may only target **hostile travelling magical effects** that pass within your weapon's reach (such as bolts, lances, spears, beams, or magical projectiles).
- Make a **Weapon Attack Roll** against the Spellbreak DC.

#### Spellbreak DC

|------------|---:|

| Greater | 14 |

- **Failure:** The spell continues normally and resolves against its target.
- **Natural 1 – Arcane Rebound:** The spell continues normally. You suffer **2d10 Arcane Damage**, lose **30 MP**, and suffer any secondary elemental effects the spell would normally inflict, if applicable.

- This rank replaces the effects of **Spellbreaker — Rank IV**.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank V is known as the **World Cleaver's Edge**. It is said that those who attain this mastery no longer see spells as overwhelming forces of destruction, but as intricate patterns of mana waiting to be unravelled. They understand that even the greatest magic possesses flaws—provided one has the courage and skill to strike them.

Legends speak of master Spellblades who stood before dragons, archmages, and ancient horrors, cutting apart torrents of magical destruction before pressing forward without hesitation. While even they cannot sever the reality-shaping power of **World Spells**, few other forms of magic remain beyond their reach.

To master Spellbreaker is to embody one of the oldest philosophies of the Spellblade Orders: magic is not an unstoppable force. Like steel, it can be studied, understood, and ultimately broken.

> *"Every spell has an ending. A master Spellblade simply chooses where it begins."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

at rank i, only the simplest travelling spells can be intercepted, making spellbreaker a difficult but immensely rewarding technique for those willing to master its risks.

# Spirit Animal

## Overview
Every Druid walks the wilds in search of harmony, but none walk alone forever. Through ancient rituals and quiet meditation, a Druid eventually encounters a Spirit Animal—a mystical guardian that embodies a single aspect of the natural world. This companion is neither a summoned beast nor a permanent pet, but a spiritual manifestation that willingly answers the Druid's call.

At this rank, your Spirit Animal cannot directly fight alongside you. Instead, it acts as a guide, scout, and conduit between you and the wilderness. It instinctively understands your intentions and communicates through emotions, instincts, and brief spiritual impressions rather than spoken words.

The form of your Spirit Animal is chosen with your Game Master and should reflect your character's personality, beliefs, or connection to nature. A wolf may represent loyalty, an owl wisdom, a fox cunning, or a stag guardianship. Regardless of its form, your companion remains a trusted ally throughout your journey.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

Every Druid walks the wilds in search of harmony, but none walk alone forever. Through ancient rituals and quiet meditation, a Druid eventually encounters a Spirit Animal—a mystical guardian that embodies a single aspect of the natural world. This companion is neither a summoned beast nor a permanent pet, but a spiritual manifestation that willingly answers the Druid's call.

At this rank, your Spirit Animal cannot directly fight alongside you. Instead, it acts as a guide, scout, and conduit between you and the wilderness. It instinctively understands your intentions and communicates through emotions, instincts, and brief spiritual impressions rather than spoken words.

The form of your Spirit Animal is chosen with your Game Master and should reflect your character's personality, beliefs, or connection to nature. A wolf may represent loyalty, an owl wisdom, a fox cunning, or a stag guardianship. Regardless of its form, your companion remains a trusted ally throughout your journey.

---

### Effects

- Spend **15 MP** to summon your **Spirit Animal**.
- The Spirit Animal remains manifested for **10 minutes**.
- Your Spirit Animal is **ethereal** and cannot attack, deal damage, manipulate physical objects, or be targeted by attacks.
- The Spirit Animal may move up to **30 metres** away from you while remaining connected through your spiritual bond.
- You may see and hear through your Spirit Animal's senses as an action. While doing so, your own body is considered **Distracted** and you have **Disadvantage** on Perception Checks made using your own senses.
- The Spirit Animal can silently communicate simple emotions, warnings, and observations to you.
- Gain **+2** to **Nature**, **Survival**, and **Tracking** **D20 Skill Checks** while your Spirit Animal is active.
- Your Spirit Animal instinctively alerts you if it notices:
  - Nearby natural hazards.
  - Dangerous terrain.
  - Wild beasts.
  - Signs of recent natural disturbances.
- The Spirit Animal cannot pass through magical barriers designed to block spirits or extraplanar beings.
- The Spirit Animal cannot enter combat or provide combat bonuses at this rank.

---

### Lore

The first meeting between a Druid and their Spirit Animal is one of the most sacred moments in Druidic tradition. Some encounter their companion beneath ancient trees, others beside tranquil rivers or beneath starlit skies, but every meeting is deeply personal and impossible to forget.

The Spirit Animal is believed to be a fragment of the world's living spirit, choosing its Druid as much as the Druid chooses it. Though incapable of physical interaction at first, it offers guidance, companionship, and perspective drawn from the untamed wilderness itself.

Among the oldest circles, it is said that a Druid who truly understands their Spirit Animal will never again feel lost, no matter how dark the forest or uncertain the path ahead.

---

> *"A Spirit Animal is not the path before you—it is the friend who reminds you why you chose to walk it."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your spiritual bond with your Spirit Animal grows stronger, allowing it to venture farther from your side while sharing more of its instincts and awareness. The connection between your souls becomes increasingly natural, requiring little effort to maintain as you begin to perceive the wilderness through two sets of senses.

Your companion has become far more than a guide. It actively scouts ahead, warns of danger, and instinctively searches for safe paths through unfamiliar terrain. Whether soaring above a dense forest canopy, slipping silently through undergrowth, or climbing rugged cliffs, it serves as an extension of your own awareness.

Although it still cannot physically interact with the world, your Spirit Animal has learned to better interpret the intentions of the creatures and environments it observes. This deeper understanding allows it to provide more accurate warnings and valuable insight before danger reveals itself.

---

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to summon your **Spirit Animal**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains manifested for **15 minutes**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains **ethereal**, unable to attack, manipulate objects, or be targeted by conventional attacks.
- Your Spirit Animal may travel up to **60 metres** away from you while maintaining your spiritual bond.
- As an action, you may perceive the world through your Spirit Animal's senses.
- While using your Spirit Animal's senses, your physical body is considered **Distracted** and has **Disadvantage** on Perception Checks using its own senses.
- Gain **+4** to **Nature**, **Survival**, and **Tracking** **D20 Skill Checks** while your Spirit Animal is active.
- Your Spirit Animal instinctively detects:
  - Natural hazards.
  - Dangerous terrain.
  - Nearby beasts.
  - Fresh tracks.
  - Signs of recent movement through the wilderness.
- Your Spirit Animal can distinguish whether nearby creatures appear **calm**, **alert**, **frightened**, or **agitated** through their natural behaviour.
- You may dismiss or resummon your Spirit Animal at any time while the duration remains active without paying an additional Mana Cost.
- The Spirit Animal cannot pass through magical barriers designed to block spirits or extraplanar beings.
- The Spirit Animal cannot enter combat or provide combat bonuses at this rank.

---

### Lore

As the bond deepens, the Spirit Animal begins to think less as a companion and more as an extension of its Druid. Thoughts, emotions, and instincts flow effortlessly between them, allowing each to understand the other without spoken language.

Many Druids describe this stage as learning to trust another set of eyes. While the Spirit Animal explores the wilderness, its discoveries become your own, revealing hidden dangers, forgotten trails, and the subtle movements of the natural world.

The elders teach that this growing trust is essential. A Spirit Animal does not serve its Druid out of obligation—it remains because the bond between them has become one of mutual respect, shared purpose, and unwavering companionship.

---

> *"When two spirits walk as one, even the quietest forest cannot keep its secrets."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 3
### Description

Your Spirit Animal has become an inseparable extension of your soul, capable of travelling great distances while maintaining an unwavering spiritual connection. The bond between you is now so refined that its instincts, senses, and emotions flow naturally into your own awareness, allowing you to perceive the wilderness with remarkable clarity.

As your companion explores, it does more than simply observe. It studies the land, watches the behaviour of wildlife, and recognises subtle changes within the environment that would escape even experienced hunters. Through your shared bond, these discoveries become your own, enabling you to make informed decisions long before danger reveals itself.

Among the Druidic Circles, reaching this stage is considered a milestone of trust. Your Spirit Animal no longer follows your commands out of duty—it acts as a true partner, anticipating your needs and carrying out your intentions with remarkable understanding.

---

### Effects

- Spend **25 MP** to summon your **Spirit Animal**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains manifested for **20 minutes**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains **ethereal**, unable to attack, manipulate physical objects, or be targeted by conventional attacks.
- Your Spirit Animal may travel up to **100 metres** away from you while maintaining your spiritual bond.
- As an action, you may perceive the world through your Spirit Animal's senses.
- While using your Spirit Animal's senses, your physical body is considered **Distracted** and has **Disadvantage** on Perception Checks made using its own senses.
- Gain **+6** to **Nature**, **Survival**, and **Tracking** **D20 Skill Checks** while your Spirit Animal is active.
- Your Spirit Animal instinctively detects:
  - Natural hazards.
  - Dangerous terrain.
  - Fresh tracks.
  - Nearby beasts.
  - Signs of recent travel through the wilderness.
  - Changes to the surrounding ecosystem caused by natural or unnatural events.
- Your Spirit Animal can distinguish the general behaviour of nearby creatures, recognising whether they are:
  - Hunting.
  - Resting.
  - Fleeing.
  - Defending territory.
  - Travelling.
- You may freely switch between your own senses and your Spirit Animal's senses without ending the ability.
- You may dismiss and resummon your Spirit Animal anywhere within **20 metres** of you while the duration remains active without paying an additional Mana Cost.
- The Spirit Animal cannot pass through magical barriers designed to block spirits or extraplanar beings.
- The Spirit Animal cannot enter combat or provide combat bonuses at this rank.

---

### Lore

Experienced Druids often describe this stage as sharing a single soul between two bodies. Distance becomes increasingly irrelevant as thoughts and instincts flow effortlessly across the spiritual bond, allowing both companions to work together without hesitation or spoken direction.

Many great Wardens relied upon their Spirit Animals to explore dangerous ruins, watch over sacred groves, and guide lost travellers through untamed wilderness. While the Spirit Animal cannot alter the physical world, its watchful presence has prevented countless disasters by revealing dangers before they could unfold.

The oldest Druidic teachings remind every practitioner that trust cannot be forced. Only through patience, respect, and shared purpose does a Spirit Animal choose to become more than a guide—it becomes family.

---

> *"A companion who shares your spirit never walks behind you or before you. They walk beside you, no matter how great the distance."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 4
### Description

Your Spirit Animal has become a true extension of your spirit, capable of exploring vast distances while maintaining an unbroken bond with you. The connection has evolved beyond shared sight and hearing; emotions, instincts, and awareness flow freely between you both, allowing each to react almost as though you were a single being.

As your companion traverses the wilderness, it perceives far more than simple movement. It recognises disturbances in ecosystems, senses changes in weather before they arrive, and notices subtle shifts in the behaviour of wildlife that often foreshadow approaching danger. Through your bond, these discoveries become instinctive knowledge rather than conscious observation.

Among the ancient Druidic Circles, reaching this stage marks the beginning of true spiritual partnership. A Spirit Animal no longer waits for commands—it understands your intentions and acts independently to protect, guide, and inform, always remaining faithful to the balance of nature.

---

- Your Spirit Animal remains manifested for **25 minutes**.
- Your Spirit Animal remains **ethereal**, unable to attack, manipulate physical objects, or be targeted by conventional attacks.
- Your Spirit Animal may travel up to **150 metres** away while maintaining your spiritual bond.
- As an action, you may perceive the world through your Spirit Animal's senses.
- While using your Spirit Animal's senses, your physical body is considered **Distracted** and has **Disadvantage** on Perception Checks made using its own senses.
- Gain **+8** to **Nature**, **Survival**, and **Tracking** **D20 Skill Checks** while your Spirit Animal is active.
- Your Spirit Animal instinctively detects:
  - Natural hazards.
  - Dangerous terrain.
  - Fresh tracks.
  - Nearby beasts.
  - Signs of recent travel.
  - Changes caused by corruption, blight, or powerful natural disasters.
- Your Spirit Animal can determine the general behaviour of nearby creatures, including whether they are:
  - Hunting.
  - Resting.
  - Defending territory.
  - Travelling.
  - Fleeing.
  - Stalking prey.
- You may freely switch between your own senses and your Spirit Animal's senses without using an action.
- You may dismiss and resummon your Spirit Animal anywhere within **50 metres** of you while the duration remains active without paying an additional Mana Cost.
- While your Spirit Animal is within **10 metres** of you, you gain **Advantage on D20 Perception Checks** relying on sight, hearing, or smell.
- The Spirit Animal cannot pass through magical barriers specifically designed to block spirits or extraplanar beings.
- The Spirit Animal cannot enter combat or provide offensive or defensive combat abilities at this rank.

---

### Lore

To the greatest Druids, the bond between guardian and Spirit Animal becomes impossible to separate. Each instinctively understands the other's purpose, allowing them to explore, observe, and protect the wilderness with extraordinary efficiency.

Many Wardens entrusted with safeguarding sacred groves rely upon their Spirit Animals to patrol vast forests without ever disturbing the delicate balance of nature. The creatures of the wild rarely fear these spiritual companions, often treating them as though they were simply another part of the forest itself.

The oldest teachings claim that when a Druid reaches this stage, the Spirit Animal no longer follows because it was summoned. It remains because the two spirits have chosen to walk the same path for the rest of their lives.

---

> *"When trust is complete, distance loses all meaning. Two spirits become one purpose."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, First Warden of the Emerald Wilds**

## Rank 5
### Description

Your bond with your Spirit Animal has reached its ultimate expression, transcending that of summoner and companion. You are now two souls united by a single purpose, capable of sharing thoughts, instincts, and senses with effortless clarity. Distance is little more than an inconvenience, and your companion acts with the same wisdom and intent as if it were your own body.

Your Spirit Animal has become the perfect scout and guide, navigating even the most dangerous wilderness without disturbing the balance of nature. It understands your intentions before they are spoken, adapting to changing circumstances and uncovering paths, dangers, and opportunities that would remain invisible to others.

Among the oldest Druidic Circles, those who achieve this mastery are known as **Wildbound Guardians**. Their Spirit Animals are regarded as sacred partners, entrusted with watching over ancient groves, sacred beasts, and places where the natural world remains untouched. Though incapable of direct combat, their presence has saved countless lives through foresight, wisdom, and unwavering vigilance.

---

Few Druids ever reach this level of spiritual harmony. The ancient circles believe that, at this stage, the Spirit Animal is no longer merely a guide gifted by nature, but a reflection of the Druid's own soul. Together they embody the balance between civilisation and wilderness, instinct and wisdom, mortal and spirit.

# spirit animal

## overview
every druid walks the wilds in search of harmony, but none walk alone forever. through ancient rituals and quiet meditation, a druid eventually encounters a spirit animal—a mystical guardian that embodies a single aspect of the natural world. this companion is neither a summoned beast nor a permanent pet, but a spiritual manifestation that willingly answers the druid's call.

at this rank, your spirit animal cannot directly fight alongside you. instead, it acts as a guide, scout, and conduit between you and the wilderness. it instinctively understands your intentions and communicates through emotions, instincts, and brief spiritual impressions rather than spoken words.

the form of your spirit animal is chosen with your game master and should reflect your character's personality, beliefs, or connection to nature. a wolf may represent loyalty, an owl wisdom, a fox cunning, or a stag guardianship. regardless of its form, your companion remains a trusted ally throughout your journey.

# Spirit Bloom

## Overview
You call forth a radiant Spirit Bloom, a magical flower infused with the essence of Life. Upon taking root, it emits a warm, soothing light that strengthens the resolve of nearby allies and reminds them of the resilience found within the natural world.

Unlike creatures summoned through Living Forest, the Spirit Bloom is stationary and serves as a beacon of protection rather than a combatant. While fragile, its presence can inspire allies to endure hardships that would otherwise overwhelm them.

Many Druids cultivate these blossoms before battles, believing that even the smallest flower can become a symbol of hope when darkness begins to close in.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

You call forth a radiant Spirit Bloom, a magical flower infused with the essence of Life. Upon taking root, it emits a warm, soothing light that strengthens the resolve of nearby allies and reminds them of the resilience found within the natural world.

Unlike creatures summoned through Living Forest, the Spirit Bloom is stationary and serves as a beacon of protection rather than a combatant. While fragile, its presence can inspire allies to endure hardships that would otherwise overwhelm them.

Many Druids cultivate these blossoms before battles, believing that even the smallest flower can become a symbol of hope when darkness begins to close in.

---

### Effects

- Summon a **Spirit Bloom** in an unoccupied space within range.
- The Spirit Bloom is **stationary** and cannot move or attack.
- The Spirit Bloom emits bright light in a **10-metre radius**.
- Allied creatures standing within the light gain:
  - **+1 to Constitution Skill Checks.**
  - **+1 to Constitution Saving Throws.**
- These bonuses are lost immediately when a creature leaves the illuminated area.
- The Spirit Bloom remains for **3 Rounds** or until destroyed.

#### Spirit Bloom Statistics

- **HP:** 5
- **AC:** 10

Only **one Spirit Bloom** may be active at a time.

---

### Lore

Spirit Blooms are said to grow where the essence of Life gathers most strongly. Though they resemble ordinary flowers, each blossom is formed from pure natural magic, carrying a fragment of the world's life force within its petals.

Druids often see these flowers as symbols of hope. Even in the aftermath of great battles, tales speak of Spirit Blooms emerging from blood-soaked earth, reminding survivors that life always finds a way to return.

Among the Verdant Circles, nurturing a Spirit Bloom is considered one of the first lessons in protecting others before oneself.

---

> *"A single flower cannot stop a storm—but it can remind us why we endure it."*  
> — **Archdruid Lysara Dawnpetal, Keeper of the Blooming Grove**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your Spirit Bloom grows stronger as more of nature's life essence flows through it. The blossom becomes larger, its petals brighter, and its roots spread further beneath the earth, allowing its restorative aura to reach more allies.

The Bloom is no longer simply a symbol of hope—it becomes a sanctuary on the battlefield. Those who stand within its radiant light find renewed determination, their bodies strengthened by the quiet resilience of the natural world.

Although it remains vulnerable to attack, experienced Druids learn to position their Spirit Bloom carefully, encouraging allies to fight around its protective aura while forcing enemies to decide whether to waste valuable attacks destroying it.

---

### Effects

- Summon a **Spirit Bloom** in an unoccupied space within range.
- The Spirit Bloom is **stationary** and cannot move or attack.
- The Spirit Bloom emits bright light in a **15-metre radius**.
- Allied creatures standing within the light gain:
  - **+2 to Constitution Skill Checks.**
  - **+2 to Constitution Saving Throws.**
  - **+1 to Strength Skill Checks.**
- These bonuses are lost immediately when a creature leaves the illuminated area.
- The Spirit Bloom remains for **4 Rounds** or until destroyed.

#### Spirit Bloom Statistics

- **HP:** 10
- **AC:** 10

Only **one Spirit Bloom** may be active at a time.

---

### Lore

As a Druid's bond with Life magic deepens, their Spirit Bloom begins to resemble the sacred flowers that grow within the oldest groves of Asteria. Their radiant petals are said to absorb the strength of the earth below before sharing it with every living creature sheltered beneath their light.

Many Druidic Circles plant living gardens around their sanctuaries using Spirit Blooms, believing that every blossom carries a fragment of the world's life force. Warriors who have fought beside these flowers often speak of an overwhelming sense of calm, even in the heart of battle.

Among the Keepers of the Blooming Grove, the appearance of a mature Spirit Bloom is considered a sign that the Druid has begun to truly understand that strength and compassion can flourish together.

---

> *"The brightest flowers do not bloom because the world is gentle. They bloom because life refuses to surrender."*  
> — **Archdruid Lysara Dawnpetal, Keeper of the Blooming Grove**

### Description

Your Spirit Bloom blossoms into a powerful conduit of Life Essence, becoming a beacon that strengthens both body and spirit. Its roots extend deep into the earth, drawing upon the vitality of the land before radiating that energy through its brilliant petals.

The Bloom's light grows brighter and steadier, allowing allies to fight with renewed endurance while empowering their physical resolve. Warriors often rally around a mature Spirit Bloom, knowing its presence can be the difference between holding the line and falling before overwhelming odds.

Though still unable to defend itself, the Spirit Bloom has become a valuable battlefield objective. Protecting it allows your allies to benefit from its blessings for far longer, while enemies are often forced to divert their attention to destroying it.

---

  - **+3 to Constitution Skill Checks.**

  - **+2 to Strength Skill Checks.**
- These bonuses are lost immediately when a creature leaves the illuminated area.
- The Spirit Bloom remains for **8 Rounds** or until destroyed.

- **HP:** 15
- **AC:** 10

Only **one Spirit Bloom** may be active at a time.

---

Within the oldest Druidic sanctuaries, Spirit Blooms of this strength are cultivated as symbols of perseverance. Their radiant light has guided travellers through dense forests, illuminated sacred ceremonies, and given exhausted defenders the strength to endure impossible battles.

Elder Druids teach that every Spirit Bloom is a reminder that life is strongest when it is shared. Just as a single flower spreads its seeds across the forest, so too does its magic spread hope to those willing to stand together beneath its light.

Many tales tell of battlefields where the only thing left standing after the fighting ceased was a solitary Spirit Bloom, still glowing peacefully amongst the silence.

# Steady Aim

## Overview
Every Ranger understands that patience is often deadlier than speed. Rather than firing the moment an opportunity presents itself, they learn to slow their breathing, steady their stance, and carefully observe their target before releasing a single, deliberate shot.

Steady Aim represents the Ranger's growing mastery of precision marksmanship. By sacrificing valuable time to line up an attack, the Ranger greatly improves the likelihood of striking their intended target. This discipline rewards careful planning and creates opportunities that reckless archers often miss.

Although the technique requires concentration, experienced Rangers know that one perfectly placed arrow is often worth far more than a dozen hurried shots.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

Every Ranger understands that patience is often deadlier than speed. Rather than firing the moment an opportunity presents itself, they learn to slow their breathing, steady their stance, and carefully observe their target before releasing a single, deliberate shot.

Steady Aim represents the Ranger's growing mastery of precision marksmanship. By sacrificing valuable time to line up an attack, the Ranger greatly improves the likelihood of striking their intended target. This discipline rewards careful planning and creates opportunities that reckless archers often miss.

Although the technique requires concentration, experienced Rangers know that one perfectly placed arrow is often worth far more than a dozen hurried shots.

---

### Effects

#### Steady Aim

The Ranger may spend **2 or 3 Action Points** carefully aiming at a single creature within the range of a ranged weapon.

The target must remain visible throughout the aiming process.

After aiming, the Ranger gains the following bonus on their **next ranged weapon attack** against that target.

| Action Points Spent | Bonus |
|---------------------|-------|
| **2 AP** | **+1 Attack Roll** |
| **3 AP** | **+2 Attack Roll** |

#### Focus Rules

- The attack must be made **before the end of the Ranger's next turn**.
- The Ranger may only aim at **one creature** at a time.
- Changing targets immediately removes the bonus.
- If the target leaves the Ranger's line of sight, the bonus is lost.
- Becoming blinded or incapacitated immediately ends the effect.
- Steady Aim only functions with **ranged weapon attacks**.

---

### Lore

The first lesson taught to every Ranger marksman is simple: a hurried arrow is a wasted arrow. Apprentices spend countless hours drawing their bow, holding their aim, and waiting for the perfect moment before they are ever permitted to loose a shot.

As their discipline grows, Rangers learn that precision is not a gift, but a skill earned through patience and repetition. Every breath, every heartbeat, and every movement is controlled until releasing the arrow becomes second nature.

Among the Ranger Lodges, mastering Steady Aim is considered the foundation of true marksmanship, forming the basis for every advanced shooting technique that follows.

---

> *"Anyone can fire an arrow. A Ranger waits until missing is no longer an option."*  
> — **Master Marksman Caelan Ashwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's discipline continues to improve, allowing them to remain calm even in the chaos of battle. Every breath, every heartbeat, and every movement is carefully controlled as they analyse their quarry before committing to the shot. What once required intense concentration now becomes second nature.

With greater experience comes greater confidence. The Ranger begins to recognise predictable movement, defensive habits, and fleeting openings that less experienced archers would overlook. By spending a few precious moments studying their target, they dramatically increase the likelihood of striking true.

Among seasoned Rangers, patience is never viewed as hesitation. It is an investment that ensures every arrow has the greatest possible chance of ending the hunt.

---

### Effects

#### Focused Aim

The Ranger may spend **2 or 3 Action Points** studying a single creature within **line of sight**.

The target must remain visible throughout the observation.

After observing, the Ranger gains the following bonus against that target:

| Action Points Spent | Bonus |
|---------------------|-------|
| **2 AP** | **+2 Attack Roll** |
| **3 AP** | **+3 Attack Roll** |

The bonus applies to the Ranger's **next ranged weapon attack** against that target.

#### Focus Rules

- The empowered attack must be made **before the end of your next turn**.
- The Ranger may only study **one creature** at a time.
- Changing targets immediately removes all accumulated focus.
- If the target leaves the Ranger's line of sight, the bonus is lost.
- Becoming blinded or incapacitated immediately ends the effect.
- Steady Aim only functions with **ranged weapon attacks**.

---

### Lore

Within the Ranger Lodges, the second rank of Steady Aim marks the point where an apprentice begins to think like a true marksman. Rather than reacting to an enemy's movements, they learn to predict them, patiently waiting for the moment when a successful shot becomes almost inevitable.

Many Rangers become respected hunters through skill alone, but those who master Steady Aim are admired for something greater—the discipline to resist taking the easy shot in favour of the perfect one. Their patience often allows them to succeed where others would fail.

---

> *"The arrow released too soon belongs to chance. The arrow released at the right moment belongs to the Ranger."*  
> — **Master Ranger Caelan Skywatch**

## Rank 3
### Description

By the third rank, the Ranger has developed exceptional battlefield patience. Rather than simply observing a target's movements, they begin recognising subtle flaws in posture, damaged armour, and predictable defensive habits. Every moment spent aiming increases the likelihood of finding the perfect opening.

The Ranger has learned that true precision is not simply striking the target—it is striking where the target is weakest. Careful preparation allows the Ranger to transform an accurate shot into a devastating one, rewarding those willing to sacrifice time for overwhelming effectiveness.

Veteran Rangers often describe this technique as allowing the prey to defeat itself. Given enough time, every creature eventually reveals a weakness.

---

### Effects

#### Focused Aim

The Ranger may spend **2 or 3 Action Points** studying a single creature within **line of sight**.

The target must remain visible throughout the observation.

After observing, the Ranger gains the following bonus against that target:

| Action Points Spent | Bonus |
|---------------------|-------|
| **2 AP** | **+3 Attack Roll** |
| **3 AP** | **+4 Attack Roll** and **+1d4 Damage** |

The bonus applies to the Ranger's **next ranged weapon attack** against that target.

#### Focus Rules

- The empowered attack must be made **before the end of your next turn**.
- The Ranger may only study **one creature** at a time.
- Changing targets immediately removes all accumulated focus.
- If the target leaves the Ranger's line of sight, the bonus is lost.
- Becoming blinded or incapacitated immediately ends the effect.

every ranger understands that patience is often deadlier than speed. rather than firing the moment an opportunity presents itself, they learn to slow their breathing, steady their stance, and carefully observe their target before releasing a single, deliberate shot.

# Survival Instinct

## Overview
Years spent surviving in the untamed wilderness have sharpened the Ranger's instincts beyond those of ordinary adventurers. Constant exposure to predators, harsh environments, and unexpected dangers has taught them to recognise subtle signs of trouble long before others become aware of them.

Survival Instinct is not a learned technique, but a collection of natural reactions developed through experience. A snapped twig, an unnatural silence among wildlife, or the faint scent of smoke is often enough to place the Ranger on alert. While others rely on preparation, the Ranger trusts instinct.

This heightened awareness allows the Ranger to react more quickly to danger, avoid natural hazards, and survive in environments that would overwhelm less experienced travellers.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

Years spent surviving in the untamed wilderness have sharpened the Ranger's instincts beyond those of ordinary adventurers. Constant exposure to predators, harsh environments, and unexpected dangers has taught them to recognise subtle signs of trouble long before others become aware of them.

Survival Instinct is not a learned technique, but a collection of natural reactions developed through experience. A snapped twig, an unnatural silence among wildlife, or the faint scent of smoke is often enough to place the Ranger on alert. While others rely on preparation, the Ranger trusts instinct.

This heightened awareness allows the Ranger to react more quickly to danger, avoid natural hazards, and survive in environments that would overwhelm less experienced travellers.

---

### Effects

- Gain **+2** to **Survival** skill checks.
- Gain **+2** to checks made to detect **natural hazards**, including quicksand, unstable ground, rockfalls, thin ice, poisonous plants, and similar environmental dangers.
- Gain **+2** to detect **ambushes** or hidden creatures before combat begins.
- Gain **+2** to resist becoming **Lost** while travelling through natural environments.
- You may forage for food and fresh water at **twice the normal rate**, subject to the GM's discretion.
- You require **half the normal time** to establish a safe campsite or shelter in the wilderness.

---

### Lore

Among the Ranger Lodges, Survival Instinct is considered one of the first signs that a hunter has truly embraced the wilderness. It cannot be taught through books or drills alone. Instead, it is forged through countless nights beneath the open sky, surviving storms, avoiding predators, and learning to read the world as though it were a living companion.

Veteran Rangers often claim they cannot explain how they know danger is near—they simply do. Whether it is the sudden silence of birds, the shift of the wind, or an almost imperceptible feeling that something is wrong, these instincts have saved countless lives throughout Asteria.

To the untrained eye, it appears to be luck. To a Ranger, it is simply experience speaking louder than words.

---

> *"The wilderness whispers before it strikes. A Ranger survives because they learned to listen."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's instincts continue to sharpen, becoming second nature after countless journeys through dangerous wilderness. They no longer simply recognise danger—they begin anticipating it before it fully reveals itself. Subtle changes in weather, wildlife behaviour, or the environment immediately draw the Ranger's attention.

Experience has also taught the Ranger to conserve energy and resources while travelling. They instinctively choose safer paths, identify reliable sources of food and water, and establish secure camps with remarkable efficiency. What would take others hours of careful planning becomes routine for a seasoned Ranger.

Among the Ranger Lodges, reaching this level is considered the point where a Ranger can confidently guide an expedition through even the most hostile regions of Asteria.

---

### Effects

- Gain **+4** to **Survival** skill checks.
- Gain **+4** to checks made to detect **natural hazards**, including quicksand, unstable ground, rockfalls, thin ice, poisonous plants, and similar environmental dangers.
- Gain **+4** to detect **ambushes** or hidden creatures before combat begins.
- Gain **+4** to resist becoming **Lost** while travelling through natural environments.
- You may forage for food and fresh water at **three times the normal rate**, subject to the GM's discretion.
- You require **half the normal time** to establish a safe campsite or shelter.
- Gain **+2** to saving throws against **natural diseases and natural poisons**.

---

### Lore

Veteran Rangers often joke that the wilderness itself begins to guide those who survive long enough. While outsiders dismiss this as superstition, experienced hunters know that years spent living among nature cultivate instincts that cannot be learned from books or training grounds.

Many expeditions owe their survival to a Ranger noticing the smallest warning signs—a sudden change in birdsong, fresh claw marks on a tree, or the scent of rain carried by the wind. Such observations often mean the difference between arriving safely and walking into disaster.

Within the Lodges, Rangers of this rank are frequently entrusted with leading scouting parties and long-distance expeditions, for their instincts have proven reliable time and time again.

---

> *"Maps show where the road was. Instinct tells you where it should never go."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The Ranger's survival instincts have become an inseparable part of who they are. Every sense is constantly evaluating the world around them, allowing them to react to danger with remarkable speed and confidence. Their experience enables them to notice threats long before they become obvious, often avoiding danger altogether rather than simply surviving it.

By this stage, the Ranger has learned to thrive in environments that would overwhelm most travellers. Whether crossing frozen tundras, scorching deserts, dense forests, or towering mountain ranges, they instinctively adapt to changing conditions while guiding both themselves and their companions safely through the wilderness.

Among the Ranger Lodges, this level of mastery earns the title of **Pathfinder**, recognising those trusted to lead expeditions into the most dangerous regions of Asteria.

---

### Effects

- Gain **+6** to **Survival** skill checks.
- Gain **+6** to checks made to detect **natural hazards**, including unstable terrain, traps, rockfalls, thin ice, poisonous plants, and similar environmental dangers.
- Gain **+6** to detect **ambushes** or hidden creatures before combat begins.
- Gain **+6** to resist becoming **Lost** while travelling through natural environments.
- Gain **+4** to saving throws against **natural diseases** and **natural poisons**.
- You may forage for food and fresh water at **four times the normal rate**, subject to the GM's discretion.
- You require only **one-quarter of the normal time** to establish a safe campsite or wilderness shelter.
- You and creatures travelling with you ignore **non-magical difficult terrain** while travelling outside of combat.

---

### Lore

Rangers who achieve the third rank of Survival Instinct become renowned throughout Asteria as guides capable of crossing regions that others consider impassable. Their understanding of the natural world extends far beyond tracking prey—they read the land itself, predicting dangers before they arise and finding safe passage where none appears to exist.

Many kingdoms employ such Rangers to escort caravans, military expeditions, and explorers into the unknown. Their reputation is built not upon the monsters they have slain, but upon the countless lives they have brought home safely.

Within the Ranger Lodges, apprentices are taught that surviving the wilderness is no longer enough. A true Pathfinder ensures that everyone under their guidance survives as well.

---

> *"The wilderness is neither friend nor foe. It simply rewards those wise enough to understand it."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger's instincts now border on supernatural, though they remain entirely the product of experience, discipline, and countless years spent surviving where few others could. Every sound, scent, and subtle movement is unconsciously processed, allowing the Ranger to anticipate danger before it fully reveals itself.

No environment feels truly hostile anymore. Frozen tundras, scorching deserts, ancient forests, and monster-infested swamps become familiar territory where the Ranger can move with confidence. Their instincts extend beyond personal survival, allowing them to guide companions safely through the harshest regions of Asteria.

Within the Ranger Lodges, those who attain this rank are known as **Wayfinders**, trusted to lead expeditions into lands that have never before been explored.

---

### Effects

- Gain **+8** to **Survival** skill checks.
- Gain **+8** to checks made to detect **natural hazards**, including unstable terrain, hidden pitfalls, avalanches, poisonous flora, quicksand, and similar environmental dangers.
- Gain **+8** to detect **ambushes**, hidden creatures, and concealed natural threats before combat begins.
- Gain **+8** to checks made to avoid becoming **Lost** in natural environments.
- Gain **+6** to saving throws against **natural diseases**, **natural poisons**, and **environmental hazards**.
- You may forage for food and fresh water at **five times the normal rate**, subject to the GM's discretion.
- You require only **one-quarter of the normal time** to establish a secure campsite or wilderness shelter.
- You and creatures travelling with you ignore **non-magical difficult terrain** while travelling and suffer no movement penalty from natural terrain outside of combat.
- You have **Advantage** on initiative rolls when combat begins as the result of a natural ambush or environmental encounter.

---

### Lore

Only the most accomplished Rangers ever achieve the fourth rank of Survival Instinct. Their reputation spreads far beyond the Ranger Lodges, and kings, merchants, and explorers alike seek their guidance before venturing into dangerous lands. Stories tell of Wayfinders leading entire expeditions across continents without losing a single traveller, avoiding disasters that others never even realised existed.

To these Rangers, survival is no longer about endurance—it is about understanding the wilderness as a living, ever-changing world. They read the wind like a map, recognise danger in the silence of birds, and instinctively choose the safest path long before others realise there was ever a choice.

---

> *"The greatest guide is not the one who knows every path. It is the one who always knows which path not to take."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has become one with the wilderness. Every sense operates in perfect harmony, constantly reading the environment without conscious thought. A subtle shift in the wind, the sudden silence of wildlife, or a barely visible footprint is enough for the Ranger to recognise danger long before it threatens them.

To a master Ranger, survival is no longer a skill—it is instinct. They move through the harshest regions of Asteria as though they were home, adapting effortlessly to changing conditions while guiding others with absolute confidence. Where others see an impassable wilderness, the Ranger sees opportunity, safety, and countless paths forward.

The greatest Rangers are said to possess an almost mythical awareness of their surroundings. Whether these stories are exaggerated or not, one truth remains unchanged: very few who travel beside a master Ranger fail to return home.

---

### Effects

- Gain **+10** to **Survival** skill checks.
- Gain **+10** to checks made to detect **natural hazards**, including unstable terrain, hidden sinkholes, avalanches, poisonous flora, quicksand, thin ice, and similar environmental dangers.
- Gain **+10** to detect **ambushes**, hidden creatures, concealed traps, and environmental threats before combat begins.
- Gain **+10** to checks made to avoid becoming **Lost** in natural environments.
- Gain **+8** to saving throws against **natural diseases**, **natural poisons**, and **environmental hazards**.
- You may forage for food and fresh water at **six times the normal rate**, subject to the GM's discretion.
- You require only **one-tenth of the normal time** to establish a secure campsite or wilderness shelter.
- You and creatures travelling with you ignore **all non-magical difficult terrain** while travelling.
- You have **Advantage** on Initiative rolls whenever combat begins due to an ambush or environmental encounter.
- Once per **Long Rest**, if you would be **Surprised**, you may ignore the **Surprised** condition.

---

### Lore

Only the legendary Huntmasters of Asteria ever reach the fifth rank of Survival Instinct. Their names become synonymous with exploration, endurance, and impossible journeys. They are the guides sought by kings venturing into forgotten ruins, by scholars crossing uncharted continents, and by adventurers chasing legends beyond the edge of the known world.

The oldest Ranger Lodges teach that a master Ranger no longer survives because they are stronger than nature, but because they have learned to become part of it. The wilderness no longer feels hostile in their presence; instead, it seems to reveal its secrets willingly. Every rustling leaf, shifting cloud, and distant animal call becomes another piece of a story only the Ranger can truly understand.

Many believe these instincts are supernatural gifts. Rangers simply smile and continue walking, knowing that every lesson was earned through years of hardship, perseverance, and respect for the wild.

---

> *"The wilderness never stops speaking. The greatest Rangers are simply the ones who never stopped listening."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Pathfinder of the Emerald Lodge**

None

# Thorned Fortress

## Overview
Your mastery over living plant magic allows you to reinforce your summoned guardians with dense bark, razor-sharp thorns, and resilient vines.

Whether it is an Entling, a Spirit Bloom summon, or another plant-based creature under your control, your summons become living fortresses that punish those foolish enough to engage them in close combat.

The thorns that cover their bodies are more than simple defences. They instinctively react to danger, tearing into enemies that strike them or become ensnared within their grasp.

Many Druids believe this blessing was first taught by the Elder Ents themselves, who learned long ago that the strongest defence is one that discourages an enemy from attacking in the first place.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

Your mastery over living plant magic allows you to reinforce your summoned guardians with dense bark, razor-sharp thorns, and resilient vines.

Whether it is an Entling, a Spirit Bloom summon, or another plant-based creature under your control, your summons become living fortresses that punish those foolish enough to engage them in close combat.

The thorns that cover their bodies are more than simple defences. They instinctively react to danger, tearing into enemies that strike them or become ensnared within their grasp.

Many Druids believe this blessing was first taught by the Elder Ents themselves, who learned long ago that the strongest defence is one that discourages an enemy from attacking in the first place.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- All **Plant-based Summons** you control gain the **Thorned** trait.
- Plant-based summons gain:
  - **+10 Maximum HP**
  - **+1 Attack Damage**
- Whenever a creature hits one of your Plant-based summons with a **melee attack**, it immediately suffers **2 Piercing Damage** from the creature's thorns.
- If one of your Plant-based summons successfully **Grapples** a creature, the grappled creature suffers **2 Piercing Damage** at the **start of each of its turns** while the grapple is maintained.
- Thorn damage ignores non-magical armour but may still be reduced by abilities or resistances that reduce **Piercing Damage**.

---

### Lore

The oldest forests in Asteria are home to trees whose bark is harder than stone and whose thorns have grown for centuries. These ancient guardians survive not through aggression, but by making every attack against them costly.

Druids who master Thorned Fortress learn to weave that same natural resilience into their summoned companions. Bark thickens, vines tighten, and thorns emerge wherever an enemy dares to strike.

Among the Verdant Circles, this gift is viewed as a symbol of nature's quiet strength. A forest does not chase its enemies—it simply ensures they regret every step they take within it.

---

> *"Strike a thorn once, and you curse the thorn. Strike a living forest, and you soon realise the thorn was showing mercy."*  
> — **Elder Brambleheart, Keeper of the Ironwood Grove**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your mastery over living plant guardians continues to grow, allowing thicker bark and stronger thorned vines to form around your summoned allies.

The once modest defensive thorns now develop into dense natural armour, making your summons significantly more resilient in battle. Their grasp tightens, and every attempt to break free from their embrace comes at a painful cost.

Experienced Druids often shape their summoned guardians into the front line of battle, allowing them to absorb attacks while the forest slowly wears down those who refuse to retreat.

To many within the Druidic Circles, Thorned Fortress is proof that nature's greatest strength is not its ability to attack—but its ability to endure.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- All **Plant-based Summons** you control gain the **Thorned** trait.
- Plant-based summons gain:
  - **+20 Maximum HP**
  - **+2 Attack Damage**
  - **+2 to Grapple Checks**
- Whenever a creature hits one of your Plant-based summons with a **melee attack**, it immediately suffers **3 Piercing Damage** from the creature's thorns.
- If one of your Plant-based summons successfully **Grapples** a creature, the grappled creature suffers **3 Piercing Damage** at the **start of each of its turns** while the grapple is maintained.
- Thorn damage ignores non-magical armour but may still be reduced by abilities or resistances that reduce **Piercing Damage**.

---

### Lore

As a Druid's bond with the forest deepens, their summoned guardians begin to resemble the ancient defenders that watch over the oldest groves of Asteria.

Layers of bark harden like living armour while thorn-covered vines instinctively wrap around any creature that ventures too close. Every wound inflicted upon these guardians is answered by the forest itself.

The oldest Ents are said to have developed these natural defences over thousands of years, their bark becoming almost impenetrable while their thorns served as a warning to those who sought to destroy the wild.

Druids who master Thorned Fortress do not simply summon allies—they summon pieces of the forest's enduring will.

---

> *"The forest does not fear those who strike first. It simply outlasts them until they strike no more."*  
> — **Grovekeeper Maelis Briarroot, Warden of the Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

Your summoned guardians now embody the relentless resilience of the oldest forests. Their bark grows thicker than ironwood, while long, barbed vines coil around their limbs, waiting to punish anything that comes within reach.

Enemies quickly learn that every strike against these guardians carries a price. The deeper they become entangled, the more the living thorns tear into flesh and armour alike.

At this stage, your plant summons are no longer simple defenders. They become wardens of the battlefield, capable of locking enemies in place while the forest slowly overwhelms them.

Many Druids consider this the point where their summons truly become extensions of the Living Forest itself.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- All **Plant-based Summons** you control gain the **Thorned** trait.
- Plant-based summons gain:
  - **+30 Maximum HP**
  - **+4 Attack Damage**
  - **+6 to Grapple Checks**
- Whenever a creature hits one of your Plant-based summons with a **melee attack**, it immediately suffers **4 Piercing Damage**.
- If one of your Plant-based summons successfully **Grapples** a creature, the grappled creature suffers **4 Piercing Damage** at the start of each of its turns.
- Grappled creatures must succeed on a **Constitution Check (DC 15)** at the start of their turn or suffer **1d4 Bleeding Damage**.
- Thorn damage ignores non-magical armour but may still be reduced by abilities or resistances that reduce **Piercing Damage**.

---

### Lore

Ancient records tell of forests where even the bravest warriors refused to tread. Not because the trees moved, but because every branch, vine, and thorn seemed determined to drive intruders away.

Druids who master Thorned Fortress begin to recreate these legendary guardians through their summons. Every layer of bark becomes stronger, every thorn sharper, and every vine more determined to hold those who threaten the balance of nature.

To stand against one of these guardians is to wage war against the patience of the forest itself. Every wound inflicted is answered in kind, until even the strongest enemies find themselves exhausted by the unyielding embrace of living wood.

---

> *"The wise fear the beast's bite. The wiser fear the tree that refuses to let go."*  
> — **Archdruid Rowan Thornbark, Warden of the Ironwood Circle**

## Rank 4
### Description

Your command over living plant guardians reaches a level few Druids ever achieve. Thick layers of enchanted bark encase your summons, while ancient thorned vines constantly regenerate across their bodies, making them exceptionally difficult to bring down.

The forest no longer merely protects its guardians—it actively punishes those who challenge them. Every strike against your summons is met with a painful reminder that nature is both patient and relentless. Enemies who become trapped within their grasp quickly find themselves bleeding beneath an endless mass of barbed vines.

Veteran Druids often position their summoned guardians at the heart of the battlefield, allowing them to hold the line while allies fight from the safety of the living fortress they have created.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- All **Plant-based Summons** you control gain the **Thorned** trait.
- Plant-based summons gain:
  - **+40 Maximum HP**
  - **+6 Attack Damage**
  - **+6 to Grapple Checks**
- Whenever a creature hits one of your Plant-based summons with a **melee attack**, it immediately suffers **6 Piercing Damage**.
- If one of your Plant-based summons successfully **Grapples** a creature, the grappled creature suffers **6 Piercing Damage** at the start of each of its turns.
- Grappled creatures must succeed on a **Constitution Check (DC 13)** at the start of their turn or suffer **1d6 Bleeding Damage**.
- Thorn damage ignores non-magical armour but may still be reduced by abilities or resistances that reduce **Piercing Damage**.
- Plant-based summons gain **Resistance to non-magical Slashing Damage** as their bark hardens into living armour.

---

### Lore

Among the oldest groves of Asteria stand trees that have endured countless wars, storms, and disasters. Their bark bears the scars of centuries, yet they continue to grow stronger with each passing season.

Druids who master Thorned Fortress begin to emulate these ancient guardians. Their summoned companions become living bastions whose purpose is not simply to fight, but to endure. Every thorn, every vine, and every layer of bark exists to protect the balance of nature and those who fight beside it.

The greatest forest wardens teach that true strength is measured not by how hard one strikes, but by how long one can stand against the darkness.

---

> *"An axe may wound the bark, but the forest remembers the hand that swung it."*  
> — **High Warden Sylvara Rootheart, Keeper of the Ironwood Grove**

## Rank 5
### Description

Your mastery over the Living Forest reaches its ultimate expression. The guardians that answer your call become legendary protectors, clad in ancient bark and covered in countless enchanted thorns that have grown for centuries.

Every branch, vine, and thorn becomes a weapon of defence. Those who attack your summons quickly discover that every strike is answered by the forest itself. Their bark becomes almost impossible to penetrate, while their grasp tightens with the unyielding strength of ancient roots.

To the Druids of old, this stage represents the perfect balance between strength and patience. The forest does not pursue its enemies, nor does it seek conquest. Instead, it stands firm, allowing those who threaten the natural world to defeat themselves against its living walls.

An Elder Ent protected by Thorned Fortress is said to resemble the oldest trees in Asteria—silent, immovable, and utterly relentless.

---

### Effects

- This is a **Passive Talent**.
- All **Plant-based Summons** you control gain the **Thorned** trait.
- Plant-based summons gain:
  - **+50 Maximum HP**
  - **+8 Attack Damage**
  - **+8 to Grapple Checks**
- Whenever a creature hits one of your Plant-based summons with a **melee attack**, it immediately suffers **8 Piercing Damage**.
- If one of your Plant-based summons successfully **Grapples** a creature, the grappled creature suffers **8 Piercing Damage** at the start of each of its turns.
- Grappled creatures must succeed on a **Constitution Check (DC 10)** at the start of their turn or suffer **2d6 Bleeding Damage**.
- Thorn damage ignores non-magical armour but may still be reduced by abilities or resistances that reduce **Piercing Damage**.
- Plant-based summons gain **Resistance to non-magical Slashing and Piercing Damage**.
- Once per round, when a Plant-based summon is reduced below **50% of its maximum HP**, thorn-covered vines surge across its body, granting it **Temporary HP equal to 10% of its maximum HP**. This effect may trigger **once per summon**.

---

### Lore

The oldest legends speak of forests so ancient that invading armies simply vanished beneath their canopies. Those who survived claimed that the trees themselves fought back, their living guardians refusing to yield even after suffering terrible wounds.

These stories are believed to have inspired the creation of Thorned Fortress. Rather than teaching Druids how to create stronger summons, the talent teaches them how to awaken the ancient resilience that already exists within every guardian spirit of the forest.

To witness an Elder Ent protected by Thorned Fortress is to understand why entire kingdoms once feared entering the sacred groves of Asteria. The guardian does not rage or pursue. It simply endures, standing between the innocent and those who would bring harm, until the forest itself has claimed victory.

---

> *"Strength fells a tree. Patience grows a forest. Endurance protects it for eternity."*  
> — **Grand Archdruid Elarion Wildroot, Guardian of the First Grove**

None
