# Trophy Hunter

## Overview
The greatest Rangers do not simply hunt—they learn from every victory. Each dangerous beast, monstrous predator, and legendary creature defeated becomes another lesson etched into memory. By studying the anatomy, behaviour, and weaknesses of their prey, the Ranger steadily builds an unmatched understanding of the world's most dangerous creatures.

Trophy Hunter marks the beginning of this journey. Rather than collecting trophies for vanity, the Ranger preserves them as reminders of hard-earned knowledge. Every fang, claw, horn, or hide represents another hunt survived and another weakness uncovered. Against creatures they have studied before, the Ranger fights with calm confidence, knowing exactly where to strike and what mistakes to avoid.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

The greatest Rangers do not simply hunt—they learn from every victory. Each dangerous beast, monstrous predator, and legendary creature defeated becomes another lesson etched into memory. By studying the anatomy, behaviour, and weaknesses of their prey, the Ranger steadily builds an unmatched understanding of the world's most dangerous creatures.

Trophy Hunter marks the beginning of this journey. Rather than collecting trophies for vanity, the Ranger preserves them as reminders of hard-earned knowledge. Every fang, claw, horn, or hide represents another hunt survived and another weakness uncovered. Against creatures they have studied before, the Ranger fights with calm confidence, knowing exactly where to strike and what mistakes to avoid.

---

### Effects

- Whenever you personally participate in defeating a **Beast**, **Monster**, or other GM-approved creature, you may spend **1 hour** harvesting a trophy from its remains.
- Record the harvested trophy in a **Trophy Journal**.
- While fighting a creature of a species recorded within your Trophy Journal:
  - Gain a **+2 bonus to attack rolls** against that species.
  - Gain a **+2 bonus to Survival, Nature, and Investigation** checks made to identify, track, or study that species.
- You may only benefit from **one Trophy Hunter bonus** at a time.
- Harvesting a trophy does not prevent normal harvesting of crafting materials.

---

### Lore

Within the Ranger Lodges, every trophy tells a story. Some display the claw of a cave bear that nearly ended their first hunt, while others preserve the fang of a wyvern or the feather of a great roc. These keepsakes are not symbols of pride alone—they are lessons carried into every future hunt.

Veteran Rangers often possess collections spanning decades, each one representing a creature whose secrets they have uncovered. Apprentices are encouraged to study these trophies, for the wisdom gained from a single successful hunt may one day save countless lives.

---

> *"The greatest reward from every hunt is not the trophy—it is the knowledge that ensures the next one ends the same way."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's collection of trophies has grown into a living record of experience. Every hunt adds another lesson, allowing the Ranger to recognise subtle differences between creatures of the same family and predict their behaviour before battle even begins. The knowledge gained through years of hunting becomes just as deadly as any weapon they carry.

As the Trophy Journal expands, the Ranger develops an instinct for identifying vulnerable anatomy, common attack patterns, and survival habits. Against familiar prey, hesitation disappears, replaced by calm confidence earned through countless successful hunts.

---

### Effects

- Whenever you personally participate in defeating a **Beast**, **Monster**, or other GM-approved creature, you may spend **1 hour** harvesting a trophy from its remains.
- Record the harvested trophy within your **Trophy Journal**.
- While fighting a creature belonging to a species or creature family recorded within your Trophy Journal:
  - Gain a **+3 bonus to attack rolls** against that species or family.
  - Gain a **+3 bonus** to **Survival**, **Nature**, and **Investigation** checks made to identify, track, or study that species or family.
  - Gain **Advantage** on checks made to recall information about that species.
- You may only benefit from **one Trophy Hunter bonus** at a time.
- Harvesting a trophy does not prevent normal harvesting of crafting materials.
- The GM may allow closely related creatures to count as the same creature family (for example, Wolves, Dire Wolves, and Elder Wolves).

---

### Lore

Veteran Rangers often say that every scar tells a story, but every trophy tells a lesson. Over time, the Trophy Journal becomes more than a catalogue of victories—it becomes a field guide filled with hard-earned knowledge gathered through countless dangerous encounters.

Within the Ranger Lodges, apprentices are encouraged to study the journals of experienced hunters before undertaking dangerous expeditions. Many legendary beasts have been defeated not through overwhelming strength, but because a Ranger recognised a familiar weakness preserved within the pages of a Trophy Journal.

---

> *"Strength wins a hunt once. Knowledge wins every hunt that follows."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

Years of relentless hunting have transformed the Ranger into a living bestiary. Every creature added to the Trophy Journal deepens their understanding of the natural world, allowing them to recognise strengths, weaknesses, and behaviours with only a brief observation. To the Ranger, no trophy is merely a keepsake—it is another lesson that may save lives during future hunts.

This accumulated knowledge grants the Ranger remarkable insight into familiar prey. By studying trophies and recalling past encounters, they instinctively recognise where to strike, which attacks to avoid, and how best to exploit the creature's natural weaknesses. Against known prey, experience becomes as valuable as skill.

---

### Effects

- Whenever you personally participate in defeating a **Beast**, **Monster**, or other GM-approved creature, you may spend **1 hour** harvesting a trophy from its remains.
- Record the harvested trophy within your **Trophy Journal**.
- While fighting a creature belonging to a species or creature family recorded within your Trophy Journal:
  - Gain a **+4 bonus to attack rolls** against that species or family.
  - Gain a **+4 bonus** to **Survival**, **Nature**, and **Investigation** checks made to identify, track, or study that species or family.
  - Gain **Advantage** on checks made to recall information about that species.
- After successfully identifying a creature recorded in your Trophy Journal, you learn one of the following (GM's choice if unknown):
  - One Resistance.
  - One Immunity.
  - One Vulnerability.
  - One notable combat behaviour or special ability.
- You may only benefit from **one Trophy Hunter bonus** at a time.
- Harvesting a trophy does not prevent normal harvesting of crafting materials.

---

### Lore

Senior Rangers often spend as much time studying their Trophy Journals as they do hunting. Every page records another hard-earned lesson, allowing future encounters to begin with knowledge instead of uncertainty. To outsiders the collection appears to be a display of impressive trophies; to a Ranger it is a lifetime of experience preserved for the next hunt.

Within the Ranger Lodges, journals belonging to legendary hunters are treasured relics. Entire generations of Rangers have survived impossible encounters simply because a forgotten note revealed a creature's weakness before the battle began.

---

> *"Every beast carries a weakness. A Trophy Hunter simply learns to remember them all."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger's Trophy Journal has become one of the finest collections of hunting knowledge in Asteria. Years of studying monsters, beasts, and legendary creatures have taught the Ranger that every family of creatures shares common instincts, weaknesses, and methods of survival. What was once knowledge of individual species now extends to entire bloodlines.

Rather than relying on memory alone, the Ranger instinctively recognises subtle traits shared between related creatures. A dragon's stance, a wolf's hunting pattern, or the posture of an undead guardian immediately reveals valuable information gathered from countless previous hunts. Against familiar creature families, the Ranger rarely enters battle unprepared.

---

### Effects

- Whenever you personally participate in defeating a **Beast**, **Monster**, or other GM-approved creature, you may spend **1 hour** harvesting a trophy from its remains.
- Record the harvested trophy within your **Trophy Journal**.
- While fighting a creature belonging to a **recorded creature family**, gain:
  - **+5 bonus to attack rolls**.
  - **+5 bonus** to **Survival**, **Nature**, and **Investigation** checks made to identify, track, or study that creature family.
  - **Advantage** on checks made to recall information about that creature family.
- After successfully identifying a creature recorded in your Trophy Journal, immediately learn **two** of the following:
  - One Resistance.
  - One Immunity.
  - One Vulnerability.
  - One notable combat behaviour or special ability.
- Once per encounter, you may reroll a failed **Nature**, **Survival**, or **Investigation** check made against a recorded creature family. You must use the new result.
- You may only benefit from **one Trophy Hunter bonus** at a time.
- Harvesting trophies does not prevent normal harvesting of crafting materials.

---

### Lore

Master Trophy Hunters are no longer recognised by the number of trophies they possess, but by the knowledge they carry into every hunt. Entire creature families become familiar to them, allowing even newly encountered variants to be understood through years of accumulated experience. Few creatures can truly surprise a Ranger who has spent decades studying the natural world.

Within the Ranger Lodges, the journals of these hunters are considered priceless archives. Generations of Rangers continue to add new discoveries, ensuring that every successful hunt strengthens those who will one day follow the same path.

---

> *"Every creature leaves behind more than a trophy. It leaves behind the wisdom to defeat the next one."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has become one of Asteria's greatest Trophy Hunters, possessing a Trophy Journal that spans a lifetime of legendary hunts. Every beast, monster, and apex predator defeated has left behind more than a physical trophy—it has contributed to an unparalleled understanding of the natural world. No hunt is wasted, and every encounter strengthens the Ranger's mastery over future prey.

The Trophy Journal is now considered a priceless archive, containing knowledge that cannot be found in books or taught through study alone. When facing a familiar creature, the Ranger instinctively recognises its strengths, weaknesses, behaviours, and patterns of attack before battle has truly begun. To many, it appears almost supernatural, yet it is simply the reward of surviving countless impossible hunts.

---

### Effects

- Whenever you personally participate in defeating a **Beast**, **Monster**, or other GM-approved creature, you may spend **1 hour** harvesting a trophy from its remains.
- Record the harvested trophy within your **Trophy Journal**.
- While fighting a creature belonging to a **recorded creature family**, gain:
  - **+6 bonus to attack rolls**.
  - **+6 bonus** to **Survival**, **Nature**, and **Investigation** checks made to identify, track, or study that creature family.
  - **Advantage** on checks made to recall information about that creature family.
- Immediately learn **all known**:
  - Resistances.
  - Immunities.
  - Vulnerabilities.
  - Combat behaviours.
  - Special abilities.
  - Natural weaknesses.
- Once per encounter, you may reroll a failed **Attack Roll**, **Nature**, **Survival**, or **Investigation** check made against a recorded creature family. You must use the new result.
- You may only benefit from **one Trophy Hunter bonus** at a time.
- Harvesting trophies does not prevent normal harvesting of crafting materials.

---

### Lore

Only a handful of Rangers throughout history have ever completed a Trophy Journal worthy of legend. These individuals are sought by kingdoms, guilds, and scholars alike, for their knowledge of the world's most dangerous creatures surpasses that of nearly every library in existence. Their journals become treasured relics, copied and preserved so future generations may continue the endless pursuit of understanding the wilderness.

Among the Ranger Lodges, these masters are known simply as **Trophy Hunters**—a title that carries immense respect. They do not hunt for glory or recognition, but because every creature overcome adds another page to the ever-growing story of the wild. Their greatest weapon is no longer their bow or blade, but the wisdom earned through every hunt they have survived.

---

> *"The greatest trophy is not the fang upon your wall—it is the knowledge that ensures no creature defeats you twice."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Trophy Hunter**

# Unyielding Conviction

## Overview
There are moments when even the greatest champions falter. A failed leap, a crippling curse, or a test of will can mean the difference between salvation and ruin. Yet a Paladin does not surrender to failure so easily. Through unwavering faith, you may call upon your patron to grant you one final opportunity to overcome the impossible.

When invoking Unyielding Conviction, you place your trust entirely in your patron. Your own skill gives way to divine guidance as fate itself is rewritten for a single fleeting moment. This blessing is never granted lightly, demanding both physical endurance and divine energy to invoke.

Those who witness this miracle often describe it as impossible to explain. To the faithful, however, the answer is simple—where conviction is absolute, even fate may bend.

## Rank 1
### Description

There are moments when even the greatest champions falter. A failed leap, a crippling curse, or a test of will can mean the difference between salvation and ruin. Yet a Paladin does not surrender to failure so easily. Through unwavering faith, you may call upon your patron to grant you one final opportunity to overcome the impossible.

When invoking Unyielding Conviction, you place your trust entirely in your patron. Your own skill gives way to divine guidance as fate itself is rewritten for a single fleeting moment. This blessing is never granted lightly, demanding both physical endurance and divine energy to invoke.

Those who witness this miracle often describe it as impossible to explain. To the faithful, however, the answer is simple—where conviction is absolute, even fate may bend.

### Effects

- **Once per Long Rest**, after failing a **Saving Throw** or **Skill Check**, you may invoke **Unyielding Conviction**.
- Spend **10 MP** and **10 SP** to activate this ability.
- Repeat the failed roll using your **Luck Modifier** in place of the modifier normally applied to the roll.
- If the original action required additional **MP, SP, HP, consumables, charges, ammunition, or other resources**, those costs must also be paid again before the second attempt is made.
- If the failed roll involved **multiple dice** (such as **Advantage** or **Disadvantage**), you may reroll **only one** of those dice. The rerolled die replaces its original result before determining the final outcome.
- The repeated attempt is treated as a completely new roll.
- You must accept the result of the second attempt, even if it is lower than the original.
- Additional effects granted by your patron's **Divine Authority** apply where applicable.

### Lore

The scriptures of every faith tell stories of champions who faced certain failure, only to find the strength to rise once more. Some speak of an unseen hand guiding them, while others recall hearing nothing more than a quiet whisper urging them to stand again. Whatever form the miracle takes, all agree that it is not earned through strength alone, but through absolute trust in one's patron.

Among the faithful, Unyielding Conviction is regarded as one of the purest demonstrations of divine favour. A patron does not guarantee success, nor do they erase failure. Instead, they grant their champion one final opportunity to prove that their faith is worthy of the miracle they have received.

> *"The gods do not promise victory. They promise that those who refuse to yield will never stand alone."*  
> **— High Marshal Aurelius, First Champion of the Sacred Host**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your faith has deepened beyond simple perseverance. When adversity threatens to overwhelm you, your patron's guidance becomes clearer, allowing destiny itself to shift ever so slightly in your favour. Though failure may still come, your conviction grants you another opportunity to prove your worth through unwavering devotion.

Each time you invoke Unyielding Conviction, you reaffirm the sacred bond between yourself and your patron. It is not a miracle born from desperation, but a conscious act of trust, placing your fate into divine hands and accepting whatever outcome follows.

Those who witness such moments often believe they have seen fate rewritten. The faithful know the truth—it is simply the reward of absolute conviction.

### Effects

- **Once per Long Rest**, after failing a **Saving Throw** or **Skill Check**, you may invoke **Unyielding Conviction**.
- Spend **15 MP** and **15 SP** to activate this ability.
- Repeat the failed roll using your **Luck Modifier** in place of the attribute modifier normally applied to the roll.
- If the original action required additional **MP, SP, HP, consumables, charges, ammunition, or other resources**, those costs must also be paid again before the second attempt is made.
- If the failed roll involved **multiple dice** (such as **Advantage** or **Disadvantage**), you may reroll **only one** of those dice. The rerolled die replaces its original result before determining the final outcome.
- Gain **+2** to the repeated roll.
- The repeated attempt is treated as a completely new roll.
- You must accept the result of the second attempt, even if it is lower than the original.
- Additional effects granted by your patron's **Divine Authority** apply where applicable.

### Lore

The greatest Paladins teach that faith is strongest when tested. Every trial overcome strengthens the covenant between champion and patron, until even fate itself seems willing to offer one final opportunity. Such miracles are never guaranteed, nor are they given freely. They are gifts entrusted only to those who have demonstrated unwavering devotion through both triumph and hardship.

Across the temples of Asteria, stories are told of champions who survived impossible ordeals because they refused to surrender when all hope seemed lost. Whether facing ancient dragons, enduring terrible curses, or standing against overwhelming armies, they prevailed not through strength alone, but because their conviction never wavered.

> *"The faithful do not ask the gods to change destiny. They ask only for the strength to meet it one final time."*  
> **— High Marshal Aurelius, First Champion of the Sacred Host**

## Rank 3
### Description

Your faith has become an unwavering beacon, allowing your patron's guidance to shine through even in moments of absolute despair. When others would accept failure, you refuse to yield, trusting completely in the divine covenant that binds your soul to a higher purpose. Every miracle granted through Unyielding Conviction is a testament to the unbreakable trust between champion and patron.

Though fate may appear fixed, your conviction allows you to challenge it one final time. This blessing is never given lightly, demanding both physical endurance and divine power before your patron answers your plea. Those who witness such moments often believe destiny itself has been rewritten.

### Effects

- **Once per Long Rest**, after failing a **Saving Throw** or **Skill Check**, you may invoke **Unyielding Conviction**.
- Spend **20 MP** and **20 SP** to activate this ability.

Many believe miracles are extraordinary events granted only in the darkest hours. The faithful know differently. Miracles are not rewards for perfection—they are granted to those who continue standing when every reason to surrender has already passed. Such conviction cannot be forged overnight, but only through years of unwavering devotion.

The oldest scriptures tell of champions who survived impossible trials through nothing more than faith and determination. Whether escaping ancient curses, resisting overwhelming magic, or completing sacred rituals against impossible odds, they endured because their patron judged their purpose unfinished.

> *"Conviction is not the certainty that you will succeed. It is the certainty that you must try once more."*  
> **— High Marshal Aurelius, First Champion of the Sacred Host**

# Veinlock

## Overview
A Bloodhunter soon learns that blood is more than life—it is movement. Every heartbeat drives muscles, every pulse fuels strength, and every flowing vein keeps a creature alive. Through Sangramancy, the Bloodhunter can momentarily seize control of that flow, causing the blood within an enemy's body to thicken and resist its natural movement.

This technique is known as **Veinlock**. Rather than inflicting overwhelming pain, the Bloodhunter briefly restricts circulation, causing muscles to stiffen and reactions to slow. The effect is subtle but devastating, robbing even the fastest prey of the speed they rely upon to escape.

Veinlock is most effective against creatures already suffering from open wounds. Fresh blood provides the Sangramancer with a stronger connection to the target, allowing the manipulation to spread more easily through the circulatory system. Veteran Bloodhunters often combine Blood Rite with Veinlock, weakening their prey before closing in for the kill.

The technique is completely ineffective against creatures without circulating blood. Constructs, most undead, oozes, and similar beings simply possess no living blood for the Bloodhunter to command.

## Rank 1
### Description

A Bloodhunter soon learns that blood is more than life—it is movement. Every heartbeat drives muscles, every pulse fuels strength, and every flowing vein keeps a creature alive. Through Sangramancy, the Bloodhunter can momentarily seize control of that flow, causing the blood within an enemy's body to thicken and resist its natural movement.

This technique is known as **Veinlock**. Rather than inflicting overwhelming pain, the Bloodhunter briefly restricts circulation, causing muscles to stiffen and reactions to slow. The effect is subtle but devastating, robbing even the fastest prey of the speed they rely upon to escape.

Veinlock is most effective against creatures already suffering from open wounds. Fresh blood provides the Sangramancer with a stronger connection to the target, allowing the manipulation to spread more easily through the circulatory system. Veteran Bloodhunters often combine Blood Rite with Veinlock, weakening their prey before closing in for the kill.

The technique is completely ineffective against creatures without circulating blood. Constructs, most undead, oozes, and similar beings simply possess no living blood for the Bloodhunter to command.

### Effects

- As an **Action**, target one creature with circulating blood within **15 metres**.
- Spend **15 MP**, sacrifice **5 HP**, and gain **5 Blood Points (BP)**.
- The target must succeed on a **Constitution Saving Throw** against your **Sangramancy DC**.
- On a failed save, the target becomes **Veinlocked** for **2 Combat Rounds**.
- While Veinlocked, the target:
  - Has its **Movement Speed reduced by 50%**.
  - Cannot take the **Dash** action.
  - Has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.
- If the target is currently suffering from a **Bleeding** effect, it has **Disadvantage** on the Constitution Saving Throw.
- A creature may only be affected by one instance of Veinlock at a time.
- Veinlock has **no effect** on creatures without functioning blood unless another Bloodhunter ability specifically states otherwise.

### Lore

Among the Bloodhunter Orders, Veinlock is often the first true display of offensive Sangramancy taught to apprentices. Unlike Blood Rite, which channels one's own blood into a weapon, Veinlock reaches outward, proving that another creature's blood can be manipulated just as easily as one's own.

Many apprentices struggle with the technique at first. They instinctively try to force the blood to stop completely, only to find the connection breaks under such strain. Masters instead teach them to think of a river rather than a dam—slowing the current just enough that the prey begins to stumble under its own weight.

Experienced Bloodhunters know that a fleeing monster is often more dangerous than a cornered one. Veinlock was created not to kill, but to ensure that once the hunt begins, the prey can never outrun the hunter.

> *"Every creature believes its legs will carry it to safety. They forget who commands the blood that moves them."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 2
### Description

With greater mastery of Sangramancy, the Bloodhunter learns that blood does not merely power movement—it dictates timing, balance, and reaction. By exerting finer control over a target's circulatory system, the Bloodhunter can cause muscles to seize at precisely the wrong moment, disrupting even the most disciplined warriors.

The victim feels as though their own body has begun to betray them. Their limbs become sluggish, reactions slow, and every attempt to defend themselves is delayed by a heartbeat. While the effect lasts only moments, those moments are often all a Bloodhunter requires to end the hunt.

Experienced Bloodhunters rarely use Veinlock to simply immobilise prey. Instead, they exploit hesitation. Every delayed step, every failed dodge, and every missed opportunity creates another opening for Sangramancy to inflict greater suffering. When combined with Blood Rite and a well-maintained Bleeding effect, Veinlock transforms even the swiftest enemy into easy prey.

However, manipulating another creature's blood demands greater sacrifice from the Bloodhunter. More blood is offered, more Blood Points are accumulated, and the whispers of Bloodlust grow louder with every successful use.

### Effects

- As an **Action**, target one creature with circulating blood within **20 metres**.
- Spend **20 MP**, sacrifice **8 HP**, and gain **10 Blood Points (BP)**.
- The target must succeed on a **Constitution Saving Throw** against your **Sangramancy DC**.
- On a failed save, the target becomes **Veinlocked** for **3 Combat Rounds**.
- While Veinlocked, the target:
  - Has its **Movement Speed reduced by 50%**.
  - Cannot take the **Dash** action.
  - Cannot take **Reactions**.
  - Has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.
- If the target is suffering from a **Bleeding** effect, it has **Disadvantage** on the Constitution Saving Throw.
- If the target is both **Bleeding** and your **Marked Prey**, it also suffers **-2 to Dexterity Saving Throws** while Veinlocked.
- A creature may only be affected by one instance of Veinlock at a time.
- Veinlock has **no effect** on creatures without functioning blood unless another Bloodhunter ability states otherwise.

### Lore

Bloodhunter veterans describe the Second Rank of Veinlock as the moment Sangramancy changes from simple manipulation into complete battlefield control. Rather than merely slowing prey, the Bloodhunter begins controlling the rhythm of combat itself. A delayed parry, a missed opportunity, or a failed escape often determines the outcome of an entire hunt.

Many Bloodhunters compare the circulatory system to a river. At first they merely slowed its current. Now they learn to create sudden surges and blockages, forcing the body to move against its own instincts. To onlookers, the victim appears exhausted or clumsy. Only another Sangramancer understands that every heartbeat is being manipulated by an unseen hand.

The Orders warn that every successful Veinlock reinforces the Bloodhunter's confidence in controlling another living being. Used carelessly, that confidence may one day tempt the hunter to believe every creature exists only to have its blood commanded—a dangerous belief that has led many promising Bloodhunters toward Bloodlust.

> *"A warrior's greatest strength is timing. Steal a single heartbeat... and you've already won the battle."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 3
### Description

By the Third Rank, Veinlock has evolved beyond simply slowing an opponent. The Bloodhunter can now disrupt the rhythm of a creature's entire circulatory system, causing muscles to seize, reflexes to falter, and limbs to respond sluggishly to even the simplest commands. Every heartbeat becomes a battle between the creature's will and the Bloodhunter's Sangramancy.

At this level, experienced Bloodhunters no longer use Veinlock merely to prevent escape—they use it to dictate the pace of combat. Enemies find themselves unable to reposition, react, or unleash their full strength before the Bloodhunter closes the distance. The technique is especially feared amongst monsters that rely upon speed, overwhelming attacks, or coordinated movements.

The stronger the Bloodhunter's connection to their prey, the more devastating Veinlock becomes. A bleeding target offers countless paths through which Sangramancy may flow, allowing the Bloodhunter to tighten their control with terrifying precision. Many veteran hunters deliberately inflict wounds before invoking Veinlock, ensuring their prey becomes trapped both physically and psychologically.

Despite its effectiveness, Veinlock remains a dangerous technique. Every manipulation of another creature's lifeblood demands a greater sacrifice from the Bloodhunter, feeding Blood Points into the growing storm within their own soul.

### Effects

- As an **Action**, target one creature with circulating blood within **25 metres**.
- Spend **30 MP**, sacrifice **12 HP**, and gain **15 Blood Points (BP)**.
- The target must succeed on a **Constitution Saving Throw** against your **Sangramancy DC**.
- On a failed save, the target becomes **Veinlocked** for **4 Combat Rounds**.
- While Veinlocked, the target:
  - Has its **Movement Speed reduced by 75%**.
  - Cannot take the **Dash** action.
  - Cannot take **Reactions**.
  - Suffers **-1 Action Point** (minimum of 1 Action Point remaining).
  - Has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity Saving Throws.
- If the target is suffering from a **Bleeding** effect, it has **Disadvantage** on the Constitution Saving Throw.
- If the target is both **Bleeding** and your **Marked Prey**, it also suffers **-2 to Constitution Saving Throws** while Veinlocked.
- A creature may only be affected by one instance of Veinlock at a time.
- Veinlock has **no effect** on creatures without functioning blood unless another Bloodhunter ability specifically states otherwise.

### Lore

Among the Bloodhunter Orders, the Third Rank is known as **The Crimson Grip**. Few techniques inspire greater fear amongst intelligent monsters, for those who have witnessed it know that escape becomes nearly impossible once the Bloodhunter has seized control of their blood.

Masters teach that blood is the language spoken by every living creature. A skilled Sangramancer does not force the blood to obey—they convince it to flow differently, causing the body to betray itself one heartbeat at a time. To outsiders, the victim simply appears exhausted or slow. Only another Bloodhunter understands the invisible battle taking place beneath the skin.

Veterans caution their apprentices that Veinlock should never be used carelessly. Every successful manipulation strengthens the Bloodhunter's confidence in commanding another creature's lifeblood, and that confidence can easily become arrogance. Those who forget that blood is sacred often discover too late that Sangramancy is always willing to command its master as readily as it commands its prey.

> *"The body obeys the blood. Command the blood... and the body has no choice but to follow."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 4
### Description

Master Bloodhunters understand that blood is more than a source of life—it is the thread that binds every movement together. At the Fourth Rank, Veinlock allows the Bloodhunter to seize that thread with frightening precision, disrupting the flow of blood throughout an opponent's body until every movement becomes a struggle.

Victims often describe the sensation as though invisible chains have wrapped themselves around every muscle. Their limbs refuse to respond, their heartbeat becomes uneven, and every attempt to fight against the Sangramancy only causes their own blood to resist them further. Even the strongest warriors find themselves trapped inside bodies that no longer obey.

Against bleeding prey, the technique becomes devastating. Every open wound strengthens the Bloodhunter's connection, allowing Sangramancy to spread effortlessly through the target's circulatory system. Veteran Bloodhunters deliberately combine Blood Rite, Blood Scent, and Veinlock into a relentless sequence—find the prey, wound the prey, then ensure the prey can never escape.

Only creatures with functioning blood can be affected. Those without a living circulatory system remain beyond the reach of this technique, a limitation every Bloodhunter quickly learns to respect.

### Effects

- As an **Action**, target one creature with circulating blood within **30 metres**.
- Spend **40 MP**, sacrifice **16 HP**, and gain **20 Blood Points (BP)**.
- The target must succeed on a **Constitution Saving Throw** against your **Sangramancy DC**.
- On a failed save, the target becomes **Veinlocked** for **5 Combat Rounds**.
- While Veinlocked, the target:
  - Has its **Movement Speed reduced to 0**.
  - Cannot take the **Dash** action.
  - Cannot take **Reactions**.
  - Suffers **-1 Action Point** (minimum of 1 Action Point remaining).
  - Has **Disadvantage** on Dexterity and Constitution Saving Throws.
- At the end of each of its turns, the target may repeat the Constitution Saving Throw, ending Veinlock on a success.
- If the target is suffering from a **Bleeding** effect, it has **Disadvantage** on all Saving Throws made to end Veinlock.
- If the target is both **Bleeding** and your **Marked Prey**, it suffers **1d8 Blood Damage** at the start of each of its turns while Veinlocked.
- A creature may only be affected by one instance of Veinlock at a time.
- Veinlock has **no effect** on creatures without functioning blood unless another Bloodhunter ability specifically states otherwise.

### Lore

Within the Bloodhunter Orders, the Fourth Rank is known as **The Crimson Prison**. Few techniques inspire greater terror among monsters, for those who survive it often speak of being fully conscious while their own bodies refused every command.

Masters teach that Veinlock is not about overwhelming force. Instead, it is absolute precision. A Bloodhunter learns exactly which veins to constrict, which muscles to starve of blood, and which heartbeat to interrupt. To observers, the victim appears frozen by fear. In truth, they are imprisoned by their own blood.

The greatest Bloodhunters consider Veinlock an act of mercy. A fleeing monster endangers countless innocent lives. By ending the chase before it truly begins, the Bloodhunter ensures the hunt concludes swiftly and with as little unnecessary suffering as possible. Yet every use reminds the hunter how easily Sangramancy can command another living being—and how dangerous such power becomes when restraint is forgotten.

> *"The fastest prey still carries blood. That is all the advantage I require."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

## Rank 5
### Description

At the pinnacle of Sangramancy, the Bloodhunter no longer merely influences the blood of another creature—they command it. Every heartbeat, every contraction of muscle, and every surge of adrenaline becomes another thread woven into the Bloodhunter's control. To those who witness the technique, it appears as though time itself has slowed around the victim. In reality, it is their own blood refusing to obey.

Master Bloodhunters use Veinlock only when a hunt must end. Ancient dragons attempting to take flight, legendary beasts preparing their final charge, and powerful fiends readying devastating magic have all been brought to a standstill by a hunter who understands the language of blood better than the creature carrying it.

The connection forged through Blood Rite, Blood Scent, and Blood Communion reaches its absolute peak at this rank. A wounded Marked Prey becomes almost impossible to escape with, as every drop of blood flowing through its veins strengthens the Bloodhunter's control.

Yet such mastery demands an immense sacrifice. The Bloodhunter pours an overwhelming amount of Sangramancy into another living being, flooding themselves with Blood Points in the process. Every use brings them dangerously close to Bloodlust, forcing them to decide whether ending the hunt is worth risking the monster growing within.

### Effects

- As an **Action**, target one creature with circulating blood within **35 metres**.
- Spend **50 MP**, sacrifice **20 HP**, and gain **25 Blood Points (BP)**.
- The target must succeed on a **Constitution Saving Throw** against your **Sangramancy DC**.
- On a failed save, the target becomes **Veinlocked** for **6 Combat Rounds**.

### Lore

The Fifth Rank of Veinlock is spoken of with equal parts admiration and fear throughout every Bloodhunter Order. It is a technique so precise that masters claim it is no longer the Bloodhunter controlling another creature's blood—it is the blood itself recognising the authority of Sangramancy.

Stories tell of Apex Bloodhunters stopping charging giants mid-stride, grounding dragons before they could take flight, and freezing ancient vampires just long enough for the final strike to be delivered. These tales have become legends, yet every Bloodhunter knows they were purchased through immense sacrifice. Such absolute control can only be achieved by allowing the darkness within to rise alongside the power.

The elders warn that Veinlock is the ultimate temptation of Sangramancy. To command another creature's lifeblood so completely is to stand upon the edge of believing all life exists to be controlled. The greatest Bloodhunters never forget that blood is sacred, for the moment they do, the hunt ends—and Bloodlust begins.

> *"Every heart beats to the rhythm of blood. Learn that rhythm... and even legends shall stand still."*  
> — Grand Bloodhunter Serik Vaelor

# veinlock

## overview
a bloodhunter soon learns that blood is more than life—it is movement. every heartbeat drives muscles, every pulse fuels strength, and every flowing vein keeps a creature alive. through sangramancy, the bloodhunter can momentarily seize control of that flow, causing the blood within an enemy's body to thicken and resist its natural movement.

this technique is known as **veinlock**. rather than inflicting overwhelming pain, the bloodhunter briefly restricts circulation, causing muscles to stiffen and reactions to slow. the effect is subtle but devastating, robbing even the fastest prey of the speed they rely upon to escape.

veinlock is most effective against creatures already suffering from open wounds. fresh blood provides the sangramancer with a stronger connection to the target, allowing the manipulation to spread more easily through the circulatory system. veteran bloodhunters often combine blood rite with veinlock, weakening their prey before closing in for the kill.

the technique is completely ineffective against creatures without circulating blood. constructs, most undead, oozes, and similar beings simply possess no living blood for the bloodhunter to command.

# Vigilant Protector

## Overview
A true Paladin never truly lowers their guard. Even during moments of rest, your unwavering faith allows your patron to quietly guide your senses toward approaching danger. Though your body may sleep, your spirit remains ever watchful, instinctively alert to hostile beings that threaten those under your protection.

When battle is joined, that same divine awareness allows you to react with remarkable speed. Rather than watching helplessly as an ally suffers a devastating blow, you instinctively place yourself between them and danger, trusting your faith, armour, and unwavering resolve to endure what others cannot.

To those who travel beside you, your presence offers more than protection—it offers peace of mind. They know that, while you still stand, someone is always watching over them.

## Rank 1
### Description

A true Paladin never truly lowers their guard. Even during moments of rest, your unwavering faith allows your patron to quietly guide your senses toward approaching danger. Though your body may sleep, your spirit remains ever watchful, instinctively alert to hostile beings that threaten those under your protection.

When battle is joined, that same divine awareness allows you to react with remarkable speed. Rather than watching helplessly as an ally suffers a devastating blow, you instinctively place yourself between them and danger, trusting your faith, armour, and unwavering resolve to endure what others cannot.

To those who travel beside you, your presence offers more than protection—it offers peace of mind. They know that, while you still stand, someone is always watching over them.

### Effects

#### Passive — Ever Vigilant

- Even while **resting**, **sleeping**, or otherwise not actively standing watch, you remain spiritually alert.
- You may still attempt **Perception Checks** to detect the approach of **hostile creatures or humanoids** that present an immediate threat to you or your allies.
- These Perception Checks are made with **Disadvantage**.
- **Ever Vigilant** cannot be used to detect traps, poisons, hidden objects, environmental hazards, magical effects, or any other non-creature dangers.
- Additional passive effects granted by your patron's **Divine Authority** apply where applicable.

#### Active — Vigilant Protector

- **Reaction**
- Spend **10 MP** and **30 SP**.
- **Cooldown:** **4 Rounds**.
- When an allied creature within **5 metres** is targeted by a melee or ranged weapon attack, you may activate **Vigilant Protector**.
- Move up to **2 metres** towards the targeted ally without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- You must end this movement adjacent to the targeted ally.
- You may choose to become the new target of the triggering attack.
- Resolve the attack against your own **AC**, armour, resistances, and defensive effects.
- If you cannot reach the targeted ally, this ability cannot be activated.

### Lore

The oldest Paladin Orders teach that vigilance is the first duty of every guardian. Long before blades are drawn or shields are raised, a watchful protector has already begun safeguarding those entrusted to their care. Through unwavering devotion, a Paladin's patron grants subtle guidance, stirring their senses whenever hostile creatures draw near, even as they rest.

Many tales speak of champions who awoke moments before an ambush or stepped between an ally and certain death with impossible speed. Whether these moments were instinct, discipline, or divine intervention is a matter of faith. To a Paladin, however, the answer is simple—their duty is to stand between darkness and those who cannot defend themselves.

> *"A guardian's greatest strength is not the shield they carry, but the vigilance to raise it before danger strikes."*  
> **— Sir Garrick, Warden of the Eternal Gate**

## Rank 2
### Description

Your devotion has sharpened your instincts beyond those of an ordinary guardian. The quiet guidance of your patron grows clearer, allowing your senses to remain attentive even while your body rests. Though you may sleep beside your companions, your spirit remains ever watchful, instinctively searching for approaching threats before they strike.

On the battlefield, your reactions become faster and more decisive. You instinctively move to shield your allies from danger, placing yourself between them and the enemy with unwavering confidence. Every successful intervention reinforces your reputation as a steadfast protector whose first instinct is always to defend others.

### Effects

#### Passive — Ever Vigilant

- Even while **resting**, **sleeping**, or otherwise not actively standing watch, you remain spiritually alert.
- You may still attempt **Perception Checks** to detect the approach of **hostile creatures or humanoids** that present an immediate threat to you or your allies.
- These Perception Checks are made with a **−2 penalty** instead of **Disadvantage**.
- **Ever Vigilant** cannot be used to detect traps, poisons, hidden objects, environmental hazards, magical effects, or any other non-creature dangers.
- Additional passive effects granted by your patron's **Divine Authority** apply where applicable.

# Volley

## Overview
The Ranger channels primal magic into a single arrow before firing it high into the heavens. As the arrow reaches its peak, it bursts into countless spectral copies that descend upon the battlefield in an unrelenting rain of magical arrows. Rather than striking a single target, Volley transforms the chosen area into a deadly storm where every heartbeat brings the threat of another falling arrow.

At its earliest stage, the Ranger has only limited control over this magical barrage. Once unleashed, the spectral arrows cannot distinguish friend from foe, forcing allies and enemies alike to seek shelter or risk being caught beneath the storm. Though dangerous to everyone within its reach, a well-placed Volley can completely reshape the battlefield and halt an advancing force.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

The Ranger channels primal magic into a single arrow before firing it high into the heavens. As the arrow reaches its peak, it bursts into countless spectral copies that descend upon the battlefield in an unrelenting rain of magical arrows. Rather than striking a single target, Volley transforms the chosen area into a deadly storm where every heartbeat brings the threat of another falling arrow.

At its earliest stage, the Ranger has only limited control over this magical barrage. Once unleashed, the spectral arrows cannot distinguish friend from foe, forcing allies and enemies alike to seek shelter or risk being caught beneath the storm. Though dangerous to everyone within its reach, a well-placed Volley can completely reshape the battlefield and halt an advancing force.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 120 MP.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Long Rest**.
- Choose a point you can see within **60 metres**.
- Spectral arrows rain down in a **10-metre radius** centred on the chosen point.
- The volley remains active **until the start of the second Initiative Order after your own**.
- A creature must make a **DC 13 Agility (Dodge) Check**:
  - The first time it enters the affected area on its turn.
  - Or when it starts its turn within the affected area.
- A creature can only be affected **once** by each use of Volley.
- On a failed check, the creature takes **6d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- On a successful check, the creature takes **half damage**.
- **All creatures**, including allies, are affected by Volley.
- Volley requires a **clear path to the sky** and cannot be used underground, beneath a solid roof, or inside enclosed structures unless the GM determines there is sufficient overhead clearance.
- The spectral arrows disappear immediately after striking and cannot be recovered.

---

### Lore

Volley is considered one of the Ranger Lodges' oldest battlefield techniques, created for the rare occasions when a single arrow was not enough to turn the tide of battle. By surrendering precision for overwhelming area control, the Ranger commands the wilderness itself to answer their call, transforming one arrow into a storm capable of scattering entire warbands.

The earliest practitioners quickly learned that such power demanded restraint. Until complete mastery is achieved, the magical arrows recognise no friend or foe, making careful positioning as important as the technique itself. Veteran Rangers often warn apprentices that a poorly placed Volley can be just as dangerous to allies as it is to their enemies.

---

> *"One arrow begins the hunt. A thousand arrows decide its end."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's mastery over Volley continues to grow, allowing them to sustain a larger and more devastating rain of spectral arrows. What was once an uncontrollable barrage now falls with greater precision, covering a wider portion of the battlefield while maintaining its relentless assault. Though allies are still at risk, an experienced Ranger learns to position the storm where it will inflict the greatest harm upon their enemies.

As the enchanted arrow bursts overhead, countless shimmering copies spiral downward in waves, forcing creatures to either abandon their ground or endure the unending rain of magical projectiles. Few formations can remain intact beneath such overwhelming pressure.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 140 MP.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Long Rest**.
- Choose a point you can see within **75 metres**.
- Spectral arrows rain down in a **15-metre radius** centred on the chosen point.
- The volley remains active **until the start of the second Initiative Order after your own**.
- A creature must make a **DC 15 Agility (Dodge) Check**:
  - The first time it enters the affected area on its turn.
  - Or when it starts its turn within the affected area.
- A creature can only be affected **once** by each use of Volley.
- On a failed check, the creature takes **7d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- On a successful check, the creature takes **half damage**.
- **All creatures**, including allies, are affected by Volley.
- Volley requires a **clear path to the sky** and cannot be used underground, beneath a solid roof, or inside enclosed structures unless the GM determines there is sufficient overhead clearance.
- The spectral arrows disappear immediately after striking and cannot be recovered.

---

### Lore

Those who survive a Rank II Volley often describe it as standing beneath a violent storm rather than an attack. The sky darkens with spectral arrows, each one guided by primal magic instead of a Ranger's hand. Escape becomes the only sensible option, as remaining beneath the barrage invites certain injury.

Within the Ranger Lodges, apprentices are taught that Volley is as much a tool of battlefield control as it is a weapon. A well-placed barrage can scatter enemy formations, deny strategic ground, and force even the most disciplined warriors to abandon their positions.

---

> *"A hunter does not always need to strike the prey. Sometimes, they simply decide where the prey is allowed to stand."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The Ranger's command over primal magic has matured into a truly devastating battlefield technique. A single enchanted arrow now unleashes a relentless storm capable of engulfing entire formations, forcing enemies to abandon fortified positions or endure an unceasing rain of spectral arrows. Every volley is guided by the will of the wilderness, transforming open ground into a deadly killing field.

Although the Ranger's control has improved considerably, the magical storm still shows no favour. Friend and foe alike must respect its destructive power, making careful positioning and battlefield awareness essential to those fighting alongside the Ranger.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 160 MP.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Long Rest**.
- Choose a point you can see within **90 metres**.
- Spectral arrows rain down in a **20-metre radius** centred on the chosen point.
- The volley remains active **until the start of the second Initiative Order after your own**.
- A creature must make a **DC 17 Agility (Dodge) Check**:
  - The first time it enters the affected area on its turn.
  - Or when it starts its turn within the affected area.
- A creature can only be affected **once** by each use of Volley.
- On a failed check, the creature takes **8d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- On a successful check, the creature takes **half damage**.
- **All creatures**, including allies, are affected by Volley.
- Volley requires a **clear path to the sky** and cannot be used underground, beneath a solid roof, or inside enclosed structures unless the GM determines there is sufficient overhead clearance.
- The spectral arrows disappear immediately after striking and cannot be recovered.

---

### Lore

Only experienced Rangers are entrusted with the third rank of Volley. By this stage, the technique is no longer viewed as merely a powerful attack but as a method of controlling the battlefield itself. Entire companies have been forced to abandon defensive positions as waves of shimmering arrows descended from above, leaving no safe place to stand.

Veteran Huntmasters teach that Volley is not intended to eliminate every foe outright. Its true strength lies in forcing the enemy to move exactly where the Ranger wants them to go, allowing allies to exploit the chaos while the storm rages overhead.

---

> *"The wisest prey does not fear the arrow. It fears the ground the hunter has chosen."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger's mastery over Volley has reached a level where the primal magic responds to their intent as much as their aim. The storm of spectral arrows no longer falls as an indiscriminate barrage, but as a controlled rain directed toward those the Ranger wishes to punish. Entire battlefields can be reshaped as allies advance beneath a sky that only their enemies need fear.

The arrow still ascends into the heavens before splitting into countless magical copies, but the Ranger now instinctively guides the storm's path through primal will. Enemies find themselves trapped beneath a relentless downpour while companions move unhindered through the chaos, allowing coordinated assaults that were once impossible.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 180 MP.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Long Rest**.
- Choose a point you can see within **105 metres**.
- Spectral arrows rain down in a **20-metre radius** centred on the chosen point.
- The volley remains active **until the start of the second Initiative Order after your own**.
- When activating Volley, you may designate **up to 5 allied creatures** that are **immune** to this ability's effects.
- A creature must make a **DC 19 Agility (Dodge) Check**:
  - The first time it enters the affected area on its turn.
  - Or when it starts its turn within the affected area.
- A creature can only be affected **once** by each use of Volley.
- On a failed check, the creature takes **9d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- On a successful check, the creature takes **half damage**.
- All creatures not designated as immune, including neutral creatures, are affected normally.
- Volley requires a **clear path to the sky** and cannot be used underground, beneath a solid roof, or inside enclosed structures unless the GM determines there is sufficient overhead clearance.
- The spectral arrows disappear immediately after striking and cannot be recovered.

---

### Lore

Few Rangers ever develop enough control to command Volley without endangering their companions. Those who do are regarded as battlefield tacticians as much as hunters, capable of directing a magical storm with remarkable precision while their allies advance unharmed beneath it.

Within the Ranger Lodges, this achievement marks the transition from master hunter to battlefield commander. Entire warbands have marched confidently through a storm of spectral arrows, trusting completely in the judgement of the Ranger who called it forth. To witness such mastery is to understand that the wilderness itself now fights beside them.

---

> *"A storm without control is destruction. A storm guided by a Ranger is victory."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has perfected one of the Ranger Lodges' most feared techniques. A single enchanted arrow is loosed into the heavens where it bursts into an immense storm of primal energy, creating an unrelenting rain of spectral arrows across the battlefield. Every arrow is guided by the Ranger's will, striking only those they deem worthy of the hunt.

No longer an indiscriminate barrage, the final form of Volley demonstrates complete mastery over both archery and primal magic. Allies advance unhindered beneath the storm while enemies desperately seek shelter from a relentless rain that seems to pursue every movement. Entire battlefields can be dominated with a single shot, allowing the Ranger to dictate the flow of combat from incredible distances.

Among the Ranger Lodges, only the greatest Huntmasters are entrusted with this technique. To witness a master unleash Volley is to watch the sky itself become the Ranger's greatest weapon.

---

### Effects

- **Cost:** 200 MP.
- **Uses:** 2 uses per **Long Rest**.
- Choose a point you can see within **120 metres**.
- Spectral arrows rain down in a **25-metre radius** centred on the chosen point.
- The volley remains active **until the start of the second Initiative Order after your own**.
- When activating Volley, you may designate **any number of allied creatures** that are **immune** to this ability's effects.
- A creature must make a **DC 21 Agility (Dodge) Check**:
  - The first time it enters the affected area on its turn.
  - Or when it starts its turn within the affected area.
- A creature can only be affected **once** by each use of Volley.
- On a failed check, the creature takes **10d8 Magical Piercing Damage**.
- On a successful check, the creature takes **half damage**.
- Creatures that fail the Dodge Check have their **Movement Speed reduced by half until the end of their next turn** as spectral arrows pin them down and disrupt their advance.
- Volley requires a **clear path to the sky** and cannot be used underground, beneath a solid roof, or inside enclosed structures unless the GM determines there is sufficient overhead clearance.
- The spectral arrows disappear immediately after striking and cannot be recovered.

---

### Lore

The fifth rank of Volley is considered the pinnacle of battlefield archery. Few Rangers throughout history have possessed the discipline, magical control, and experience required to command such a devastating storm without endangering those fighting beside them. Those who achieve this mastery are remembered not only as legendary hunters, but as protectors capable of turning impossible battles into decisive victories.

Stories tell of entire armies brought to a halt beneath a sky filled with spectral arrows while allied forces advanced untouched through the storm. To the Ranger Lodges, this technique is the ultimate expression of the hunter's creed—not simply to defeat the prey, but to control the battlefield so completely that escape becomes impossible.

---

> *"When the heavens answer the hunter's call, even armies learn there is nowhere left to run."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Huntmaster of the Emerald Lodge**

# Weathered Predator

## Overview
The first lesson every Ranger learns is that nature is neither cruel nor kind—it simply exists. Rain will fall, winds will howl, and bitter cold will claim the unprepared. Through countless journeys beneath open skies, the Ranger's body gradually adapts to these everyday hardships, becoming far more resilient than that of an ordinary traveller.

Weathered Predator reflects the beginning of this adaptation. The Ranger no longer dreads travelling through relentless rain or sleeping beneath the stars. Their body naturally resists common weather-related illnesses, allowing them to continue the hunt while others seek warmth and shelter.

Though far from immune to nature's fury, the Ranger has taken the first steps toward becoming one of the wilderness' true survivors.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

The first lesson every Ranger learns is that nature is neither cruel nor kind—it simply exists. Rain will fall, winds will howl, and bitter cold will claim the unprepared. Through countless journeys beneath open skies, the Ranger's body gradually adapts to these everyday hardships, becoming far more resilient than that of an ordinary traveller.

Weathered Predator reflects the beginning of this adaptation. The Ranger no longer dreads travelling through relentless rain or sleeping beneath the stars. Their body naturally resists common weather-related illnesses, allowing them to continue the hunt while others seek warmth and shelter.

Though far from immune to nature's fury, the Ranger has taken the first steps toward becoming one of the wilderness' true survivors.

---

### Effects

- Gain **Advantage** on saving throws against contracting **weather-related illnesses**, including:
  - Common Cold.
  - Influenza (Flu).
  - Similar non-magical illnesses caused by prolonged exposure to rain, damp conditions, or changing weather.
- Reduce penalties caused by **heavy rain** by **50%**, including penalties to travel, perception, or ranged attacks where appropriate (GM discretion).
- Double the time you can comfortably remain in wet weather before making checks against exposure.
- Gain **+2** to Survival checks made during rainfall or storms.

---

### Lore

Among the Ranger Lodges, apprentices are rarely given comfortable lodgings. Instead, they are encouraged to experience the wilderness in all its forms—walking through days of relentless rain, sleeping beneath soaked cloaks, and learning that discomfort is simply another part of the journey.

Veteran Rangers often joke that they stopped noticing the rain years ago. What once felt cold and miserable has become little more than another companion upon the trail. This quiet resilience is the first step towards enduring the far greater trials that await in Asteria's wild places.

---

> *"Rain only bothers those who still believe they'll stay dry."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's body continues to adapt to the harsh realities of the wilderness. Long days spent traversing frozen trails, enduring relentless snowfall, and surviving bitter mountain nights have hardened both body and mind. Conditions that force most travellers to seek shelter become little more than another challenge to overcome.

While snow and freezing temperatures remain dangerous, the Ranger has learned how to conserve body heat, recognise the earliest signs of exposure, and keep moving when others would falter. This resilience allows them to remain effective during hunts, even when winter itself becomes an enemy.

Among the Ranger Lodges, mastering the frozen wilderness is considered the first true test of a hunter's endurance.

---

### Effects

- Gain **Advantage** on saving throws against **Hypothermia**, **Frostbite**, and other non-magical cold-weather conditions.
- Reduce penalties caused by **snowfall** and **freezing temperatures** by **50%**, including penalties to travel, perception, and ranged attacks where appropriate (GM discretion).
- Double the amount of time you can safely remain in freezing environments before making Constitution or Endurance checks for exposure.
- Gain **+2** to **Survival** checks made in snowy or frozen environments.
- Ignore movement penalties caused by **light snow** and **shallow snow** outside of combat.

---

### Lore

Every Ranger remembers their first true winter. Endless snow, freezing winds, and bitter nights teach lessons that cannot be learned anywhere else. Those who endure emerge with a newfound respect for the cold, understanding that preparation and perseverance matter far more than strength alone.

Veteran Rangers often travel through snowstorms with little concern, reading tracks hidden beneath fresh snowfall and navigating blizzards by instinct. To them, winter is no longer an obstacle—it is simply another season in which the hunt continues.

Within the Ranger Lodges, surviving the frozen wilds marks the transition from apprentice to seasoned hunter, proving that the wilderness cannot easily claim those who have learned to respect it.

---

> *"Winter does not care how strong you are. It only asks how long you can endure."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

Having conquered the relentless cold, the Ranger now learns to endure the opposite extreme. Scorching deserts, blazing grasslands, volcanic plains, and relentless summer heat are no longer insurmountable obstacles. Through experience and discipline, the Ranger has learned to regulate their body, conserve precious water, and recognise the warning signs of heat exhaustion long before they become life-threatening.

Every expedition across sun-scorched landscapes teaches another lesson in survival. The Ranger instinctively seeks shade, travels with the rhythm of the environment, and understands that patience is often more valuable than speed. What would cripple an inexperienced traveller becomes another challenge to overcome.

Within the Ranger Lodges, surviving both the frozen north and the burning south is considered proof that a hunter has begun to master every face of the wilderness.

---

### Effects

- Gain **Advantage** on saving throws against **Heat Exhaustion**, **Heatstroke**, **Dehydration**, and other non-magical heat-related conditions.
- Reduce penalties caused by **extreme heat** and **desert environments** by **50%**, including penalties to travel, perception, and ranged attacks where appropriate (GM discretion).
- Double the amount of time you can safely travel in extreme heat before making Constitution or Endurance checks for exposure.
- Consume **50% less water** while travelling through hot or arid environments.
- Gain **+2** to **Survival** checks made in deserts, badlands, volcanic regions, and other hot environments.

---

### Lore

The deserts of Asteria have claimed more lives than many wars. Endless dunes, shimmering heat, and a complete absence of water quickly humble those who underestimate them. Rangers who survive these harsh lands develop an understanding of the sun that few others ever achieve, learning to work with the environment rather than against it.

Among experienced Rangers, it is often said that true endurance is measured not by how long one can march, but by how well one adapts when the world itself becomes the enemy. Those who master the burning wilderness are respected throughout the Lodges, for they have proven that no climate alone can halt the hunt.

---

> *"The desert offers no mercy. It simply rewards those wise enough to respect it."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

By the fourth rank, the Ranger has endured nearly every climate Asteria can offer. They have crossed frozen mountain passes during blizzards, survived weeks beneath relentless desert suns, navigated torrential monsoons, and hunted through violent storms that would force entire caravans to seek shelter.

The Ranger's body and instincts have adapted to nature's most violent expressions. While ordinary travellers struggle against the elements, the Ranger remains focused on the hunt, treating extreme weather as another obstacle to overcome rather than a reason to turn back.

Within the Ranger Lodges, those who reach this level are known as **Stormwalkers**, hunters whose determination is said to rival the fury of nature itself.

---

### Effects

- Gain **Advantage** on saving throws against all **non-magical weather-related conditions**, including:
  - Hypothermia.
  - Frostbite.
  - Heat Exhaustion.
  - Heatstroke.
  - Dehydration.
  - Weather-related illnesses.
- Reduce penalties caused by **blizzards**, **sandstorms**, **torrential rain**, **high winds**, and similar non-magical weather events by **50%**.
- Gain **+4** to **Survival** checks made during severe weather.
- Double the amount of time you can safely travel through extreme weather before making Constitution or Endurance checks for exposure.
- Natural weather no longer imposes penalties on your ranged weapon attacks unless visibility is completely obscured.
- Ignore movement penalties caused by **deep snow**, **loose sand**, and **heavy mud** outside of combat.

---

### Lore

Only the most accomplished Rangers earn the title of Stormwalker. These hunters have faced nature at its most unforgiving and emerged stronger for it. Their stories tell of tracking prey through raging blizzards, crossing deserts during sandstorms, and pursuing monsters through storms that shattered entire forests.

The Ranger Lodges teach that nature is never an enemy to be conquered, but a force to be understood. Those who survive its greatest trials learn to move with the storm instead of against it. To witness a Stormwalker calmly continue the hunt while lightning tears across the sky is to understand why they are respected throughout Asteria.

---

> *"Most flee when the storm arrives. A Ranger knows the storm often hides the perfect opportunity to hunt."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has become a true master of the wilderness. Years of enduring nature's harshest trials have forged a body and mind capable of thriving where others merely survive. Rain no longer soaks their resolve, freezing winds fail to slow their stride, and blistering deserts cannot break their determination. The wilderness has become their home.

Every environment tells a story, and the Ranger has lived them all. They understand when to move, when to rest, and how to adapt before nature's fury can take its toll. Companions often find themselves surviving impossible journeys simply because they chose to follow a Ranger who has mastered the wild.

Among the Ranger Lodges, those who achieve this rank are honoured as **Wardens of the Wild**, individuals whose knowledge and endurance are considered the pinnacle of mortal survival.

---

### Effects

- Gain **Advantage** on all saving throws against **non-magical environmental effects**, including:
  - Weather-related illnesses.
  - Hypothermia.
  - Frostbite.
  - Heat Exhaustion.
  - Heatstroke.
  - Dehydration.
  - Altitude sickness.
  - Fatigue caused by natural climates.
- Ignore **all penalties** caused by **non-magical weather**, including:
  - Heavy rain.
  - Snowfall.
  - Blizzards.
  - Sandstorms.
  - High winds.
  - Extreme heat.
  - Extreme cold.
- Gain **+6** to all **Survival** checks made in natural environments.
- You require only **half the normal food and water** needed to survive while travelling through natural environments.
- Natural weather never imposes penalties on your ranged weapon attacks or vision unless visibility is completely obscured.
- You automatically succeed on checks to establish a safe campsite or shelter in natural environments, provided suitable materials are available.
- You may travel for **twice as long** in non-magical extreme environments before making Constitution or Endurance checks for fatigue or exposure.

---

### Lore

The title **Warden of the Wild** is rarely bestowed, for it represents the highest expression of a Ranger's relationship with nature. These legendary hunters are spoken of in stories as though they belong to the wilderness itself. They cross frozen tundras without complaint, traverse endless deserts with little more than a waterskin, and emerge from storms that leave entire expeditions stranded.

The Ranger Lodges teach that this mastery is not achieved by conquering nature, but by respecting it. Every storm endured, every mountain crossed, and every frozen night survived becomes another lesson carried for life. Those who reach this level no longer fight against the wilderness—they move with it, understanding its rhythms as naturally as their own heartbeat.

To many, such resilience appears supernatural. Rangers simply smile, knowing that every lesson was earned one difficult journey at a time.

---

> *"Nature does not grant favour to the strongest. It rewards those who learn to endure every season beneath its endless sky."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, Warden of the Emerald Lodge**

## Prerequisites
None

## Scaling
See individual rank details.

## Synergy
Information coming soon.

## GM Notes
GM-only information coming soon.

### description

by the fourth rank, the ranger has endured nearly every climate asteria can offer. they have crossed frozen mountain passes during blizzards, survived weeks beneath relentless desert suns, navigated torrential monsoons, and hunted through violent storms that would force entire caravans to seek shelter.

the ranger's body and instincts have adapted to nature's most violent expressions. while ordinary travellers struggle against the elements, the ranger remains focused on the hunt, treating extreme weather as another obstacle to overcome rather than a reason to turn back.

within the ranger lodges, those who reach this level are known as **stormwalkers**, hunters whose determination is said to rival the fury of nature itself.

---

### effects

- gain **advantage** on saving throws against all **non-magical weather-related conditions**, including:
  - hypothermia.
  - frostbite.
  - heat exhaustion.
  - heatstroke.
  - dehydration.
  - weather-related illnesses.
- reduce penalties caused by **blizzards**, **sandstorms**, **torrential rain**, **high winds**, and similar non-magical weather events by **50%**.
- gain **+4** to **survival** checks made during severe weather.
- double the amount of time you can safely travel through extreme weather before making constitution or endurance checks for exposure.
- natural weather no longer imposes penalties on your ranged weapon attacks unless visibility is completely obscured.
- ignore movement penalties caused by **deep snow**, **loose sand**, and **heavy mud** outside of combat.

---

### lore

only the most accomplished rangers earn the title of stormwalker. these hunters have faced nature at its most unforgiving and emerged stronger for it. their stories tell of tracking prey through raging blizzards, crossing deserts during sandstorms, and pursuing monsters through storms that shattered entire forests.

the ranger lodges teach that nature is never an enemy to be conquered, but a force to be understood. those who survive its greatest trials learn to move with the storm instead of against it. to witness a stormwalker calmly continue the hunt while lightning tears across the sky is to understand why they are respected throughout asteria.

---

> *"most flee when the storm arrives. a ranger knows the storm often hides the perfect opportunity to hunt."*  
> — **grand ranger elyas thornwood**

## rank 5
### description

the ranger has become a true master of the wilderness. years of enduring nature's harshest trials have forged a body and mind capable of thriving where others merely survive. rain no longer soaks their resolve, freezing winds fail to slow their stride, and blistering deserts cannot break their determination. the wilderness has become their home.

every environment tells a story, and the ranger has lived them all. they understand when to move, when to rest, and how to adapt before nature's fury can take its toll. companions often find themselves surviving impossible journeys simply because they chose to follow a ranger who has mastered the wild.

among the ranger lodges, those who achieve this rank are honoured as **wardens of the wild**, individuals whose knowledge and endurance are considered the pinnacle of mortal survival.

---

  - dehydration.
  - altitude sickness.
  - fatigue caused by natural climates.
- ignore **all penalties** caused by **non-magical weather**, including:
  - heavy rain.
  - snowfall.
  - blizzards.
  - sandstorms.
  - high winds.
  - extreme heat.
  - extreme cold.
- gain **+6** to all **survival** checks made in natural environments.
- you require only **half the normal food and water** needed to survive while travelling through natural environments.
- natural weather never imposes penalties on your ranged weapon attacks or vision unless visibility is completely obscured.
- you automatically succeed on checks to establish a safe campsite or shelter in natural environments, provided suitable materials are available.
- you may travel for **twice as long** in non-magical extreme environments before making constitution or endurance checks for fatigue or exposure.

---

### lore

the title **warden of the wild** is rarely bestowed, for it represents the highest expression of a ranger's relationship with nature. these legendary hunters are spoken of in stories as though they belong to the wilderness itself. they cross frozen tundras without complaint, traverse endless deserts with little more than a waterskin, and emerge from storms that leave entire expeditions stranded.

the ranger lodges teach that this mastery is not achieved by conquering nature, but by respecting it. every storm endured, every mountain crossed, and every frozen night survived becomes another lesson carried for life. those who reach this level no longer fight against the wilderness—they move with it, understanding its rhythms as naturally as their own heartbeat.

to many, such resilience appears supernatural. rangers simply smile, knowing that every lesson was earned one difficult journey at a time.

---

> *"nature does not grant favour to the strongest. it rewards those who learn to endure every season beneath its endless sky."*  
> — **grand ranger elyas thornwood, warden of the emerald lodge**
